entries.review_description: Drawing canvas. The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome. Captured in light mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: Resting canvas reads cleanly. The top palette row shows five well-spaced circular swatches with the active purple one clearly ringed for selection state; all sit fully inside the 375px width with even gaps and no clipping or crowding. The blank textured canvas fills the remaining height with no stray marks or overlap. The docked red trash button in the upper right is high-contrast and legible against the canvas. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron at the bottom left and the gear at the bottom right are each visible as distinct shapes, sitting in opposite corners well clear of the palette and of each other. No text is present to fit or truncate, no scrolling region is in view, and no overlay is open. Touch targets in the palette and the trash button are generously sized and separated.

entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: The dark-mode canvas is a near-uniform dark charcoal with a subtle noise texture; the top palette bar sits on a slightly darker strip, and every color swatch (purple, blue, yellow, white, multicolor) reads with strong separation against it. The selected purple swatch's ring indicator is clearly visible. The docked round trash button is a saturated pink/red disc with a bright yellow glyph — high contrast against both the canvas and the palette bar. The bottom-corner chevron and the settings gear are faint gray glyphs, but both shapes are locatable in the frame, which is the floor those parent-facing controls owe; their subdued weight is the intended resting styling. No text is present to evaluate. Nothing in the image is illegible or ambiguous under night mode.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: The sign-in surface renders cleanly at 375×812. Hierarchy is clear: "Back to drawing" link and the dotted "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark share the top row without collision, "Admin" is the dominant heading with "Manage AI access codes" as a subordinate line, and the "SIGN IN" label with its trailing rule separates the form section. The input and "Sign in" button sit on one row, are vertically aligned, share consistent corner rounding, and both meet comfortable touch-target height; the placeholder "Admin access key" fits inside the field with room to spare and the button label is fully contained. Margins are even on both sides and consistent between the header, heading, and form block. No clipping, overlap, truncation, or overflow is visible. The large empty area below the form is the expected result of a single-field signed-out state, not a layout fault. No modal or scrolling region is present to assess.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in surface is mostly sound: "Admin" and "Manage AI access codes" are near-white on the dark ground and read cleanly, the purple "Sign in" button carries white bold text with a clearly visible fill, and the "← Back to drawing" link is a bright purple that stands well clear of the background. The weak points are the small gray secondary text. The "SIGN IN" section eyebrow is tiny, letter-spaced uppercase in a dim gray that sits only modestly above the panel color, and the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark next to the dot cluster in the header is the same treatment at similar or smaller size — both are legible when looked at directly but sit near the practical floor for small text at this size in dark mode. The field placeholder "Admin access key" is likewise a muted gray inside a dark input whose border is only a faint outline, so the input's edges and its prompt both read softly against the page. None of these are unreadable, and none of them are the primary path (the heading, the field, and the button are all clear), so this reads as a minor polish issue rather than a blocker. No element in the frame is illegible or lost.
entries.recommendation: Lift the small gray secondary text one step in dark mode — the "SIGN IN" eyebrow, the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark, and the input placeholder — and brighten the text input's border slightly so the field boundary and its prompt both clear a comfortable contrast margin at these small sizes.

entries.surface_description: The complete release history at its opening position.
entries.critique: The Changelog opening screen reads cleanly at 375×812. Hierarchy is clear and well-ordered: the "← Back to drawing" link and dotted SPLOTCH wordmark sit on one header line without collision, the "Changelog" H1 dominates, the two-line intro sits at a comfortable measure, and the CONTENTS card with its "7 releases ›" affordance is separated by a rule before the release stream begins. Within the entry, "Version 1.5.0" / "August 12, 2026" / emoji-led "✨ New" and "🚀 Improved" subheads / bulleted items form four distinct, correctly ranked levels. Spacing is even and rhythmic — consistent bullet leading, consistent gaps between subhead groups, matching left margins across all text blocks with the bullet list indented as a set. No text is clipped or overlapping; multi-line bullets wrap normally and no line collides with the right edge. Touch targets are legible: the back link and the CONTENTS row read as tappable, and the CONTENTS row spans the full card width with generous vertical padding. The thinned, washed-out "Smoother iPad drawing, coloring, undo," line at the bottom edge is the app's scroll-fade cue painted over the last line, so it is not a legibility fault; all content clear of that strip is fully crisp. No modal or scrim is present. I found no actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_description: The complete release history at its opening position.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the changelog's opening view holds up throughout. Body copy, the "Changelog" title, "Version 1.5.0", the emoji-led "New" and "Improved" section headings, and every bullet render as light gray/near-white on the near-black page, all clearly legible. The purple back link and the "7 releases ›" accent inside the contents card carry enough luminance against the slightly lifted card fill to be read as interactive without straining. Secondary text — the "CONTENTS" eyebrow and the "August 12, 2026" date — is intentionally quieter but still resolves cleanly at this size. The bullet glyphs and the thin divider rule above "Version 1.5.0" are faint, which is appropriate for structural, non-informational marks. The partially washed-out final line at the bottom edge is the scroll fade painted over the last row, so it is excluded from the contrast judgement; all content clear of that strip is legible.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
At its opening position the page is clean and well ordered: theme toggle and brand mark at the top, a full-width "CONTENTS · 16 sections ›" row, then the "← Back to drawing" link, the two-line H1, a lead paragraph, a small sources line, and the lavender "Not sure? Start here" card. Hierarchy is unambiguous — the H1 dominates, the lead paragraph sits a clear step below, the sources line a step below that. Spacing is even and nothing is clipped, overlapped, or truncated; the title breaks cleanly and every line of body copy wraps inside the 375px width. The CONTENTS row and the back link are comfortably tappable, and the sun/moon toggle pills are generously sized.

The one visible weakness is inside the "Not sure? Start here" card. Its prose is set in a light gray-violet on a light lavender fill, noticeably lighter than the body text just above it on white, and it is interrupted every few words by purple monospace token names (--surface, --font-size-sm, --ease-pop, …). The result is a long paragraph whose baseline text is the weakest-contrast running copy in the frame while the inline code — secondary detail — is the strongest thing in the card. For the block positioned as the orientation entry point, the emphasis is inverted and the prose reads harder than the plain body copy it summarizes.

Also worth noting, though not itself a defect: the sources line under the lead sets links and code at very small size with dot separators and runs to three lines; it holds together but is the densest small type on the screen.
entries.recommendation: Darken the "Not sure? Start here" card's prose to at least the contrast of the body copy above it, so the running sentences read as strongly as the inline token names rather than weaker than them.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast is broadly sound at the opening position. The H1 "Splotch design system", the lead paragraph, the "← Back to drawing" link, the "CONTENTS / 16 sections ›" bar, and the SPLOTCH wordmark all render at high luminance against the near-black page and are easily legible. The theme toggle's active moon glyph sits on a lighter pill and is clearly distinguishable from the inactive sun. Within the purple "Not sure? entries.critique: Layout, hierarchy and text fit are sound at 375x812: "Send us feedback" leads clearly, the intro paragraph wraps without overflow, the segmented control, textarea, checkbox, privacy note, primary button and "What happens next" card stack with consistent gutters and vertical rhythm. No clipping, overlap, or horizontal overflow is visible; the bottom card thins into the app's documented scroll fade, so its lower lines are the cue being drawn, not a defect. Two visible issues: (1) the unselected segment label "I have an idea" is rendered as mid-gray text on the light-gray inactive track, markedly lower contrast than the selected "Something's broken" on its white chip — this is an active, tappable control, so its label should stay clearly legible while still reading unselected; (2) the "Include device info" checkbox is a small square about one text line tall with no visible padded hit area, and there is no visual indication that its two-line label extends the target, leaving touch-target clarity below what the rest of the form's controls (full-width button, large tap chips) establish.
entries.recommendation: Darken the unselected segment label ("I have an idea") to a text tone that clearly passes body-text contrast against the inactive gray track, relying on the white chip and elevation rather than faded text to signal selection; and give the "Include device info" checkbox a minimum 44x44 tap area with its label included in the hit region.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this screen is mostly sound: the "Send us feedback" heading, the intro paragraph, the "What went wrong?" label, and the white-on-purple "Send report" button all read cleanly against the near-black page. The textarea placeholder and its border are visible, and the "What happens next" card's heading and first list line are legible (the thinning on the following line sits in the fade strip and is not judged).

Two muted-gray text treatments sit noticeably weaker than everything else. The inactive segmented-control label "I have an idea" is a low-contrast gray on a gray pill; it is the only affordance telling a parent the form has a second mode, and at a glance it reads more like disabled text than a tappable alternative. The privacy note beneath the checkbox ("Your report goes to our private support tracker. Please don't include personal details…") is the faintest block of type in the frame — small, gray, and dimmer than the checkbox label above it — despite carrying the instruction not to paste personal data. The checkbox label itself is mid-gray and borderline but still readable. None of this is hidden, so it is a legibility weakness rather than a failure.
entries.recommendation: Lift the muted gray used for the inactive tab label ("I have an idea") and the privacy note under the checkbox to a brighter dark-theme foreground (roughly the tone of the intro paragraph) so both clear ~4.5:1 against their backgrounds, keeping the inactive tab distinguishable from the selected one via its pill background rather than by dimming its text.

entries.critique: At the opening position the page reads cleanly. Hierarchy is unambiguous: a back link and wordmark in the header, a large bold "Privacy policy" title, a plain-language intro paragraph, then a small uppercase letter-spaced "THE SHORT VERSION" eyebrow with a rule running to the right edge, followed by the summary card. Type sizes step down sensibly and line lengths sit at a comfortable measure for 375px with generous, even line spacing. The card of six points is well structured — each row pairs a colored pill with a bold lead phrase and lighter continuation, separated by hairline dividers with consistent vertical rhythm; the color pills align to the first text line and no text collides with them. Nothing is clipped horizontally, no text overlaps, no element overflows its container, and margins are symmetric left and right. The only interactive element visible, "← Back to drawing," is legible, purple-tinted to read as a link, and sits with clear space around it in the top-left. The card simply continues past the bottom edge of the viewport, which is ordinary scroll continuation at an opening capture rather than a fit or clipping fault. Contrast is adequate throughout: dark heading text, medium-gray body copy, and the small "Last updated August 20, 2026" line, while the lightest text on screen, is still readable at its size. No actionable visible issue.

entries.critique: Night-mode rendering of the privacy policy at its opening position. Page ground is a deep near-black navy; the "Privacy policy" heading and the intro paragraph are near-white and read cleanly at a glance. The "← Back to drawing" link is rendered in a light lavender/purple that stays clearly separated from the dark ground and reads as a link. The bulleted card sits on a slightly lifted panel with a faint purple border that is visible without competing with the text; inside it, bold lead-ins ("No ads.", "No tracking.", "No accounts.", "No analytics.", "No surprises.", "Works offline.") are near-white and the trailing explanatory clauses are a lighter gray that remains comfortably legible at this size. The colored pills (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple) are decorative markers, not information carriers, and each is distinct against the panel. The dimmest type in the frame is the "THE SHORT VERSION" eyebrow and the "Last updated August 20, 2026" line, both mid-gray on dark; they are secondary metadata, remain fully readable letter by letter here, and the divider rule beside the eyebrow is faint but is decorative. No text in the capture is washed out, blurred, or lost into the background, and nothing shows a color pairing that collapses in night mode. No actionable contrast or legibility defect is visible.

entries.critique: The Android tab of the beta sign-up page renders cleanly at 375×812. Hierarchy is clear: back link and brand mark on one row, a two-line H1 ("Join the Splotch beta"), an intro paragraph, then a two-tab row with Android selected and marked by both purple label/icon and a full-width underline, so the active tab is unambiguous. Below it, the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" eyebrow with its trailing rule separates the step list, and numbered circular badges plus bold step titles give each step a consistent, scannable start. Spacing is even between steps and between paragraph and CTA; the tab row's touch height and the full-width "Join the testers group" button are comfortably tappable, and the button's white-on-purple label is centered with generous padding. Text fit is good — no truncation, no overlap, no awkward hyphenation; inline bold ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester") is used consistently for UI references. The bottom line of step 2 thins out into the soft gradient at the page edge, which is this app's scroll-continues cue drawn over the last line rather than a legibility fault; all content clear of that strip is fully legible. No clipping, no overlap, no visual-consistency breaks visible in the frame.

entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this Android tab is largely sound: the "Join the Splotch beta" heading and intro paragraph are near-white on the dark ground, body copy in both steps is light gray and comfortably legible, bolded run-in phrases ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester") read clearly against surrounding text, and the purple "Join the testers group" button carries white label text with ample contrast. The active Android tab is purple with a purple underline and the inactive "iPhone / iPad" tab is dimmer gray - a clear, readable selected/unselected pair. The bottom of the frame thins into the scroll fade, which is the intended cue and not judged. One element falls short: the numbered step badges. The "1" and "2" sit inside small circular discs whose fill is only marginally lighter than the page background, and the numerals are rendered in a dim muted tone at a very small size. Against the crisp white step titles beside them ("Join the testers group", "Opt in on Google Play"), the digits read as barely-there smudges - at a glance the discs look nearly empty. These numerals are load-bearing wayfinding for a sequential instruction list, and the body copy cross-references them ("the same account you used in step 1"), so a reader who cannot resolve the digit loses the reference. This is primary instructional content in the main reading column, not a subdued-by-design parent control and not a scrim. Below the bar for a separate finding: the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" eyebrow is small, wide-tracked gray caps noticeably dimmer than the content it introduces - legible, but the weakest text in the frame after the step digits.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-number badges' contrast: brighten the numeral to the same near-white (or light purple) as the step title beside it, and/or lighten the disc fill so the circle and digit separate clearly from the page background at that small size.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this iOS TestFlight tab is broadly sound: the headline, body paragraphs, and the "Get TestFlight from Apple" button (white on saturated violet) all read cleanly against the near-black page, and the active "iPhone / iPad" tab is clearly distinguished by its violet label and underline. The eyebrow label "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" is small and letterspaced but stays legible. The dimming of the last visible line of body text at the bottom edge is the scroll fade being drawn and is not counted here.

The one visible weakness is the numbered step markers. The "1" and "2" numerals sit inside small dark plum/maroon discs, and the digit is rendered in a muted tone only slightly lighter than the disc fill. At this size the numerals read as smudges rather than as digits — noticeably harder to resolve than the bold white step titles beside them ("Install TestFlight", "Accept the invitation"). Since these markers carry the ordering information for a multi-step instruction sequence, they should not be the least legible text on the screen. The inactive "Android" tab label is gray, which is appropriate for an unselected tab, and remains readable.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the step numerals inside the circular step markers — lighten the digit toward the body-text foreground (or darken the disc fill) so the "1"/"2" clear roughly 4.5:1 against their disc and read as digits at 375px width.

entries.critique: The screen is a single centered stack: purple blob mark, "Oops!" heading, a two-line body message, and a filled "Start over" pill button. Hierarchy is unambiguous — heading is the largest and darkest element, body text is smaller and gray, and the only action is the highest-saturation object in the frame. Spacing is even and rhythmic (blob → heading → body → button), and the whole group sits slightly above optical center, which reads intentional. Text fits within comfortable side margins; the body wraps to two lines with a balanced ragged break and no orphan word. No clipping, truncation, or overlap anywhere. The button is a large pill with generous horizontal and vertical padding, well above minimum touch-target size, and its label is centered with clear padding on all sides; its affordance is obvious against the near-white background. Contrast is fine for the heading and the white-on-purple button label; the gray body copy is lighter but still legible at this size, and it is supporting text rather than a control. No overlays, scrim, or scrolling region is present, so nothing to assess there. Visual consistency holds: one purple family across the blob and button, one type family, consistent centering axis.

entries.critique: The Sound settings card renders cleanly at 375 × 812. Hierarchy reads top-down: title row ("Sound" with a back chevron at left and a close X at right), a grouped card containing the master Sound toggle plus a Volume row with its slider, then the "WHAT MAKES SOUND" section label above Drawing and Deleting rows. Group padding, row heights, and the gaps between the two groups are even; label baselines align with their icons and toggles. All text fits on one line with no truncation, wrapping, clipping, or overlap — "Volume" and its "50%" value sit at opposite ends of the row with ample space between. Toggles are full-size pill switches, clearly in the on state, with generous tap area; rows are tall enough to read as targets themselves. The slider fill at roughly half the track matches the stated 50%. The card's bottom edge closes below the Deleting row with normal padding and no cut-off content, so nothing indicates an unscrolled overflow. The canvas, top color palette, trash button, and both bottom-corner glyphs sit under the dialog scrim, dimmed as expected; the chevron and the settings gear are both locatable in the lower corners. Visual language is consistent with the rest of the settings surface — same purple accent, same rounded group cards, same emoji/glyph icon treatment.

entries.critique:
The Tool Drawer settings card is well ordered and legible in light mode: the header row (back chevron, "Tool Drawer" title, circular X) is balanced, the two top setting cards and the "DRAWING TOOLS" group are separated by clear spacing, and every row uses the same height, icon column, label baseline, and right-aligned toggle. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping; the helper line under "Enable Advanced Controls" wraps cleanly to two lines inside its card. Toggles and the close button are comfortably sized touch targets.

The one visible inconsistency is the Button Size control: the value reads "100%" at the right of the row, but the filled portion of the slider ends at approximately the midpoint of the track, with the remaining half unfilled. As presented, the numeric readout and the thumb position contradict each other — a viewer of this screen cannot tell whether 100% is the maximum (in which case the fill is wrong) or the middle of a wider range (in which case nothing on screen says so).

The drawing-tools list also ends flush at the card's lower edge just below the "Undo" row with plain white space and no fade along that edge, so there is no visible cue as to whether the list continues; this is ambiguous rather than clearly wrong, since the last row is fully drawn and clear of any edge treatment.
entries.recommendation: Make the Button Size slider fill agree with its readout — either fill the track fully when the value reads 100%, or label the range (e.g. show min/max endpoints or "50–150%") so a mid-track thumb at 100% is self-explanatory.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the Tool Drawer card is broadly sound: the card sits well above the darkened page behind it, row labels (Enable Advanced Controls, Button Size, Crayon, Magic brush, Eraser, Stroke width, Undo) render near-white on the dark row fills and are crisply legible, the purple toggles read clearly as on against both the row fill and the card, the filled portion of the Button Size slider is unmistakable against its unfilled track, and the back chevron and close X are legible glyphs inside visible outlined circles. The tool emoji glyphs also hold up.

The weak points are both secondary type. The helper line "Show and hide individual on-screen buttons" is rendered in a mid-gray that sits close in luminance to the row fill it is painted on; it is readable but visibly the faintest text on the card, and it is the only place a control's behavior is explained. The "DRAWING TOOLS" section header is small, letterspaced, all-caps gray on the card background — the smallest and lightest text in the frame, and letterspaced caps at that size lose stroke weight, so it reads as a faint band rather than a clear divider. Neither is illegible, but both are the elements most likely to drop below comfortable reading in a dim room, which is exactly the condition night mode targets.

The faint chevron and gear at the bottom of the frame are locatable in shape and are the intended resting styling of those parent-facing controls, so they are not counted here. Nothing on the card is clipped, smeared, or lost to the scrim.
entries.recommendation: Lift the two secondary text tones in dark mode — raise the helper/subtitle gray (e.g. "Show and hide individual on-screen buttons") and the "DRAWING TOOLS" section header to at least a 4.5:1 luminance against the surface each is painted on, and give the small letterspaced caps header a slightly heavier weight so its strokes survive at that size.

entries.critique: The Coloring settings card is well structured overall — clear title row, visible close button, three legible grouped rows, and adequate touch targets — but the middle row has two visible defects. First, the label "Download over mobile data" extends to the exact left edge of its toggle with no visible gap, unlike rows 1 and 3 which have ample clearance; the text reads as having outgrown its column and crowds the control. Second, the gray grouped background for that row terminates just below the toggle, so its supporting text ("Allows automatic picture downloads when Wi-Fi isn't available") sits on the white card surface, while the equivalent supporting text in the "Coloring book" and "Downloaded pictures" rows is enclosed within the gray container. Two rows of the same type are containerized differently, breaking the visual consistency of the group. Hierarchy, spacing rhythm elsewhere, the destructive Remove button, the scrim over the canvas, and the faint corner glyphs are all fine and locatable.
entries.recommendation: Give the "Download over mobile data" row the same treatment as its siblings: reserve a fixed minimum gap (≥12pt) between the label column and the toggle so the label wraps rather than running flush to the switch, and extend that row's gray grouped background to enclose its supporting description text as rows 1 and 3 do.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the open Coloring card is broadly sound: the "Coloring" title, the row labels ("Coloring book", "Download over mobile data", "Downloaded pictures"), and the white close X all read cleanly against the dark card and its slightly lighter row surfaces. The purple/white on-toggle and the white off-toggle knob are clearly distinguishable, and the secondary descriptor lines stay legible at their reduced weight. The corner settings glyph and expand chevron are faint by design and both locatable; the dimmed canvas and palette behind the card are the dialog scrim, so neither is a finding.

The fill is also only marginally lighter than the row card behind it, so the button's edge is faint and it reads more like tinted text than a pressable target. It stays readable, but with less margin than the surrounding UI.

The back chevron in the top-left circular button is also the dimmest of the card's three chrome controls, but it is clearly locatable and far less marginal than the destructive button.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in the AI Art settings card is largely sound: the "AI Art" heading, back and close buttons, row labels ("Create AI Images", "Customize AI Style"), their description copy, the "Access Code" label, the monospace `daycare-club` field value, and the red "Forget" button all read clearly against the dark card surface. The purple enabled toggles are easily distinguished from the gray off-state toggle.

One legibility weakness is visible. The explanatory paragraph in the access-code block — "You have special access via an access code — AI art is on us, no API key needed. Forget the code any time to remove it." — is rendered in a distinctly dimmer gray than the sibling description text elsewhere in the same card ("A finished drawing can now be turned into an AI picture based on it." and "Offers a small set of distinct styles to pick from before the picture is generated."). Only the bolded "special access" span holds normal contrast; the remainder of the sentence, which carries the actionable instruction about removing the code, is the faintest body copy in the card. This paragraph sits in the middle of the card, well clear of the bottom fade strip, so the dimness is not the scroll-fade cue.

The dimmed "Auto-Save AI Images" row at the card's bottom edge is under the fade gradient and is judged as the scroll cue, not a contrast finding. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable in the frame, meeting their findability floor.
entries.recommendation: Raise the access-code explainer paragraph ("You have special access… Forget the code any time to remove it.") to the same foreground color token used by the other row descriptions in this card, letting the bold "special access" span provide emphasis rather than carrying the paragraph's legibility.

entries.critique: In all three segmented controls (Generating an AI image, Reporting an AI result, Viewing external links), the unselected options "Every time" and "Per session" are drawn in a dim mid-gray on the segment track's own dark gray fill. The two values sit close together, so these labels read as washed out and near-disabled, markedly weaker than the selected "Never" label, which is crisp white on its darker filled segment. This is not the scroll fade — it is equally true in the topmost card, which sits well clear of the faded bottom strip, so it is the resting styling of the unselected segments. Because these are live, tappable choices on a parental-control screen, the dimming visually implies unavailability and a parent scanning in night mode may not read them as selectable. Secondary and smaller: the back chevron at top-left is a purple glyph on a purple disc close to it in value, so the arrow shape is faint against its container, though still locatable. The rest of the card holds up in dark mode: the "Parent Center" title, the intro paragraph, each card heading and its explanatory line, and the X in the close button all carry strong contrast against their surfaces.
entries.recommendation: Raise the unselected segment label color in dark mode to a light gray meeting at least 4.5:1 against the segment-track fill, keeping it one step below the selected label's white so selection still reads through contrast hierarchy rather than through the unselected options appearing disabled.

entries.critique:
The Feedback card is well ordered: back chevron and close button flank the title, "SEND FEEDBACK" labels the section, the intro text wraps cleanly at four lines, and the segmented control → question → textarea → checkbox → disclaimer → submit sequence reads top to bottom without overlap or clipping. Nothing is cut off by the card edges, the textarea placeholder fits on two lines, and the checkbox label wraps correctly to two lines beside its box. The page behind is scrimmed as expected and the bottom-corner chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable.

Two visible issues, both minor. First, the active segment "Something's broken" is horizontally cramped: its white pill has only a few pixels of breathing room between the text and the pill's left and right edges, while the inactive "I have an idea" sits with generous space around it, so the pair looks unbalanced and the active label reads as nearly overflowing its own chip. Second, "Send report" is rendered in white on a pale lavender fill, which is the weakest text contrast in the card — plausibly a disabled-until-typed state, but as drawn it is the primary action and its label is noticeably harder to read than the secondary body copy and the disclaimer above it.
entries.recommendation: Add horizontal padding inside the active segment pill so its label has the same side breathing room as the inactive segment, and darken the "Send report" fill (or its label color) so the primary action's text contrast is at least as strong as the surrounding body copy.

One visible deviation from the stated overlay behavior: the scrim reaches the canvas and the two bottom-corner glyphs (both read correctly dimmed), but the row of color swatches along the top edge is at full saturation and brightness — the purple, blue, gold, black, and rainbow discs are the highest-contrast elements in the whole frame, sitting above the darkened surround. With a modal open, attention is pulled to the top strip rather than held by the card, and the swatches read as still-interactive.

Secondary, lower confidence: the back chevron at top-left is a pale lavender glyph on a very light lavender disc, noticeably weaker than the adjacent X. It is locatable, so this is not a findability failure, but the two header affordances have markedly unequal contrast.
entries.recommendation: Extend the modal scrim over the top color-palette strip so the swatches darken with the rest of the page behind the Updates card, matching the treatment already applied to the canvas and the bottom-corner controls.

entries.critique: The frame shows a clean, well-ordered drawing screen. The top palette strip holds five circular swatches evenly spaced with consistent diameters and gaps; the active purple swatch is marked with a clear ring, and the multicolor "more colors" swatch reads distinctly from the solid colors. Nothing in the row is clipped, crowded, or overlapping, and the strip is separated from the canvas by a subtle divider so hierarchy between controls and drawing surface is legible. Touch targets in the row are generously sized and clearly separated for a 375pt width. The canvas fills the remaining space with the tiled paper texture rendering evenly, and the single purple stroke sits unobstructed with no controls overlapping it. The docked round trash button in the upper right is intact and readable, its icon fully within the visible portion. At the bottom, the chevron in the left corner and the gear in the right corner are both locatable as distinct shapes against the canvas, sitting quietly as intended, with no collision or crowding against the screen edges. No text is present to fit or truncate, no modal or scrolling region is open, and no element is cut off, misaligned, or inconsistent in styling.

entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The frame shows the palette strip along the top, an empty textured canvas with a single purple stroke, the docked round trash button at the top right, the faint settings gear at the bottom right, the faint collapse chevron at x≈33, y≈411, and the expanded Actions Panel: six round buttons (undo, AI wand, camera, coloring book, stroke-width wave, brush) stacked from y≈470 to y≈780.

Findable-glyph floor: both parent-facing controls pass — the chevron shape is locatable above the button stack and the gear is locatable in the bottom-right corner. Their low contrast is the settled resting style, so it is not reported.

The actionable issue is the Actions Panel column itself. Every one of the six round buttons is cut off by the left viewport edge: only roughly the right two-thirds of each white disc is on screen, and each disc's left arc is missing rather than curving closed. Unlike the trash button, which reads clearly as a deliberate dock (a full-strength colored shape hugging the right edge with a small deliberate overhang), this column reads as six discs whose left portions have run off the canvas — the icons sit visually off-center inside the remaining disc area, pushed toward the right. That weakens touch-target clarity (the tappable circle has no visible left boundary, so the target's extent is ambiguous) and breaks visual consistency with the trash button's cleaner dock treatment.

Secondary, smaller: the bottom-most button (brush) at y≈780 sits roughly a button-radius from the 812px bottom edge with no visible breathing room below it, so the column terminates flush against the screen bottom, while the settings gear on the same baseline has clear margin around it — the two bottom controls do not share a common bottom inset.

Hierarchy, text fit, and overlap are otherwise clean: no labels are present to wrap or truncate, no button overlaps another or the stroke, spacing between the six buttons is even, and no scrim or scrolling region is present in this frame to judge.
entries.recommendation: Give the Actions Panel column a left inset so each round button's disc is fully on screen (or, if it is meant to dock like the trash button, match that treatment — a full-strength shape with only a small clearly intentional overhang and the icon centered in the visible area), and add a bottom inset to the last button so it clears the screen edge by the same margin as the settings gear.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast reads correctly across the frame. No scrim is present (canvas, top palette and corner glyphs are all at full brightness), so every element is in scope. The five top palette swatches are fully saturated fills against the near-black bar with clear separation, and the selected purple swatch carries a visible ring. The docked trash button's coral-to-pink fill and white trash glyph are the strongest contrast in the frame and read instantly. The purple drawn stroke on the dark textured canvas is clearly legible. The collapse chevron above the panel and the settings gear in the bottom-right are thin gray glyphs with no backing — faint, as intended — but both shapes are locatable in the image (the chevron's V above the undo button, the gear's toothed disc at the lower right), so neither trips the findability floor. No text is present to assess. No element in the frame falls below usable legibility for its role.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
The brush flyout renders as a white rounded column to the right of the Actions Panel, holding four tools top-to-bottom: pen (active), crayon, paintbrush, eraser. Hierarchy is clear — the active pen is the only item with a lavender-tinted rounded tile and purple border, so current selection is unambiguous at a glance. No scrim is present, and the palette, trash button, chevron, and settings glyph are all at full brightness; the chevron at the left edge (~y=411) and the settings gear at bottom-right are both locatable, so no findability floor is breached. No text appears in the flyout, so there is no text-fit risk. Nothing is clipped: the card's rounded corners sit fully inside the viewport and all four glyphs are clear of the card edges. The flyout does not overlap the Actions Panel column — it abuts it with a visible gap — and the eraser sits comfortably above the bottom edge. Content fits the card with no fade, so no scrolling region is implicated.

The one actionable observation is touch-target clarity: only the selected pen carries a tile. The crayon, paintbrush, and eraser are bare glyphs on white with no container, disc, or divider, so their tappable bounds are inferred rather than shown. Compounding this, the glyph pitch is uneven — the active tile's lower edge sits close to the crayon while the crayon→brush→eraser gaps are visibly larger — so the first inactive target reads as cramped against the selection and the column has a slightly irregular rhythm. These are child-facing drawing tools at full scope, not the deliberately quiet parent controls, so the missing affordance is a real if minor cost.
entries.recommendation: Give every tool in the flyout the same tile footprint as the active pen — an identically sized rounded container, transparent when unselected and filled/outlined when selected — and equalize the vertical gaps between all four tiles so the active pen no longer crowds the crayon below it.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in this frame is mostly sound. The tool glyphs in the flyout (pen, crayon, Magic Brush, eraser) are bright, saturated multicolor icons that separate cleanly from the near-black canvas, and the selected pen is unambiguous — its tile carries a bright purple border plus a lighter fill, readable at a glance. The top-bar color swatches are fully saturated against the dark header, and the trash button's coral fill with yellow bin glyph is the highest-contrast element on screen. No scrim is present, so the canvas and corner buttons are judged at full brightness: undo, AI, and screenshot read dim, which is the documented disabled styling; the chevron above them and the settings gear in the bottom-right are faint gray glyphs, but both shapes are locatable in the image, so they meet the findability floor.

The unselected tiles (crayon, Magic Brush, eraser) and the panel behind them sit at near-identical dark values to the canvas, and their rounded outlines are only a hair lighter than the background. The flyout therefore has no perceptible edge in night mode — the four icons appear to float directly on the canvas, and the boundary between tile and not-tile is inferable only from the selected item's purple ring. entries.recommendation: Lift the dark-theme flyout surface and unselected tile borders a few steps above the canvas value — a slightly lighter panel fill plus a visibly brighter tile outline — so the flyout edge and each tap target are discernible without relying on the selected item's purple ring.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: The honeycomb grid overruns its card. On the staggered rows (orange/red row 2, blue row 5, purple row 6, teal row 7) the rightmost hexagon is sheared flat against the card's right edge, losing its right point, while the non-offset rows end with a clear margin. The result is visibly asymmetric padding and several swatches that read as broken rather than merely offset — the clipping is at the card boundary, not the viewport. Separately, the card shows no close, done, or dismiss control anywhere on it, and no fade at any edge indicating scrollable content, so the open dialog offers no visible way out. Hierarchy, swatch spacing, touch-target size (hexes roughly 60px across, comfortably tappable), and the outlined current-color hex at bottom left read fine; the dimmed canvas, top palette, and the two thin corner glyphs are the expected scrim and quiet-control styling and are not counted here.
entries.recommendation: Inset the honeycomb by half a hex-width so the staggered rows nest inside the card's horizontal padding instead of being clipped by the right edge, and add a visible close/done control to the picker card.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: Most of the honeycomb reads well against the dark card, but the bottom two rows of low-luminance swatches lose their edges in night mode. The dark-brown hexagons at the right end of the brown row and the charcoal/slate hexagons in the final row sit at nearly the same luminance as the card's dark surface, so their hexagonal silhouettes are hard to resolve as separate, selectable targets — the darkest one is only readable because a faint stroke has been drawn around it, and the browns beside it get no such help. The neighboring dark swatches also read as near-identical to each other, so a user cannot tell which color they are about to pick without tapping. Elsewhere contrast is fine: the mid- and high-chroma swatches separate cleanly, the white and pale pinks hold their shape, and the top-edge palette circles are legible. The bottom-corner chevron and the settings glyph are both locatable in the frame, so no finding there.
entries.recommendation: Give every swatch a consistent hairline border (or a subtle outer ring/shadow) in dark mode rather than only the darkest one, so the low-luminance browns and charcoals keep a visible hexagon edge against the card surface and are distinguishable from each other.

The settings glyph in the bottom-right corner and the pen tool in the bottom-left remain locatable on the scrim. No night-mode contrast or legibility defect is visible in this frame.

entries.critique: The dialog scrim does not extend to the full viewport. The color palette row at the top of the frame (purple, blue, gold, black, and multicolor swatches) renders at full saturation and brightness on a white strip, while the canvas behind the "Farm" card is visibly darkened and blurred. The bottom corners behave the same way: the brush button at lower-left and the settings glyph at lower-right sit on undimmed white rather than on the scrim. Because those five large filled swatches are the most saturated pixels anywhere in the frame and span the full 375px width, they compete with the open card for attention instead of receding behind it. Everything else in the card is sound: the "Farm" title, back chevron, and close X are legible and adequately spaced with clear touch targets; the two-column grid has even gutters and consistent card radii; the line-art thumbnails are crisp; there is no text clipping or overlap; and the third row thinning toward the bottom edge is the scroll fade being drawn, with the two full rows above it sitting clear of the faded strip.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim across the full viewport so the top color-palette strip and the bottom-corner controls are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, instead of the scrim stopping short of the screen's top and bottom edges.

entries.review_description: Coloring-page picker. A coloring book drilled into its page grid. Captured in night mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open coloring-page card is mostly sound: the "Farm" title is near-white on the dark card and reads cleanly, and the thumbnail line art is drawn in light strokes on a card fill lighter than the page, so each animal outline stays legible despite thin strokes. The bottom row of thumbnails thins toward the edge, which is the scroll fade being painted; the dimmed palette and corner glyphs behind the card are the dialog scrim — neither is judged.

The one weak spot is the back chevron in the card header. It is a mid-gray glyph inside a disc whose fill sits only slightly above the card background, so both the disc edge and the arrow are markedly dimmer than the "Farm" label beside them and than the close X on the opposite side, which reads noticeably brighter. Unlike the deliberately recessed parent-facing glyphs, this is a filled-disc control inside the open dialog and the primary way back to the category list, so it should not be the faintest element in its own header row. It stays findable, so this is a low-severity contrast shortfall rather than a lost control.
entries.recommendation: Raise the back chevron's glyph and disc-fill luminance in dark mode so it matches the close X in the same header row (target roughly 4.5:1 for the arrow against the card fill).

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique:
Top palette row, canvas, and corner controls read cleanly at 375×812. Hierarchy is right: the color swatches and the red trash button carry the strongest weight, the canvas is unobstructed in its center, and the two parent-facing glyphs (chevron at mid-left, gear at bottom-right) are both locatable in the frame — faint by design, so no contrast finding there. The undo/AI/screenshot buttons in the Actions Panel show the expected disabled low-contrast treatment on an empty canvas. No text is present to clip or wrap; no overlap of interactive elements; no modal open.

One thing is visible and not covered by the stated design intent: the entire expanded Actions Panel column (undo, coloring-book, AI, screenshot, stroke-width, brush) sits half past the left viewport edge, not just the trash button. Each round button shows only its right half, so the icon glyphs are horizontally bisected — the undo arrow, the wave, and the pen read as partial shapes and the touch target's true extent is ambiguous, since roughly half of each control lies off-screen and unreachable. The docking exception given is specific to the trash button; this column is a different control group and its truncated icons weaken tap-target clarity.

Also worth noting descriptively: no active-page chip is visible anywhere in the frame despite the capture being described as a selected page with one.
entries.recommendation: Shift the expanded left-edge Actions Panel column inward so each round button and its icon are fully on-screen (or center the glyph within the visible half), reserving the half-off-edge docking treatment for the trash button it was designed for.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility read well. The white line art sits at high contrast against the dark charcoal canvas — every outline (cat, hay bale, clouds, butterfly, flowers, grass) is crisply separable, including the dense spiral shading on the bale. The top palette row shows saturated swatches (purple, blue, yellow, white, multicolor) on a near-black bar with a clear light selection ring on the active purple swatch, so the current color is unambiguous. The red-gradient trash button is the strongest element on screen and its white trash glyph stays legible on it. In the Actions Panel, the undo, AI, and screenshot-adjacent buttons show reduced contrast consistent with the documented disabled state on an empty canvas; the enabled screenshot/photo and brush/stroke-width buttons keep bright, saturated glyphs. The collapse chevron at the top of the panel and the settings gear in the opposite corner are faint low-contrast gray glyphs, which is their documented resting appearance — both shapes are still locatable in this frame, so the findability floor is met. No text is present that fails to resolve, and no element disappears into its background.

entries.critique:
Frame shows an empty light canvas with the color palette strip across the top, the docked round trash button at the right edge, the collapse chevron at bottom-left, the settings gear at bottom-right, and the clear-gesture coachmark drawn over the canvas (a large pink arc, a ghosted trash disc, and a pointing-hand glyph about a third down the screen).

Judging the coachmark only on what is drawn: the ghost trash disc, the hand glyph, and the pink drag arc are each rendered at legible size, hold clear separation from one another, and sit against empty canvas with no text to fit or clip. The arc running past the right edge reads as the path continuing toward the docked button, not as a truncated element.

Everything else in normal scope reads clean. The five palette swatches are evenly spaced with a clear selected-state ring on the first, none crowded or cut. The docked trash button's edge overhang is the settled design. The chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both locatable — their shapes are plainly identifiable — and their quiet weight is the intended parent-facing styling. No overlapping controls, no text overflow, no scrolling region in frame, and the coachmark does not obscure any control it needs to point at.

No actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_description: The accept ring and paper wash while held past threshold.
entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique:
The frame shows the clear gesture held past threshold: the docked red trash button is lit with a red glow, and a red "accept" ring is drawn around it. Hierarchy reads correctly — the red button plus ring is the dominant element, the color palette across the top is unchanged and legible, and the two parent-facing glyphs (chevron bottom-left, settings gear bottom-right) are both locatable as thin gray shapes, which is their intended resting appearance. Text fit and modal scrolling are not exercised here; no overlap, no clipping of palette swatches, no crowding. The soft warm wash across the canvas and the faint pale stroke remnant are the intended "clearing is underway" effect.

One thing worth noting on visible evidence: the accept ring is anchored on a button that sits at the screen edge, so the great majority of the ring's circumference falls outside the viewport. What remains on screen is a single arc sweeping up and off the top-right, which reads more like a stray drawn stroke on the canvas than a progress/confirmation ring around the button — the ring's shape as a ring is not perceivable. Because this is the only feedback distinguishing "held past threshold" from a plain press, the confirmation signal is weaker than the intent implies. The glow around the button does carry some of that signal, so this is a degradation rather than a failure.
entries.recommendation: Scale or reposition the accept ring so a closed (or near-closed) ring is visible within the viewport around the docked trash button — e.g. draw it at a radius that fits on-screen, or offset its center inward — so the past-threshold state reads as a ring rather than an arc that leaves the frame.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility hold up in this frame. The clear button is a saturated red disc with a bright yellow trash glyph on it — the highest-contrast pairing on the screen, unmistakable against the near-black canvas, and its glow reads clearly as an active/held state. The accept ring is a red stroke that stays visible along its whole visible arc against the dark ground. The color swatches along the top edge are fully saturated and separable from each other and from the background, and the selected swatch's ring is legible. The faint icon wash across the lower canvas is the stated intended effect for a clear-in-progress, so its low contrast is not judged. Both parent-facing glyphs meet the findability floor: the chevron in the bottom-left and the gear in the bottom-right are each locatable as distinct shapes, with the gear's spokes and center resolvable; their quietness is the specified resting styling. No text is present in the frame to evaluate. Nothing visible reads as an unintended contrast or legibility failure.

entries.review_description: Install banner. The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes. Captured in light mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique: The install banner's text column is over-constrained. Title "Add Splotch to your home screen" wraps to three lines and the subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" to two, all inside roughly the left 40% of the card, while the "How?" pill and round close button take the right side. The title reads as a paragraph instead of a headline, flattening the hierarchy against the smaller subtitle, and the card has unused horizontal room that would resolve it. Vertical padding is also uneven — the subtitle's last line sits closer to the card's bottom edge than the title does to the top. No text is clipped or truncated. Nothing else in the frame is actionable: the top palette row is evenly spaced with a clear purple selection ring, the docked trash button is intact at the right edge, the three canvas strokes render cleanly, and the banner neither overlaps nor obscures any other control. The "How?" pill and the ✕ are both unambiguous, well-separated, adequately sized targets. No scrolling region is in view.
entries.recommendation: Widen the banner's text column — tighten the gap between the copy and the "How?" pill and the pill/close-button cluster — so the title fits in one or two lines rather than three, and equalize top and bottom padding around the text block.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The install banner sits on the dark canvas as a rounded card with a thin purple border, and its primary elements hold up in night mode: "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white bold text on the near-black card and reads cleanly at a glance, the Splotch mark keeps its color identity, and the purple "How?" pill is clearly the primary action. The close "×" is a light gray glyph on a slightly lighter dark disc — subdued, but its shape is plainly locatable and it reads as a dismiss control.

The one weak spot is the supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app." It is rendered in a mid-gray at a noticeably smaller size than the title, against the card's near-black fill, and it is the dimmest text in the frame — visibly fainter than both the title above it and the "×" beside it. At this size it is the kind of text that needs more separation from the background, not less, and here it gets less; it reads as filler rather than as the sentence that actually explains what tapping "How?" will do. Nothing about it is a scrim, a fade, or a disabled state — the banner is at full brightness and this is the copy's own styling.

The purple "How?" pill with white label is acceptable but not generous: the purple is light enough to be friendly on the dark card, which correspondingly narrows the margin against the white text. It is legible here and I would not flag it on its own, but it leaves little headroom if the label size ever shrinks.

The canvas strokes, the top color palette, and the trash button all read normally in night mode and raise no contrast concern.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the banner's secondary line ("Opens full-screen, just like a real app") to a brighter gray so this small-size explanatory text clears 4.5:1 against the card's near-black fill, keeping it visibly below the title but well above its current near-vanishing weight.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique: The expanded install-banner card is clipped at the bottom of the viewport. Its rounded border is visible along the top, left and right, but never closes along the bottom — the outline runs straight off the frame edge and the final instruction line ("see it, tap ⌄ \"View More\" first.") sits roughly 40px from the bottom of the 812px screen with no bottom padding or corner radius rendered, and no scrolling to recover it. On iPhone 13 mini this also puts the last line into the home-indicator region. Everything above reads well: palette row, canvas strokes, app icon, title, subtitle, the purple "How?" button and the outlined ✕ close button all have clear separation and legible touch targets, and the inline Share/⊞/chevron glyphs in the instruction sentence are identifiable. A lesser issue: the title wraps to three lines in a narrow column beside "How?" while empty space remains beneath the button, making the header column feel over-tight.
entries.recommendation: Anchor the expanded install card above the bottom safe area — offset it by env(safe-area-inset-bottom) plus the same ~16px inset used on its left and right edges — so its rounded bottom border and internal padding render fully below the "View More" line at 375 × 812.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this install-banner overlay is largely sound. The card sits on a dark charcoal fill with a purple outline that separates it clearly from the darker canvas behind it. The headline "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white bold text and reads crisply. The instruction paragraph below the divider ("Tap Share at the bottom of the screen, then choose 'Add to Home Screen'...") is light gray with the key phrases bolded to near-white; both the body weight and the bolded phrases are comfortably legible, and the inline Share and plus glyphs and the chevron are all visible as distinct shapes. The "How?" pill is a saturated purple with white label — the white-on-purple pairing is legible at this size and weight, though it is the tightest of the button pairings here. The circular close button is a mid-gray "x" on a slightly lighter dark disc; it is findable and its shape is unambiguous.

The one element that is measurably weaker than everything around it is the two-line subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app". It is rendered at the smallest type size in the card, in a muted gray that sits noticeably closer to the card background than any other text in the frame, and it is set immediately beneath much brighter bold headline text, which further suppresses it. Unlike the corner chevron and settings glyphs, this is not a control that is meant to recede — it is explanatory copy inside the primary attention-holding card, so its dimness costs comprehension rather than serving a deliberate quiet-control styling. At a glance the phrase reads as a gray smudge under the headline rather than as a sentence.

Nothing else in the frame reads as a night-mode contrast fault: the top color palette and the docked trash button are at full saturation, the purple strokes on the canvas hold clearly against the textured dark ground, and the card's border is visible without being harsh.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the banner's subtitle ("Opens full-screen, just like a real app") in dark mode to at least the same gray value used for the instruction paragraph below the divider, so the supporting copy clears a normal body-text contrast ratio instead of sitting near the card fill.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique: The parent-gate card itself is sound: clear hierarchy from logo → "Grown-Ups Only" → subtitle → equation → keypad → footer link, consistent gutters, no clipped or truncated text, no overlap, and no scrolling needed at 375×812. Keypad keys and the top-right close button are comfortably sized, well-separated touch targets, and the two dashed answer slots clearly signal a two-digit response. The empty third cell in the bottom keypad row is a normal keypad convention, not a defect. The actionable issue is the scrim: the canvas and corner controls behind the dialog are visibly darkened, but the color-palette swatch row along the top edge is still at full brightness on a white ground, with a hard horizontal scrim edge visible just beneath it. Those saturated swatches are the brightest, most chromatic thing in the frame, pull attention away from the gate card, and their undimmed state implies they are still interactive while the rest of the page is blocked.
entries.recommendation: Extend the modal scrim over the full page, including the top color-palette strip, so the swatch row is darkened and blurred along with the canvas and corner buttons, leaving the gate card as the only element at full brightness.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast inside the parent gate card is mostly solid: "Grown-Ups Only" is near-white on the dark card, the subtitle "Solve the problem to continue" is clearly readable, the 0–9 keypad digits are white on distinctly lighter gray keys, and the two operand chips (purple 6, blue 5) carry white numerals with strong separation. The close ✕ in its circular outline at top right is locatable and legible.

Two elements sit noticeably weaker than everything else on the card. The multiplication "×" and the "=" between the operands and the answer slots are rendered small in a mid-gray that reads much dimmer than the digits they join — they are the only thing telling the parent what operation to perform, so they carry real meaning rather than being decoration. Similarly, the footer line "Manage these checks in" and the "Settings › Parent Center" row beneath it (with its small gear and people glyphs) are drawn in a dim gray at small type; the row is discernible but visibly the faintest text on the card, and the tiny gear/person icons in particular lose shape.

The empty answer slots are dashed gray rings — faint, but as unfilled affordances that is adequate and they are clearly located. Background canvas, palette, corner chevron/settings glyph and the docked trash button all sit behind the gate's scrim and are excluded per the stated conventions; the settings glyph in the lower-right is still locatable in the frame.

No blocking failure — the gate can be read and solved — but the operator symbols and the footer link row are below the legibility of the rest of the card in this theme.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground value of the "×" and "=" operators toward the keypad-digit brightness (they are semantic, not decorative), and lift the footer block — "Manage these checks in" plus the "Settings › Parent Center" row and its small gear/person icons — to a brighter gray so the smallest text on the card is not also the dimmest.
