entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The style grid reads well overall: two even columns, consistent square thumbnails with matching illustration content so styles are genuinely comparable, labels centered under each tile with adequate spacing, and a clear "Pick a style" header paired with a well-sized circular close button in the top-right that has obvious touch-target clarity. The scrim behind the card is doing its job — the palette row along the top edge and the corner controls are darkened and blurred, and the settings glyph in the bottom-right is still locatable. Contrast and legibility of the card's own text and controls are fine.

The actionable issue is the bottom edge of the scrolling grid. The fourth row of thumbnails is cut flat at the card's bottom boundary at full saturation and full sharpness, with no gradient fade over the last row and no other continuation cue, and both of that row's labels are cut away entirely. Against the soft-fade convention used elsewhere in this app, this edge reads as a hard crop rather than as content thinning out, so it looks like the card was clipped rather than like there is more to scroll to. It also sits very close to the screen bottom (roughly 50px of margin versus the larger gap above the card), tightening the cut further and leaving the last row half-presented with no name attached to either style.
entries.recommendation: Apply the app's standard soft gradient fade over the bottom row of the style grid so the cut row visibly thins toward the card edge, and add a little bottom inset to the card so the partially revealed row reads as scrollable content rather than a hard crop.

entries.review_description: AI style picker. Style selection over the child’s drawing preview. Captured in night mode on iPhone 13 mini in portrait at 375 × 812. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the open "Pick a style" card is largely sound: the title and the style labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker) render as light gray/white on the dark card and read cleanly, and the style thumbnails are bright, saturated, and easily told apart from one another against the card ground. The bottom row of thumbnails thins toward the card edge, which is the scroll fade being drawn, and the darkened, blurred canvas and top palette behind the card are the dialog scrim — neither is judged. The one weak element is the card's own close control in the top-right: the × glyph and its thin ring are both mid-gray on a dark slate ground, noticeably dimmer than the card title sitting on the same background, and the ring is thin enough that its stroke carries little weight. It is the dialog's primary dismiss affordance and is not one of the two intentionally recessed parent-facing glyphs, so it should be reading at full strength rather than at roughly the level of quiet background chrome.
entries.recommendation: Raise the close button's contrast in dark mode — lighten the × glyph and its ring toward the same near-white used by the "Pick a style" title (or give the circle a lighter filled disc behind the glyph) so the dismiss control is as legible as the card's heading.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The AI-generating dialog reads clearly overall: the scrim darkens the canvas and top palette behind it, the progress dial is the dominant element, and "Making your picture…" / "This takes about 30 seconds" sit in correct type hierarchy above a single pill action. The close button is fully visible and unambiguous, and both bottom-corner parent glyphs (chevron left, gear right) are locatable on the scrim. Text fits on one line each with no truncation or overlap.

Two spacing issues are visible. First, the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill runs to the very bottom of the white card — its lower edge is flush with the card boundary, with no bottom padding to match the generous padding elsewhere in the card, so the primary action looks pinned to the edge rather than seated in the card. Second, the tall blurred preview panel is mostly empty: roughly 250px of blank white sits above the dial and another ~250px below it, so the dial floats in a large void while the label and button are crowded into a thin strip beneath. The proportion between the empty preview area and the tight text/button block is the main visual imbalance on the screen.
entries.recommendation: Add bottom padding inside the card equal to its side padding so the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill is inset from the card's lower edge rather than flush with it, and reduce the preview panel's height (or tighten the dial's vertical centering) so the blank space above and below the dial no longer dwarfs the label-and-button block.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the AI-generating card reads well. "Making your picture…" is near-white on the dark card and fully legible; the secondary line "This takes about 30 seconds" is a muted gray but still clearly readable at this size. The "Keep drawing while you wait" pill uses white label text on a saturated purple fill that separates plainly from the card surface. The close × is white inside an outlined circle at the card's top-right and stands off the dark backdrop. The progress dial is high-chroma pink/purple against the dark preview panel with a white center dot, so its fill angle is easy to read. Both parent-facing glyphs on the scrim — the chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right — are locatable, meeting the findability floor; their faintness is the intended resting styling. Background canvas, top palette and corner buttons are dimmed by the dialog scrim, so their softness is not a contrast finding. No element on the card or over the scrim falls below legibility here.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique: The AI-result dialog reads cleanly at 375×812. Hierarchy is unambiguous: the generated image dominates the card, the filled purple "Download" pill is the single obvious primary action, and the attribution/report chip sits subordinate below the card. The card has even margins on both sides, generous internal padding around the image, and comfortable space between image, button, and card edge; nothing is cramped. Text fit is clean — "Download" and "AI-generated picture · Report" both sit on one line with room to spare, no truncation, wrapping, or baseline collision. No clipping of card content: the image is fully within its rounded frame, and the close button's deliberate overhang at the top-right corner is a standard offset placement that still keeps the full X glyph and its disc visible against the white card and image. Overlap is controlled — the close disc has an opaque white fill and ring so the glyph never competes with the artwork beneath it, and the chip is drawn on top of the scrim with high-contrast white text on a dark pill. Touch targets are clear: the Download pill is a large full-width-ish target, and the close button is a distinct circular disc of adequate diameter, well clear of the image's tappable area. The card fits entirely within the viewport with no scrolling needed and no fade edge, so there is no cut-off content to signal. The page behind is scrimmed as intended — the palette row along the top, the docked round trash button at the right edge, and the two corner glyphs (chevron at bottom-left, settings gear at bottom-right, both locatable) are dimmed by that scrim, which is the expected treatment. Visual consistency holds: rounded-rectangle language across card, image, pill, and chip; a single accent purple used only for the primary action; consistent corner radii and shadow weight.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
Dark-mode contrast on this screen is mostly fine: the close button's white ✕ on its dark disc reads clearly, and the "Download" pill is a saturated purple with white text and icon that stands out strongly against the card. The card surface itself is a lighter slate than the scrimmed page behind it, so the card separates cleanly.

The one legibility problem is the caption row drawn on the scrim below the card: "AI-generated picture · Report". It is small, thin gray type sitting directly on the near-black darkened page, and it is the weakest text in the frame by a clear margin — noticeably fainter than any type inside the card. This is not background content dimmed by the scrim; it is drawn on top of the scrim and is part of the overlay, so it owes full contrast. The "Report" affordance is the worse half: its label is the same low-contrast gray as the surrounding caption, and its small flag icon is a dull muted red on black, so nothing marks it as a tappable control rather than more caption text. A safety/reporting action for AI output is exactly the control that should not be the hardest thing on the screen to read in night mode.

The two parent-facing corner glyphs are both locatable — the chevron at bottom left and the gear at bottom right are visible as shapes — so their faintness is the intended resting styling, not a finding. The docked trash button at the top right and the palette swatches along the top edge sit behind the scrim and are judged accordingly.
entries.recommendation: Lift the overlay caption row out of scrim-level gray: raise "AI-generated picture" to a mid-light gray clearing 4.5:1 against the darkened backdrop, and give "Report" distinct interactive treatment — brighter label text plus a flag icon in a lighter, less muted red — so it reads as an actionable control rather than trailing caption text.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique: The confirmation card itself is well formed: clear title, body text that fits without truncation, two labeled thumbnails, and a Cancel / Send report button pair with ample touch targets and no overlap or text clipping. Two visible issues stand out. (1) The thumbnail labeled "The drawing behind it" is an empty white tile with only a short purple bar clipped at its top edge; beside the fully rendered AI picture on the left it conveys nothing about what is being sent, and the purple bar reads as a cut-off element. (2) The circular close × belonging to the card behind renders at full strength above the confirmation card, so two dismiss affordances (× and Cancel) are simultaneously visible with no clear separation of layers, leaving it ambiguous which surface the × closes.
entries.recommendation: Render the actual drawing (or an explicit "no drawing" placeholder) in the second thumbnail with its top edge clipped cleanly, and hide or scrim the underlying card's × while this confirmation dialog is open so Cancel is the only visible dismiss control.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open card is mostly sound: "Report this picture" is near-white on a dark purple-gray surface and reads crisply, the body paragraph is a light gray that stays comfortably legible at this size, and both buttons carry white labels — "Send report" on a saturated purple fill and "Cancel" on a muted purple fill — that separate clearly from their backgrounds and from each other. The close × sits on a dark circular disc at the top right and its glyph is visibly lighter than the disc, findable without hunting.

The weak spot is the pair of thumbnail captions, "The AI picture" and "The drawing behind it". They are set several steps smaller than the body copy and in a dimmer gray, so they are the faintest text on the card by a clear margin; at 375px wide on a small phone in night mode they read as washed into the panel rather than as labels, and "The drawing behind it" is the longer of the two and the one a parent most needs to parse to understand what is being sent. entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal card itself is well formed: the palette emoji, the headline "Let's try drawing something else!", the two-line body, the "For grown-ups" label and the "Report this refusal" pill sit in a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy with even spacing and generous card padding. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping; both lines of body copy fit comfortably within the card width. The circular close button sits clear of the card's top-right corner at a comfortable tap size, and the report pill is full-width-ish with adequate height. Nothing in the card requires scrolling.

The one visible problem is in the scrim. The page behind the dialog is darkened and blurred as expected — canvas, trash button, stroke-width bar, and the bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are all dimmed — but the color palette strip along the top edge is not. The five swatches and their surrounding background render at full brightness, and the scrim begins at a hard, straight horizontal seam immediately below that strip. This reads as an unintended gap in the overlay rather than a deliberate treatment: it leaves the brightest, highest-saturation elements on the screen (the purple, blue, gold, black and rainbow discs) competing with the refusal card for attention, which works against the stated purpose of the scrim, and the crisp seam line across the full width is itself a visible artifact.

The parent-facing chevron (bottom left) and settings gear (bottom right) are both locatable as shapes despite the scrim, so their quiet styling is arriving as intended and is not a finding here.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to cover the full viewport including the top color-palette strip, so the swatches are darkened and blurred along with the rest of the page and the hard horizontal seam below the palette disappears.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open refusal card is mostly sound: the heading "Let's try drawing something else!" and the two-line body copy both read as near-white/light-gray on the dark card surface with comfortable separation, and the circular ✕ close button in the top-right is a solid white ring and glyph that stands clearly off the card.

The actionable problem is the primary action, "Report this refusal." Its label is rendered in a light-violet sitting on a muted violet-gray fill of very similar lightness — the two differ mainly in saturation rather than luminance, so the label reads hazy against its own pill. It is the weakest text in the frame despite being the only tappable action in the card, and on a small dark screen a viewer has to work to resolve the words.

Secondary and milder: the "For grown-ups" caption above the button is small, thin, and mid-gray on the dark card, noticeably dimmer than the body copy. As a quiet parent-facing label that is defensible, but it sits close to the floor for text of that size.

The thin gray chevron at bottom-left and the settings gear at bottom-right are both locatable in the frame, so they meet the findability floor and are not reported.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance contrast of the "Report this refusal" button by lightening the label toward near-white (or darkening/desaturating the violet fill) so the pair differs in lightness rather than only in hue, targeting at least 4.5:1 for the button text against its fill in night mode.

entries.critique: The AI error dialog is scrimmed over the page, but the scrim stops short of the top color-palette strip: the swatch row keeps a white background, fully saturated colors and a crisp selection ring, and the scrim's top edge shows as a hard horizontal line directly beneath it. entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique: The section heading "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" overlaps the bottom border of the access-codes card. The card's outline passes directly through/behind the heading text with zero clearance, and unlike the comparable "ACCESS CODES · 2" heading — which has ample space above it and a clean trailing hairline rule — this heading has no breathing room and its trailing rule is absent because the card edge occupies that band. Visually the two sections collide, and the "page-inventory-harness" row appears to belong to the grants section rather than to the codes card. The collision is aggravated by the second code row growing taller when "page-inventory-harness" wraps to two lines, pushing the card down into the margin the heading required. Secondary, lower-severity: the bare chevron glyphs in each code row have no visible bounds or hit-area affordance, leaving their touch target ambiguous beside the clearly outlined "Copy" buttons in the same rows — these are primary admin list controls, not the deliberately recessed parent-facing corner glyphs. The two metric tiles at the bottom are truncated by the viewport, which is simply the page continuing below the fold and not a defect. Everything else reads well: the persistence warning card and the free-grant memory notice have comfortable padding and legible amber-on-cream text, the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code token fits its line, the Add-a-code field and Add button are well proportioned, and header hierarchy from "Admin" down through the caption is clear.
entries.recommendation: Add vertical margin above the "FREE GENERATION GRANTS" section heading so it clears the access-codes card's bottom border — match the spacing that precedes "ACCESS CODES · 2" — and apply the same trailing hairline rule to it for consistency between the two section headings.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin screen is largely sound: the page title, the "Back to drawing" link, the code names (daycare-club, page-inventory-harness), the "Copy" button labels, the "Sign out" and "Add" buttons, and the large metric numerals (0/500, 0) all read cleanly against the near-black background. The two cream notice cards invert to dark brown text on pale yellow and are the most legible text in the frame; the Netlify Blobs warning, including the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip, is easy to read.

The weak points are the muted gray secondary text. The subtitle "Manage AI access codes" and, more noticeably, the small letter-spaced section labels "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" sit at a low-saturation gray close in value to the dark surface; at this size with wide tracking they are the first thing to fade at a glance, and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" is the hardest string on the screen to read. The input placeholder "Add a code…" is similarly faint against the field's dark fill, and the stat-card captions "Provider starts today" / "Sampled successes" are dimmer than their numerals by a wide margin. None are illegible, but they carry the structural labeling of the page.

The disclosure chevrons beside each code row are thin gray glyphs but their shapes are locatable, and the card borders and row divider, while subtle, remain visible as separations.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the muted gray used in dark mode for the small-caps section labels ("ACCESS CODES · 2", "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0"), the stat-card captions, and the input placeholder so they clear roughly 4.5:1 against the page surface — small letter-spaced type needs more headroom than body text, not less.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin screen is mostly sound: the header, the cream warning cards with near-black body text, the purple "Add" and "Sign out" buttons, and the bold monospace code names (daycare-club, page-inventory-harness) all read cleanly against the dark ground, and the expanded row's "Copy link" / "Remove" actions are legible at a glance.

The weak points are the muted gray text tier. The section labels "ACCESS CODES · 2" and especially "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" are small, letterspaced, all-caps gray on near-black and sit at visibly low contrast — the second one, over the slightly lighter area, is the faintest text in the frame and takes effort to read. The subtitle "Manage AI access codes" is in the same gray family and is the dimmest of the top-of-page text. The "Add a code…" placeholder is likewise quite dim inside its field; the field's own border is faint enough that the input reads as a low-emphasis region overall, though the border is still traceable.

The "Remove" label is rendered in a muted red on a dark gray button face; against the neighboring "Copy link" purple it is the lower-contrast of the two, and a destructive action is the one that least benefits from being the dimmer label. It remains readable here, so this is secondary to the gray labels.

Nothing in the frame is illegible, and the outlined "Copy" buttons and the collapse/expand chevrons on the rows are clearly visible.
entries.recommendation: Lift the muted gray tier used for the small-caps section headers ("ACCESS CODES · 2", "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0"), the "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, and the "Add a code…" placeholder to a lighter gray that clears 4.5:1 against the dark background — these are small, letterspaced, or all-caps, so they need more contrast than body text, not less.

entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: Resting canvas reads cleanly. The top palette row sits in its own bar with even spacing and a clear selected state (purple ring on the first swatch); the multicolor picker at the right end is distinct from the five solid swatches and none of the circles are clipped by the bar or crowded at either end. The drawing surface below is a full-bleed textured off-white with no stray content, no overlap, and no text to fit or truncate. The docked round trash button at the top right and the two parent-facing glyphs — the collapse chevron at bottom left and the settings gear at bottom right — are all locatable; both thin gray glyphs are clearly findable as shapes despite their intentionally low contrast, and they sit far from the palette and from each other, so nothing competes for the child's attention. Hierarchy is correct for a blank canvas: the color tools are the loudest element, the destructive clear action is set apart at the edge, and the parent controls recede. Touch targets are unambiguous — swatches are large discs with generous gaps, the trash is a big disc, and the corner glyphs each have clear empty space around them. No modal or scrolling region is open in this frame, and there is no visible clipping, overflow, or inconsistency in shape language, corner radii, or spacing.

The right end of the swatch row thins out under the scroll fade, which is the app's own overflow cue rather than a legibility fault. No text is present to assess. Nothing here is actionable on contrast or legibility grounds.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: The signed-out admin surface renders cleanly at 440 × 956. Hierarchy is unambiguous: "Admin" as the dominant title, a one-line subtitle, then a "SIGN IN" section label with a rule that terminates cleanly at the right gutter. Left and right margins match, and the input + button row sits flush to the same measure as the divider above it. Text fits everywhere — no truncation, wrapping, clipping, or overlap; the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark and its dot cluster fit within the top-right gutter with clearance from the "Back to drawing" link on the opposite side. The access-key field and the purple "Sign in" button are the same height, vertically aligned, with visible gap between them, and both read as comfortably tappable; the button's white label on purple has strong contrast, and the field's placeholder is clearly weaker than the entered-value state would be, as expected for a placeholder. The "Back to drawing" link is colored and arrow-prefixed, so its affordance is legible. The large empty area below the form is simply an unpopulated single-field sign-in page at tall-phone height, not a layout fault — nothing is stranded, misaligned, or cut off by the viewport. No scrolling region, overlay, scrim, or corner-control styling is present in this frame to assess.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in surface is generally sound: "Admin" and the "Sign in" button label are near-white on the dark ground and read crisply; "Manage AI access codes" is a light gray that stays comfortably legible; the placeholder "Admin access key" is dimmer but still readable and correctly reads as placeholder rather than value; the input's border is faint but the field's slightly lighter fill makes its bounds locatable. The purple "← Back to drawing" link and the purple "Sign in" button fill both hold up against the near-black background, and the white button label on purple is clean. The one weak spot is the "SIGN IN" section eyebrow above the field: it is small, letter-spaced, all-caps, and rendered in a muted gray only a little above the background — noticeably fainter than every other piece of text in the frame, and the thin rule beside it is fainter still. Unlike the deliberately recessed parent-facing glyphs described as settled, this is a section label on a signed-out form, so it should carry ordinary body-label contrast. It remains findable, hence low rather than higher.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "SIGN IN" eyebrow (and its adjoining rule) to a lighter gray meeting at least 4.5:1 against the dark page background, since it is small, uppercase, and letter-spaced.

Hierarchy is unambiguous: back link and brand mark on one top row, "Changelog" as the dominant page title, a two-line subtitle, a bordered CONTENTS row with a "7 releases ›" affordance, a rule, then "Version 1.5.0" paired right-aligned with its date, followed by emoji-labeled "New / Improved / Fixed" subheads over bulleted notes. The last visible bullet under "Fixed" thins toward the bottom edge, which is the app's scroll-fade cue being drawn over the final line rather than a legibility fault; all content clear of that strip is fully crisp. No overlay or scrim is present. Nothing actionable is visible.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique: Opening view of the styleguide reads cleanly at 440×956. Hierarchy is clear: theme toggle + "Design system" + brand mark in a compact header, a full-width "CONTENTS — 16 sections ›" row acting as a nav affordance, then the H1, deck, sources line, a tinted "Not sure? Start here" callout, and the "PART 1 / Foundations" section opener. Vertical rhythm is consistent, gutters are even left and right, and the page bottom cuts mid-section as expected for a scrolling document. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems: long inline code tokens (`--font-weight-bold`, `lib/design/tokens.ts`) wrap within the measure instead of overflowing, and nothing collides with the callout's rounded edges. The CONTENTS row is a comfortably tall full-width target with a chevron, and the sun/moon segmented toggle has two clearly separated halves. One weak point: the "Sources:" metadata line sets its non-code prose ("→", "· the icon set · the shipped components", the parenthetical tail) in a very light gray at the page's smallest size, noticeably fainter than everything around it, and it wraps to a third line that trails off as a barely-visible fragment. Unlike the surrounding body and callout text this line sits below the legibility of its neighbours without any evident intent to recede.
entries.recommendation: Darken the small "Sources:" metadata line to the same muted-text token used elsewhere for secondary prose (or bump it one step from the faintest gray) so its non-code words, including the wrapped "the icon set · the shipped components" tail, match the legibility of the rest of the page.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Most of this opening view holds up in night mode. The page title, the intro paragraph, the "Back to drawing" link in violet, the PART 1 / Foundations heading, and the section body copy are all bright warm-white or saturated violet on the near-black ground and read cleanly. The theme toggle pill, the CONTENTS bar with its "16 sections ›" affordance, and the palette dots in the header are all clearly resolved. The "Not sure? Start here" card is the one place with a raised surface, and its heading and the highlighted token names (--surface, --radius-lg, --font-size-sm, brand, --ease-pop) sit at a comfortable step above the muted purple panel; its running prose is dimmer than the page body but still tracks line to line without effort.

The one actionable weakness is the "Sources:" metadata line directly under the intro. It is the smallest type on the screen and it is set in a desaturated mid-gray that lands close to the page background, so the non-code words — "Sources:", "·", "the icon set", and especially the trailing wrap "the shipped components" — sit well below everything around them. The monospace file paths inside it (lib/design/tokens.ts, tokens.css, npm run gen:tokens, lib/palette.ts) are legible because they are tinted violet and carry the code styling, which makes the contrast gap inside a single line obvious: the connective prose reads noticeably fainter than the tokens it is joining. At this size the gray is doing double duty as both "small" and "quiet," and the two compound. This is a provenance line on a living styleguide — the exact place a reader goes to confirm where a value came from — so it should not be the least readable text in the frame.

Nothing else here rises to a finding. The header wordmark "SPLOTCH" is gray and small but set in wide tracking on an empty field and stays clearly readable, and the CONTENTS label's letterspaced gray is a deliberate eyebrow treatment that remains findable and scannable.
entries.recommendation: Lift the non-code text in the "Sources:" line to the same muted-foreground token used for the intro paragraph (or one step brighter than its current gray), so the connective prose and the trailing "the shipped components" wrap reach at least the contrast of the violet code spans they sit between.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: The screen reads cleanly at 440×956. Hierarchy is clear: back link and brand mark at top, a large "Send us feedback" heading, an explanatory paragraph, then the segmented "Something's broken / I have an idea" control, the "What went wrong?" label, textarea, checkbox, privacy note, primary button, and a tinted "What happens next" card. All text wraps within the viewport with consistent left/right margins; no clipping, truncation, or overlap anywhere. The textarea placeholder sits fully inside its box with the resize grip visible at the corner and no text spilling. The segmented control shows an unambiguous selected state (white raised pill with border) against the gray track, and its inactive label stays legible. The full-width "Send report" button, the tab halves, the checkbox row, and the back link are all comfortably tall enough to read as tappable, and the "privacy policy" link is underlined and color-differentiated. Vertical rhythm is even, with sensible grouping between label and field, and the ordered list in the footer card is aligned and unclipped. Nothing scrolls or overlays in this frame, so no fade or scrim behavior is under test. The generous whitespace below the last card is just the end of a short page.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this screen is broadly sound: the H1, body copy, field label, button label, and the "What happens next" card all sit clearly above their backgrounds, and the purple "Send report" button carries white text at strong contrast.

One element is measurably weaker than everything around it: the unselected segment "I have an idea" in the Something's broken / I have an idea toggle. It is mid-gray text sitting on the lighter gray fill of the inactive half, so foreground and background are close in luminance — it reads noticeably fainter than the selected segment's near-white label on its dark fill, and is the hardest text in the frame to resolve. Because the inactive half is the *lighter* of the two, the pairing works against itself: the surface brightened while the label did not. This is a real toggle option the user must be able to read to know the form has two modes, so its dimness is not an intentional de-emphasis of a parent-only control — it is a selectable choice presented at borderline legibility.

Secondary and not separately actionable: the textarea placeholder and the "Your report goes to our private support tracker…" caption are both deliberately subdued gray, but both stay clearly resolvable against the dark surfaces and read as normal secondary-text styling rather than a contrast fault. The "privacy policy" link is underlined and lighter than the surrounding card text, so it is distinguishable without relying on hue alone.
entries.recommendation: Raise the label color of the unselected segmented-control option ("I have an idea") to a light neutral close to the selected segment's text — keeping the fill difference as the selection cue — so the inactive choice stays legible against its lighter gray track in dark mode.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
The opening view is clean and well-formed: the "← Back to drawing" link and the Splotch dot logo sit clear of each other at the top, the "Privacy policy" H1 and intro paragraph wrap without clipping or overlap, and the six-item summary card has even row spacing, consistent color-chip alignment, and clear bold-lead/regular-detail typography. The "CONTENTS / 8 sections ›" row is legibly grouped and reads as a tappable disclosure. Nothing is cut off, overlapping, or crowded at 440 × 956, and the section rules ("THE SHORT VERSION", "THE DETAILS") give a consistent divider treatment.

The one visible hierarchy slip: "Last updated August 20, 2026" is placed *below* the "THE SHORT VERSION" section rule, so it visually belongs to that section rather than to the document as a whole. Metadata about the policy is being parented to a content section it doesn't describe, which momentarily reads as though the short version was last updated on that date. It is small, low-contrast, and does not break the layout — hence low severity.

Secondary, minor: the "← Back to drawing" link is a text-only target near the top-left with no surrounding button affordance; its tap area is not visually delimited, though the label is large enough to be legible and plausibly tappable.
entries.recommendation: Move the "Last updated August 20, 2026" line above the "THE SHORT VERSION" divider — directly beneath the intro paragraph — so it reads as document-level metadata rather than as a property of that section.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this page is largely sound: the "Privacy policy" heading, the intro paragraph, the bold lead-ins ("No ads.", "No tracking.", …) and the trailing "What stays on your device" heading all sit as near-white or light-gray on the near-black ground and read cleanly. The card's own panel is distinguishable from the page by a visible violet-tinted border and slightly lifted fill, and the colored pills give each row a legible anchor. The "8 sections ›" link renders in a light violet that stays clearly readable against the contents strip.

The weak spots are all small, low-weight secondary type. The section eyebrows "THE SHORT VERSION" and "THE DETAILS" are small uppercase gray with wide letter-spacing, and "THE DETAILS" in particular reads visibly dimmer than the eyebrow above it — at that size and stroke weight it is the faintest text in the frame and looks below the 4.5:1 that small text needs. "Last updated August 20, 2026" and the "CONTENTS" label sit in the same dim gray band, only slightly brighter. None of these are decorative — they are the page's structural signposts and the document's currency date — so they are carrying real information at the contrast level normally reserved for de-emphasized chrome. The secondary (non-bold) halves of the card rows, e.g. "We don't follow you around the internet." and "Every request the app makes is described on this page.", are a step brighter and read acceptably, but they set the ceiling that the eyebrows fall well short of.

No other night-mode contrast problem is visible: nothing in the frame is illegible, no text is lost into the background, and no element shows a night-mode-specific inversion or color failure.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground gray used for the small uppercase section eyebrows ("THE SHORT VERSION", "THE DETAILS", "CONTENTS") and the "Last updated" line in dark mode so each measures at least 4.5:1 against the page and card backgrounds — bring them up to roughly the brightness of the card's secondary body text, and make "THE DETAILS" match "THE SHORT VERSION" rather than sitting a step darker.

entries.critique: The Android tab of the beta page renders cleanly at 440 × 956. Hierarchy is clear and linear: header link and brand row, an H1, an intro paragraph, a two-tab selector with the Android tab marked by purple label, icon tint, and a full-width underline, then a "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" section rule, then numbered steps. Each step pairs a small numbered disc with a bold title, a body paragraph, and (for steps 1 and 2) a full-width purple action button — a consistent, repeating rhythm that makes the sequence easy to follow. Spacing is even: gutters are symmetric, paragraph leading is comfortable, and the gap between a step's text and its button is consistent between steps 1 and 2. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping; the long intro and body paragraphs wrap normally with no orphaned or colliding lines. Both purple buttons are full-width bars with generous vertical padding, unambiguously tappable, and the two tabs are wide targets with a clear selected state. Bolded inline phrases ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester") are legible and don't disturb line rhythm. At the bottom edge, step 3's body thins out over its last lines — that is the page's soft gradient fade marking that the scroll region continues, painted over the content rather than beside it, so it is the scroll cue arriving and not a legibility fault; the content sitting clear of that strip is fully sharp. Contrast on headings, body copy, and button labels is strong throughout. No actionable visible issue.

entries.review_description: Beta sign-up · Android. Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page. Captured in night mode on iPhone 16 Pro Max in portrait at 440 × 956. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this Android tab is largely sound: the heading, body copy, bold inline emphasis ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester"), the section label "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID", the step titles, and the "← Back to drawing" link all sit clearly against the near-black page. Both purple CTA buttons carry white labels on a mid-purple fill that stays legible, and the active/inactive tabs are distinguishable — "Android" in purple with its underline versus "iPhone / iPad" in lighter gray. The thinning of step 3's copy at the bottom edge is the scroll fade being drawn and is not judged.

The one weak spot is the small numerals inside the circular step markers (1, 2, 3). They are rendered as tiny glyphs in a muted tint on discs only slightly lighter than the page background, and they read markedly fainter than the step titles beside them. At this size the numeral is the smallest text in the frame while also having the least separation from its own fill, so the ordering cue — the thing that tells a parent which step they are on — is the hardest element on the page to read.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-number markers in dark mode: lighten the numeral toward the body-text color and/or darken or saturate the disc fill so the small numeral clears a comfortable contrast margin against its badge, matching the legibility of the step titles it labels.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: The iOS tab renders cleanly at 440×956. Hierarchy is clear and consistent: page title, intro paragraph, a tab row with the active "iPhone / iPad" tab marked by purple label, purple icon and a thick underline against a plain gray Android tab, then an uppercase "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" section label, then numbered steps with circled numerals, bold step headings, body copy and full-width purple CTA buttons. Spacing is even — consistent gutters left and right, uniform gaps between step heading, body, and button, and consistent rhythm between steps 1, 2 and 3. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping; the longest lines ("TestFlight is Apple's app for trying prerelease apps.", "Get TestFlight from Apple", "Open the Splotch invitation") all fit within their containers with margin to spare. Both CTA buttons are full-width, tall, and clearly tappable; the "← Back to drawing" link at top sits with adequate clearance from the header logo. The page continues past the bottom edge, and the step-3 line thinning out to gray at the very bottom is the scroll fade being painted over the last line, which is the intended cue rather than a legibility fault. Judging on the content clear of that faded strip, nothing is unreadable. No modal or overlay is present in this frame, so there is nothing to assess for scrim contrast or modal scrolling. I see no actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast is broadly sound: the "Join the Splotch beta" heading, intro paragraph, step headings ("Install TestFlight", "Accept the invitation", "Install Splotch") and body copy all read as near-white on the near-black page, and the two purple CTA buttons carry white labels at comfortable contrast. The active "iPhone / iPad" tab is purple with a purple underline and is clearly distinguishable from the inactive "Android" tab. The "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" eyebrow is small dimmed caps but still readable. The soft thinning of the step-3 sentence at the bottom edge is the scroll fade being drawn and is not judged.

The one weak spot is the numbered step badges. The digits 1, 2 and 3 are set very small in a dark tinted disc whose fill sits only slightly above the page background, and the numeral itself is a muted low-saturation tone rather than a light one. At a glance the "1" in particular reads as a smudge inside its circle rather than a legible figure, and the badges are the sole ordinal cue for a three-step sequence, so their weakness costs more than decorative dimming would. The step headings beside them are unaffected, which limits the impact.
entries.recommendation: Raise the numeral color inside the step badges to a light foreground tone (and lighten the disc fill slightly) so the 1/2/3 digits reach the same readability as the step headings they label.

entries.surface_description: The shared SvelteKit error boundary rendered for an unknown route.
entries.critique: The screen shows a single vertically-centered stack: a purple splotch mark, "Oops!" as a bold heading, a two-line gray subtitle, and a filled purple "Start over" pill button. Hierarchy is unambiguous — mark, heading, body, action — with clearly graded type sizes and consistent spacing between each step. All text fits within generous side margins; the subtitle wraps naturally onto two lines with no truncation, clipping, or overlap anywhere in the frame. The button is a large filled pill with high-contrast white label, comfortably above minimum touch size, and is the only interactive target on the screen, so there is no ambiguity about what to tap. Content sits entirely clear of the top and bottom safe areas, no scrolling region or overflow is present, and the light background is uniform. Palette and rounded-shape language are consistent with the app's playful identity.

entries.critique: Dark-theme rendering of the shared error boundary. The heading "Oops!" is near-white on the near-black background and reads at full strength. The supporting line "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." is a lighter gray, dimmer than the heading by design, but it stays clearly legible across both wrapped lines with no smearing or thinning. The "Start over" button pairs white label text with a mid-tone purple fill; the label is crisp and the pill separates cleanly from the dark ground. The purple blob above the heading is decorative and carries no text. No element on this screen falls below a usable night-mode contrast level.

entries.critique: The Settings dialog reads cleanly at 440×956. Title and close button are balanced across the card header, and the nine visible rows share one icon/title/subtitle template with consistent height, radius, inset, and vertical rhythm (a slightly larger gap after Sound reads as a deliberate group break). All titles and subtitles fit on a single line with no truncation, clipping, or overlap, and icons are centered against their text blocks. The Appearance and Sound controls sit well inside the card, are large enough to read as tappable, and show clearly distinct off/on states. The bottom edge shows the app's soft gradient fade painted over the Feedback row, which is the scrolling cue being drawn rather than a legibility fault; every row clear of that strip is fully legible. The page behind the card is under the dialog scrim, so the dimmed color palette and the faint corner chevron and settings glyphs are the scrim plus their intended resting styling — both glyph shapes are still locatable. No compact phone-landscape shell or orientation segments are present in this frame, so the orientation-segment intent has nothing to evaluate against here. No actionable visible issue.

A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation. Captured in light mode on iPhone 16 Pro Max in portrait at 440 × 956. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique: The Appearance card renders cleanly: title, back chevron, and close X sit on one row with even spacing; the Theme row's segmented control shows Light selected with a clear raised white pill against the gray track, and Dark/System labels are fully legible with no truncation; the "Lock device rotation" row and its off-state toggle align to the same card gutters. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems, and the scrim behind the card is the expected dialog treatment. The one visible issue is touch-target sizing on the back chevron at the top-left: its circular hit area measures roughly 36 px across at this 440-pt-wide capture, noticeably smaller than the 40 px close button beside it and below the comfortable minimum, and the chevron glyph inside it is small and light relative to the button. Its purpose is also slightly ambiguous next to the close X — two dismiss-adjacent controls of different sizes on the same row — but that is a secondary concern to the size itself.
entries.recommendation: Enlarge the top-left back control's tappable circle to at least match the close button (≈44 px), keeping the glyph optically centered, so both header controls present equal, comfortable touch targets.

entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique: The Appearance card is legible in night mode overall: "Appearance", "Theme", and "Lock device rotation" are near-white on the dark card, and the selected "Dark" segment reads clearly with its crescent icon. The scrim-dimmed canvas, palette, and faint corner chevron/gear behind the dialog are the expected overlay and quiet-control styling, not findings. Two weak spots on the card itself: (1) the back chevron in the top-left is a small muted-purple glyph on a dark gray disc that barely separates from the card — it is the dimmest interactive mark in the overlay, visibly weaker than the "x" close button on the same row despite being an equally important navigation control; (2) the unselected segment labels "Light" and "System" are medium gray on a lightly-raised gray segment track with a thin contrast margin, and their icons (sun, half-disc) are dimmer still, with the sun glyph nearly dissolving into the track.
entries.recommendation: Raise the back chevron's glyph to the same foreground tone as the "x" close icon and give its disc the same border treatment so the two header controls read at matching strength, and lift the unselected segment label and icon color a step so "Light" and "System" hold a clear margin against the segment track.

entries.surface_description: The Sound section where full settings fit; compact phone landscapes show the quick-toggle shell that replaces it.
entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique: The Sound settings card reads cleanly: title, close button, a grouped Sound toggle with its Volume slider, and a labeled "WHAT MAKES SOUND" group with Drawing and Deleting rows. Text fits without truncation or overlap, the 50% value aligns with the fill position, toggles and the close button are comfortably sized, and the card sits over the expected page scrim with no clipping. The one weak point is the circular back control at the top-left of the card: its chevron is a pale lavender glyph on a near-white gray disc, noticeably lighter than the "Sound" title beside it and than every other control on the card. It is an in-card navigation affordance rather than one of the deliberately recessed corner glyphs, so its low contrast reads as unintended — the disc is visible but the chevron itself is easy to miss, which makes the button's purpose ambiguous at a glance. Everything else in the frame is consistent and legible.
entries.recommendation: Darken the back chevron inside the top-left circular button on the settings card so the glyph reads at a strength comparable to the close "×", instead of a pale lavender stroke on a near-white disc.

entries.surface_description: The Sound section where full settings fit; compact phone landscapes show the quick-toggle shell that replaces it.
entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique: The open Sound card sits on a scrimmed page, so only the card is judged. Its primary text ("Sound" title, "Sound", "Volume", "Drawing", "Deleting", "50%") is near-white on the dark card surface and reads cleanly, and the purple toggles with white knobs are unambiguous. Two weak points inside the card: the back chevron in the top-left disc is a muted purple glyph on a barely-lighter-than-card disc — the glyph is locatable but is by far the lowest-contrast interactive element in the card and is easy to mistake for a decorative dot at a glance; and the "WHAT MAKES SOUND" section label is a mid-gray at small caps size, dimmer than needed even for a secondary label. The volume slider's unfilled track is also only marginally lighter than the card, so the track's extent (and thus the 50% position) is hard to read without the numeric label. Everything else in the card — close X, row icons, toggle states — is legible in night mode.
entries.recommendation: Raise the back-chevron glyph to a near-white or full-strength accent on a more clearly differentiated disc so it matches the close X in weight, and lift the "WHAT MAKES SOUND" label and the unfilled volume track a step brighter against the card surface.

entries.critique: The Tool Drawer card renders cleanly at 440 × 956. Title "Tool Drawer" sits with a back chevron on the left and a clearly outlined round close button at the top right, both with adequate target size and separation. The two settings rows ("Enable Advanced Controls" with a toggle plus helper text, "Button Size" with its 100% value and filled track) sit in distinct light-gray blocks with even padding and no text truncation or overlap; the toggle and slider thumb are unambiguous. The "DRAWING TOOLS" caption reads as a section header above a two-column grid of purple pills — Crayon, Magic brush, Eraser, Stroke width, Undo — each with an icon, a fully legible label, and a right-aligned checkmark; nothing wraps, clips, or collides, and the trailing odd item in the last row is a normal grid remainder. The card's bottom edge shows clean padding after the last pill with no fade strip, so no content is cut off mid-scroll. Behind the card the canvas, top color palette, docked trash button, bottom-left chevron and bottom-right settings glyph are all dimmed by the dialog scrim, which is expected; both corner glyphs remain locatable. This is the full-settings drawer, not the compact phone-landscape shell, so the orientation-segment intent does not apply here. No actionable visible issue.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast across the Tool Drawer card holds up. The card sits on a scrimmed, darkened page, so judgement is on the card itself: the "Tool Drawer" title and the row labels ("Enable Advanced Controls", "Button Size") are near-white on a dark slate surface and read cleanly. The secondary line "Show and hide individual on-screen buttons" and the "100%" value are dimmer gray but still clearly legible at this size. The purple tool chips carry white labels and white check glyphs with ample separation from the fill, and their small colored icons (crayon, eraser, magic brush, stroke width, undo) stay distinguishable against the purple. The "DRAWING TOOLS" section header is the weakest text — muted gray, small, letterspaced caps — but it remains readable and is a low-stakes grouping label. The toggle's white knob and lilac track are unambiguous in the on state, and the Button Size slider fill is clearly distinct from its unfilled track. The circular back chevron and the X close button are visible against the card. Both parent-facing corner glyphs (bottom-left chevron, bottom-right gear) are locatable in the frame, meeting the findability floor. No text or control in this image is illegible or below a usable contrast level.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in the open Coloring card is generally sound: the title "Coloring", the row labels ("Coloring book", "Download over mobile data", "Downloaded pictures"), and both toggles read clearly against the dark card, and the close (×) glyph in the top-right circle is crisp. Secondary helper text ("Show coloring pages and download new books automatically", "Allows automatic picture downloads when Wi-Fi isn't available", "7 of 7 extra books · 15.2 MB", "Every coloring book is ready offline") is dimmer gray but still resolves as text.

Two items are weaker than the rest of the card. The back chevron at the top-left sits in a filled circular button whose fill is barely separated from the card behind it, and the chevron glyph is a muted violet-gray that reads noticeably fainter than the × on the opposite side — an odd asymmetry between two peer controls on the same card, and not covered by the intentionally-quiet corner-glyph styling since this one is drawn as a real button. The destructive "Remove downloaded pictures" button is the lowest-contrast text in the card: red-tinted label on a desaturated red-tinted fill, with the label riding close to its own background and the button edge hard to make out.

Nothing in the frame is illegible, and no glyph is unlocatable.
entries.recommendation: Raise night-mode contrast on the two weak card controls: give the back chevron the same glyph lightness and circle-fill separation as the × close button, and lighten the "Remove downloaded pictures" label (and/or strengthen its fill/border) so the destructive action clears a comfortable text-contrast margin against its tinted background.

entries.critique:
The AI Art card is the open dialog, so it's the thing to judge, and most of it holds up in night mode: the "AI Art" title, the two toggle labels ("Create AI Images", "Customize AI Style", "Auto-Save AI Images"), and their gray descriptive subtext all sit clearly against the card's dark surface, and the purple/white toggles and the circled close button read strongly.

Two spots in the access-code block are weaker than the rest of the card. The value "daycare-club" inside the input is rendered in a muted gray monospace on an only slightly lighter inset field — it is the one piece of user-specific data on this screen that a parent may actually need to read or transcribe, and it is dimmer than the ordinary body copy above it. The explanatory paragraph above it ("You have special access via an access code — AI art is on us, no API key needed. Forget the code any time to remove it.") is likewise set at a lower value than the subtext under the toggles, with only the bolded "special access" reaching normal weight, so the sentence as a whole recedes. The "Forget" button's reddish label on its dark red fill is the third-weakest element, though it is still identifiable.

Everything outside the card — the dimmed color swatches along the top, the trash button, the corner chevron and settings glyph — is behind the dialog scrim or is the intended quiet parent-control styling, so none of that is a finding. The chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable in the bottom corners.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground value of the access-code field text ("daycare-club") and the surrounding access-code paragraph to match the body-copy gray used for the toggle descriptions, so the code itself is the most legible text in that block rather than the least.

entries.critique: The Parent Center card reads well overall: clear title, back and close affordances, readable body copy, and four consistently structured action rows. In each segmented control, the white "Never" pill is not contained by its gray track — its rounded right edge and border sit a few pixels outside the track's right boundary, and its top/bottom edges extend slightly past the track's height, so the selected pill visibly overhangs the container on every row instead of nesting inside it. This is consistent across all four controls, so it reads as a systematic sizing/inset error rather than a one-off. Everything else checks out: no text clipping or wrapping faults, spacing between cards is even, the card's bottom edge shows no truncated content, and the parent-facing chevron and gear glyphs below the scrim are locatable. entries.recommendation: Constrain the selected segment pill to the segmented-control track — give the track a small inner padding (e.g. 2px) and size the pill to the track's inner box (border-box sizing, accounting for the pill's border) so its rounded edges nest inside the track on all four rows instead of overhanging the right and vertical edges.

entries.critique:
The Parent Center card itself is legible in night mode: the "Parent Center" title, the four action headings ("Generating an AI image", "Reporting an AI result", "Viewing external links", "Sending feedback"), the intro paragraph, and the per-action explanation lines all read clearly as light gray/white on the dark card, and the circular back and close buttons in the header are clearly visible.

The visible weakness is in the three-way segmented controls. In each row the chosen segment ("Never" in all four) is rendered as a fill *darker* than the surrounding track and barely distinguishable from the card behind it; its only separation is a thin, very low-contrast outline. The unchosen segments ("Every time", "Per session") sit on a lighter gray track. The result in dark mode is that the selected option reads as a recessed hole rather than a highlighted choice, and at a glance the lighter unselected segments draw the eye more than the active one. The selected-state boundary is the lowest-contrast edge on the card, which matters because these segments encode whether a grown-up check is required before a drawing is sent to OpenAI or a report leaves the app.

Secondarily, the unselected label text ("Every time", "Per session") is a mid-gray on a mid-gray track and is noticeably dimmer than the white "Never" label — readable, but the weakest text in the card.

The parent-facing chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both locatable as shapes on the scrim, so they meet their findability floor.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the selected segment in the segmented controls in night mode — give the active pill a lighter fill (or a clearly brighter accent border/tint) than the unselected track instead of a near-card-background dark fill, and lift the unselected label gray so both states are distinguishable at a glance.

entries.critique:
The Install card itself is in good shape: clear title with a back chevron and a well-sized round close button, an "iOS" section label, and two numbered rows ("1. Install as App", "2. Enable Guided Access") with generous padding, consistent row height, full text fit, no clipping, wrapping, or overlap. Chevron affordances on the rows are visible and the rows are comfortably above touch-target size. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable. No modal scroll region is present — the two rows sit clear of the card's bottom edge with no fade — and hierarchy (title > section label > rows) reads correctly.

The one visible inconsistency is the scrim coverage. The canvas behind the dialog is clearly darkened, but the color palette strip along the top edge and the red trash button are rendered at full, unmuted brightness — the saturated swatches and the bright red trash disc are the highest-chroma elements in the frame and pull attention away from the open card, which is the opposite of what a full-page scrim is meant to do. The scrim's top boundary is also visible as a hard horizontal seam just below the palette, which reads as an unintended layering gap rather than a deliberate edge.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the top color-palette strip and the trash button so the entire page behind the Install card is darkened uniformly, eliminating the hard horizontal seam below the palette and the full-brightness swatches competing with the card.

entries.critique:
In this dark-mode Install card, the primary content holds up: "Install", "Install as App", and "Enable Guided Access" are near-white on the dark card and read cleanly, and the numbered "1."/"2." markers in purple are legible against the row fills. The ✕ close glyph and the purple back chevron in its circular disc are both clearly visible.

Two elements on the card fall short. The "iOS" section label above the list is small, all-lowercase/small-caps sized, and rendered in a dim gray that sits only marginally above the card background — it is the weakest text on an otherwise well-lit card, and it is the only thing telling the user which platform the two steps below apply to, so it is carrying real meaning at sub-threshold contrast. Separately, the "›" disclosure chevrons at the right edge of both rows are drawn in a gray that is noticeably dimmer than the row labels beside them; they are still locatable, but they are the affordance signalling that these rows are tappable and they read as much fainter than the text they belong to.

The card sits on a scrimmed page, so the darkened canvas, dimmed palette swatches along the top, the softened trash button, and the faint corner chevron and gear are the scrim and the intended resting styling rather than contrast findings; both corner glyphs remain findable in the frame.
entries.recommendation: Lift the on-card secondary grays in dark mode: raise the "iOS" section-header color to at least ~4.5:1 against the card surface (roughly a light gray rather than the current mid-gray), and brighten the row disclosure "›" chevrons to at least ~3:1 so the tappable affordance tracks the brightness of the row labels next to it.
