entries.critique:
The Feedback card reads cleanly: a clear back chevron and close button, a "SEND FEEDBACK" eyebrow, a two-option segmented control with the active "Something's broken" pill legibly distinguished, a labeled textarea with placeholder, a consent checkbox, a privacy note, and a primary action. Nothing is clipped, overlapped, or pushed outside the card; the page behind sits under the expected dialog scrim, and the corner chevron and gear glyphs are locatable. Text fit is fine, including the wrapped "Include device info (helps us reproduce the bug)" label, whose checkbox is top-aligned to the first line as expected. Touch targets for the segments, textarea, checkbox row, and close button all look adequately sized.

One visible weakness: the "Send report" button renders as white text on a pale lavender fill, making its label the hardest-to-read text in the card — noticeably weaker than the body copy above it, despite being the primary action. If this is a disabled state for the empty form, it is not clearly distinguishable from an enabled primary button; if it is enabled, the label contrast falls short for a call to action. Either way the button's state is ambiguous from the pixels alone.

Secondary and minor: the small gray privacy paragraph under the checkbox is the lightest text in the card and sits near the edge of comfortable readability at that size, though still legible.
entries.recommendation: Give "Send report" an unmistakable state treatment — enabled: solid saturated brand purple with full-strength white label; disabled: a clearly neutral gray fill with a darker gray label rather than a washed-out tint of the brand color — so the label stays readable and the button's availability is obvious at a glance.

entries.critique: The frame reads cleanly. The top color palette sits in its own white band with even spacing, consistent circle sizes, and a clear purple selection ring on the active swatch that matches the ink color of the stroke on the canvas — selection state and result agree. The canvas below is an unbroken tiled paper texture with the single purple stroke rendered crisply at full width, no tearing or tile seams visible. The trash button is docked at the right edge as intended, its icon fully legible within the visible portion. The chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both locatable as distinct shapes, meeting the findability floor for those intentionally quiet parent-facing controls. All interactive elements are generously sized and well clear of one another and of the screen edges; no text is present to fit or clip, nothing overlaps, and no overlay or scrolling region is open to evaluate. Spacing between the palette band and the top of the canvas is uniform, and the bottom controls sit at matching vertical offsets in their opposite corners.

The top palette bar is a near-black strip carrying six saturated swatches (purple, blue, green, yellow, white, multicolor) that all separate cleanly from it, and the selected purple swatch is marked by a distinct ring that is readable against both the swatch and the bar. No text is present to assess, and no element in the frame is lost to the background.

entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The frame reads cleanly overall. The top swatch row is evenly spaced with the active purple swatch clearly ringed; the canvas is unobstructed; the single purple stroke sits well clear of every control. The docked trash button, the faint chevron at y≈555, and the faint gear in the bottom-right corner are all locatable, and the undo/AI/screenshot buttons show the expected reduced-contrast disabled treatment while the coloring-book, stroke-width, and brush buttons below them are at full strength — a legible two-tier hierarchy within the panel. No text is present to clip or wrap, no overlap between the drawer column and the canvas stroke or the gear, and every round button is a comfortable ~50px target with consistent ~12px vertical rhythm.

One thing is worth flagging: the drawer column is bottom-anchored with only ~8px of clearance below the last (brush) button, whose lower edge sits at roughly y≈948 of 956. That matches the ~8px left inset, so it is visually consistent, but it places the bottom-most and most-used tool directly in the strip along the bottom edge of the screen where the system home-gesture area lives on this device. The other five buttons have full clearance; only the last one is pressed against the edge. There is no visible clipping — the button renders whole — so this is a reachability/mis-trigger risk rather than a layout break, and the fixed column also means the six buttons exactly fill the space between the chevron and the bottom edge with no room to grow.
entries.recommendation: Raise the drawer column's bottom anchor so the last button clears the bottom edge by the device safe-area inset (~34px) instead of the current ~8px, keeping the brush button out of the home-gesture strip.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
The brush flyout reads cleanly: four tool tiles (pen, crayon, magic brush, eraser) in a single white rounded column, the active pen marked with a filled lavender tile and purple outline so selection is unambiguous, and even vertical rhythm between the tiles with no clipping, overlap, or text to fit. The page behind is at full brightness, consistent with a no-scrim flyout, and the palette row, trash button, chevron, and settings gear are all locatable. Tool glyphs are large and well separated; each occupies roughly a 64px cell, so touch targets are clear and non-adjacent by accident. The flyout sits immediately right of the Actions Panel column without colliding with the brush button that anchors it.

The one visible issue is bottom inset. The flyout card's lower edge stops about 10px from the frame bottom, so the eraser tile — the last row — sits inside the iPhone home-indicator gesture strip. Every other floating element in the frame keeps a visibly larger margin: the Actions Panel buttons end around 20px up, and the palette row has comparable breathing room at the top. The result is both a swipe-conflict risk on the eraser and a small consistency break, since the flyout is the only surface that runs nearly flush to the edge.
entries.recommendation: Raise the brush flyout's bottom offset so its card clears the home-indicator safe area — match the ~20px margin the Actions Panel column already uses, letting the flyout grow upward from its anchor rather than downward into the gesture strip.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique: The flyout is a clean white rounded card holding five stroke previews in a single vertical column, at full page brightness with no scrim, sitting immediately right of the Actions Panel without overlapping it. Hierarchy reads correctly: each row is a diagonal brush stroke in the active purple, the selected third option is marked with a tinted fill and a purple rounded outline, and progression from thin to thick is legible top to bottom. Spacing between rows is even, the card's internal padding is consistent on all sides, nothing is clipped by the card edge or the viewport, and the card is fully visible with no fade strip, so no scroll region is in play. Row heights are roughly square and comparable to the adjacent round buttons, so touch targets read as adequate and separable. No text is present, so there is no fit or truncation risk. The chevron above the Actions Panel and the settings gear in the bottom-right corner are both locatable as faint gray glyphs, consistent with their intended quiet styling. The one weak point is the top of the ramp: options one and two render at very nearly the same visible weight and length, so the two thinnest choices are hard to tell apart at a glance, and the selected third row is only marginally heavier again — the perceptual step between the fine end of the scale is much smaller than the step between the two thick options at the bottom, which are clearly distinct. Nothing else here is actionable.
entries.recommendation: Widen the perceptual gap at the thin end of the stroke ramp so the first three previews differ as visibly as the bottom two — e.g. increase the spread of preview line weights (or lengthen the thin strokes) rather than mapping preview thickness linearly to the underlying brush size.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: The color-picker card clips its own content: the rightmost column of hexagons (dark red, burnt orange, dark green, navy, violet, dark brown, charcoal) is cut with a flat vertical edge flush against the card's right boundary, showing no right point, while the left column has clear padding — the honeycomb grid is horizontally off-center within the card. This is a hard crop at a container edge, not the app's soft scroll fade, and it leaves seven swatches as partial shapes with reduced touch area at the boundary. Secondarily, the card shows no title and no visible close/dismiss control, so exiting the overlay depends on picking a color or tapping the scrim. Otherwise hierarchy is sound: the scrim correctly darkens the canvas, top palette and corner controls; row and column spacing is even; the selected-swatch outline at bottom-left is legible; and both faint corner glyphs (chevron, gear) are locatable.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the honeycomb grid width (or add symmetric horizontal padding) inside the color-picker card so offset rows fit entirely — the rightmost hexagons should render their full right point with the same margin as the left column — and add a visible close affordance to the card.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the open color picker card is generally strong: the card's dark gray panel is clearly separated from the darker page behind it, and every chromatic hexagon (pinks, oranges, yellows, greens, blues, purples, magentas, browns, the white swatch) reads with ample luminance against the card. The two parent-facing corner glyphs are locatable — the chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both findable in shape.

One legibility problem: the near-black hexagon in the bottom row of the grid (fifth column) sits at essentially the same luminance as the card surface behind it. Its only affordance is a hairline outline that is itself very low contrast; the swatch's fill effectively disappears, so in night mode it reads as an empty slot or a gap in the grid rather than as a selectable black color. Every other swatch in the grid is identified by its fill; this one is not, which makes it the one cell whose color is not conveyed and whose tappability is ambiguous at a glance.

Nothing else here is actionable: the dark navy swatch in the blue row is dim but still clearly a distinct filled swatch, and the row-to-row separation of the honeycomb holds up.
entries.recommendation: Give the black/near-black swatch a visibly lighter, thicker border (or a subtle lighter backing plate behind it) in night mode so its hexagon shape and filled state read against the dark card, matching the way the white swatch reads in light contexts.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The Coloring Books dialog itself is in good shape: the title and close button sit clearly at the top, the 2-column cover grid has even gutters, every label ("Farm", "Dinosaurs", "Creatures", "Nature", "Objects", "Shapes") fits on one line without truncation or overlap, cards are large, uniform touch targets, and the partial row at the bottom carries the app's soft fade, correctly signalling more content below. Background dimming behind the card reads as the intended scrim.

The visible problem is that the scrim is not covering the whole page. The color-swatch strip along the top edge (purple, blue, green, gold, black, plus the multicolor palette button) and the round red trash button at the upper right are rendered at full brightness and saturation, sitting outside the darkened region, which begins only below them. The result is that the most chromatically intense elements in the frame — a large saturated red circle and a row of solid color discs — compete with the open dialog for attention, and the trash button in particular sits immediately adjacent to the dialog's own close button, so the brightest control on screen is one the dialog does not own. The dialog's white card is also lighter than these, so the eye lands on the top strip before the card title. Their full brightness additionally implies they are still interactive while a modal is open, which the scrim elsewhere is doing the work of denying.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog's scrim over the full viewport so the top color-swatch strip and the docked trash button are darkened and blurred along with the rest of the page, matching the treatment already applied to the canvas and bottom-corner controls.

entries.critique: The dialog itself is well-formed: header row has a back chevron, the title "Farm" at comfortable size with no truncation, and a close ✕ of matching diameter aligned on the same baseline, all with generous edge padding and clear separation as touch targets. The 2-column page grid is consistent — equal gutters, matching card radii and aspect, thumbnails scaled uniformly with even internal margin and no line art touching card edges. The partially visible third row under a soft gradient fade correctly marks continued scrolling, and the content clear of that fade is fully legible. No text overflow, clipping, or overlap is visible anywhere in the frame; the settings glyph at bottom right and the pen button at bottom left are both locatable. The one visible problem is that the dialog's scrim is applied unevenly. The canvas region behind the card is plainly darkened, but the color palette strip along the top edge and the pen/brush button at bottom left are rendered at full brightness and saturation, sitting visually in front of the dimmed page. This makes the bright swatch row compete with the card's own header for attention at the top of the frame and makes the scrim read as a band across the middle of the page rather than a single layer behind the whole dialog.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to cover the full viewport so the top color-palette strip and the bottom-left pen button are darkened along with the canvas, rather than remaining at full brightness above the scrim layer.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in this coloring-page picker holds up well overall. The "Farm" title is near-white on the dark card and reads crisply. The page thumbnails are white line art on dark tiles with strong separation, and each tile's border is visible against the card. The card itself is clearly lighter than the scrimmed page behind it, so the dialog separates from the darkened canvas and palette. The bottom row of thumbnails thins toward the lower edge, which is the scroll-fade cue being drawn, and the rows clear of it are fully legible. The settings glyph in the bottom-right corner is locatable as a gear shape, and the bottom-left corner glyphs are present in frame, so the parent-facing controls meet the findability floor.

The one weak spot is the dialog's two header controls: the back chevron at top-left and the close "×" at top-right. In both, the glyph and its surrounding ring are a mid-gray on the only slightly lighter dark card, sitting at noticeably lower contrast than the "Farm" label beside them and than the thumbnail line art below. These are in-dialog navigation controls — the only visible way back out of this drilled-in view — and their rings nearly merge with the card surface at a glance.
entries.recommendation: Raise the dark-theme foreground of the dialog header's back-chevron and close-"×" glyphs and their circular rings toward the near-white used for the "Farm" title (or give them a lighter filled disc), so both clear roughly 3:1 against the card surface.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique:
Overall the screen reads cleanly: the palette row across the top is evenly spaced with a clear selection ring on the purple swatch, the canvas is uncluttered, the docked trash button is legible against the artwork, and the collapse chevron and settings glyph are both locatable in their corners. No clipped or overflowing text, no truncation, and the expanded Actions Panel column is consistently sized and spaced.

The one visible problem is in the upper half of that panel. The undo, sparkle/AI, and camera buttons render as bare glyphs with no disc behind them (unlike the emoji, wave, and pencil buttons below, which sit on solid white circles), and they land directly on top of the black line art of the flower cluster in the lower-left of the coloring page. The undo arrow at roughly (33, 613) merges into the flower's petals and stem, and the camera glyph at (33, 737) sits over the leaf outlines. Reduced contrast on those three while disabled is the intended marking, but the loss of the disc means there is no shape separating them from the drawing underneath, so their outlines and the artwork's outlines interleave. The result is that the panel visually breaks into two halves — three floating marks and three real buttons — and the top three are hard to parse as controls or as touch targets at all, which also makes the panel's overall extent ambiguous.

This is a shape/containment issue rather than a contrast one: it would persist against any busy artwork regardless of how the disabled tint is tuned.
entries.recommendation: Keep a visible container for the undo, AI, and camera buttons in their disabled state — retain the same white (or dimmed white) circular disc used by the enabled buttons below and apply the disabled treatment to the glyph only, so the three controls stay separated from the coloring-page line art behind them and the Actions Panel reads as one consistent column.

entries.critique:
The frame is a mostly empty light canvas with the six-swatch color palette across the top, the docked round trash button at the top-right edge, and the two quiet parent-facing corner glyphs (chevron bottom-left, gear bottom-right) both clearly locatable. No text is present, so there is no text-fit or clipping issue; the palette row is evenly spaced and its swatches read as distinct, adequately sized targets.

Judging the coachmark on legibility only: the ghost trash disc and the hand glyph are drawn overlapping, and the hand's palm and finger strokes sit on top of the trash icon's lower-right quadrant, cutting into the can's body and lid. Both are dark strokes over the same pink disc, so they merge into an ambiguous blob at the intersection — the trash icon stops reading cleanly as a trash can, and the hand is hardest to parse exactly where it crosses the disc edge. The large pink arc reads clearly and stays separable; its running off the top edge past the palette is consistent with a traced path and obscures no swatch.

Nothing else in the frame shows crowding, hierarchy, or touch-target problems.
entries.recommendation: Offset the hand glyph so it clears the ghost trash disc (sit it just outside the disc's lower-right edge rather than on top of the icon), or give the hand a light knockout/halo stroke, so both shapes stay individually readable where they meet.

entries.critique: Held-past-threshold state on the clear gesture. The red trash button sits undocked in the upper-right region of the canvas with a red glow halo, and the faint washed icons across the canvas plus the pale horizontal stroke read as the intended clearing-underway effect, so I take no issue with the wash. The color palette across the top is evenly spaced, unclipped, and each swatch is a comfortable target; the active purple swatch is clearly ringed. The bottom-corner chevron and the settings gear are both locatable as thin gray glyphs, which is their resting appearance here. The one thing that does not resolve cleanly is the large red accept ring: its arc enters at the top of the canvas, curves down past the trash button, and runs off the right edge of the viewport, so a substantial portion of the ring is outside the frame. Unlike the docked trash button, whose edge overhang is deliberate, this ring is the feedback shape that signals the threshold has been reached — and with a large share of its circumference off-screen it reads as an ambiguous red arc rather than a closed ring. The strongest visual cue for "past threshold" is therefore the element least fully visible, while the fully visible cue is only the diffuse red glow around the trash icon. Everything else in the frame — hierarchy, spacing, text fit (no text is present), overlap, touch-target clarity — holds up.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the accept ring so its full circumference stays inside the viewport when the trash button is dragged near an edge — clamp the ring's center inward or reduce its radius so the closed circle always reads as complete, instead of running off the right edge as a partial arc.

entries.critique: The install banner is a full-width card docked across the bottom of the 440×956 viewport, and it fully occludes both bottom-corner controls: neither the expand/collapse chevron nor the opposite-corner settings glyph can be located anywhere in the image. The banner casts no scrim (the canvas, palette and trash button remain at full brightness), so this is straightforward overlap rather than an intentional dimming — and the elements it hides are the parent-facing controls, which is the audience the banner itself is addressing. Within the card, hierarchy is sound: app icon, bold two-line title "Add Splotch to your home screen", gray subtitle, a filled purple "How?" pill, and a circular ✕ close button, all with clear contrast and visibly distinct, adequately sized touch targets. The pressure point is horizontal space — with the icon, pill and close button consuming the row, the text column is roughly 190px, forcing the title to two lines and breaking the subtitle mid-phrase to "just like a / real app", whose second line sits tight against the card's lower padding. Nothing is truncated or clipped, the trash button's dock past the right edge is as specified, and the drawn strokes and top palette are unaffected.
entries.recommendation: Reserve space for the corner controls while the banner is up — either inset the banner so the chevron and settings glyphs remain visible beside it, or temporarily lift/reflow those two controls above the banner — and give the text column more width (e.g. tighten the icon/pill gutters) so the subtitle does not wrap into a cramped second line against the card's bottom padding.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the install banner is mostly sound: the two-line title "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white bold on the dark card and reads crisply; the "How?" pill is dark purple text on a light lavender fill, the strongest contrast pair in the frame; the "×" close glyph is a thin gray mark but its shape is clearly locatable and it sits on a plain dark field with no competing texture.

The one weak element is the supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app." It is rendered small and in a muted gray-violet that sits close to the card's own dark plum background — noticeably dimmer than the title above it and than the banner's purple border, and it wraps to a second line where the tail ("real app") gets even harder to resolve. Unlike the deliberately recessive corner glyphs, this is body copy inside an active promotional card that is asking the user to take an action, so it is meant to be read rather than to sit back. Nothing else in the frame is affected: the palette row along the top edge, the purple strokes on the canvas, and the trash button all hold clearly against the dark ground, and no scrim is in play here.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the banner's subtitle ("Opens full-screen, just like a real app") toward the near-white used by the title — enough to clear 4.5:1 against the card's dark plum fill at its small size — so the supporting copy is readable rather than sitting a step above the background.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
The expanded install banner has two visible problems.

1. Stale toggle label. The Share-sheet instructions are already expanded and filling the lower third of the card, yet the primary button still reads "How?" — the same label it carries in the collapsed state. Nothing in the frame indicates the button now collapses the guidance, and the only other control on the card is the "×" dismiss. A parent who taps "How?" again after reading has no visible cue whether they will re-expand, collapse, or re-trigger something.

2. The card runs off the bottom of the viewport. The banner's top corners are clearly rounded and there is generous padding above the header row, but the instruction block's last line ("View More" first.) sits at roughly y=912 of a 956px frame and no matching bottom corner radius, bottom padding, or card edge is visible below it. The card reads as extending past the screen edge rather than terminating, which is asymmetric with its own top treatment and leaves the final instruction line hard against the device's home-indicator zone.

Secondary, lower-confidence: the instruction paragraph mixes inline glyphs (share icon, plus-in-square, chevron) into running text at three different vertical positions, and the sentence wraps mid-phrase — "then choose / [icon] "Add to Home Screen". If you don't see it, tap / [chevron] / "View More" first." The chevron ends line two with no following word, so the reader must jump back down and left to pick up "View More". The steps are legible but the ragged wrap makes a three-step procedure read as one dense block; hierarchy here is weaker than the well-separated header/subhead/button row above it.

Everything else in view is sound: the color palette along the top is evenly spaced with a clear selected state on the purple swatch, the docked trash button reads normally, the three canvas strokes are unobstructed, and the header, subhead, button, and close control inside the card have clear separation and adequate contrast.
entries.recommendation: Give the expanded state its own affordances: swap the button label from "How?" to a collapse label (or add a rotated chevron) once the instructions are open, and add explicit bottom padding plus the matching corner radius so the card visibly terminates above the home-indicator area instead of running off the bottom edge. While there, break the Share-sheet guidance into three short numbered lines so each inline glyph stays with its own step rather than stranding the chevron at a line end.

entries.critique: The install banner's core text hierarchy survives night mode: the white "Add Splotch to your home screen" heading and the light-gray instruction body ("Tap [share] Share at the bottom of the screen, then choose [icon] "Add to Home Screen". Two high-luminance values are stacked, so the label has minimal separation from its own button and reads as a bright blob before it reads as a word — and this is the banner's primary action. Every other string in the card is light-on-dark; this one inverts the relationship without darkening the fill to compensate. Second: the sub-line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" is set small in a mid-gray dimmer than the instruction text beneath it, making it the least legible string in the card even though it sits directly under the heading. The inline glyphs in the instruction row — the Share icon, the Add-to-Home-Screen icon, and the trailing chevron — are all locatable and hold their shapes. The close "x" is dim but findable. The top color palette and the docked trash button are at full brightness and legible.
entries.recommendation: Darken the "How?" pill fill in night mode to a deep purple instead of the current light lavender so the white label clears 4.5:1, and lift the "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" sub-line to the same gray value used for the instruction body text.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique: The gate card renders cleanly. Hierarchy is clear: logo, "Grown-Ups Only" title, "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle, then the equation row (purple 4 × blue 8 = two dashed answer slots), the keypad, and a divider-separated footer. Nothing is clipped or overlapped — the card sits fully inside the 440×956 viewport with even side margins, and the close × sits in its own circular button at the top-right corner without colliding with the logo. Keys are large, evenly gridded, well spaced, and unambiguously tappable; the backspace glyph is legible. Two answer slots correctly match the two-digit product, and both are visible without scrolling — the whole dialog fits with no cut-off content. Text fit is fine at every size; no wrapping, truncation, or overflow. The empty third cell in the bottom keypad row is a conventional numeric-pad layout, not a defect. The dimmed, blurred canvas, palette, and corner buttons behind are the dialog scrim, and the footer's "Manage these checks in / Settings › Parent Center" line is small but fully readable with its icons intact.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open gate card is largely sound: "Grown-Ups Only" is near-white on the dark card, "Solve the problem to continue" is legible mid-gray, the 0–9 keypad digits are white on lighter-than-card key fills and read cleanly, the backspace glyph is visible, the operand chips (purple 8, blue 7) carry white numerals at strong contrast, and the × and = operators are clearly rendered. The circular close button's ✕ reads against its outlined disc.

The one weak element is the footer caption "Manage these checks in" — small, thin, dim gray set on the card's dark surface, noticeably fainter than every other text on the card and the hardest thing to read here. It sits below the divider with the "Settings › Parent Center" links (which are brighter and fine), so the label that explains what those links are is the least legible part of the dialog. The two dashed empty answer circles are also very faint, but they are unfilled placeholders whose job is to be quiet until a digit lands, so I do not count them.

Everything behind the card — canvas, top color palette, tool rail, corner glyphs, docked trash button — is under the dialog scrim and out of scope; the bottom-left chevron and bottom-right settings glyph are both locatable in the frame, so neither owes a finding.
entries.recommendation: Raise the footer caption "Manage these checks in" to a lighter gray (roughly the same tone as the "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle) so it clears 4.5:1 against the card surface in dark mode.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique: The "Pick a style" card reads cleanly over the dimmed, blurred canvas: the scrim isolates it, the title sits clear at the top-left, and the 4×2 grid of style tiles is evenly gutted with consistent tile size, corner radius, and label placement. All eight labels ("Magical", "Crayon", "Watercolor", "Paper", "Felt", "Sticker", "Cartoon", "Clay") fit on one line inside their column with no truncation, wrapping, or collision with the neighboring tile. Thumbnails are fully rendered with no clipping at tile edges, and the grid's outer margins are balanced left/right with adequate padding above the first row and below the last. The circular close button is fully drawn inside the card's top-right corner, visually separated from the title and from the first tile row, and is comfortably sized as a touch target; the tiles themselves are large squares with generous spacing, so no two adjacent targets crowd each other. Selection state is legible — the "Sticker" tile carries a distinct highlighted treatment that separates it from the unselected tiles. The card is not clipped by the viewport on any side and does not overlap the color palette at the top or the corner controls at the bottom in a way that obscures its own content. The grid ends cleanly above the card's bottom edge with no faded strip, indicating the content fits without scrolling. Background elements — palette swatches, trash button, actions panel, settings glyph — read dim and soft, which is the dialog scrim, and the settings glyph is still locatable in the bottom-right corner. Nothing in the frame shows an actionable hierarchy, spacing, fit, clipping, overlap, or consistency defect.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: The loading card fills nearly the full 956px viewport height, but its content occupies only the bottom fifth. The preview region spans roughly y≈40–775 and holds a single ~170px gradient dial centered in it, leaving large empty white bands (roughly 250px above and 270px below the dial) with only a faint blurred title strip stranded near the top. The result is bottom-heavy: "Making your picture…", the 30-second estimate, and the full-width "Keep drawing while you wait" button cluster at the bottom while most of the card is blank. Separately, the dial reads ambiguously as a progress indicator — a solid filled gradient disc with one thin white radial line rather than a visibly swept arc, so progress is not legible. Everything else checks out: hierarchy is correctly ordered, no text is clipped or truncated, nothing overlaps, the close ✕ has a clear circular touch target at top right, and the primary button is comfortably sized and full width.
entries.recommendation: Cap or shrink the loading card's preview region so the dial, status text, and button form one compact group instead of leaving ~500px of empty white above and below the dial, and render the dial's progress as a visibly swept arc rather than a solid disc with a single hairline.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open AI-generating card is mostly sound. "Making your picture…" renders near-white on the card's very dark plum surface and is crisply legible; "This takes about 30 seconds" is a lighter gray at small size but still comfortably readable. The close button's white ✕ on its dark disc at the card's top-right reads clearly, and the magenta/violet progress dial with its white center dot and glow is by far the highest-contrast element in the frame — its filled-versus-empty sweep is unambiguous. The blurred drawing-preview panel behind the dial is intentionally soft and carries no text to judge. Behind the card the page is scrimmed as expected: the color swatches along the top edge and the docked trash button at the right are dimmed, and the low-contrast chevron (bottom left) and gear glyph (bottom right) are both still locatable as shapes, so neither owes a finding.

The one weak spot is the primary action pill "Keep drawing while you wait." Its label is a light lavender set on a desaturated dark-purple fill, and the two sit close together in luminance — the tint of the fill pulls up toward the tint of the text rather than away from it. Compared with the white heading directly above it, the button's label visibly recedes, which is backwards for what is the card's only actionable control besides close. In night mode this is the element most likely to fall below a comfortable reading threshold on a bright-ambient screen, and it is the one place on this card where a contrast lift is actually warranted.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill in dark mode — set the label to near-white (or darken/desaturate the purple fill) so the card's primary action reads at least as strongly as the "Making your picture…" heading above it.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
The AI result dialog reads cleanly: the generated image is the dominant element, uncropped and sharp, with generous even margins inside a rounded white card; the filled purple "Download" pill is unambiguously the primary action and comfortably sized; the circular close button sits clear of the image corner with a visible outline and no overlap. Text fits without truncation or clipping anywhere, and the card is fully within the 440 × 956 viewport with no scrolling implied.

The one weak spot is the "AI-generated picture · Report" row. It is placed outside the card entirely, floating on the scrim below the card's bottom edge, which detaches the disclosure and the report action from the dialog they describe. "Report" is rendered as small low-contrast gray text plus a small flag icon with no button, pill, or outline around it, so its hit area is undefined — unlike the close button and Download pill, nothing communicates where the tappable region begins or ends, and it sits directly on a darkened backdrop where a tap slightly off-target would plausibly read as a scrim dismiss. This is a real interactive control, not a parent-facing quiet glyph like the corner chevron or settings gear, and it is the only affordance in the frame whose tap boundary is unreadable.

Secondary, minor: the color swatches along the top edge appear noticeably more saturated and bright than the rest of the darkened page behind the dialog, so the scrim treatment does not read as uniform across the full background — the palette pulls some attention away from the open card.
entries.recommendation: Move the "AI-generated picture · Report" row inside the dialog card (below the Download button) and give "Report" a defined tappable surface — a bordered or tinted pill at least 44 pt tall — so its hit area is visible and it is not a bare text target sitting on the dismiss scrim.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the AI result card is largely sound: the Download button is a saturated purple pill with white label and a white download glyph, comfortably legible; the generated image is bright and fully readable; the round ✕ close button is a white glyph on a light disc over the picture and reads clearly at a glance. The trash button's red disc and white can icon hold up against the dark page, and both quiet parent-facing glyphs — the bottom-left chevron and the bottom-right gear — are locatable in the frame, so they meet the findability floor for their intended subdued styling.

The one weak spot is the metadata/action row drawn beneath the card, on top of the darkened page: "AI-generated picture · Report" is set in small gray type, and "Report" — the only actionable target in that row — is rendered in a muted, desaturated red-brown that sits only slightly off the near-black background. Against the surrounding dark it reads as the dimmest text in the frame, and its small flag icon is dimmer still. Unlike the chevron and gear, this is not a control styled to recede: it is a labeled safety affordance presented as tappable text, and at this contrast level a parent scanning the screen in a dark room would have to hunt for it. The separating "·" is nearly invisible, which further collapses the row into a single faint smudge of gray.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the "Report" control and its flag icon beneath the AI card — give the label a brighter, less desaturated red (or plain high-contrast body text color) so it clears roughly 4.5:1 against the dark page, and match the icon's tint to it.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
The confirmation card itself is well built: "Report this picture" leads clearly, the retention paragraph wraps in four full lines with no clipping or overflow, and the Cancel / Send report buttons are large, clearly separated, and unambiguous in weight (filled purple primary vs. tinted secondary). Spacing between heading, body, thumbnails, and actions is even.

The failure is in the evidence row. "The drawing behind it" renders as an essentially blank white card — the only mark is a short purple stroke fragment at the very top, cropped so its upper half is cut by the thumbnail's top edge. Beside the fully rendered AI thumbnail directly to its left, it reads as a broken or empty image rather than the child's drawing, which defeats the purpose of showing the parent what is being transmitted. This is a crop/fit problem, not the app's documented edge-fade cue: it is a hard cut at the frame boundary of a static thumbnail, not a soft gradient over a scrolling region.

Secondary: the round × close button belonging to the AI card behind sits at full brightness above and outside the confirmation card's top-right, giving two competing dismiss affordances (× and Cancel) with nothing indicating which governs the dialog in front.
entries.recommendation: Fit the "drawing behind it" thumbnail to its frame — scale/letterbox to the stroke bounding box instead of top-cropping at native canvas coordinates — so the actual drawing is recognizable, and dim or disable the underlying card's × while the confirmation dialog is open.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Judging the open confirmation card (the page behind it is scrimmed, so the canvas, palette and corner glyphs are out of scope; the chevron and settings glyph are both locatable in the bottom corners anyway).

Inside the card, most of the type holds up in night mode: "Report this picture" is near-white on the dark plum card and reads crisply, the retention paragraph is a light gray that stays comfortably legible at body size, and the primary "Send report" button uses dark text on a bright violet fill with strong separation.

Two weaker spots are visible. The "Cancel" button is the clearest: a muted lavender label on a desaturated dark-purple fill, with the fill itself only slightly lighter than the card behind it. The label reads noticeably dimmer than the neighboring "Send report" text and the button's own edges are hard to make out, so the control reads as semi-disabled rather than as the equal-weight alternative to the primary action. The thumbnail captions ("The AI picture", "The drawing behind it") are also set in a small dim gray that sits close to the card background; they are readable but are the faintest text in the card at the smallest size, which is the least forgiving combination.

Nothing else in the card is problematic — the close button's glyph is visible against its darkened disc over the artwork, and the two thumbnails themselves are bright and clear.
entries.recommendation: Raise the Cancel button's label to a brighter near-white lavender and lighten (or add a visible border to) its fill so the secondary action reads as an enabled peer of "Send report" rather than a disabled control; apply a similar lift to the two thumbnail caption labels.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal card itself is clean: the palette emoji, headline, body copy, "For grown-ups" caption, and the "Report this refusal" pill all fit inside the card with no clipping, bad wraps, or overlap. Hierarchy reads correctly (bold headline → gray body → small caption → tinted action). The close button is a clearly tappable disc at the card's top-right that does not collide with the headline, and both it and the report button are well above minimum touch size. The card is comfortably inset from both side edges and there is no scrolling region to judge.

The one visible issue is scrim coverage. The page behind the dialog is darkened and blurred across the canvas — the purple stroke and the bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are clearly dimmed — but the top color-palette strip is still rendered at full brightness on a white background, and the docked round trash button is still fully saturated red. The scrim stops short of those two regions, leaving the highest-chroma elements in the frame competing with the open card for attention in a treatment whose purpose is for the card to hold attention.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim (darken + blur) over the top color-palette strip and the docked trash button so the whole page behind the refusal card is suppressed uniformly, matching how the scrim already treats the canvas and corner controls.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique: The refusal card itself carries most of its text well: the headline "Let's try drawing something else!" is near-white on the dark card and the two-line body copy below it is comfortably legible, as is the circular close button with its bright outline and glyph. Two elements on the card fall short in night mode. The primary action, "Report this refusal," puts a light lavender label on a desaturated purple fill; the two tones are close enough in lightness that the label loses definition against its own button, which is the one control on this card a grown-up is meant to act on. Just above it, the "For grown-ups" line is set in a small, dim gray that sits only slightly above the card's own surface tone — noticeably weaker than the body copy it labels, and hard to resolve at a glance despite being the cue that tells an adult the button below is theirs. The parent-facing chevron and settings glyphs in the bottom corners are both locatable, and the canvas behind reads as expected.
entries.recommendation: On the refusal card in dark mode, raise the "Report this refusal" label to near-white (or darken/desaturate the button fill) so the label clears 4.5:1 against its own fill, and lighten the "For grown-ups" gray to at least the body copy's tone.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique: The error card itself is clean: emoji, a single line of copy, and a well-formed circular close button at the top right with an unambiguous touch target. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems, and the card sits comfortably centered. Two visible issues. First, the copy says "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!" but the only control on the card is the ✕ close button — there is no retry affordance anywhere in the dialog, so the instruction points at an action the card does not provide. Reinforcing this, the lower third of the card is an empty white band with nothing in it, which reads as a missing element rather than deliberate breathing room. Second, the scrim is applied inconsistently: the canvas behind the card is darkened and blurred, but the color palette strip along the top edge and the round trash button at the top right remain at full brightness and full saturation, so they sit visually forward of the dimmed page and compete with the open card for attention. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable.
entries.recommendation: Add a primary "Try again" button in the empty lower area of the card so the copy's instruction has a control to match, and extend the dialog scrim over the top color palette strip and the trash button so the whole page behind the card is dimmed uniformly.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique: The error card is the element in scope: a dark gray card on a scrimmed page. Its message, "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!", is set in near-white text on the card's dark fill and reads cleanly at a glance, well above a comfortable contrast margin. The yellow frowning emoji is fully saturated and legible against the card. The circular close button in the top-right corner is drawn with a bright white ring and white X glyph, clearly separated from the card behind it and easy to locate as the only actionable control on the card. Nothing on top of the scrim is washed out or ambiguous. The dimmed palette swatches, trash button, and single purple stroke behind the card are the dialog scrim doing its job, not a contrast finding. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are faint by design, but both shapes are locatable in the frame, so they meet the findability floor. No night-mode contrast or legibility issue is visible.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Hierarchy and text fit are largely sound: the Admin title, subtitle, amber persistence warning (with the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip fitting inline without overflow), the add-code field with its Add button, and the two access-code rows with Copy buttons and expand chevrons all sit clear of each other with no clipping or overlap, and every touch target reads as a distinct control at comfortable size.

Two visible problems. First, the two section headers are styled and spaced inconsistently: "ACCESS CODES · 2" carries a trailing horizontal rule and has clear breathing room above it, whereas "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" has no rule and is set very tight beneath the bottom edge of the access-code list card — close enough that it visually attaches to that card instead of opening the section below it, weakening the top-level structure of the page.

Second, in the six free-grant metric tiles the labels wrap unevenly at this width: "Provider starts today" and "Sampled exhausted" run to two lines while "Sampled successes", "Sampled attempts", "Sampled failures" and "Sampled active" break differently, and because each value is stacked directly under its own label, the large numerals land on different vertical baselines across each row. "0/500" sits noticeably lower than the two 0s beside it in the top row, and in the bottom row "0" under "Sampled exhausted" drops below its neighbors. The result is a ragged, unaligned numeric row where the numbers are the thing meant to be scanned.
entries.recommendation: Give the metric tiles a fixed two-line label area (or bottom-align the value within each tile) so the numerals share a baseline across each row, and treat the "FREE GENERATION GRANTS" header like "ACCESS CODES" — same trailing rule and the same top margin above it — so it reads as a new section rather than a caption on the card above.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast is broadly sound. White headings ("Admin", the mono code names daycare-club and page-inventory-harness) separate strongly from the near-black page and the slightly lighter card fills. The purple "Sign out" and "Add" buttons carry white labels that read cleanly; the "Copy" outline buttons keep a legible lavender label with a visible border; the large metric values (0/500, 0) are bright white and unmistakable. The two cream advisory banners invert to light panels, but their dark amber/brown text on cream reads without effort, including the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip.

The weak tier is the dimmest gray text on the dark ground. The "Add a code…" placeholder is the faintest text in the frame — weaker than the surrounding input border and close to washing into the field fill, which matters because it is the only label identifying that input. The six metric captions ("Provider starts today", "Sampled successes", "Sampled attempts", "Sampled failures", "Sampled active", "Sampled exhausted") sit at a similarly muted gray at small size; readable, but first to fade, and at least anchored by their large white values. The subtitle "Manage AI access codes" and the small-caps section rules ("ACCESS CODES · 2", "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0") are on that same low tier, though tracking and placement make them easier to pick up.

Nothing is illegible and no control is unfindable, so this is a tuning note rather than a blocking failure.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the dark-theme placeholder color on the "Add a code…" input and the six metric caption labels to a gray that clears 4.5:1 against their card fills; they are the only text on screen falling below the legibility of everything around them.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
The screen reads cleanly: page title, amber warning notice, add-code field, and the code list form a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy. The expanded row for `daycare-club` is unambiguous — its chevron is rotated up and sits in a filled lavender square while the collapsed `page-inventory-harness` row shows a plain down chevron, so open/closed state is legible at a glance. "Copy link" and "Remove" render as two pill buttons directly beneath the expanded row, comfortably sized for touch and clearly scoped to the row above them by the card boundary and the hairline separator before the next row. Text fits without truncation: the monospace code names, button labels, the warning paragraph with its inline `ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST` code chip, and the stat-tile captions all wrap or sit within their containers. No clipping or overlap is visible, and the red tint on "Remove" distinguishes the destructive action from neutral "Copy link" without shouting.

One visible inconsistency: the "ACCESS CODES · 2" section header is followed by a horizontal rule running to the right edge, but the parallel "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" header below the code card has no rule. Two headers in the same style (small, letterspaced, uppercase, gray) at the same structural level are decorated differently, weakening the second section's read as a peer — it sits tight under the code card and, without its rule, reads more like a caption attached to that card than the start of a new section. Its top spacing is also visibly tighter than the gap given the first header.

The bottom row of stat tiles being cut by the viewport is ordinary scroll, and "Sampled exhausted" wrapping to two lines while its siblings sit on one is normal within a fixed grid.
entries.recommendation: Give "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" the same trailing horizontal rule as "ACCESS CODES · 2", and match its top margin to the spacing above the first section header so the two read as peers.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin screen is largely sound: the page title, the mono row identifiers ("daycare-club", "page-inventory-harness"), the "Copy" / "Copy link" labels, the "Add" primary button, and the stat-tile numerals all read crisply against the dark ground, and the two cream advisory banners carry dark amber text at strong contrast — a deliberate light-on-dark inversion that stays fully legible.

Two weak spots are visible. First, the destructive "Remove" label in the expanded row is a desaturated red sitting close in luminance to the dark button fill behind it; next to "Copy link" (near-white on the same fill) it is clearly the harder of the two to read, and it is the one action on the row where a misread carries consequence. Second, the small uppercase section labels — "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" — and the "Add a code…" placeholder are a mid-gray that thins out against the page background at that size and letterspacing; the grant label is the faintest text in the frame.

These are text-contrast issues in ordinary page content: no overlay, scrim, scroll fade, or disabled-state styling is present in this capture.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the "Remove" label's red to a higher-luminance tint so it clears roughly 4.5:1 against its dark button fill — matching the legibility of "Copy link" beside it — and lift the small uppercase section labels and the input placeholder to a brighter gray at the same time.

entries.critique: Resting canvas in light mode at 744×1133. The top color strip renders as one clean row of eleven circular swatches, evenly spaced, all fully drawn with no clipping at either end; the active purple swatch is clearly marked with a ring, and the rainbow "more colors" button at the right end is distinct from the plain swatches. The round trash button sits docked at the right edge below the palette, partially past the viewport as specified. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron is visible in the bottom-left corner and the gear is visible in the bottom-right, each as a thin gray glyph with no backing shape — their faintness is the intended resting styling, and neither is missing or ambiguous in shape. Nothing in the frame is truncated, overlapped, or misaligned; there is no text to fit and no overlay or scrolling region open to evaluate.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique:
The sign-in card renders cleanly: "Admin" heading, subtitle, "SIGN IN" divider label, input and button all fit without clipping, truncation, or overlap. The input placeholder and the purple "Sign in" button are legible and adequately sized for touch, and the brand mark at top right sits clear of the back link. No modal or scrolling region is present to assess.

The one visible weakness is vertical layout: the card occupies only the top third of the 744 × 1133 portrait viewport, leaving roughly 760 px of flat empty background below it. On a tablet in portrait this reads as an unfinished desktop layout dropped into a taller frame rather than a deliberate composition, and it pushes the only interactive controls to the very top of the screen, away from a comfortable thumb position.

Secondary, smaller note: "← Back to drawing" is a plain small text link with no padding-defined hit area visible, making it the least touch-clear element on an otherwise touch-adequate page.
entries.recommendation: Center the sign-in card vertically in the viewport (or cap its container and center it) so the empty space is distributed above and below rather than pooling under the card, and give the "Back to drawing" link enough padding to reach a 44 px tap height.

entries.surface_description: The complete release history at its opening position.
entries.critique:
The changelog opens cleanly at 744×1133. Hierarchy is unambiguous: "Changelog" as the dominant title, a gray subtitle beneath it, then a rule-separated stack of release blocks with "Version 1.5.0" bold at left and its date right-aligned in smaller gray on the same baseline, then emoji-marked "New / Improved / Fixed" subheads over bulleted items. Type sizes step down consistently and the same pattern repeats identically for Version 1.4.0, so the structure is learnable after one block.

Spacing is even and generous — consistent gutters on both sides of the card, consistent gaps between subhead groups, and clearly larger gaps at the release boundaries than within them, so grouping reads correctly. Every line of body text fits within the measure; the one wrapping line ("Every public Splotch release, newest first, with the notes that shipped / alongside it.") wraps at a sensible point with no orphan or overflow. No text collides with the date column, no bullet overruns, no element overlaps another.

Nothing is clipped at the edges. The "← Back to drawing" link and the SPLOTCH dot-cluster wordmark sit comfortably inside the top margin without crowding each other. The "CONTENTS / 7 releases ›" row is a single full-width bordered strip — an ample, unambiguous tap target with a chevron affordance, and its purple label matches the purple back link, so tappable things are visibly a single color family distinct from the black/gray content text.

The bottom of the frame thins out across the last two lines of Version 1.4.0 — this is the app's documented scrolling fade painted over the last rows, marking that the release history continues below, and it is judged as the cue rather than a defect. All content clear of that faded strip is crisp and fully legible.

No actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Hierarchy and spacing read well at 744 wide: the sticky top bar (theme segmented control, "Design system" label, palette dots + SPLOTCH mark) and the CONTENTS bar are distinct from the scrolling body; the page title, lede, callout card, PART 1 eyebrow, and section heads step down cleanly with generous rhythm. Text fits without clipping or overlap, inline code tokens wrap inside their lines, and the two chip tables sit on a balanced two-column grid with legible name/value pairs. Touch targets — Light/Dark segments, "16 sections ›", "← Back to drawing", the source links, and the chips — are all comfortably sized. Nothing is cut off except at the natural fold.

One visible defect: the Color section's intro paragraph fades out mid-sentence. "Every color, grouped by family. Chips paint the live variable — flip the theme in the top bar and the values follow." renders at full strength, then "Tap any chip for its usage rule and both theme values." is progressively washed to near-invisible gray across its two lines. This is body copy sitting in the middle of the page, well clear of any region edge — there is no scroll boundary here for an edge fade to belong to — so the gradient is landing on ordinary prose and erasing an instruction the reader needs (that chips are tappable). Nothing else on the page shows the same treatment.
entries.recommendation: Remove the fade gradient from the Color section's intro paragraph so the full sentence, including "Tap any chip for its usage rule and both theme values," renders at normal body-text contrast; scope the fade overlay strictly to scrollable regions' edges rather than to static prose blocks.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Dark-mode contrast across the page is mostly sound: the app-bg/surface stack is clearly separated, the H1 and section headings ("Splotch design system", "Foundations", "Color") are near-white on near-black, the lead paragraph is comfortably legible, the "← Back to drawing" link and the "PART 1" purple eyebrow both read cleanly, and the color-chip tables carry dark text on light purple and light text on dark surfaces with hex values legible in both rows.

The one weak spot is the "Not sure? Start here" callout. Its heading is white on the purple ground and reads fine, but the body copy is set in a desaturated gray-lavender that sits close in luminance to the purple panel behind it, so the whole paragraph reads noticeably softer than equivalent prose on the page background directly above it. Worse, the inline code tokens inside that paragraph (`--surface`, `--border`, `--radius-lg`, `--space-4`, `--font-size-sm`, `--font-size-md`, `--text`, `--text-strong`, `--font-weight-bold`, `--font-size-xl`, `--duration-base`, `--ease-pop`) are tinted a light violet that is even closer to the panel color; at this size they are the hardest text in the frame to read, and they are exactly the strings a reader must copy accurately. Because the same tokens rendered on the page background elsewhere are legible, this is specific to the purple callout surface in night mode rather than a global type issue.

Secondary, milder: the small "Sources: …" metadata line and the trailing "Tap any chip for its usage rule and both theme values." sentence are both set in a dim gray at a small size on the near-black ground and read faint, though their shapes remain resolvable.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground contrast inside the brand-purple "Not sure? Start here" callout in dark mode — set its body text to the same near-white used for the callout heading, and give the inline code tokens a distinctly lighter/higher-chroma on-brand color (or a subtle darker token background) so they separate clearly from the purple panel.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
The page reads cleanly: clear title, one-paragraph explainer, a two-option segmented control, labeled textarea, disclaimer, primary button, and a "What happens next" callout. Hierarchy is unambiguous (H1 → tabs → field label → CTA), spacing is even, no text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping, nothing runs past the card edge, and the card is fully visible at 744 × 1133 with no scrolling region in play. Color use is consistent (purple for link, CTA, callout accent, and the privacy-policy link).

The one actionable issue is touch-target size on a tablet: the "Include device info" checkbox is drawn as a small square roughly 16–18 px on a side, noticeably smaller than any other interactive element in the frame (the segment tabs and Send report button are both comfortably tall). Its label sits beside it but there is no visible indication the row is one large target, so the apparent hit area is the small square alone — under the ~44 px comfortable finger target for a touch device.

Secondary, lower-confidence note: the two segmented tabs are unequal in visual weight and width treatment — the selected "Something's broken" is a white pill inset within the gray track while "I have an idea" is flush to the track edges, so the unselected option reads as part of the background rather than as a tappable option. It is still legible and locatable, so this is a clarity nit rather than a defect.
entries.recommendation: Enlarge the "Include device info" control's hit area to at least 44 × 44 px on touch — keep the 16 px check box visually but wrap box + label in a single tappable row with vertical padding — and give the unselected segment tab a matching inset pill (transparent fill, same insets as the selected pill) so both options read as equally tappable.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this screen is broadly sound: the H1, body paragraph, section label "What went wrong?", the active "Something's broken" tab, the purple "Send report" button label, and the numbered "What happens next" list on its purple-tinted panel all read cleanly against the dark card. The underlined "privacy policy" link and the "← Back to drawing" link are legible in purple against the panel/card grounds.

Two weak spots are visible. The textarea placeholder ("Describe what happened, and what you expected instead…") is rendered in a dim gray that sits only slightly above the input's own dark fill — noticeably fainter than every other text run in the frame, and the hardest thing here to read at a glance. Related, the "Include device info" checkbox is an unfilled square whose border is nearly the same value as the card behind it; its presence as a tappable control is easy to miss, and the small print beneath it ("Your report goes to our private support tracker…") is also a step dimmer than the surrounding body copy.

The inactive "I have an idea" tab label is lighter-weight and lower-contrast than the active one, but it remains clearly readable on its gray segment — that reads as normal selected/unselected differentiation rather than a defect. No overlay, scrim, scrolling-fade region, corner glyph, or disabled actions-panel button is present in this frame, so none of the given design context applies here.
entries.recommendation: Raise the dark-theme foreground values for the low-contrast form affordances: lighten the textarea placeholder and the small print under the checkbox to at least a mid-light gray meeting 4.5:1 against their backgrounds, and strengthen the unchecked checkbox border so the control is unmistakable against the card.

entries.critique: The privacy policy opens cleanly at 744×1133. Hierarchy is clear and consistent: "Back to drawing" link and Splotch wordmark on one header row, an H1 "Privacy policy" with a two-line intro, then two uppercase rule-flanked section labels ("THE SHORT VERSION" with a right-aligned "Last updated August 20, 2026", and "THE DETAILS"). entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this page is largely healthy: the "Privacy policy" heading, the intro paragraph, the bold lead-ins in the short-version card ("No ads.", "No tracking.", …), the "What stays on your device" subheading and its body paragraphs all render as light gray on the near-black page and read cleanly at this size. The purple "← Back to drawing" link and the "8 sections ›" affordance are distinguishable from surrounding text by both hue and weight. Card and divider borders are faint, but that reads as decoration rather than a legibility problem.

The one weak spot is the small dim-gray metadata and section-label tier. "Last updated August 20, 2026" is set at the smallest size in the frame in a muted gray that sits noticeably closer to the background than any other text on the page; the uppercase eyebrows "THE SHORT VERSION", "THE DETAILS" and "CONTENTS" use that same muted gray, though caps and letter-spacing give them slightly more presence. These stay readable but are the first things to fall away, and the date is functional information a parent may want to check. The secondary text after the bold lead-ins in the short-version card ("Ever. None.", "We don't follow you around the internet.") is a step down in brightness from the body copy but remains comfortably legible.

No overlay, scrim, scrolling fade, or actions-panel state appears in this frame, so none of the settled-design exclusions apply here.
entries.recommendation: Raise the muted-gray text token used for "Last updated August 20, 2026" and the uppercase eyebrow labels to a lighter dark-mode foreground (around the brightness of the short-version secondary text or above) so this smallest type clears 4.5:1 against the near-black page.

entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this Android beta tab is broadly sound. The page sits on a near-black ground with the H1 "Join the Splotch beta" in near-white, and the intro paragraph plus all three step bodies in a light gray that stays clearly legible at this size; the bold inline emphasis ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester") reads as distinctly brighter than the surrounding copy, so emphasis survives the dark theme. Step headings ("Join the testers group", "Opt in on Google Play", "Install Splotch") are near-white and the strongest text after the H1. The three purple CTA buttons carry white labels on a mid-purple fill that stays readable, and the active "Android" tab is distinguished from the inactive "iPhone / iPad" tab by both a brighter label and a purple underline rather than color alone. The "← Back to drawing" link and the "SPLOTCH BETA" wordmark are legible. The bottom callout ("PLEASE STAY FOR 14 DAYS") sits inside the scroll fade and is judged as the fade cue being drawn, not a defect.

The one weak point is the numerals inside the step markers. Each 1/2/3 disc is a very dark circle only marginally lighter than the page ground, and the digit inside is a dim gray-purple noticeably fainter than every other piece of text in its row — fainter even than the body copy it labels, despite being wayfinding for a sequential instruction list. At a glance the discs read as empty dots and the order has to be inferred from position rather than read. The connecting rail between them is likewise a hairline barely separable from the background, so the "these are ordered steps" structure rests almost entirely on faint marks. These are primary content markers on a task page, not the deliberately recessed parent-facing controls, so the low contrast is not covered by the settled styling.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-marker numerals to at least the brightness of the step body text, and lift the disc fill a step off the page ground, so 1/2/3 are readable at a glance in night mode.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
The iOS tab of the beta page renders cleanly at 744 × 1133 in light mode. Hierarchy is clear and correctly ordered: page title "Join the Splotch beta", a supporting paragraph, the Android / iPhone-iPad tab pair with the active iOS tab marked by both purple text and an underline, a small-caps eyebrow rule ("HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD"), then numbered steps whose bold headings, body copy, and purple action buttons form a consistent repeating unit. Vertical rhythm between steps is even, and the connecting vertical rule tying the numbered badges together reads as an intentional stepper spine.

Text fit is good: all three step paragraphs wrap within the content column with no overflow, no mid-word breaks, and no orphaned single-word lines. Button labels ("Get TestFlight from Apple", "Open the Splotch invitation", "Open Splotch in TestFlight") sit fully inside their pills with balanced padding, and each pill is sized well above a comfortable tap target with clear separation from neighboring text and from the next step. Nothing overlaps: the step badges clear the vertical spine and the headings, the tab underline clears the divider beneath it, and the header row ("← Back to drawing" left, dot-cluster wordmark right) has ample gap between its two ends. The card's rounded container has consistent inset margins on the left and right, and no element collides with or spills past those edges.

Step 4's badge is visible at the very bottom edge of the frame, which is ordinary page scroll at this viewport height rather than clipping — the badge is the start of the next section and the region continues below the fold. No text is truncated, no ellipsis appears, and no control is cut. Color usage is consistent — one purple for the active tab, links, and primary buttons; neutral gray for body copy at readable weight and size. I found no actionable visible issue in this frame.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this iOS tab is generally solid: the "Join the Splotch beta" heading and body copy render near-white on the near-black page, step headings ("Install TestFlight", "Accept the invitation", "Install Splotch") are bright and crisp, and the active "iPhone / iPad" tab is clearly distinguished from the dimmer "Android" tab by both a lighter label and the purple underline. The section eyebrow "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" is set in muted gray small caps but stays readable, and the inline bold "Install" inside step 3 is legible against the body text.

The one weak spot is the numbered step markers. Each digit (1, 2, 3, and the partly visible 4) sits inside a small dark disc whose fill is only slightly lighter than the page background, and the numeral itself is a small, dim purple-gray that reads considerably fainter than everything else in the step row — noticeably harder to resolve than the adjoining step title or body text at this size. These are not the deliberately-subdued parent-facing canvas controls; they are content-level ordinal markers in an instructional sequence, where the numbering is the thing carrying the "do these in order" meaning, so their faintness is an actionable legibility issue rather than intended de-emphasis.

The vertical connector rule linking the steps is also very dim, but as a purely decorative spine that is acceptable; the numerals are the part that needs to be read.

Purple CTA buttons ("Get TestFlight from Apple", "Open the Splotch invitation", "Open Splotch in TestFlight") carry white bold labels on a mid-purple fill that holds up at this weight and size, though they are the second-thinnest margin in the frame.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-marker numerals' contrast in dark mode — brighten the digit to a near-white or light-lavender tone and/or lighten the disc fill so the numbers read at roughly the strength of their step titles rather than fading into the background.
