entries.surface_description: The shared SvelteKit error boundary rendered for an unknown route.
entries.critique:
The error screen is a clean, well-formed centered stack: purple blob mark, "Oops!" heading, one-line explanatory sentence, and a single filled "Start over" pill. Hierarchy is unambiguous — the heading dominates, the body copy sits at a clear secondary weight, and the only interactive element is the highest-saturation object in the frame. Nothing is clipped, overlapped, or truncated; there are no scrolling regions, overlays, or corner controls in this state to assess. The button is a comfortably sized pill (roughly 152 × 54 px) with generous internal padding and clear label contrast against the purple fill, so touch-target clarity is fine on this device. Spacing between blob, heading, subtitle, and button is even and reads as an intentional rhythm.

The one visible weakness is the copy's measure. On a 744 px-wide viewport the sentence "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." is constrained to roughly 310 px, forcing a two-line wrap that strands the single word "drawing." alone on the second line. There is ample horizontal room; the orphan is a small typographic blemish on an otherwise tidy screen rather than a legibility or fit failure.

Secondary observation, not scored: the whole group sits centered on the full viewport height, which on this tall portrait frame leaves very large empty margins above and below. That reads as deliberate for a minimal error state and is not an issue on its own.
entries.recommendation: Widen the subtitle's max-width (or apply text-balance) so "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." sets on one line, or breaks at the sentence boundary rather than orphaning the final word.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog renders cleanly on the iPad mini portrait frame. Hierarchy reads correctly: card title, a left category rail with the active "Appearance" row marked by a tinted pill plus a left accent bar, and a right detail pane with "Appearance" and "Sound" section headings above grouped cards. Spacing is even between rows, groups, and the card's inner padding, and the two-column split leaves the rail and detail pane clearly separated by a hairline rule.

Text fit is good throughout — "Lock device rotation", "WHAT MAKES SOUND", and every rail label sit on one line with headroom, no truncation, ellipsis, or wrapping. No overlap or clipping inside the card; the close ✕ sits fully inside the top-right corner with clear margin from the "Settings" title. Touch targets are unambiguous: the ✕ has a visible circular outline, the Light/Dark/System segmented control shows the selected segment as a raised white chip, toggles are full-size pill switches, and the volume slider has a filled track with a "50%" readout.

The Deleting row thinning out at the bottom edge of the detail pane is the documented scroll fade being painted over the last row, so it is the scroll cue rather than a legibility fault, and everything clear of that strip is fully legible. The dimmed, blurred canvas and top color palette behind the card are the dialog scrim, and the trash button sitting past the right edge is the documented docked state. The corner chevron (bottom left) and settings gear (bottom right) are both locatable as thin gray glyphs, meeting the findability floor. No Portrait/Landscape orientation segments are present in this tablet view, so nothing to assess there.

No actionable visible issue.

entries.recommendation: Normalize the space above the "Coloring" section heading to the same section-break value used elsewhere in the pane (e.g. the spacing above "DRAWING TOOLS"), so the gap after the orphaned "Undo" chip no longer reads as an accidental empty band.

It is the only actionable control in that row and sits flush against the row's right padding, so the tappable area is thin relative to everything else in the pane.

entries.recommendation: Increase the "Choose folder" button's height to at least ~44 px (add vertical padding) so it matches the tap-target weight of the toggles in the same card group.

entries.critique:
The Settings card itself is in good shape: "Install" and "Feedback" headings, the numbered iOS steps, and the sidebar list all fit without clipping or overlap; the chevrons, the close button, and the two feedback segments read as clearly tappable; the sidebar's active "Install" row is unambiguous with its accent bar and tint. Both the sidebar and the content pane end in the documented soft fade (About row, and the description textarea), and the content clear of those strips is fully legible. The parent-facing chevron and gear glyphs in the bottom corners are locatable.

The one visible problem is the scrim's coverage. The canvas behind the dialog is clearly darkened and blurred, but the color-palette strip along the top edge is not — its white background stays pure white against the grayed page, and the ten swatches plus the multicolor button keep full saturation. The docked round trash button at the top right is likewise still at full red/white brightness. The result is that the brightest, most saturated region in the whole frame sits above the dialog rather than in it, and the eye lands on the palette row before it reaches the "Settings" title. This is a coverage gap, not the intended styling of those elements: the stated behavior is that a dialog scrim darkens the canvas, the top palette, and the corner buttons together so the open card holds attention, and here the top strip and trash button are excluded while the rest of the page is not — visible in the same image as the boundary where the dim page meets the undimmed strip.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim's stacking so it also covers the top color-palette strip and the docked trash button — raise the scrim above those layers (or lower them beneath it) so the entire page behind the Settings card is darkened and blurred uniformly, leaving the card as the brightest element in the frame.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open Settings card is generally strong: "Settings", "Install", "Feedback", the nav item labels, and the two row titles ("Install as App", "Enable Guided Access") all render as near-white on the dark card and read cleanly. The selected "Install" nav row's purple fill with white label and left accent bar is clearly distinguishable from unselected rows. The close ✕ in its circular button is legible.

The weak points are the small supporting text. The all-caps eyebrow labels "IOS" and "SEND FEEDBACK" are a mid-gray at ~11px, and the "IOS" label in particular sits directly on the card background at a noticeably dimmer level than everything around it — at a glance it reads as a smudge rather than a section label. The "›" disclosure chevrons at the right edge of both install rows are similarly faint against the row fill, weaker than any other affordance marker on the card. The Feedback body paragraph ("Found a bug or have an idea?…") is a soft gray that is readable but sits low relative to the headings above it.

The inactive segment "I have an idea" is dimmer than the active "Something's broken" pill, which is the expected active/inactive treatment rather than a contrast fault. The textarea placeholder thins out toward the bottom of the card, which is the scroll fade being painted and is not judged. Background canvas, palette, and the two corner glyphs sit under the dialog scrim; the corner chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable in the image, so no findability issue there.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance of the small caps eyebrow labels ("IOS", "SEND FEEDBACK") and the row "›" chevrons in dark mode — they are the dimmest text and glyphs on the card at the smallest sizes; bring them up toward the secondary-text level used for the Feedback body copy so they clear a comfortable small-text contrast margin against the card and row fills.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the open Settings card is broadly sound: "Settings", "Feedback", the SEND FEEDBACK label, body copy, the sidebar item labels, and the "What went wrong?" field label all read as near-white or light lavender on the dark card and are comfortably legible. entries.critique:
The left nav shows "About" as the selected item (purple bar, filled pill), but the content pane is not scrolled to About. The top ~55% of the pane is occupied by another section's content — a release-notes card with bulleted items ("Faster Settings navigation on every screen.", a "Fixed" subhead, "Settings stays open when choosing a feedback type.") and a "See all releases →" link, which belongs to the "What's New" nav item directly above About. The actual "About" heading does not appear until roughly y=600 of a 1133-tall screen, so on first look the selected section's own content (logo, tagline, Privacy Policy, View on GitHub, version string) fills only the lower third of the card. The mismatch between the highlighted nav item and the content at the top of the pane is a concrete navigation/hierarchy fault, not a styling choice.

Secondary, smaller observation on the same pane: the release-notes card is hard-cut at the pane's top edge mid-sentence ("background.") with no fade or other softening at that boundary, so it reads as truncated content rather than as a scrolled region continuing upward.

Everything else in frame is sound: the nav rows have generous, even spacing with comfortable icon/label alignment and touch-sized pill rows; the close (×) button is a clear, well-contrasted circular target in the card's top-right; text fits without clipping, wrapping, or overlap; the About block's centered logo, tagline, divider, links, and monospace version line are cleanly ordered; the darkened, blurred palette and canvas behind the card are the expected dialog scrim, and the corner chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable.
entries.recommendation: When a nav item is selected in the Settings dialog, scroll the content pane so that section's heading ("About") sits at the top of the pane rather than leaving the previous section's release-notes card filling the upper half.

entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The expanded actions drawer reads as a clean vertical stack of six round buttons docked to the left edge, with the collapse chevron above it (faint but clearly locatable as a chevron shape at ~x36, y702) and the settings gear findable in the opposite bottom corner. The color palette across the top is at full brightness with no scrim, consistent with a non-modal state; the undo, AI and screenshot buttons sit at their usual contrast, matching the single purple stroke on the canvas being enough to enable them. Spacing between the drawer buttons is even, icons are centered, nothing overlaps the artwork or the trash button, and there is no text to fit or clip.

The one visible problem is at the bottom of the stack: the last button (the brush/pen glyph) runs right up against the bottom edge of the 1133px viewport with only a couple of pixels of clearance, and its lower arc appears to meet the frame boundary. Every other button in the column has a consistent gap below it, so this last one breaks the rhythm and leaves no bottom padding or safe-area inset. On a device where the bottom edge is a gesture/home-indicator zone, a control flush against it is both harder to tap cleanly and visually reads as the panel being truncated rather than deliberately docked — the docking exemption stated for the trash button does not cover this column, which is otherwise fully inset. The settings gear in the opposite corner sits noticeably higher (~y1100 center) than this bottom button, so the two corners are not on a shared baseline either.
entries.recommendation: Add a bottom inset to the actions drawer column (safe-area-inset-bottom plus roughly the same gap used between the buttons, ~12–16px) so the last button clears the viewport edge like the rest of the stack, and align its center with the settings gear in the opposite corner.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
The brush flyout renders cleanly: four tool icons (pen, crayon, paintbrush, eraser) in a single white rounded card at the bottom-left, no scrim over the page, canvas and top color palette at full brightness. Hierarchy is correct — the selected pen carries a purple-tinted rounded highlight with a visible border, so current tool is unambiguous. Icons are evenly spaced with consistent gutters, nothing is clipped, nothing overlaps: the card's left edge clears the docked round brush button beside it, and its bottom edge clears the viewport with a small margin. No text is present, so there is no fit or truncation risk. The chevron above the Actions Panel and the gear in the bottom-right are both locatable as thin gray glyphs. The dimmed undo/AI/camera buttons read as the disabled state on an empty canvas. There is no scrolling region in this overlay.

The one soft spot is touch-target clarity for the unselected tools. Only the active pen has a drawn container; crayon, paintbrush, and eraser float as bare glyphs on the card with no disc, outline, or fill, so their tappable extent is inferred purely from icon size. The glyphs themselves are roughly 34–40px of visual mass inside a card that is only ~62px tall, which sits at or under the comfortable target floor for a child's finger, and the absence of any hit-area affordance makes near-miss taps between icons feel unresponsive rather than merely off-target. The similarity between the crayon and paintbrush glyphs at this size compounds it slightly, though both remain distinguishable.
entries.recommendation: Give each unselected tool in the flyout the same rounded container footprint as the selected pen — drawn at very low contrast or fully transparent, but sized to a ≥44pt tap region — so every icon's hit area is both visible and consistently sized, and grow the card's vertical padding enough to accommodate it.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique:
The stroke-width flyout itself is in good shape. It sits as a white rounded card anchored beside the stroke-width button in the lower left, at full page brightness with no scrim, and holds five diagonal brush previews in a single row. The width progression is legible and monotonic — hairline, thin, medium, thick, thickest — and all five render in the active purple so the previews read as live samples of the current color rather than generic icons. The selected third option is marked with a purple rounded-square outline plus a light lilac fill, which is unambiguous against the four unmarked siblings and does not crowd them. Padding inside the card is even on all four sides, the inter-swatch gaps are consistent, each preview occupies roughly a 60 px cell at 744 px width, and nothing is clipped, overlapped, or truncated. There is no text in the card, so no fit or wrapping risk. The row is fully visible end to end with no fade strip, so nothing is scrolling out of view. The card clears the settings glyph at the bottom right and does not collide with the button column it belongs to. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron sits above the button column at roughly y=702 and the settings gear at the bottom right, each thin and gray as intended. The color palette along the top and the docked trash at the right edge are undisturbed.

The one thing worth raising is outside the card but adjacent to it. The six round buttons in the left column — undo, AI, camera, coloring book, stroke width, brush — are each cut roughly in half by the left viewport edge, and the icon glyphs inside them are trimmed with them: the undo arrow, the camera body, and the wand all lose part of their left side rather than being centered in a visible half-disc. The trash button on the right is documented as deliberately docked past its edge, and this column mirrors that treatment closely enough that the docking is plainly intentional; the cost is that the glyph artwork was not re-centered for the docked state, so the icons themselves lose identifying detail rather than just the disc losing area. The undo arrow in particular reads as a partial shape. That is a small polish gap in an otherwise clean screen, not a fault in the stroke-width menu.
entries.recommendation: Nudge the icon glyphs inside the docked left-column buttons toward the visible half of each disc so the full arrow, camera, and wand shapes stay readable while the button keeps its off-edge docked position.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique: In the stroke-width flyout, preview brightness tracks stroke thickness: the two thickest chips render bright lavender and the selected middle chip is clear, but the thinnest and second-thinnest previews are drawn in a dark desaturated purple only marginally lighter than the near-black chip fill. At hairline widths that luminance gap is too small to resolve reliably in night mode, so the thinnest chip reads close to empty and the first two options are hard to tell apart — and the stroke preview is the only label these controls carry. This flyout casts no scrim, so the dimness is the chips' own styling. Elsewhere the frame is sound: top-bar color swatches are saturated and mutually distinguishable against the dark bar, both the selected color and selected width carry a visible purple selection ring, and the trash glyph reads clearly on its red disc. entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
The color-picker dialog itself reads well: the white card sits clearly above a darkened, blurred canvas, the honeycomb grid is evenly gapped, every hexagon is fully drawn with no clipping at the card edges, the selected/white swatch is distinguished by an outline, and the grid fits the card without needing to scroll (no fade strip is present, consistent with all rows being visible). Hex targets are large and unambiguous for touch. The chevron at bottom-left and the settings gear at bottom-right are both locatable.

The one visible problem is that the scrim is incomplete. The top color-palette bar spanning the full width of the screen, and the round red trash button docked at the right edge below it, are rendered at full brightness and full saturation — no darkening, no blur — while the rest of the page behind the card is clearly dimmed. Ten saturated swatches plus a black disc and a bright multicolor icon along the top edge are the highest-contrast elements in the frame, competing directly with the open card for attention, and the red trash button is the single most eye-catching object outside it. The dialog also has no visible close button, so those undimmed top-bar controls read as still-live affordances rather than as suppressed background, which is ambiguous about what is tappable while the picker is open.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full viewport so the top color-palette bar and the docked trash button are darkened and blurred with the rest of the page, rather than leaving them at full brightness above the scrim.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: Judging the open color-picker card (the page behind it is scrim-darkened, and both corner glyphs are findable, so neither is a finding). The hex grid is broadly legible in dark mode: light-to-mid swatches across the red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink and gray rows all separate cleanly from the card's dark panel and from each other. The weakness is confined to the darkest end of the palette. The bottom-right hexagon is rendered as an unfilled outline whose thin gray stroke is only marginally lighter than the card background, so the swatch reads as an empty hole rather than a distinct, selectable option. The same problem affects its neighbors: the near-black maroon and dark brown at the right end of the pink and brown rows, the deep navy at the right end of the blue row, and the dark slate tones at the right end of the bottom row all sit close enough to the panel fill that their hexagon edges lose definition and the cells merge into a single dark mass. Individual tap targets there are hard to distinguish, and a user cannot easily tell one dark swatch from the next or judge what color they are selecting. This is a genuine dark-mode-specific problem — against a light card these same swatches would be well separated.
entries.recommendation: In dark mode, give every swatch hexagon a consistent light stroke (e.g. a ~1px border at roughly 25-35% white) so cell boundaries stay visible, and raise the outline weight/lightness on the unfilled bottom-right hexagon specifically so it reads as a deliberate swatch rather than a gap in the grid.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The dialog's scrim does not cover the full page. From roughly y≈75 downward the canvas, the left tool column, the chevron and the settings glyph are all clearly darkened and blurred behind the card. But the color palette strip along the top edge (all ten swatches plus the multicolor button) and the red trash button at the upper right are rendered at full saturation and full brightness, with a crisp white background behind the swatches — they sit outside the darkened region entirely. The result is that the two highest-chroma elements in the frame (the vivid purple/red/black swatch row and the saturated red trash disc) are the brightest things on screen while a modal is open, pulling attention off the "Coloring Books" card and reading as still-live controls. The trash button also abuts the card's right edge at full strength, so it competes directly with the close button a short distance below it.

Everything else in the card holds up. The title, the close affordance, the eight cover thumbnails and their labels are all legible, evenly spaced in a clean 2-column grid with consistent card sizes and gutters, no clipping, no truncated labels, no overlap, and touch targets that are comfortably large. The grid ends cleanly above the card's bottom padding with no fade strip, so nothing is cut off.

One smaller consistency note: the header "Coloring Books" and the close button sit at a card padding of roughly 28–68px, while the thumbnail grid is inset much further (starting ~132px from the card edge). The grid is symmetric within the card, but it does not align to the header's left edge, so the title reads as hanging outside the content block rather than heading it.
entries.recommendation: Extend the modal scrim over the full viewport so the top color-palette strip and the red trash button are darkened and blurred along with the rest of the page, matching the treatment already applied to the canvas and corner controls; secondarily, reduce the grid's horizontal inset so the left edge of the first column aligns with the "Coloring Books" title.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this card reads clean. The "Coloring Books" heading is near-white on the dark card surface and unambiguous. The eight cover tiles sit on a slightly lighter panel than the card, so each tile boundary is visible, and the white line-art inside each cover renders as light strokes on a dark tile with clear separation — barn, dinosaurs, unicorn, flowers, teddy bear, shapes, rocket and vehicles are each identifiable at a glance despite thin stroke weight. All eight labels (Farm, Dinosaurs, Creatures, Nature, Objects, Shapes, Space, Vehicles) are light text on dark and read cleanly. The round close button at the card's top-right has a visible disc and a light ✕ that is easy to find. The bottom row (Space, Vehicles) thins toward the card's lower edge; that is the scroll-fade cue being drawn, and the content clear of the faded strip is fully legible. Elements drawn on top of the scrim hold up: the color palette strip along the top edge keeps its swatches distinguishable from one another and from the background, and the red trash disc at the right stays clearly separated from what is behind it. The page behind is dimmed and blurred, which is the dialog scrim. The quiet parent-facing glyphs still meet the findability floor — the gear shape is locatable in the bottom-right corner and the crayon glyph in the bottom-left. No actionable night-mode contrast or legibility defect is visible.

entries.critique: With the "Farm" coloring-page grid dialog open, the scrim darkens and blurs most of the page behind it but leaves three regions at full brightness: the entire top color-palette strip (all ten swatches plus the multicolor button, still on a white ground), the red trash button at top-right, and the bottom-left column of round tool buttons (photo/screenshot, stroke-width, brush) plus the bottom-right settings gear. The result is that the open card competes for attention with a full-contrast palette bar, and the most saturated element in the frame is the red trash button, which is not the intended target while a dialog is open. The card itself is clean: title, back chevron, and close button are well spaced and legible; the 2x3 thumbnail grid has even gutters, consistent card sizing, no clipping or overlap, and generous touch targets; no fade at the card's bottom edge, so the grid reads as complete.
entries.recommendation: Raise the dialog scrim above the top color-palette strip, the trash button, and the bottom-corner controls so the entire page behind the card is uniformly darkened, and put all actions-panel buttons on one z-level so they cannot split across the scrim.

entries.critique:
Frame shows the color palette across the top, the docked round trash button at the upper right, the chevron at bottom left and the settings gear at bottom right (both locatable), and an otherwise empty canvas with the clear-gesture coachmark drawn over it.

Judged as drawn, the coachmark has one legibility weakness: the small pink trash puck and the hand glyph are composited so the hand sits directly on top of the puck's lower-right quadrant, cutting into the trash-can silhouette's base and right rim. At this size the two marks merge into a single ambiguous blob rather than reading as "hand" plus "trash," and both sit on a near-white textured canvas where the hand's thin dark outline is the only thing carrying it. The large pink arc is a thin, light-pink hairline on off-white; it survives mainly by its size, and where it crosses the lighter upper-right region it is near the faintest legible line weight.

Everything else in frame reads normally: palette swatches are evenly spaced and unclipped, the selected purple swatch has a clear ring, the multicolor picker at the right end is distinct, and no text is present to fit or clip. The chevron and gear are faint but their shapes are findable. No modal or scrim is open, so there is no card contrast to assess.
entries.recommendation: Separate the two coachmark marks so each stays readable: offset the hand glyph so it meets the edge of the trash puck instead of overlapping its silhouette, and give the hand a subtle white halo or slight size bump so it does not merge with the puck against the near-white canvas.

entries.critique:

The trash body's white strokes are thin enough at this scale that on the textured dark canvas the icon's identity is soft. entries.recommendation: Enlarge the coachmark mark and separate its two glyphs — give the hand cursor a dark outline or offset it clear of the trash disc so both shapes stay distinct — and raise the luminance of the pink guide arc so it holds contrast against the dark canvas along its full length.

entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique:
Visible in the frame: the top color palette row (ten swatches plus a multicolor picker, evenly spaced, purple selected with a clear ring), a large mostly-empty light canvas with a faint lavender horizontal stroke near mid-page, the red trash button at roughly (497, 346) with a red glow, a large red circular arc sweeping from the top edge down and off the right edge, a thin gray chevron in the bottom-left corner, and a thin gray settings gear in the bottom-right corner. Both corner glyphs are locatable, so the quiet parent-control styling is met. No text is present anywhere in the frame, so there is no text-fit or truncation issue; spacing in the palette row is even and each swatch is a comfortably large tap target; no overlap or unintended clipping of the palette; no modal or scroll region is open.

The one thing that does not read as intended: the accept ring is drawn as an arc whose center sits well off the right edge of the screen, while the trash button it belongs to sits far inside the canvas at x≈497. Only a partial sweep of the ring is on screen, and it passes through empty canvas rather than around the button — the arc's nearest point is roughly 60–70 px to the button's right and the ring never encloses it. Read cold, the red curve looks like a stray graphic bisecting the canvas rather than a progress or accept ring tied to the held trash button, so the threshold state loses its "held past threshold on this control" meaning. The pale red wash also fills the region on the far side of the arc rather than radiating from the button, reinforcing that the ring and the button are two separate marks. Everything else in the frame is consistent and clean.
entries.recommendation: Anchor the accept ring's center on the trash button's current dragged position so the ring encircles the button (and stays fully on screen at that position) rather than being centered on the docked edge origin while the button has moved inward.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The install banner is legible and correctly positioned: it floats above the bottom edge, clear of the chevron at bottom-left and the settings glyph at bottom-right (both findable), and nothing is clipped or overlapped. Hierarchy reads correctly — bold "Add Splotch to your home screen" title, lighter secondary line, a filled purple "How?" primary action, and a distinct ✕ dismiss. Both buttons look comfortably tappable and are visually separated from each other.

The one actionable issue is text fit inside the card. The text column is squeezed to roughly a quarter of the banner's width, so the title breaks across two lines and the subtitle breaks as "Opens full-screen, just like a real / app", leaving a single-word orphan on its own line. On a 744 pt-wide portrait iPad there is ample horizontal room — the card is already ~410 pt wide with generous padding around the icon and buttons — so this wrapping is a layout allocation problem, not a space constraint. The result is a four-line block of ragged text where one or two clean lines would fit, which makes the banner taller and busier than it needs to be. Vertical rhythm inside the card is also slightly off as a consequence: the two-line subtitle pushes the text block taller than the icon and buttons, so the icon reads high-left rather than centered against the copy.

No clipping, no overlap, no scrolling region, no scrim in this frame.
entries.recommendation: Let the banner's text column take the available width (reduce the fixed/implicit max-width on the title+subtitle block, or drop the icon/button gutters) so the title fits on one line and the subtitle does not leave "app" orphaned on a line by itself; vertically center the icon against the resulting text block.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
On the install banner card itself, the heading "Add Splotch to your home screen" is bright white on the near-black card and reads cleanly. Two other elements on the same card do not hold up in night mode:

1. The supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" is a mid-gray at a noticeably smaller size than the heading. Its strokes thin out and sit close to the card fill, making it the least legible text in the frame — and it is the line doing the explanatory work. It reads markedly dimmer than the "How?" label beside it, which is at similar scale but far brighter.

2. The "×" dismiss glyph at the right end of the card is a thin gray cross with no fill or outline. Unlike the corner chevron and settings glyph, this is a control on an opaque card competing directly with a bright "How?" affordance next to it, so the card presents one obvious action and one nearly invisible one. Its shape is locatable, so this is not a findability failure, but its weight is well below what a dismiss control on a persistent prompt needs against this dark card.

The "How?" pill's light purple label is legible. Elsewhere in the frame — the top palette row, the docked trash button, the canvas strokes, and the bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs (both locatable) — shows no night-mode contrast problem.
entries.recommendation: Lift the banner card's two secondary elements in dark mode: raise "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" to a light-gray/near-white at roughly 4.5:1 against the card fill and bump it a size step so its thin strokes survive, and strengthen the "×" glyph with a lighter stroke color or a subtle circular hit-surface so it reads as an offered action alongside "How?".

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
The expanded install banner is legible and correctly positioned: title, subtitle, "How?" button and a close × are all present, the instruction paragraph is fully visible with its inline Share and add-to-home-screen glyphs, and nothing is clipped or overlapped. The chevron (bottom-left) and settings glyph (bottom-right) are both locatable, and the docked trash button at top-right is as intended.

The one actionable issue is text fit in the banner header. The title/subtitle column is squeezed by the "How?" button and close ×, so on this 744-wide portrait viewport the title breaks into two lines ("Add Splotch to your / home screen") and the subtitle wraps to three lines with a single-word orphan ("app") on the last. The header block ends up noticeably taller than the button beside it, with the subtitle's last line sitting close to the instruction paragraph and reading cramped rather than as a deliberate two-tier hierarchy. The instruction paragraph below shows the same raggedness in smaller degree — its final line is the orphan "first." — and its bottom edge sits tighter to the card boundary than the left inset, so the card's padding reads asymmetrical.

There is ample horizontal room: the card occupies only about half the screen width, so the wrapping is a card-width/column-allocation choice rather than a viewport constraint. It is the only place in the frame where spacing and hierarchy visibly degrade; touch targets ("How?", ×) are clearly sized and separated.
entries.recommendation: Widen the install banner card (or give the title/subtitle column more width relative to the "How?" button) on tablet-width portrait viewports so the title fits on one line and the subtitle wraps to at most two, and equalize the card's bottom padding with its side insets so the final instruction line isn't tighter to the edge than the text is to the sides.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
In the expanded install banner the primary layer holds up in night mode: the "Add Splotch to your home screen" title is near-white bold on the dark card and reads instantly, the "How?" pill is a solid light-lavender fill with dark text and is the clearest control in the card, and the instruction sentence ("Tap [share] Share at the bottom of the screen, then choose "Add to Home Screen". If you don't see it, tap [chevron] "View More" first.") sits at a light gray that stays legible at this size, with the quoted phrases bolded so the two things to look for stand out. The inline share and add-to-home glyphs are rendered brightly enough to be identified as icons rather than smudges.

The weak element is the supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" directly under the title. It is set several steps smaller than the instruction sentence and in a dimmer gray than that sentence, so it is the one piece of banner copy that goes soft against the dark card and reads as filler rather than information — noticeably harder to pick out than text of similar function elsewhere in the card. The close "×" at the top right is also a thin mid-gray glyph, dimmer than the "How?" button beside it, but its shape is unambiguous and it sits in the expected corner, so it clears the findability floor.

Nothing else in the frame is a contrast fault: the chevron at bottom left and the settings gear at bottom right are locatable as shapes, the trash button is fully saturated, and the palette across the top edge is at full brightness.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" subtitle in the install banner to at least the size and gray value used for the instruction sentence below it, so it clears roughly 4.5:1 against the card's dark fill instead of sitting a step below the rest of the banner copy.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
The gate card itself is clean: logo, "Grown-Ups Only" title, subtitle, the 3 × 6 = with two dashed answer slots, a 1–9/0/backspace keypad, and a divider above the "Manage these checks in Settings › Parent Center" footer. Hierarchy reads top-down correctly, all text fits on one line with no clipping or overlap, keypad keys are large and evenly gapped with clear hit areas, the close X sits in its own outlined disc clear of the logo, and nothing in the card is cut off or scrolled.

The visible problem is the scrim's coverage. The page behind is darkened and blurred — the canvas, the left-column round buttons, the chevron and the bottom-right settings glyph all sit under it — but the color palette strip along the top edge and the round red trash button at the top right are plainly *not* darkened: the ten swatches are at full saturation and the trash disc is bright red with a crisp white icon, brighter than anything on the page except the card itself. Sitting undimmed while everything else recedes, the trash reads as still live and competes with the gate for attention at the moment the user is being asked to stop and authenticate — and it is the destructive control. The palette strip likewise still reads as an active toolbar above a modal.

Secondary and minor: the last keypad row leaves an empty third cell to the right of the backspace key, so the 3-column grid ends visibly ragged rather than balanced.
entries.recommendation: Raise the parent-gate scrim above the top color-palette strip and the trash button so they are darkened and blurred with the rest of the page, matching the scrim coverage the other dialogs get.

entries.critique:
On the parent-gate card the primary content holds up in night mode: "Grown-Ups Only" is near-white on the dark card, the ten keypad digits and the backspace glyph are white on mid-dark gray tiles with clear separation, and the two operand chips (white "3" on purple, white "9" on blue) are legible. The scrimmed page behind — palette, trash button, actions panel, corner glyphs — is out of scope, and the corner chevron and settings gear are both locatable.

Two elements on the card itself sit noticeably weaker than everything around them. The pair of dashed answer circles to the right of "=" are drawn in a gray only marginally lighter than the card fill; against the darkened surface they nearly vanish, and they are the one target the parent must find to know where the answer lands. The "×" and "=" operators are similarly thin and dim, so the equation reads as two colored chips with faint marks between them rather than a stated problem. The footer block is also on the weak side — "Manage these checks in" is a small dim gray line — though "Settings › Parent Center" beneath it is brighter and carries the meaning, so the footer is a lesser concern than the answer slots.
entries.recommendation: Raise the answer-slot dashed outlines and the ×/= operator glyphs to a clearly brighter gray against the card fill (at least the weight of the "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle), so the empty answer targets and the equation structure are unambiguous in night mode.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The "Pick a style" dialog itself is well-formed: the card is centered, its 4×2 grid of style thumbnails is evenly gutter-spaced, all eight labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) fit on one line under their tiles with no truncation or wrapping, the tiles are large touch targets, nothing overlaps or clips, and the whole grid fits inside the card with no scrolling region in play. The close button is a clear filled circular target at the card's top-right. The dimmed, blurred canvas, palette strip, and corner buttons behind are the dialog scrim; the docked trash button, the faint chevron above the actions panel, and the faint settings glyph at bottom-right are all locatable in the frame.

The one actionable issue is inside the open card: the eight style names are rendered in a light gray that sits close to the white card background, noticeably weaker than the thumbnails above them. These labels are the sole text that identifies each option — the thumbnails are near-identical mountain scenes, so distinguishing "Felt" from "Clay" or "Paper" requires reading them. At this weight and tone they are the least legible element on an otherwise high-contrast card, which also reads as a hierarchy inversion: the label carrying the meaning is quieter than the picture that cannot convey it alone. The "Pick a style" heading is similarly light for a dialog title.
entries.recommendation: Darken the eight style-name labels (and the "Pick a style" heading) to a near-body-text gray so they meet normal text contrast on the white card, since the labels — not the near-identical thumbnails — are what actually distinguish the options.

The heading and all eight style labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) are near-white on the dark card surface and read cleanly at this size. entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: The AI-result loading dialog itself is well formed: card centered, progress dial large and unambiguous, and the "Making your picture…" heading, "This takes about 30 seconds" subline, and "Keep drawing while you wait" pill stack in a clean descending hierarchy with even spacing. No clipped, wrapped, or overlapping text; the pill is a comfortably large touch target; the close button reads clearly at the card's top-right corner; the blurred preview panel behind the dial is legible as a placeholder. Both the bottom-left collapse chevron and the bottom-right settings gear are locatable. The actionable problem is that the scrim is incomplete. The canvas behind the card is visibly darkened and blurred, but the color-palette strip along the top edge is not — its swatches (purple, blue, teal, green, olive, orange, brown, red, magenta, black, plus the multicolor button) are at full saturation and brightness, and the round red trash button at the top right is likewise undimmed, making its saturated red the strongest color accent in the frame after the dial. So while a modal is open and demanding attention, the top band of the screen still reads as live, tappable, and visually louder than the card's own controls: the purple pill and the gray close button both lose the contrast contest to the red trash and the palette row. The scrim's top edge also cuts a hard horizontal line directly beneath the palette, so the page reads half-dimmed rather than deliberately layered.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full viewport so the top color-palette strip and the red trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, removing the hard scrim edge beneath the palette and letting the card's pill and close button be the brightest interactive elements on screen.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
The AI result card itself is clean: the generated picture fills the card edge-to-edge with even padding, the Download button is a well-sized filled pill with clear label and icon, the close X is a solid disc at the top-right corner with enough separation from the image, and the "AI-generated picture · Report" caption sits legibly below the card. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems inside the card, and the collapse chevron and settings glyph are both locatable in the bottom corners.

The visible problem is the scrim. Behind the card the canvas is darkened and blurred as expected, but the color palette row along the top edge and the round trash button at the top right are rendered at full, unmodified brightness — the saturated swatches and the red trash icon are the highest-chroma, highest-contrast elements in the frame, brighter than anything on the open card. The scrim appears to stop below the top toolbar rather than covering the whole page, so the modal does not actually win attention: the eye lands on the palette strip first, and the trash button in particular sits immediately beside the card's close X at full strength, two competing top-right targets. The intended reading — page recedes, card holds focus — is not achieved along the top edge.

Secondary, smaller: the "Report" affordance is a small text-plus-flag label floating on the scrim with no visible hit area, which reads as an ambiguous touch target on a tablet compared with the clearly bounded Download and close controls.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full viewport so the top color palette and the trash button are darkened and blurred like the rest of the page, leaving the AI result card and its caption as the only full-brightness elements.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
The confirmation dialog itself is well-formed: title, retention paragraph, two labeled thumbnails, and a Cancel / Send report pair all fit their card with even padding, no clipping, no overlap, and no truncation. Button labels are centered and fully visible, and the primary/secondary weighting is clear.

The one visible problem is layering. The scrim behind this dialog darkens the top color palette and the corner controls, but the AI result card underneath is left at full brightness — and its round white "×" close button at the card's top-right corner renders at full contrast, sitting visually above the dimmed surroundings and only ~150px from the dialog's edge. While a confirmation is open, the frame therefore shows two competing dismiss affordances of similar prominence (the bright × and the dialog's own Cancel), with nothing indicating which one the confirmation belongs to or that the × is currently out of scope. The undimmed AI image also weakens the "one card holds attention" intent that the scrim over the rest of the page is establishing.
entries.recommendation: Extend the confirmation dialog's scrim over the AI result card too — including its top-right "×" close button — so the palette, the result card, and its close control all dim together and Cancel / Send report are the only full-contrast targets in the frame.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the report-confirmation card is broadly sound. The heading "Report this picture" is near-white on the dark violet card and reads crisply; the retention paragraph ("The AI picture, drawing behind it, selected art style... deleted after 30 days.") is a light lavender-gray on that same card and stays comfortably legible at its size across all five lines. The primary "Send report" button is white text on a saturated purple fill — the strongest element on the card, correctly carrying the emphasis. The two thumbnail captions, "The AI picture" and "The drawing behind it", are legible light text. The close X at the top of the AI card is drawn on the scrim layer and is clearly findable.

The one weak point is the "Cancel" button. Its fill is only a shade or two off the card's own background, so the button reads as a soft patch rather than a control, and its label is a muted lavender rather than the near-white used on the heading. Against its own fill the label is the dimmest text on the card, and the fill/card edge is the faintest boundary in the frame. Legibility survives, but it is the element with the least headroom here, and the deliberate de-emphasis of a secondary action has been pushed to where the control's own edge is hard to resolve.

Everything behind the card — the canvas, the top color palette, the corner glyphs, the Download button and the "AI-generated picture · Report" footer — is under the dialog scrim, so its dimness is the scrim and not judged.
entries.recommendation: Raise the Cancel button's label toward the same near-white used for the card heading, and lighten its fill (or add a visible border) enough that its edge separates clearly from the card background, while keeping it visually secondary to "Send report".

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal card itself is well-built: title, body, "For grown-ups" label, and the report button stack in clear reading order with even spacing, no clipping, no overlap, and no text overflow; the close X is a well-sized, clearly bounded touch target in the card's top-right, and the chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable in the bottom corners.

Two visible problems, both about how the card separates itself from the page:

1. No scrim. The page behind this dialog is at full brightness — the ten saturated palette swatches along the top edge, the multicolor palette button, and the red trash button all render at full contrast and full saturation. Those are the loudest pixels in the frame, and they pull the eye above and to the right of the card rather than into it. The card's own separation from the canvas is only a soft drop shadow against a plain white-gray field, which is weak by comparison, so the moment of a safety refusal is the moment the screen is least focused.

2. The "Report this refusal" button reads as low-contrast and near-disabled. Its label is a light purple on a pale lavender fill — a much narrower contrast range than the near-black title and dark-gray body text directly above it, and visibly softer than any other filled control in the frame. Because reduced contrast is this app's own convention for unavailable buttons, the one parent-facing action on this card looks like it cannot be pressed. Its hit area is generous and its bounds are legible; the issue is purely the label-on-fill contrast and the "disabled" reading it creates.

The two compound: the palette above is vivid while the card's only action is washed out, so visual weight sits almost exactly opposite to where the interaction is.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique:
The error dialog reads cleanly: scrim dims the palette, canvas stroke, and both corner glyphs (the chevron at bottom-left and the settings gear at bottom-right are both locatable), and the white card holds attention. The emoji, single line of copy, and circled X close button are legible, unclipped, and non-overlapping, and the copy fits on one line with margin to spare.

The one visible issue is the card's vertical composition. Content occupies roughly the top half of the card (emoji at ~y525–580, text at ~y603), while about 90px of empty white sits below the text before the card's bottom edge at y700 — far more than the ~90px above the emoji once the close button row is accounted for. The block reads top-weighted rather than centered, and the empty lower band looks like a slot where a missing element should be. Reinforcing that impression: the card tells the user to "try again" but offers no retry control — the only tappable thing on it is the small X in the corner, so the instruction has no matching affordance, and the dead space sits exactly where such a button would go.

Touch-target clarity is otherwise fine: the close button is a clearly outlined ~44px circle. No clipping, no overlap, no scrolling region in the card, and the trash button's docked overhang at the right edge is the intended treatment.
entries.recommendation: Fill the empty lower band of the error card with a primary "Try again" button beneath the message, or, if dismissal is the only intended action, tighten the card's bottom padding to match the top so the emoji and text read as vertically centered.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin page is largely solid: the "Admin" heading, the code rows (`daycare-club`, `page-inventory-harness`), the metric numerals, and the tile labels all read cleanly as light text on the near-black page and on the dark tile fills. The two advisory banners are rendered as light cream cards with dark ink; their internal contrast is strong and their text is fully legible, though they are the only high-luminance surfaces in an otherwise dark frame.

The weak points are the secondary gray text. The "Add a code…" placeholder inside the input sits only slightly above the field's own dark fill and is the faintest text in the frame. The two small-caps section labels, "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0", are set in a dim gray at small size and letter-spaced caps, which further thins the strokes against the page. The "Copy link" action, a muted lavender-gray at ~13px, reads noticeably weaker than the outlined "Copy" button and the red "Remove" beside it, even though all three are equally live controls — the middle action of a three-action row is the hardest of the trio to see. These are all readable at close inspection but are the elements most likely to fail a contrast threshold and to be missed at a glance.

Nothing here is illegible, and no text is lost against its background, so this is a low-severity tightening rather than a blocking defect.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance of the dark-theme secondary text tokens: lighten the "Add a code…" placeholder and the "ACCESS CODES" / "FREE GENERATION GRANTS" small-caps labels to at least 4.5:1 against their backgrounds, and bring "Copy link" up to match the contrast of the "Copy" and "Remove" actions it sits between.

entries.critique:
The access-codes list card and the following section header collide. The "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" label and its horizontal rule sit directly on the bottom border of the codes card — the label's baseline area overlaps the card edge and the rule merges with the card's bottom stroke, so the card looks unterminated and the two sections read as one. Two smaller things in the same rows: the focused "Copy link" control renders as a hard square black outline that clashes with the rounded purple-outline styling of the neighboring "Copy" buttons, and "Remove" is bare text with no border or padding box while its two siblings are outlined buttons — on a tablet where these are the inline row actions, the destructive control is the one with the least defined tap target and the least obvious hit area. Otherwise hierarchy, text fit, and the stat-tile grid are clean: no clipping, no truncation, headings and body text all fit, and the two-line/one-line tile wrap is consistent.
entries.recommendation: Add vertical margin below the access-codes list card (matching the spacing used above the "ACCESS CODES" header) so the "FREE GENERATION GRANTS" label and rule no longer sit on the card's bottom border; while there, give "Remove" the same bordered, padded button box as "Copy"/"Copy link" and replace the black square focus outline with the app's rounded purple focus ring.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast is mostly sound: the "Admin" heading, "Manage AI access codes", the section labels, the monospace code names, the "Sign out" pill, the "Add code" button and all eight stat tiles read cleanly as light text on the dark card, and the two cream notice banners carry dark text on a light ground that is fully legible. Two legibility problems are visible in the row-action cluster. First, the focused "Copy link" button on the "daycare-club" row has a hard white focus ring drawn tight against its label, and the ring's left and right edges sit directly on the glyphs — the leading "C" and trailing "k" are cut into by the white stroke, so the label is harder to parse in focus than unfocused. Second, the unfocused tertiary actions are noticeably weaker than their neighbors: "Copy link" on the "page-inventory-harness" row is muted lavender-gray with no border on the dark row ground, and "Remove" is a desaturated red on that same ground; both fall clearly below the bordered "Copy" label beside them and below body text elsewhere. entries.critique: The resting canvas reads cleanly. The top palette is a single full-width row of evenly spaced, generously sized round swatches with consistent diameter and gaps; the active purple swatch is marked with a clear ring, and the multicolor "more colors" button sits at the right end on its own white chip, distinct from the fixed swatches without overlapping them. The red trash button is docked at the right edge in its intended docked position, fully legible against the canvas. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron in the bottom-left corner and the gear in the bottom-right corner are visible as thin gray shapes at matching size and inset, symmetric across the bottom edge. There is no text on this screen, so no fit or truncation concerns, and no overlay or scrolling region is open to assess. Nothing visible is actionable.

The color palette strip sits on a near-black bar, and every swatch — including the mid-gray and the pure white one at the right end — separates cleanly from that bar and from its neighbors; the multicolor "more colors" flower at the far right is equally readable. No text, control, or state cue in the frame falls below usable contrast in this theme.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique:
Everything in the card renders cleanly: "Admin" heading, the "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, the "SIGN IN" rule-label, the input with its "Admin access key" placeholder, and the purple "Sign in" button all fit with no clipping, overlap, or text truncation. Hierarchy inside the card is clear and the top row ("← Back to drawing" left, dot cluster + "SPLOTCH ADMIN" right) is balanced.

The problem is page-level composition at this viewport. The card is pinned to the top and stretched nearly the full 1032px width, ending at roughly y=380, so about 1000px — nearly three-quarters of the 1376px portrait height — is empty gray. The sign-in form itself is a single short row anchored at the far left of that very wide card, leaving a large blank region to the right of the "Sign in" button and inside the card's own bottom padding. The result reads as an unfinished or mis-laid-out page rather than a deliberate composition: the eye lands on a wide, shallow band of content floating above a void.

Touch targets: the input and "Sign in" button are comfortably sized. "← Back to drawing" is set at small link scale in the card's top corner and offers a noticeably thinner tap area than the primary controls, though it remains legible and locatable.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the sign-in card to a centered fixed max-width (roughly 480–560px) and center it vertically in the viewport instead of letting it span the full 1032px width pinned to the top, so the form row fills its card and the ~1000px of empty gray below is distributed as balanced margin.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in card is mostly sound: "Admin" reads near-white on the raised charcoal card, "Manage AI access codes" is comfortably legible, the "← Back to drawing" link carries a distinct violet tint, and the "Sign in" button's white label sits on a mid-violet fill with clear separation. The weak points are all small, low-weight gray text. The "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark is set in tiny letterspaced uppercase in a muted gray against the card and is noticeably fainter than everything around it; the "SIGN IN" section label above the divider is the same treatment and is the dimmest text on the page. Both are small enough that the reduced contrast has real cost — the section label in particular is the only thing naming the form. The field placeholder "Admin access key" is also quite dim inside the input, though as placeholder text that is a milder concern. The input's own border is a low-contrast outline against the card fill, so the field edge is faint but still traceable. Nothing here is illegible, and no element disappears into the background.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the small uppercase gray text — the "SIGN IN" section label and the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark — and the input placeholder in dark mode so they clear roughly 4.5:1 against the card fill, since all three are small-size, low-weight type where the current muted gray falls short.

entries.surface_description: The complete release history at its opening position.
entries.critique: The page opens cleanly. Hierarchy is unambiguous: "Changelog" at large weight, a two-line subtitle at body size, then a left "CONTENTS" rail and a right release column separated by a hairline rule. Within each release, the version number and its right-aligned date sit on one baseline, category headers ("New", "Improved", "Fixed") are emoji-marked and bolded a step below the version heading, and bullets sit a further step down — three legible levels. Spacing is consistent: even bullet leading, equal gaps between category blocks, and a generous divider-separated gutter between Version 1.5.0 and Version 1.4.0 that reads as a real record break. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping anywhere; the longest bullets ("A new page chip shows and clears the current coloring page.", "Magic brush and picture saves recover from rare canvas failures.") end well inside the card's right edge, and no line wraps awkwardly. The contents rail rows are comfortably sized two-line targets (version + date) with the active row given a filled lavender pill and a left accent bar, so current position is clear and each row is easy to hit. The "← Back to drawing" link is a distinct purple against the near-white card, and the dotted SPLOTCH logo sits in the opposite corner without crowding it. The tall empty area under the contents rail is the expected consequence of a short nav beside a long article and does not read as a defect at this width. Content continues past the bottom of the frame at the top of a scroll, which is the correct resting state for an opening capture. Nothing here is actionable.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast holds up across the frame. The "Changelog" heading and the version headings sit near-white on the deep charcoal page, the intro paragraph and all bullet copy render as light gray at comfortable weight, and every list item is fully readable from top to bottom. Divider rules between releases are faint by design and do not carry meaning that text does not already convey. No text is lost to the background, no element is illegibly dim, and nothing in view depends on a color distinction that fails in dark mode.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
The page opens cleanly: strong title/lede hierarchy, a well-separated left nav with a clearly marked active item ("Color"), generous section rhythm, and roomy list rows that read as comfortable touch targets on this width. No overlap, no truncated labels, no clipped text at the viewport edge, and the two-column swatch grid aligns consistently.

One visible defect: in the "BRAND & UNTHEMED" swatch card, the filled color rows do not respect the card's rounded rectangle. The `--brand-rgb` and `--clear-gradient-rest` bars extend a couple of pixels past the right edge established by the `--brand` and `--on-brand` rows above them, and the bottom `--clear-gradient-rest` row terminates with square corners where the card's corner radius should be, so the red fill visibly juts out at the bottom-left and bottom-right of the card. The same card's neighbours ("GROUND & SURFACES", "TEXT INK", "ICON INK") keep clean rounded bottoms, which makes the inconsistency conspicuous side-by-side.

Two smaller notes, both readable but slightly inconsistent: the `--icon-muted` row sets white text over `#737373`, the thinnest text-on-fill contrast among all the swatches shown, and the hex values mix shorthand (`#333`, `#555`, `#666`, `#fff`) with full six-digit values (`#1f1f1f`, `#f5f5f5`) within the same grid, so the value column doesn't read as one system.
entries.recommendation: Clip the swatch rows to the card's shape — apply `overflow: hidden` plus the card radius to the swatch card container (or inherit the bottom corner radius on the last row) so the `--brand-rgb` and `--clear-gradient-rest` fills stop at the card edge and the bottom row's corners round like the adjacent cards.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the styleguide's opening screen is largely sound. The page ground is a near-black plum; headings ("Splotch design system", "Foundations", "Color") and body prose render in bright off-white and read cleanly. The purple "Not sure? Start here" callout keeps its body copy light on a mid-purple field, and the inline code tokens inside it (--surface, --border, --radius-lg, --ease-pop) are tinted a slightly warmer/lighter shade that stays distinguishable from the surrounding sentence without dropping out. Sidebar navigation items are legible, and the active "Color" row is marked by a filled violet pill with white label that reads unambiguously as selected. The Light/Dark segmented control in the top bar shows the active "Dark" segment as a filled lozenge with a bright label while the inactive "Light" segment stays lighter-gray but still plainly readable.

The color chips are the densest contrast surface here and they behave: each swatch is painted in its own value with the token name and hex set in dark ink on the light-to-mid chips (--text-strong #eceaf2, --icon-ink #dedce8, --brand #ab71e1, --clear-gradient-rest salmon) and in light ink on the dark chips (--app-bg #17171d, --surface #23232b, --border #3d3d49). Even the darkest chips in the GROUND & SURFACES and HAIRLINES groups keep their labels and hex values clearly readable, which is the hard case for a token table in night mode.

The one place legibility softens is the small supporting metadata. The sources line under the lede ("Sources: lib/design/tokens.ts → tokens.css (npm run gen:tokens) · lib/palette.ts · the icon set · the shipped components") and the trailing caption in the Color intro ("Tap any chip for its usage rule and both theme values.") are set at a smaller size than the body copy *and* in a dimmer gray, so the two reductions compound. The wrapped second line of the sources string in particular reads as faint against the near-black ground. This is real running text carrying instructions (how to interact with the chips) and provenance, not decorative chrome, so it is a different case from the intentionally quiet parent-facing glyphs described for the drawing screen. Nothing here is illegible, but it is the weakest ink in the frame and the smallest, and it is the copy that tells a reader what tapping a chip does.
entries.recommendation: Raise the small metadata copy in dark mode — the "Sources: …" provenance line and the "Tap any chip for its usage rule and both theme values." caption — from the dimmest muted gray to the standard body ink (or one step up from --text-soft), so that size reduction and color reduction are not stacked on the same instructional text.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: Layout is clean: clear hierarchy (back link, large title, intro, tab pair, labeled textarea, checkbox, disclaimer, primary button, side panel), no clipping, no overlap, all text fits its container, and the "What happens next" panel wraps without overflow. Two visible issues on a touch device: (1) the "Include device info (helps us reproduce the bug)" checkbox is roughly 22x22 px with no visible extended hit area or row affordance around its label, far below a comfortable finger target and by far the smallest interactive element next to the ~60 px tabs and 48 px "Send report" button; (2) the inactive tab "I have an idea" is mid-gray text on a light-gray segment while the active "Something's broken" is near-black on white, so the unselected option reads as disabled rather than as the alternate choice — a problem because bug-vs-idea is the first decision on the page. Lower stakes: the card ends near the vertical midpoint, leaving roughly 700 px of empty gray below on a 1032x1376 portrait frame, concentrating the whole form in the top half.
entries.recommendation: Enlarge the checkbox to ~24 px and make the checkbox plus its label a single tappable row at least 44 px tall, and darken the inactive tab label ("I have an idea") to about the body-text gray so both tabs read as selectable rather than one appearing disabled.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
Night-mode legibility is broadly good: the "Send us feedback" heading, the body paragraph, the "What went wrong?" label, both tab labels ("Something's broken" selected, "I have an idea" unselected), and the purple "What happens next" card all hold strong contrast, including the underlined privacy policy link. The "Send report" button has white text on saturated purple with ample separation, and the "← Back to drawing" link reads clearly in violet.

Two dim gray items are weak against the near-black card. The textarea placeholder "Describe what happened, and what you expected instead…" is noticeably fainter than any other text in the form, yet it is the only cue telling the user what to write. The disclaimer under the checkbox ("Your report goes to our private support tracker. Please don't include personal details like names or email addresses.") is set both small and gray, making it the faintest text in the frame despite carrying privacy guidance meant to be read. Additionally the checkbox is only a thin gray outline square on the dark card, so its unchecked state is easy to miss beside its adequately contrasted label.
entries.recommendation: Raise the night-mode gray used for the textarea placeholder, the privacy disclaimer line beneath the checkbox, and the checkbox border to a lighter step so all three clear the same contrast floor as the surrounding body copy on the dark card.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique: Layout, hierarchy and text fit are all sound at this viewport. The page card, header row ("← Back to drawing" opposite the dotted SPLOTCH mark), H1, intro, and the two labeled section rules ("THE SHORT VERSION" with the right-aligned "Last updated August 20, 2026", "THE DETAILS") are cleanly aligned to a consistent left margin with even vertical rhythm. The six-item summary card has uniform row spacing, consistent colored pill markers, and clear bold-lead/regular-detail contrast; no row wraps or collides. The two-column details area reads correctly: the sidebar list of seven section links is legible with adequate row height and a clearly marked active item ("What stays on your device", tinted with a left accent bar), and the body column's headings and paragraphs are comfortably measured with no clipping, overlap, or overflow. Body text sits at good contrast on white; the muted section labels and timestamp are deliberately secondary and still readable. The bottom edge cuts mid-content ("Making an AI picture"), which is ordinary page scroll at the opening position, not a fit fault. The one actionable defect is copy, and it is plainly visible: the third body paragraph ends "Unlike a setting, either one is sent to us — once when a grown-up adds it…", which contradicts itself and appears to be missing a negation or a clause; on a privacy policy this sentence carries meaning about when a code or key leaves the device, so the malformed wording is a real problem rather than a typo.
entries.recommendation: Fix the garbled sentence in the "What stays on your device" section — "Unlike a setting, either one is sent to us" — so the condition under which an access code or OpenAI key is transmitted is stated unambiguously.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this page is broadly sound: the "Privacy policy" heading, the intro paragraph, the six bulleted short-version lines, the sidebar nav items, and the long body copy under "What stays on your device" all sit as light gray/near-white on the near-black ground and read cleanly at this size. The colored pill markers beside each short-version line and the SPLOTCH dot row are decorative and legible enough for their role, and the "← Back to drawing" link is distinguishable as an accent-purple link.

The weak spots are the small uppercase metadata: the section eyebrows "THE SHORT VERSION" and "THE DETAILS", and the right-aligned "Last updated August 20, 2026". These are rendered in a mid-gray that is only slightly brighter than the divider rules running beside them, at a small letter-spaced caps size, so they carry noticeably less contrast than any other text in the frame — the date in particular nearly merges with the hairline it sits on. The active sidebar item "What stays on your device" is also the one nav label whose purple-on-purple-tinted pill reads dimmer than its inactive siblings below it, which inverts the usual selected-state emphasis, though its shape and wording remain readable.

None of this is a scrim, fade, or disabled-state effect — no overlay or scroll fade is present in this frame, so these are genuine styling contrast values.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the small uppercase metadata text — the "THE SHORT VERSION" / "THE DETAILS" eyebrows and the "Last updated" date — to a brighter gray than the divider rules they sit against so this small caps type clears normal body-text contrast in dark mode, and brighten the active sidebar item's label so the selected state is at least as bright as the inactive items.
