entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: Android tab of the beta page renders cleanly at 1032×1376. Hierarchy is clear and consistent: page title, intro, tab bar with the active Android tab marked by purple text plus underline, a "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" section rule, then four numbered steps on a vertical connector rail. Each step pairs a numbered disc, a bold heading, a body paragraph, and (steps 1–3) a filled purple CTA; step 4 is correctly marked OPTIONAL in small caps beside its heading. Spacing between steps is even and the rail aligns with the disc centers throughout. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping: the paragraphs wrap within the content column, the button labels sit centered with comfortable padding inside their pills, and the green "PLEASE STAY FOR 14 DAYS" callout contains its three wrapped lines with its left accent bar intact. Touch targets read clearly — the three CTAs are large pills, the tab items have generous hit areas, and the feedback URL is underlined as a link. Text contrast is good: dark gray body on white card, white on purple buttons, dark green on the pale green callout. The step discs vary in tint (pink, cream, green, blue) which reads as deliberate playfulness rather than inconsistency, and the numerals inside remain legible. The last visible line of step 4 thins out toward the bottom edge; that is the app's scroll fade painted over the final line, so the region is judged on the content sitting clear of it, which is intact. No modal or overlay is present in this frame. Nothing actionable is visible.

Night-mode contrast on this page is broadly sound: the H1, body copy, bold inline emphasis, the purple CTA buttons with white labels, the active "Android" tab, and the callout's body text all read cleanly against the near-black page and card fills. The green "PLEASE STAY FOR 14 DAYS" eyebrow and its left accent bar hold up, and the underlined feedback URL is clearly distinguishable as a link.

The one weak spot is the step numerals. Each of 1–4 sits as a small, dim purple digit inside a dark circular chip whose fill is only marginally lighter than the page background. At this size the digits are near the threshold — legible if you look for them, but the sequence does not read at a glance the way the step headings beside it do, which undercuts the numbered structure the page depends on. The same faint treatment applies to the "OPTIONAL" tag beside step 4 and, to a lesser degree, the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" section eyebrow, though those are secondary labels and carry less weight.

The bottom edge of the frame shows content thinning out over the last line of step 4's paragraph, which is the scroll-fade cue rather than a legibility fault, so it is excluded from this assessment.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-numeral treatment in dark mode: brighten the digits toward the body-text tier (or use a light-on-purple fill for the chip) so 1–4 read at a glance rather than sitting near threshold against their dark circles.

entries.review_description: Beta sign-up · iOS. TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page. Captured in light mode on iPad Pro 13-inch (M4) in portrait at 1032 × 1376. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: The iOS tab of the beta page reads cleanly at 1032 × 1376 in light mode. Hierarchy is unambiguous: page title, intro paragraph, a two-tab row where the active "iPhone / iPad" tab is marked by both purple text and an underline, then a labeled section rule ("HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD") introducing four numbered steps. Each step pairs a numbered badge, a bold heading, a body paragraph, and one purple CTA of consistent height, radius, and label weight, with a vertical connector rule tying the sequence together. Step 4's "OPTIONAL" tag sits inline with its heading at a smaller, lighter treatment, correctly subordinating it without breaking the heading line. Spacing is even between steps and within them; no crowding between paragraph and button. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapped: the inline bold "Install", the underlined feedback URL, and the italic "what?" all sit on their baselines and wrap normally. Buttons are comfortably above minimum touch-target size at this width and are well separated from each other and from the link text, so tap intent is clear. Body measure is comfortable and does not run edge to edge. At the bottom edge, "OR JUST EMAIL ME" thins out under a soft gradient — that is the app's own scroll-continues cue painted over the last line, not a rendering or legibility fault, and all content clear of the faded strip is fully legible. No overlays or scrims are present in this frame, so nothing here bears on modal scrolling or dialog contrast.

entries.surface_description: TestFlight instructions, on the iOS tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this iOS beta page is largely sound: the h1, body copy, and step headings are near-white on the near-black card and read cleanly, the underlined feedback URL is distinguishable from surrounding text, and the active "iPhone / iPad" tab is marked by both a purple label and an underline rather than color alone.

The one actionable weakness is the numbered step badges. Each is a small circular disc filled with a very dark desaturated plum that sits only a hair above the page background, with the numeral drawn in a muted mid-tone at small size. At 1, 2, 3 and 4 the digit is visible but is the faintest text in the content column — weaker than the "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" eyebrow and far weaker than the step titles beside it. These numerals are not decorative: the body copy cross-references them ("skip straight to step 2"), so a reader who has to squint to confirm which disc is 2 loses the function the badges exist to serve.

Lower-weight observation from the same frame: the white bold label on the purple primary buttons ("Get TestFlight from Apple", "Open the Splotch invitation", "Open Splotch in TestFlight", "Send feedback") is legible, but white-on-mid-purple is the thinnest foreground/background separation here at normal text size, with little headroom left.

The bottom strip ("OR JUST EMAIL ME") thins toward the frame edge, which is the scrolling-region fade being drawn, and is not judged.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the step-number numerals to near-white or bright lavender and lift the badge disc fill a step or two above the page background, so each digit reads at a glance beside its step title given the copy refers to steps by number.

entries.surface_description: The shared SvelteKit error boundary rendered for an unknown route.
entries.critique:
The screen is clean and reads correctly: illustration blob → "Oops!" heading → one-line explanation → a single filled "Start over" pill. Hierarchy is unambiguous, nothing is clipped or overlapping, the heading and button label fit their boxes, and the button is a generously sized, clearly tappable target with strong white-on-purple contrast. No modal, scroll region, or corner controls are present in this frame to assess.

Two minor things are visible. First, the subtitle's measure is very narrow for a 1032 px-wide viewport — "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." breaks after "fresh," leaving a single orphaned word ("drawing.") on line two directly above the button. On a tablet-width screen there is ample room for this sentence to sit on one line, and the orphan makes the block look accidentally wrapped rather than composed. Second, the whole group sits noticeably above the vertical midpoint of the frame — the blob-to-button stack occupies roughly the 530–840 px band of a 1376 px-tall screen, leaving a much larger empty field below than above it. It doesn't read as centered or as deliberately top-anchored; it reads as slightly floated. The subtitle gray is also light against the near-white ground, but it is legible at this size and secondary by intent.

Nothing here is broken or blocking — this is polish on an otherwise well-composed error state.
entries.recommendation: Widen the subtitle's max-width (or drop its font size slightly) at tablet breakpoints so "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." fits on one line instead of orphaning "drawing.", and center the blob/heading/subtitle/button stack on the viewport's vertical midpoint rather than letting it sit above center.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this error screen holds up. "Oops!" is near-white on a very dark neutral ground — maximum separation. The two-line body copy ("Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing.") sits at a lighter gray, clearly dimmer than the heading but still comfortably readable at this size, with crisp letterforms and no haloing or color fringing against the dark background. The "Start over" pill uses white bold label text on a mid-tone purple fill; the label reads cleanly and the pill itself separates well from the dark page, so both the control and its affordance are easy to spot. The purple blob mark above the heading is decorative and carries no text. Nothing in the frame is washed out, muddied, or lost to the dark theme.

entries.critique: The Settings dialog renders cleanly on the 1032×1376 iPad Pro 13 portrait frame in light mode. Hierarchy is clear: title "Settings" top-left, close button top-right, a left nav column of ten labeled icon rows with "Appearance" selected via a tinted pill and left accent bar, and a right detail pane grouped under "Appearance" and "Sound" headings with a small-caps "WHAT MAKES SOUND" subheading. Spacing is even and consistent between rows, cards, and the two columns; no text is truncated, wrapped awkwardly, or overlapping any control. The Theme segmented control fits Light/Dark/System with icons at comfortable width and the selected state is unambiguous. Toggles, the volume slider with its "50%" value, and the nav rows are all at generous, clearly separable touch sizes. The detail pane's scrolling region shows the expected soft fade over the "Deleting" row at the card's bottom edge, which is this app's documented scroll cue; content clear of that strip is fully legible. The page behind is under the dialog's scrim, so the dimmed palette, docked trash button, and the two corner glyphs are the scrim rather than element styling — and both corner glyphs (the chevron at bottom-left, the gear at bottom-right) remain locatable. No phone-landscape orientation segments appear in this capture, so that design intent is not exercised here. Nothing actionable is visible.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in the Settings card is broadly sound: "Settings", "Appearance", "Sound", the sidebar item labels, and the row labels ("Theme", "Lock device rotation", "Sound", "Volume", "Drawing") are near-white on dark charcoal surfaces and read cleanly. The selected sidebar row (Appearance) is marked by a purple tint plus a left accent bar, both visible. Toggles are distinguishable: purple-filled with white knob for on, gray track with white knob for off. The "Deleting" row at the bottom edge sits under the scroll fade and is excluded from judgement, as is the dimmed canvas/palette behind the scrim.

Two weak spots are visible. First, the small caps section header "WHAT MAKES SOUND" is rendered in a mid-gray at a small size directly on the card background; it is the faintest text in the open card and is noticeably harder to resolve than every other label around it. Second, in the Theme segmented control the selected "Dark" segment is filled *darker* than the unselected track, so selection is signalled by a near-black patch on a dark-gray strip — the two tones are close, and the only other cue is a subtle border. The "Light" and "System" labels themselves are legible, but which segment is active reads weakly at a glance in night mode; the same control in light mode would normally use a lighter-than-track fill, and here the low tonal separation is the issue rather than any text contrast.

No glyph is unlocatable: the bottom-left chevron and bottom-right settings gear are faint by design and both are findable in the frame. Everything else in the card meets a reasonable night-mode legibility bar.
entries.recommendation: Raise the tonal separation of the Theme segmented control's selected segment in dark mode — give the active "Dark" pill a lighter (or accent-tinted) fill than the surrounding track rather than a near-black one — and lift the "WHAT MAKES SOUND" section header to a lighter gray so it is not the dimmest text in the card.

Row structure is consistent — icon, label, description, trailing toggle — with toggles vertically centered on the label line and comfortably sized targets; the "Remove downloaded pictures" destructive button is visually distinguished by its red-on-tinted-pink treatment and sits inside its card with even padding. No text is clipped or truncated, no labels collide with their toggles, and no elements overlap. Nav labels, icons, and row spacing are uniform down the rail; card corner radii, gutters, and inter-card gaps are consistent across both sections. The right pane's content thins toward the bottom edge over the "special access" line, which is the app's own scroll-fade cue marking more content below, and the content clear of that strip is fully legible. The page behind is darkened and blurred by the dialog scrim, so the muted canvas, corner glyphs, and docked trash button are the scrim rather than styling faults; the bottom-left chevron and bottom-right gear glyphs are both locatable in the frame. Nothing actionable is visible.

entries.review_description: Settings · Coloring. The Coloring section where full settings fit; compact phone landscapes show the quick-toggle shell that replaces it. Design intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation. Captured in night mode on iPad Pro 13-inch (M4) in portrait at 1032 × 1376. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. entries.critique:
The open Settings card is the element in scope (the canvas, palette strip, trash button and corner glyphs behind it sit under the dialog scrim). Within the card, night-mode contrast is generally sound: "Settings", the section headings "Coloring" and "AI Art", the active "Coloring" nav row, the row titles, and the white-on-purple/white-on-gray toggles all read cleanly against the near-black card. Secondary descriptions ("Show coloring pages and download new books automatically", "Allows automatic picture downloads when Wi-Fi isn't available", the "7 of 7 extra books · 21.3 MB" metadata) are dimmer but stay legible. The thinning of the "You have special access…" line at the bottom is the scroll fade being painted, not a defect.

The one weak spot is the "Remove downloaded pictures" button: its muted red-pink label sits on a dark desaturated maroon fill, and the two tones are close enough in both lightness and hue that the text loses definition compared with every other control on the card — noticeably softer than the white label/text pairings elsewhere. Since it is the destructive action in this section, it is the one element that should not be the hardest to read. The inactive nav labels (Sound, Tool Drawer, AI Art, etc.) are also on the dim side but remain clearly resolvable and read as an intentional inactive state.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the "Remove downloaded pictures" destructive button in dark mode — lighten the label toward a brighter red/near-white and/or darken the maroon fill so the text/fill pair clears 4.5:1, matching the definition of the other card controls.

entries.critique:
The AI Art settings pane is well organized: a clear "AI Art" heading, consistent setting cards (icon + label + right-aligned toggle + description beneath), an active "AI Art" nav row marked redundantly by tint and a left accent bar, and a soft fade over "Saving" indicating the right pane scrolls. Toggles, the Forget button, and the circular close button all present comfortable touch targets at this 1032x1376 size. No clipping, overlap, or wrapping failures are visible; the nav column and content pane are cleanly separated, and card-to-card spacing is even.

The one actionable issue is the Access Code field: the value "daycare-club" is drawn in a light gray monospace on a light gray filled input, visually indistinguishable from placeholder text. Because the surrounding copy states a code is currently applied and offers a Forget action, this field is the only element confirming which code is active, yet it is the lowest-contrast text in the card. A reader cannot tell whether the string is a stored value or a format hint.
entries.recommendation: Render the Access Code value at the same body-text color/weight as the setting descriptions rather than in placeholder gray, so an applied code is clearly distinguishable from an empty field.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in the Settings card is mostly sound: the "Settings" and "AI Art" headings, the nav labels (Appearance … About), the row titles (Create AI Images, Customize AI Style, Auto-Save AI Images), the "Forget" button label, and the close × all read cleanly against the dark card. Toggle states are distinguishable — the purple filled tracks vs. the gray off-track on Auto-Save, each with a bright white knob. The active "AI Art" nav row is legible against its purple-tinted selected background, and the left accent bar is visible. The faded "Saving" heading at the card's lower edge is the scroll fade being drawn and is not judged.

The one weak spot is the Access Code field: the value "daycare-club" is rendered in a dim monospace gray that sits noticeably below the surrounding body copy in luminance, on a field whose background is barely separated from the card. It reads more like disabled placeholder text than like the actual code, and this is the one string on the panel a parent may need to read character-by-character (distinguishing a hyphen, or an l/1/I) rather than skim. The explanatory paragraph above it ("You have special access via an access code — …") is also on the dimmer side, though the bolded "special access" carries it and the sentence stays readable. Secondary descriptions under each toggle row are dimmer than their titles by design and remain legible at this size.
entries.recommendation: Raise the Access Code value's text color toward the card's primary foreground (near the row-title white rather than the secondary gray) so the code reads as live, selectable content instead of placeholder text, and lighten the input's fill slightly so the field boundary is visible in dark mode.

entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique:
The Settings card renders cleanly overall: the sidebar list, the "Saving" group of three rows, and the Parent Center table all have consistent spacing, legible labels, and no clipped or overlapping text. The scrim over the canvas and palette, and the fade over the "Generating an AI image" row at the card's bottom edge, are the documented scroll/overlay treatments and are not counted against it.

One visible fit issue: on both toggle switches in the Saving group, the white knob is drawn larger than the pill track it sits in, so it overhangs the track on the top, bottom, and outer edge rather than nesting inside it. On the "Auto-Save on Delete" toggle (off state) the knob visibly bulges past the gray track outline; on the "Camera button" toggle (on state) it pushes past the right end of the purple fill. The controls remain readable as on/off, but the knob-vs-track proportion reads as a sizing bug and is inconsistent with the otherwise tidy geometry of the card (circular close button, radio group, rounded row cards).

Secondary, minor: the Parent Center column header "PER SESSION" wraps to two lines while "EVERY TIME" also wraps and "NEVER" stays on one, giving the header row a slightly ragged, uneven baseline against the radio column beneath it. Alignment of each header to its radio is correct, so this is cosmetic only.
entries.recommendation: Reduce the toggle knob diameter (or increase the track height) so the knob sits fully inside the switch track with even padding on all sides in both the on and off states.

entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique:
The Parent Center pane reads well overall: clear title, supporting sentence, consistent card rows with bolded action name plus explanation, and a legible sidebar with the active item marked by a purple bar and tint. The dialog scrim behavior and the faded partial row at the bottom of the scroll region are expected per the stated conventions.

One actionable defect: in each of the four rows the selected "NEVER" option is drawn as a white rounded box that overhangs the right end of the gray segmented track it sits in — the white pill's right edge and its purple outline sit on top of / past the track's rounded corner instead of nesting inside it, so the track's rounded end is visually cut. This repeats identically on all four rows, so it reads as a layout bug rather than styling. The two unselected radios sit comfortably inset, which makes the overhang more conspicuous by comparison.

Secondary, lower-confidence observation: the header labels "EVERY TIME" and "PER SESSION" wrap to two lines while "NEVER" stays on one, leaving the header baseline ragged above the columns. It is readable and the labels do align over their columns, so this is cosmetic.

Touch targets, text fit within the cards, and spacing between rows look adequate; no clipped or overlapping text was seen.
entries.recommendation: Give the segmented radio track enough horizontal padding (or shrink the selected pill) so the selected option's white box and outline nest fully inside the gray track's rounded ends rather than overhanging the right edge on every row.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog itself is in good shape: clear "Settings" title, a legible left nav with the active Feedback row marked by a purple bar and tinted pill, well-spaced form fields, an accessible close button, and a "Updates" heading thinning out at the bottom edge that reads as the intended scroll fade rather than clipping. Text fits, nothing overlaps, and the segmented "Something's broken" / "I have an idea" control has clear selected/unselected states with generous touch targets.

The visible problem is the scrim's coverage. The canvas behind the card is clearly darkened and blurred, but the color palette strip along the top edge and the round red trash button at the top right are rendered at full brightness and full saturation — the fourteen swatches are the most vivid, highest-contrast elements anywhere in the frame, brighter than anything inside the open card. Per the stated behavior, an overlay of this kind darkens the canvas, the top palette, and the corner buttons together so the open card holds attention; here the top strip escaped that treatment, so the eye lands on the swatch row before it lands on "Feedback." The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable and sit correctly behind the scrim, which makes the untreated top band look like a coverage gap rather than a deliberate exception.

Secondary, lower-confidence: the "Send report" button is white text on a pale lavender fill with weak contrast; if that is the disabled state for an empty textarea it is fine, but nothing else in the frame distinguishes it from an enabled primary button.
entries.recommendation: Extend the settings-dialog scrim over the top color-palette strip and the trash button so the whole page behind the card is darkened and blurred uniformly, as it already is for the canvas and the bottom-corner controls.

entries.critique:
Judging night-mode contrast only, the card itself is mostly solid: "Feedback", the section text, the nav labels, and the active "Feedback" nav row all read cleanly on the dark card, and the close button's × is clearly visible. The faded "Updates" heading at the card's bottom edge is the scroll fade, and the dim canvas behind is the dialog scrim — neither is a finding.

One real issue: the primary "Send report" button. Its label is rendered in a desaturated gray-lavender against a muted purple fill of very similar lightness, so the text nearly dissolves into the button — noticeably weaker than every other label on the card, including the secondary body copy above it. Whether or not this is meant to read as an inactive state, it is the one control the whole panel funnels toward, and its label is the hardest text in the card to read.

Secondary, lower-weight: the disclaimer line under the checkbox ("Your report goes to our private support tracker…") sits at a dim gray that is legible but close to the floor, and the unchecked "Include device info" checkbox is a nearly borderless dark square whose outline is hard to distinguish from the field background.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "Send report" label to a near-white foreground against its purple fill so the primary action's text clears a comfortable contrast margin in dark mode; if the button is intentionally disabled here, distinguish that state by fill opacity rather than by fading the label into the fill.

entries.surface_description: The What's New section where full settings fit; compact phone landscapes show the quick-toggle shell that replaces it.
entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation. In the wide split-pane Settings shell, What's New and About are the two trailing sections of one continuous pane rather than independently paged views, so this capture records their shared trailing region. The table-of-contents highlight follows the reading position: it remains on What's New while that section is at the reading line and moves to About only at the pane's true scroll end. A viewport tall enough to show the entire trailing region can therefore produce the same capture when opened from either section.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the Settings dialog is largely sound: the "Updates" and "About" headings, the card's date line, the ✨/🚀/🛠 group labels, and all bullet body text render as near-white or light gray on the dark card and read cleanly at a glance. The left table-of-contents labels (Appearance through About) are legible, and the emoji-style section icons stay saturated against the dark ground. The close (×) glyph in its thin circle at the card's top-right is dimmer than the heading beside it but its shape is clearly locatable. Background canvas, top color palette, and the two bottom-corner parent glyphs are behind the dialog scrim, so their dimness is the scrim and out of scope; the trash button and corner chevron/gear are per the settled decisions.

The one weak element is the "See all releases →" link. It is rendered in a muted violet that sits close in luminance to the dark panel behind it, noticeably fainter than every other piece of text in the pane — including the body bullets directly above it — despite being the only actionable link in this region. The selected "What's New" row in the table of contents uses a similar violet on a violet-tinted highlight bar; it is readable, but it too is the lowest-contrast label in that list, so the same hue is doing double duty at the edge of comfortable legibility. Neither is illegible, but the link in particular is the kind of text a parent scanning in a dark room could skim past.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the violet used for the "See all releases →" link (and the selected "What's New" label) in dark mode to a higher-luminance tint so it clears roughly 4.5:1 against the dark panel and reads at least as strongly as the body bullets above it.

The sidebar shows "About" as the selected item (highlighted lavender row), but the content pane is not scrolled to the About section. The top ~60% of the pane is occupied by the tail of the previous section's release notes — "🚀 Improved" and "🔧 Fixed" bullet lists plus a "See all releases →" link, with a partially faded line above them — and the "About" heading does not appear until roughly the vertical middle of the card. A user tapping About lands on content belonging to What's New, and must scroll to reach the section they chose; the selected-row highlight and the visible content disagree.

Sidebar rows have consistent icon/label alignment and generous touch height. The scrim over the canvas and palette, the docked trash button, and the faint chevron and settings glyphs in the bottom corners are all present as intended.
entries.recommendation: When a sidebar section is selected, scroll the content pane so that section's heading ("About") sits at the top of the visible pane, rather than leaving the previous section's content occupying the pane.

In night mode the Settings card reads cleanly overall: the sidebar labels, the What's New "Improved"/"Fixed" headings and bullet copy, the "About" heading, and the "See all releases →" link all sit at comfortable brightness against the dark card and its slightly lighter inset panel. The active "About" row is legible against its purple selected fill, and the close ✕ in the top-right is visible against the card.

entries.critique: Single purple stroke on the tiled paper canvas in light mode. The top color palette renders as one full-width row of evenly spaced round swatches with consistent diameter and gaps; the active purple swatch carries a clear selection ring, and the rainbow "more colors" swatch terminates the row at the right edge without crowding or overlap. No swatch is clipped by the top edge or by the row's right end. The trash button sits docked at the upper-right with part of it past the edge, which is its intended docked state, and it does not collide with the palette above it or with the stroke. The stroke itself is drawn cleanly with no visible tearing or tile seams across the canvas texture. The chevron in the bottom-left and the gear in the bottom-right are both locatable as distinct glyph shapes at their corners, sitting quietly as intended, and each has ample empty space around it for a touch target. There is no overlay or scrim in this frame, no text to fit or truncate, and no scrolling region. Nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off, and spacing between the three control zones (top palette, docked trash, bottom corners) is generous and uniform.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility hold across everything visible. The top palette bar renders on a near-black strip: all fifteen color swatches plus the multicolor picker separate cleanly from the bar, and the currently selected purple chip carries a visible selection ring. The single purple ink stroke sits well clear of the dark textured canvas and is unambiguously legible along its whole length. The docked trash button in the top right uses a saturated pink/red fill with a light trash glyph, giving strong contrast against both its own fill and the canvas behind it. entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The Actions Panel column at the lower left is rendered with its left half outside the viewport. All six round buttons (undo, AI, screenshot, coloring-book, stroke-width, brush) are cut vertically at x = 0: each shows only its right portion, so the white discs read as half-pills flush against the screen edge and every glyph sits off-center within its remaining visible area. The declared docking exception in this app covers the round trash button at the top right, which is indeed correctly docked past the right edge; it does not cover this panel, and nothing in the frame suggests the drawer is mid-animation — the expand chevron above it is in its expanded (down) state and the column is at rest.

Consequences visible here: the effective tap width of each of the six controls is roughly halved, so touch-target clarity is degraded for the whole drawer; the icons are no longer optically centered in their containers, which breaks the visual consistency with the fully-drawn circular color swatches along the top edge and the fully-drawn trash button; and the chevron at the top of the column is horizontally centered on the *clipped* discs rather than on their true centers, so the affordance and the stack it controls do not align to a common axis.

Everything else in the frame reads cleanly. The palette row is evenly spaced with the active purple swatch clearly ringed, the single purple stroke on the canvas is crisp, the low-contrast chevron and the bottom-right settings gear are both locatable as shapes, there is no scrim or overlay in play, no text is present to fit or truncate, and no elements overlap.
entries.recommendation: Inset the Actions Panel column from the left viewport edge so each round button and its chevron render at full width (e.g. a left margin at least equal to the button radius plus the safe-area inset), reserving the past-the-edge docking treatment for the trash button.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
The brush flyout itself reads well: four tools (pen, crayon, paintbrush, eraser) sit in one rounded white card with even spacing, no clipping, no overlap, and the active pen is clearly marked with a lavender fill and purple outline — selection state is unambiguous and every glyph is fully drawn inside the card. The card is anchored beside its trigger without covering the color palette or the settings glyph, and the page behind it is at full brightness, correct for a flyout that casts no scrim. The parent-facing chevron above the left column and the settings gear at bottom right are both locatable as shapes.

The actionable problem is the column of round Actions Panel buttons the flyout belongs to. All six (undo, AI, camera, coloring book, stroke width, and the brush trigger) are cut vertically by the left edge of the viewport — roughly the left third of each disc is off-screen, so the circles render as half-pills with icons sitting off-center in what remains. The stated exception covers only the trash button docked at the right edge; nothing given makes this left column deliberately docked past the edge, and unlike the trash it is the app's whole primary control stack rather than one button. The consequence is touch-target clarity: the visible hit area of each button is smaller than the drawn control implies, and the truncated discs no longer read as the same button shape used elsewhere. The brush trigger at the bottom is the worst case, since it is the button the open flyout points back to and its active relationship to the flyout is hard to read when its own outline is incomplete.

Undo, AI, and screenshot are at reduced contrast, which is the expected disabled styling on an empty canvas. No text is present to fit or truncate, and no scrolling region is in frame.
entries.recommendation: Inset the left-hand Actions Panel column from the viewport edge (roughly 12–16px of leading padding) so each round button renders as a complete circle with its full touch target on screen, matching the disc shape used elsewhere; reserve the deliberate past-the-edge docking for the trash button only.

entries.surface_description: Pen, crayon, Magic Brush, and eraser in the shared flyout.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast and legibility of the brush flyout is broadly sound. The page behind the flyout is at full brightness (no scrim), so the flyout, the palette strip, and the corner controls all keep normal scope.

The four flyout tools — pen, crayon, Magic Brush, eraser — are drawn as multi-color glyphs on near-black tiles. Their saturated bodies (yellow crayon, pink eraser, colored bristles) carry clear luminance separation from the dark ground and are individually identifiable at a glance. The selected pen is marked with a lighter tile fill plus a purple outline, and that selected state is distinguishable from the three unselected tiles.

Two softer spots, both mild: (1) the tile plates themselves sit only a shade above the canvas, so the flyout reads as floating glyphs rather than a bounded group — the boundary between the flyout container and the canvas is very low contrast in dark mode; (2) within several glyphs the darkest parts — the pen barrel, the Magic Brush handle, the outline strokes around each tool — fall close to the tile background, so the silhouette of each tool partially dissolves into its plate and only the colored segments carry the shape. Neither prevents identification, but both reduce crispness relative to the same icons in a lighter context.

The top color palette is high contrast against the black strip, with the active swatch ringed clearly. The trash button is fully legible. The chevron and the settings glyph are faint by design and both are locatable in the frame, so no finding there. The undo, AI, and screenshot buttons show the intended disabled-state reduced contrast on an empty canvas.
entries.recommendation: Raise the dark-mode contrast of the brush flyout's own surface — give the tile plates and the flyout container a slightly lighter fill (or a subtle 1px light border) than the canvas — so each tool's dark outline and handle segments separate from their background instead of dissolving into it.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique:
The stroke-width flyout itself reads well: five previews in one rounded card, ascending thickness left to right, the selected third option marked with a lilac fill and purple outline, ample even gaps, no text to fit or clip, no overlap with the card, and no scrim (correctly, per the flyout rules). The trash button, the chevron, and the settings glyph are all locatable and behave as described.

The visible problem is the Actions Panel column itself. Every one of its buttons — undo, AI, screenshot, coloring-book, the stroke-width toggle, and the brush toggle — is cut by the left edge of the viewport, with roughly the left third to half of each rounded square missing. Only the trash button is documented as deliberately docked past an edge; this column is not, and it does not read as an intentional dock because the buttons are square, flush-cropped, and the chevron above them sits fully inside the frame at a different left offset than the buttons' visible centers. The result is a row of half-buttons whose touch targets and icon centers are pushed against and past the boundary, which weakens both the tap affordance and the visual alignment of the whole column against the flyout that opens beside it.

Secondary, milder: the flyout card's left edge starts immediately beside the clipped brush/stroke buttons with only a thin gap, so the panel and the flyout crowd each other; with the column properly inset this gap would need re-checking.

The reduced contrast on undo, AI, and screenshot is the documented disabled state on an empty canvas and is not counted here.
entries.recommendation: Inset the Actions Panel column so each round/rounded button sits fully inside the left viewport edge with a consistent margin (matching the chevron's inset), and re-space the stroke-width flyout so it clears the restored column with a visible gap.

entries.critique: The stroke-width flyout sits on the dark canvas with no scrim, so the whole frame is in scope. The five width tiles use rounded dark-charcoal chips that separate cleanly from the surrounding panel and canvas, and each preview stroke is drawn in a light lavender-purple that reads strongly against the near-black tile fill — even the thinnest (leftmost) preview stays a continuous, clearly visible line rather than dissolving into the tile, and the five weights are distinguishable from one another at a glance. The selected third tile is marked with a bright purple ring plus a lighter tile fill; the ring is clearly brighter than the unselected tile borders, so the current choice is unambiguous in night mode. Above, the color palette swatches keep full saturation and are separated by a dark strip, and the docked trash button's yellow glyph on the coral disc is high contrast. In the Actions Panel, the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons render dim, which is their documented disabled treatment; the coloring-book, brush-style, and pen buttons below them are at full contrast and legible. The collapse chevron above the panel and the settings gear in the opposite bottom corner are both locatable as faint gray glyphs — their intended resting appearance. No text in the frame is unreadable and no control loses its shape against the night-mode background.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: The honeycomb grid is clipped along the right edge of the card. Because the odd rows are offset by half a cell, their rightmost hexagons run into the card boundary and are sliced off vertically — visible in the orange row, the amber row, the green row, the blue row, the purple row, the pink row and the brown row, each of which ends in a flat vertical cut instead of a hexagon point. The even rows end cleanly with a full hexagon and a small gap, so the ragged, half-cut cells read as a layout overflow rather than an intended edge. The clipped cells are also still large enough to look tappable, so it is unclear whether they are real swatches or decoration. Separately, the top color strip and the red trash button are rendered at full brightness and saturation while the entire canvas behind the card is darkened, so those elements sit visually above the picker rather than behind it and compete with the open card for attention. Otherwise hierarchy is fine: the white card is clearly the focus, spacing between rows is even, the currently-selected white swatch is legibly outlined in the bottom-left, there is no text to fit or overlap, individual hexagons are comfortably large touch targets, and both the bottom-left chevron and the bottom-right settings glyph are locatable.
entries.recommendation: Fix the right-edge overflow of the honeycomb grid — size the offset rows so their last hexagon fits fully inside the card's horizontal padding (e.g. one fewer cell on offset rows, or scale cell width to the card), so no swatch is rendered as a vertically sliced partial hexagon.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the open color-picker card is generally sound: the hexagon grid sits on a dark elevated card that is distinguishable from the scrimmed page behind it, and every hue row — pinks, oranges, yellows, greens, blues, purples, magentas, browns, grays — reads at full saturation with clean edges and no muddying. The white swatch at the bottom-left of the grid separates strongly from its surround. The top-edge palette strip and the trash button behind the scrim are dimmed as expected for a dialog, and both bottom-corner glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron in the lower left and the settings gear in the lower right are faint but their shapes are findable in the image.

The one contrast problem is the darkest swatch, bottom row, second from the right. Its fill is essentially the same near-black as the card surface it sits on, so the hexagon reads as a hole in the grid rather than as a selectable color; only a hairline outline distinguishes it, and that outline is itself thin and low contrast against the card. Every other swatch in the grid announces its color by fill; this one announces it only by a barely-visible border, so at a glance the grid appears to have a missing tile in the last row. This is specific to night mode, where the card background has moved toward the same value as the swatch.
entries.recommendation: Give the near-black swatch a visible separation from the dark card in night mode — either lighten the card surface beneath the grid, or strengthen that swatch's outline (brighter stroke, greater width) so its hexagon reads as a filled color chip rather than a gap in the grid.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The Coloring Books card itself is in good shape: two-column grid with even gutters, uniform card sizes, line-art thumbnails on clean white tiles, single-word labels centered and fully legible with no truncation, clipping, or overlap. The title and the round close button in the top-right are clearly separated and the close button is a comfortably large tap target. The grid ends flush after Vehicles with clear space below and no fade strip, so the full inventory of eight books reads as complete.

The one visible problem is the scrim. entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique: The open Coloring Books card is the element in scope; the darkened, blurred canvas and palette behind it are the dialog scrim and not judged. Within the card, the "Coloring Books" heading is near-white on the dark panel and reads crisply. The eight cover thumbnails are drawn as white line art on slightly raised dark tiles — the strokes stay thin but hold clear separation from the tile fill, and every subject (farm, dinosaurs, unicorn, ladybug, toys, shapes, rocket, vehicles) is identifiable at a glance. The eight caption labels are a light gray set against the tile background; they sit below full white but remain comfortably readable at this size, with no label blending into its tile. The circular close control in the top-right renders as a gray ✕ on a subtly lighter disc — quieter than the heading, but the disc gives it an edge and the glyph shape is unambiguous. Tile borders are faint yet sufficient to bound each card, and the selected/unselected state of the tiles is not in question here. Nothing in the card is illegible, washed out, or lost to the dark ground.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique: The Farm page-grid dialog reads cleanly. Header row is unambiguous: back chevron at left, "Farm" title beside it, close X at the right, all on one baseline with generous clearance from the grid below; both are circular hit areas well above a comfortable touch size at this width. The 2×3 grid of page thumbnails uses even column and row gutters and equal card sizes, and the card padding around the grid is consistent left, right, top and bottom. Each thumbnail's line art sits fully inside its rounded card with no cropping, overlap, or spill; the six cards fill the card exactly, ending flush with no fade strip, so nothing is hidden behind a scroll cue. There is no text in the grid to fit or truncate, and the single text element (the title) is fully rendered at a comfortable weight. Behind the dialog, the palette strip, the docked trash button, the left-edge Actions Panel and the bottom-right settings glyph are all dimmed by the dialog scrim — that is the scrim, and the collapse chevron and settings gear glyphs remain locatable in the frame. Visual consistency between the card's rounded geometry, the thumbnail card radii, and the header controls holds.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
The open "Farm" page-grid dialog lays a scrim over the page, so the judgement is the card itself. Inside the card the substance holds up well in night mode: the "Farm" title is near-white on the dark card surface and reads cleanly, and the six thumbnails render as thin white line art on dark tiles with crisp, unbroken outlines — whiskers, grass blades, fence rails, and bubble outlines all stay separable at this size, and each tile's surface is a shade lighter than the card so the grid cells are distinguishable. The color palette strip, the red trash button, and the corner tool glyphs sit behind the scrim and are dim for that reason.

The one weak spot is the pair of card-chrome controls: the back chevron at top-left and the close × at top-right. Both are drawn as mid-gray glyphs on a circular disc that is itself only marginally lighter than the card background, so glyph, disc, and card all sit within a narrow band of dark gray. They are locatable — I can find both shapes — but they are noticeably the lowest-contrast elements inside a card that is otherwise bright and confident, and unlike the corner parent-facing glyphs these are the dialog's own primary navigation and dismissal affordances, which are meant to be found by the person using the card. Their contrast is well below the title beside them and below the artwork they sit above.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the back-chevron and close-× glyphs in the dialog header (and slightly raise their disc fill against the card surface) so both reach at least 3:1 against their backing in night mode, bringing them closer to the "Farm" title's weight rather than leaving them the dimmest elements in the card.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique:
The screen reads clearly overall: the top color palette is a single legible row with the active swatch marked by a ring, the line-art page has generous margins and no overlap with controls, and the parent-facing chevron (top of left stack) and settings gear (bottom right) are both locatable as faint gray glyphs, so they meet the findability floor. Undo, AI, and camera show the expected disabled reduced contrast.

The actionable problem is the left-hand Actions Panel column. Six round buttons (undo, AI, camera, coloring-book, stroke-width, brush) are each bisected by the left viewport edge — roughly half of every disc and a visible portion of each glyph sits outside the frame. Unlike the trash button, which is docked as a deliberate single control, this is the whole primary tool stack: the brush and stroke-width icons in particular lose their left half, and the truncated circles give no clear tappable boundary, so the touch target reads as ambiguous rather than as an intentional dock. On a 1032 px-wide portrait canvas there is ample left margin available, so the truncation is not a space constraint.

The top palette row also sits flush against the top edge with the swatch circles very slightly cropped, which compounds the sense that the layout is drawn without safe-area inset, though that one is minor on its own.

No text is present to mis-fit, nothing overlaps the artwork, and no overlay or scrim is open in this frame.
entries.recommendation: Inset the left Actions Panel column so the round tool buttons (undo, AI, camera, coloring-book, stroke-width, brush) sit fully inside the viewport with their discs and glyphs whole, reserving the deliberate off-edge docking for the trash button alone.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility hold across the frame. The coloring-page line art is drawn in near-white strokes on the dark charcoal canvas, so every outline — cat, butterfly, clouds, flower, grass — stays crisp and continuous at full size and at small stroke widths (whiskers, fur ticks, the tail spiral). The top color palette renders as fully saturated discs with clear separation from the dark bar behind them; the selected swatch at far left carries a visible ring indicator that reads distinctly against both its own fill and the background, and the white and gray swatches at the right end remain individually distinguishable rather than merging into one another or into the bar. The red trash button at top right has a strong fill against the canvas with a legible white glyph inside the visible portion. In the left-edge Actions Panel, the enabled buttons — the stroke-width/wave glyph and the brush/pencil — show clear filled icons at full contrast, and the coloring-book card button reads plainly; the undo, AI, and screenshot glyphs above them sit at reduced contrast, which is the documented disabled treatment while the canvas has no strokes and not a contrast finding. The collapse chevron above the panel and the settings gear in the opposite bottom corner are faint low-contrast gray glyphs with no disc behind them, exactly as specified; both shapes are locatable in the image, so they clear the findability floor. No overlay or scrim is present, and no text is rendered on this screen, so there is no small-type or on-scrim legibility to fault.

entries.critique:
The frame is otherwise clean. The top color palette fits edge-to-edge with even spacing, no clipping or crowding, and the active purple swatch is clearly ringed; the multicolor picker sits at the right end of the row. The canvas is empty, so there is no overlap, text fit, or hierarchy conflict to assess. The docked round trash button at top right reads at full contrast. Both parent-facing controls are findable: the collapse chevron at bottom left and the settings gear at bottom right are faint by design but their glyph shapes are clearly locatable. No scrim, no scrolling region, no disabled action buttons visible.

Judging the coachmark strictly on what is drawn rather than on whether it explains the gesture: the ghost trash puck with the pointing-hand cursor at center-right is legible. The pink gradient disc, the white trash glyph inside it, and the black-outlined hand are all distinct against the pale paper texture at this size. The weak part is the guide arc. It is a hairline pink stroke that exits the frame at both the top edge and the right edge, so a substantial portion of the drawn path — including wherever it begins and ends — is outside the viewport. What is left on screen is a bare curve with no visible terminus at either end, and its stroke is thin enough relative to the puck that it reads as an unrelated background shape rather than as part of the same mark. There is no caption or label anywhere in the frame, so the arc is the only element carrying the path, and it is the element that is cut.
entries.recommendation: Bring the guide arc fully inside the viewport by insetting its radius and center so both ends terminate on-canvas, and increase or dash its stroke weight so it visibly reads as belonging to the trash puck rather than as a stray background curve.

entries.critique:
Night-mode frame: color palette strip along the top renders at full saturation against the dark chrome, each swatch clearly separated by its dark gap; the selected purple swatch's ring is visible. The docked round trash button at the top right reads strongly — saturated red-pink disc, white trash glyph, high contrast. The chevron at bottom left and the gear at bottom right are both faint gray glyphs but their shapes are locatable in the image, so they meet the findability floor. Canvas is empty and evenly dark with a subtle paper texture; no scrim is present, so all elements are at their normal weight.

On the coachmark itself, judged only on what is drawn: the small trash badge with the white pointing-hand cursor near the center is crisp and legible — the badge's red-orange fill and white glyph separate well from the dark canvas, and the hand's white stroke with its dark outline stays readable where it overlaps the badge. The weak element is the long arc that traces the gesture path. It is a hairline stroke in a desaturated pink (#e0707f-ish) laid on the near-black canvas, and its contrast is marginal: along its upper run (roughly the top third, where it passes through the faint red glow) the line thins and its edges blur into the background, so the path is easier to infer from the brighter lower run than to actually follow. entries.recommendation: Increase the coachmark arc's stroke weight (roughly 1.5–2× current) and lift its lightness/opacity for dark mode so the whole path — including its upper run through the red glow — holds a consistent, clearly visible contrast against the near-black canvas.

entries.critique:
Held-past-threshold state on a mostly empty canvas (one thin lavender stroke). The top palette row, the chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are all locatable and unclipped; the docked red trash button is legible with a clear yellow glyph and a red glow.

The visible problem is the accept ring. It is drawn at a radius so large that only a single arc segment crosses the frame — entering the top edge near x≈600 and exiting the right edge around y≈530 — with its center and most of its circumference outside the viewport. It therefore does not read as a ring, target, or progress indicator; it reads as a stray red curve, and the pale red wash it encloses sits over the empty upper-right corner rather than around the control being acted on. Worse for state legibility, the trash button sits directly on that arc, straddling it, so nothing in the frame communicates that the gesture is inside the accepted region. From this image you cannot tell whether threshold has been crossed — the only threshold cues present (arc, wash) are ambiguous with respect to the button they qualify.

The stated intent describes faint icons washed over the canvas signalling that clearing is underway; no such icons are visible anywhere in the frame, only a flat pale red gradient, so that intended semantic cue is absent at this rendering.

Nothing else: no clipping of interactive content, no overlap, no text to fit, no scrolling region.
entries.recommendation: Scale and position the accept ring so its full circumference is visible and roughly concentric with the trash button, and on threshold fill its interior (with the intended wash icons rendered at visible opacity) so the button reads as unambiguously inside the accepted region rather than sitting on an off-screen arc.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The install banner is legible and well-placed: it sits above the bottom edge, clear of the collapse chevron at bottom-left and the settings glyph at bottom-right, with no overlap or clipping of any control. The "How?" pill and the round × dismiss button are both clearly rendered, comfortably sized as touch targets, and visually distinguished (filled purple primary vs. outlined secondary), so the primary action reads first. Hierarchy inside the card is correct — icon, bold two-line title, lighter subtitle, then actions.

The one visible problem is text fit in the card's text column. On a 1032 px-wide viewport the banner is only about 420 px wide, so both strings wrap badly in the narrow column that remains after the icon and the two buttons: the title breaks as "Add Splotch to your / home screen", and the subtitle breaks as "Opens full-screen, just like a real / app", leaving the orphaned word "app" alone on the last line. That last line also sits very close to the card's bottom border — the space below "app" is visibly tighter than the space above the title, so the block reads bottom-crowded rather than optically centered against the button group beside it. Nothing is truncated or cut off, but the ragged orphan plus the uneven vertical padding make the card look cramped on a display with a large amount of unused horizontal room on either side.
entries.recommendation: Widen the install banner's max-width on tablet-class viewports (or reduce the text column's constraints) so the title and subtitle each fit on a single line without the orphaned "app", and equalize the card's top/bottom padding so the text block is vertically centered against the How?/× button group.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The install banner is a light card sitting on the dark night-mode canvas, so it reads as its own surface. The title "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-black on white and is fully legible. The Splotch logo mark, the "How?" pill (purple label on a light lavender fill) and the "×" close glyph all hold up.

The one contrast problem is the supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app". It is set very small and in a light gray on the white card — noticeably fainter than the title above it and the weakest text in the frame. At this size it thins out and is hard to read at a glance, which matters because it is the line that explains what tapping "How?" actually gets you. Unlike the corner chevron and settings glyphs, this is primary banner copy, not an intentionally recessed parent control, so the quiet treatment is not earned here.

The parent-facing controls are findable: the collapse chevron at bottom-left and the settings gear at bottom-right are both locatable as thin gray glyphs against the dark canvas, which is their intended resting appearance. The palette row along the top edge, the docked trash button, and the purple strokes on the textured dark canvas all separate cleanly from the background in night mode.
entries.recommendation: Darken and slightly enlarge the banner's secondary line ("Opens full-screen, just like a real app") so it reaches at least 4.5:1 against the white card — a mid-to-dark gray at the same or larger size as the "How?" label rather than the current light gray at small size.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique: The expanded Share-sheet guidance tells the user to "Tap ⬆︎ Share at the bottom of the screen," but the capture is an iPad Pro 13-inch in portrait, where Safari's Share control is in the top toolbar. The visible copy directs a parent to the wrong edge of the screen on the very device shown, defeating the purpose of the expanded instructions. Layout itself is sound: the two-line title "Add Splotch to your home screen" clears the "How?" pill and the round close button with no overlap; the inline share, add-to-home, and chevron glyphs sit inline without colliding with surrounding words; the card is fully within the 1032 × 1376 viewport with nothing clipped and no scrolling region in play; the bottom-left chevron and bottom-right gear are both locatable. One minor spacing note: the card's lower edge sits roughly 18 px from the bottom of the frame versus ~305 px of clearance on each side, so it reads pinned rather than placed, though no content is lost.
entries.recommendation: Make the Share-location wording device-aware: on iPad, render "Tap ⬆︎ Share at the top of the screen" (top-right toolbar) rather than the iPhone-specific "at the bottom of the screen," or fall back to a neutral phrasing such as "Tap ⬆︎ Share in the Safari toolbar."

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique: In the expanded install banner, the two-tier text hierarchy holds up unevenly in dark mode. The heading "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white bold and clearly legible; the "How?" pill (white on purple) and the "×" close glyph both read cleanly. Below the divider, the instruction sentence is drawn in two weights: the emphasized fragments ("Add to Home Screen", "View More", "Tap") sit at a bright near-white and read well, but the connective body copy — "Share at the bottom of the screen, then choose", "If you don't see it, tap", "first." — is a mid-gray that sits noticeably closer to the dark card fill than to the emphasized words around it. It is still readable at this size, but it is the weakest text in the frame and is carrying the actual procedural instruction, not decoration. The same mid-gray is used for the subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app", which is the smallest text on the card and the dimmest; at that size the drop in contrast is more felt than in the instruction line. The two inline iOS glyphs (the Share icon and the "+" box) render at roughly that same gray weight and are the least distinct marks on the card, which matters because the instruction depends on the reader matching those shapes to icons on their own device. Everything else here is sound: the card's fill separates clearly from the dark canvas, the border and rounded corners are visible, and the purple strokes on the canvas behind are unaffected. The corner chevron and settings glyph are locatable at bottom-left and bottom-right respectively, and their faintness is the intended resting styling.
entries.recommendation: Lift the mid-gray used for the banner's secondary text — the subtitle and the unemphasized words of the instruction sentence — and for the two inline iOS glyphs, to a lighter gray in dark mode so the connective copy and icon shapes sit closer in weight to the emphasized fragments rather than fading toward the card fill.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
The gate card itself is clean: centered logo, "Grown-Ups Only" title and "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle read clearly, the 8 × 5 = prompt with two dashed answer slots is well aligned, and the 3-column keypad (1–9, then 0 and backspace) has generous, evenly spaced, unambiguous touch targets with no clipping, overlap, or text overflow. The close button sits clear of the logo, and the "Manage these checks in ⚙ Settings › 👪 Parent Center" footer fits on one line above the card edge. No scrolling region is in play — the card fits fully in the viewport with margin above and below.

The one visible problem is the scrim. Every other element in the frame is at full brightness: the color palette across the top is fully saturated, the red trash button at the right edge is at full strength, and the entire left-hand Actions Panel (undo, AI, screenshot, coloring book, stroke width, brush) is crisp and fully contrasted, as is the settings gear at bottom right and the collapse chevron. Nothing behind the card is darkened or blurred. For a modal guarding a sensitive operation this reads as a page with a card floating on it rather than a blocking gate: the drawing tools compete visually with the challenge, and there is no visual signal that the background is inert. The bright, high-chroma palette strip along the top edge in particular pulls attention away from the card, which sits mid-screen against plain white.

Judged on its own the card's contrast and legibility are good — dark title text on white, dark digits on light-gray keys, colored 8 and 5 chips with white numerals all read easily at this size.
entries.recommendation: Apply the same page scrim the other dialogs use to the parent gate — darken and blur the canvas, the top color palette, the trash button, and both corner control clusters behind the card — so the gate reads as blocking and the challenge holds attention.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the parent gate card is broadly sound: the card surface separates well from the dimmed canvas behind it; the "Grown-Ups Only" title, the "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle, all ten white keypad numerals on their dark gray keys, the backspace glyph, and the circular close × are all clearly legible; the gray footer line "Manage these checks in Settings › Parent Center" resolves along with its two inline icons. Both parent-facing corner controls are findable as shapes (collapse chevron above the actions panel, settings gear at bottom right).

The weak point is the equation row. The left operand "9" is white text on a light lavender/orchid disc — the lowest-contrast text in the card, visibly softer than the "8" on the deeper blue disc next to it and softer than every keypad numeral. It is still readable but it is the one element you must look at rather than simply see, and it is a value the parent has to read correctly to pass the gate. The two empty answer slots are faint dashed rings sitting close to the card fill; as empty placeholders that is defensible on its own, but together with the pale left operand it makes the equation line the dimmest band on an otherwise strongly contrasted card.
entries.recommendation: Darken the lavender operand chip's fill in dark mode (or switch its numeral to a dark foreground) so the "9" reaches contrast comparable to the "8" on the blue chip and the white keypad numerals.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The "Pick a style" card itself is clean: two rows of four thumbnails on an even grid, consistent tile size and gutters, labels ("Magical", "Crayon", "Watercolor", "Paper", "Felt", "Sticker", "Cartoon", "Clay") fully legible with no truncation, wrapping, or overlap, and no clipping at the card edges. The close button is a clearly bounded, comfortably sized circular target in the top-right, and all eight tiles read as generously sized touch targets. No fade strip is visible on the card, and all eight options fit without scrolling, so nothing is hidden.

The one visible problem is the scrim. The canvas, the docked trash button, the bottom-corner Actions Panel buttons, the chevron, and the settings glyph are all clearly darkened and pushed back behind the dialog — but the color palette strip along the top edge is not. Its sixteen swatches render at full saturation and full brightness, with crisp white ring highlighting on the selected purple swatch and the multicolor picker at the right, visibly brighter and more contrasty than anything else outside the card. On a page where every other background element has been dimmed, that untreated strip becomes the second-most visually assertive thing in the frame after the dialog itself, competing with "Pick a style" for the eye and undercutting the modal's claim on attention. The mismatch also reads as an inconsistency in how the overlay is applied, since the same scrim plainly reaches every other background region.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the top color-palette strip so it dims and blurs along with the canvas and corner controls, rather than rendering at full brightness above the overlay.

entries.critique: The open "Pick a style" card is the element to judge here, and its night-mode contrast holds up. The header "Pick a style" and all eight style labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) are near-white on the card's dark charcoal surface, crisp and easily read at a glance. The card itself is a lighter panel than the near-black page behind it, so its edges are clearly defined. The eight thumbnails are full-brightness illustrations that stay distinguishable from one another — the moon/sun, cloud, tree, and hill shapes remain readable in every tile, including the darker Crayon and Paper renderings. The current selection (Sticker) is marked with a bright white outline that reads unambiguously against both the thumbnail and the card. The close button in the top-right is a gray ✕ inside a thin ringed circle; it is dimmer than the card text but the glyph and its ring are clearly locatable and separate from the surface, adequate for a non-text control. On the page outside the card, the top color palette, the trash button, and the corner button stack are all still findable; the reduced-contrast undo/AI/screenshot buttons in the Actions Panel are the documented disabled state, and the chevron above the panel and the settings glyph in the bottom-right corner are both locatable in the image, which is the only floor those two owe. No legibility failure visible.
