entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: The AI "Making your picture…" dialog lays a scrim over the page, but coverage is incomplete. The canvas and the two bottom-corner parent controls are visibly darkened and blurred, yet the color palette strip along the top edge and the round red trash button on the right render at full brightness and saturation — the swatches are vivid, the multicolor palette button is crisp, and the trash disc is the most saturated element in the frame besides the progress dial. Against the uniformly dimmed remainder of the page this breaks the "open card holds attention" intent: the eye is pulled to the top strip and the right edge, and those controls read as still live while a blocking dialog is up. Separately, the preview card is a roughly 1050px-tall near-empty white panel containing only the centered dial and a faint blurred title band near the top; no drawing preview is discernible, so the card reads as a large empty box with substantial dead space above and below the spinner. Text fit is clean throughout — "Making your picture…", the 30-second subline, and the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill are all fully legible with adequate spacing, and the close button in the top-right corner is a clear, unambiguous target. No clipping, overlap, or truncation is visible.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog's scrim to cover the top color-palette strip and the trash button the same way it covers the canvas and bottom-corner controls, so every element behind the AI card is uniformly darkened and the open card is the only thing at full contrast.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: Judging only the open AI card and what is drawn on top of the scrim: the heading "Making your picture…" is near-white on the dark panel and reads cleanly; the secondary line "This takes about 30 seconds" sits a step down in gray but remains legible; the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill is white text on saturated purple with adequate separation; the close button's white × and ring stand out against the dark panel. Both parent-facing corner glyphs (chevron bottom-left, gear bottom-right) are locatable in frame, and the docked trash button is unaffected. The one night-mode legibility weakness is the progress dial: the completed and remaining sectors are pink and purple-magenta at very similar lightness, distinguished only by a thin dark hairline, and a heavy magenta bloom around the disc further softens that edge against the dark card. The result is that the amount of progress is difficult to read at a glance — the state is inferable only from the hairline's angle rather than from any luminance difference between the two halves. Impact is limited because the accompanying text conveys the expected duration.
entries.recommendation: In dark mode, give the progress dial's remaining sector a distinctly darker, desaturated fill (or drop it to a low-opacity track) so the completed arc separates from it by luminance, not hue, and reduce the surrounding magenta glow so the boundary between the two sectors stays crisp.

entries.critique:
The AI result card reads well on its own: the generated image is large and uncropped, the white card frames it with even margins, the circled × sits clear of image detail in the top-right corner, and the "Download" pill and the "AI-generated picture · Report" caption below the card are legible with comfortable touch sizing. entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog's scrim over the top color-palette strip and the trash button so the whole page behind the AI result card is darkened uniformly, as it already is over the canvas and bottom-corner controls.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
Judging only what the night-mode scrim leaves in scope: the open AI result card and the footer row drawn on top of the scrim.

The card itself holds up. The generated picture is bright and fully legible; the round close button at its top-right is a white glyph on a dark disc with a light ring, cleanly separated from the busy sky behind it; the "Download" pill is white text and icon on saturated purple against the card's near-black surface — a strong, unambiguous target.

The weak spot is the footer line under the card: "AI-generated picture · Report". Both parts are small and muted on the near-black page. The label reads as mid-gray on black, and "Report" plus its flag glyph are a desaturated red on that same black — red is the worst-performing hue at low luminance on a dark ground, and here it carries an actionable control, not decorative text. It is the least legible element in the frame and the one thing a parent may need to find and act on. This is not the deliberate quiet parent-facing styling of the chevron and gear (both of which I can locate, bottom-left and bottom-right); it is a labeled text link inside the result card's own content flow, so it owes normal small-text contrast.

Nothing else: the scrimmed palette strip, trash button, chevron, and gear all read as the intended scrim or quiet styling rather than contrast faults.
entries.recommendation: Raise the footer row's contrast on the near-black surface: lighten "AI-generated picture" toward a light gray, and re-tone the "Report" link and flag glyph from desaturated red to a lighter red/salmon (or light gray text with a red flag) so both clear ~4.5:1 at that small size in dark mode.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Layout, spacing, and text fit inside the confirmation card are sound: the title, the retention paragraph, the two labelled thumbnails, and the Cancel / Send report pair all sit on a consistent left margin with even gaps, no clipping, wrapping, or overlap, and both buttons are comfortably sized for touch. The primary action is correctly the filled purple one.

The visible problem is separation. This confirmation dialog is drawn directly onto the AI result image at full brightness — the cat, mug, and background village are fully saturated and detailed right up to the card's edge, and the surrounding result card, its close button, the Download button, the "AI-generated picture · Report" bar, and the top color palette are all still at full strength. Nothing behind this dialog is darkened or blurred, so the white card is competing with a high-contrast, high-detail photograph rather than resting on a calmed page. The card carries no visible border or shadow edge either, so its boundary against the light mug and pale background at the lower left is faint. Given that every other overlay in this app dims the page behind it, this second-level dialog reads as the one confirmation that does not claim focus — and it is the one asking for an irreversible send.

Secondary: the two thumbnails are unequal in weight — the left one is a full-bleed image, the right is a nearly blank white tile with a single thin stroke and no border against the white card, so "The drawing behind it" reads as a missing or failed thumbnail rather than a sparse drawing.
entries.recommendation: Apply the app's standard dim-and-blur scrim behind this confirmation dialog so the AI image, result card, Download button, and top palette recede, and give the empty-looking "drawing behind it" thumbnail a light border or tinted background so it reads as a real preview.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal card itself reads well: palette emoji, bold headline, two-line body, a quiet "For grown-ups" label, and a pill-shaped "Report this refusal" button in a clear hierarchy, with a 44px circled close button in the top-right that has ample clearance from the text. Text fits on its lines with no clipping, wrapping, or overlap; the card needs no scrolling.

The visible problem is the scrim. The canvas behind the dialog is darkened, but the top color-swatch row and the round red trash button are not — they render at full saturation against the dimmed page, so sixteen bright color discs and a strong red circle sit at the very top of the frame competing with the modal for attention. In this frame the brightest, highest-contrast elements on screen are behind the dialog, not in it. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are locatable, and the intended dimming reaches the canvas, so this is specifically the top strip escaping the overlay's darkening rather than the scrim being absent.

Secondary: the dialog is horizontally centered but vertically centered on the page, which places it just below the stray purple stroke; that is fine. Card interior padding is slightly bottom-light — the button sits about 45px above the card's lower edge versus ~40px of top inset above the close button — but the imbalance is minor and not actionable on its own.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full viewport so the top color-palette row and the trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, matching the treatment already applied to the rest of the page behind the card.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the refusal card is mostly sound: the "Let's try drawing something else!" heading reads as near-white on the dark card surface, the two-line body copy ("That picture didn't work — try drawing something different!") is clearly legible, the circular close button's ring and × are visible against the card, and the "Report this refusal" button carries white label text on a muted purple fill with enough separation to read at a glance.

The one weak element is the small "For grown-ups" caption between the body copy and the button. It is rendered at a noticeably smaller size than the body text and in a dim mid-gray that sits only a little above the card's own dark fill — visibly the lowest-contrast text in the card, and it dims further rather than holding up because it is the smallest type in the frame. Unlike the corner chevron and settings glyphs, this is a text label inside the open dialog, so the card's own legibility floor applies to it. It is still findable, but it reads as faded rather than deliberately quiet, and it is the label that tells a parent the button below it is the adult-facing action.

No other night-mode contrast problem is visible: the color palette along the top edge keeps each swatch distinguishable from the dark ground and from its neighbours, the selected first swatch shows a clear light selection ring, the trash button at the top right reads at full strength, and the purple stroke on the canvas is plainly visible against the near-black background. The bottom-corner chevron and settings glyphs are faint but locatable, which is their intended resting appearance.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "For grown-ups" caption on the refusal card to a lighter gray with clear separation from the card fill (or bump it to the body-copy size), so the smallest text in the dialog meets the same night-mode legibility floor as the heading and body lines.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique:
The server-error card is centered over a scrimmed canvas: 😕 emoji, "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!", and a circular ✕ close button top-right. Text fit, clipping, and overlap are clean, and the ✕ is a clearly sized, well-separated target.

Two visible issues. First, the scrim is incomplete: the canvas and both bottom-corner glyphs are darkened, but the entire color palette strip along the top edge and the red trash button render at full brightness and saturation. They read as live and tappable while a modal is open, and the palette is the highest-contrast, most attention-grabbing element in the frame — competing with the card it should be sitting behind, rather than receding with the rest of the page.

Second, the card is bottom-heavy: the emoji and message sit in the upper portion, with roughly 90px of empty white beneath the text and nothing in it. Combined with copy that says "Please try again!" while offering only a close button, the empty region reads as a missing action — the instruction has no target, and dismissing returns the child to the canvas with no path back to the AI action.
entries.recommendation: Extend the modal scrim over the top color palette and the trash button so the whole page behind the card is dimmed consistently with the other dialogs, and place a primary "Try again" button in the card's empty lower region so the copy's instruction has an actual control.

entries.critique: Layout is clean and fits the 1032×1376 portrait viewport with no clipping, overlap, or truncated text; the warning banner, code chip, and metric values all render fully. Three polish issues are visible. (1) Table row actions are inconsistent and touch-unfriendly: "Copy" is a bordered pill while "Copy link" and "Remove" are bare text links at similar size with no visible hit area, and "Remove" — the destructive action — is the weakest-styled and sits only ~10px from its neighbor. (3) Section-label spacing is uneven: "ACCESS CODES · 2" has clear space above it, but "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" is pressed against the bottom of the table's last row, so it reads as attached to the section above it rather than the one below.
entries.recommendation: Give the row actions consistent, touch-sized affordances — render "Copy link" and "Remove" as bordered buttons matching "Copy" (min ~44px tap height, extra gap and destructive color on "Remove") — and add top margin to the "FREE GENERATION GRANTS" label matching the "ACCESS CODES" label; separately, set the metric grid to a column count that divides 7 evenly enough to avoid a lone orphan tile (e.g. 4 per row).

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Judging night-mode contrast and legibility only.

Core body content holds up well: the "Admin" heading, "Manage AI access codes", the monospace code values (daycare-club, page-inventory-harness), the large metric numerals, the "Add code" and "Sign out" buttons, and the "Back to drawing" link all read cleanly as light-on-dark.

Two problems are visible:

1. Un-themed light surfaces. Both alert panels — the "Netlify Blobs is unavailable…" warning and the "Free grant monitoring is using local memory…" notice — render as near-white cream cards with dark brown/amber text on an otherwise near-black page. Text inside them is legible, but they are clearly light-theme components never given a dark treatment: they are by far the brightest regions in the frame and dominate the page in night mode, reading as glare panels on a dark-adapted screen. The cream fill also swallows the ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST inline code chip, whose light-gray pill on cream is the weakest text in either banner.

2. Section divider labels are too faint. "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" are small, letter-spaced, all-caps gray glyphs on the dark card — the dimmest text on the page, visibly below the contrast of everything around them; at this size and tracking they are hard to read rather than merely quiet. The thin rules beside them are similarly near-invisible. Secondary metric labels ("Sampled successes", "Sampled in flight", etc.) are dimmer than ideal but still comfortably readable.

The table header row ("CODE" / "ACTIONS") is dim but legible; the "Copy link" and "Remove" text actions are adequately contrasted.
entries.recommendation: Give the two alert banners a dark-mode variant — deep amber-tinted fill with a warm border and light amber text instead of the cream light-theme card — and restyle the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST chip to match; then lift the section divider labels ("ACCESS CODES · 2", "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0") to a gray meeting at least 4.5:1 against the card background.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
In the Actions column, the focused "Copy link" control on the daycare-club row is drawn with a hard black rectangular focus ring sitting directly on the label's bounding box with no padding or offset: the left and right edges of the ring cut across the "C" and the final "k", so the focused text visibly collides with its own indicator. It is the one focused control in the frame and the worst-looking element as a result — the unfocused "Copy link" in the row below reads cleanly. The ring style also matches nothing else here: "Copy" is a rounded purple-outlined pill, while this indicator is a square high-contrast black box.

Related: "Copy link" and "Remove" are bare text at roughly body size, beside a "Copy" that is a real bordered button. On a 1032 px-wide tablet these two secondary/destructive actions have no visible hit area — the only size cue is the glyph height of the words — and "Remove" is the most consequential of the three with the weakest affordance.

Everything else holds up: header, both warning banners, section rules, the add-code row, table headers, and the stat cards are legible with adequate spacing, no clipping, no overlap, and text fits its containers. The seven stat cards wrapping to a second row with the last left-aligned is normal grid behavior, not a defect.
entries.recommendation: Give the text actions a proper focus treatment and hit area: replace the tight black rectangle with a rounded focus ring offset ~2–3 px in the app's purple accent, and give "Copy link" and "Remove" the same padded, ≥44 px-tall tappable box as the "Copy" button so the ring sits outside the label and the touch targets are visible.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast is mostly sound: the page uses near-white body text and headings on a very dark charcoal panel, the "Admin" title, "Manage AI access codes", column headers, code values in monospace, and the stat-card labels and numerals all read cleanly. Sign out and Add code are white-on-purple pills with adequate separation, and the focused "Copy link" ring is a bright white outline that is unmistakable against the dark row.

The one real contrast problem is the pair of light-cream notice banners, which are the only light surfaces in an otherwise dark UI. Within them the amber/orange text is the weak part: the second banner's entire line ("Free grant monitoring is using local memory and will reset with this server instance.") is a warm orange on a pale cream field and visibly washes out — it is the lowest-contrast running text in the frame and reads noticeably fainter than the dark-brown sentences in the first banner. In the first banner the same orange is used for the bold lead-in "Netlify Blobs is unavailable." and for the inline `ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST` code token; the bold weight partly rescues the lead-in, but the code token is small, letter-spaced monospace in that same weak orange and is the hardest string on the page to resolve. These banners also carry the most consequential information on the screen (changes will not persist), so the weakest text is attached to the highest-stakes message.

Secondary, lower-impact: the "Copy link" label sits as a muted gray-lavender directly beside the outlined "Copy" button and the pink "Remove", so within one action cluster three different text weights compete; "Copy link" is the dimmest of the three and reads as if it were the disabled one, though it is still legible. The "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" section eyebrows are also dim small-caps gray, but they are structural labels and remain findable.
entries.recommendation: Darken the amber text inside the two cream notice banners to a deep amber/brown that clears 4.5:1 against the cream fill — apply it to the full sentence in the free-grant banner, the bold "Netlify Blobs is unavailable." lead-in, and especially the inline `ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST` code token, which as small letter-spaced monospace should be the darkest of the three.

entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique:
Blank canvas with a left-edge palette column (2x5 grid: purple selected with a ring, blue, teal, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, black, and a multicolor more-colors swatch), the docked round trash button at the right edge, the expand chevron at the bottom-left of the canvas area, and the settings gear at the bottom-right. Hierarchy reads correctly: the saturated swatches and the red trash button dominate, and the two parent-facing glyphs sit back as intended while remaining findable. Swatch spacing is even in both axes, the grid is vertically centered with comparable top and bottom margins, and no swatch is clipped by the bottom or left edge. The selection ring on the active purple swatch is clearly distinguishable. Touch targets are generous, roughly 64px across with clear separation. The trash button's overhang past the right edge is the documented docked state, not clipping. No text is present, so no fit or truncation risk; no overlap between the palette column and the canvas, and the chevron and gear sit clear of the palette and of each other. No overlay or scrim is open, so there is no modal scrolling to assess. Nothing in this frame is actionable.</critique>

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: Single centered card on a light gray page. Hierarchy is clear and correctly ordered: "Back to drawing" link top-left in purple, the color-dot mark with "SPLOTCH ADMIN" top-right, a large bold "Admin" heading, a "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, then a "SIGN IN" section label with a rule, and a row holding the "Admin access key" input and a purple "Sign in" button. Spacing is even and generous with no crowding and no overlap. All text fits on one line with no truncation or wrapping. The input and button share a baseline and matched heights, and the button label is centered with adequate padding. Touch targets read clearly: the field and the "Sign in" button are both comfortably tall for a finger, and the back link sits clear of other hit areas. Contrast is adequate throughout: near-black heading and subtitle on white, readable mid-gray placeholder and section label, white on saturated purple for the button. The rounded card is inset with page background visible left, right, and top, so the layout has adapted to the short landscape viewport rather than being squeezed. entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in surface is largely sound: "Admin" is near-white on the dark card, "Manage AI access codes" is a light gray that stays comfortably legible, the "Sign in" button uses white on a saturated purple fill, and the input's border is visible against the card. entries.critique: At its opening position in landscape (812 × 375), the page shows only chrome: back link, page logo, an oversized "Changelog" title, a two-line description, a large empty gap, and the collapsed CONTENTS row. Not a single release entry — the actual content of the page — is visible, and the CONTENTS card sits right at the bottom edge with nothing after it, so there is no visual evidence that anything follows. entries.recommendation: At short viewport heights (landscape phones), compress the changelog header — reduce the title size and the gap between the description block and the CONTENTS card — so at least the first release entry is partly visible at the opening scroll position.

entries.critique: At the opening position the styleguide reads cleanly at 812×375. The header row (Light/Dark segmented toggle, "Design system" label, and the swatch-dot + SPLOTCH wordmark) sits on one line with clear separation and no crowding or overlap; the active "Light" segment is distinguished from "Dark" by both fill and weight. The Contents card spans the full width with even internal padding, and "16 sections ›" is right-aligned in link color within a row tall enough to tap unambiguously. Below the divider, hierarchy is clear: a small purple "← Back to drawing" link, a large bold H1, a two-line body paragraph at comfortable measure and leading, then a smaller de-emphasized sources line. Type ramp, color use, and vertical rhythm are consistent across both bands. No clipping, truncation, or overlap is visible; the paragraph wraps naturally and the monospaced source paths sit inline without breaking the line box. The sources line sits at the bottom edge of the viewport with its trailing text ending short of the right margin — tight, but not cut. Nothing in the frame shows an actionable text-fit, contrast, spacing, or touch-target defect.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: In this 812 × 375 landscape frame the whole viewport is spent on chrome and preamble: the back link, the "Send us feedback" display heading, a three-line explanatory paragraph, and the Something's broken / I have an idea segmented control. The first actual input appears only as a sliver of a field edge clipped by the bottom of the frame, so nothing the user came here to fill in is reachable without scrolling. Hierarchy, alignment, and spacing within what is shown are clean — generous left margin, consistent gutters, the heading clearly dominant, the paragraph fully wrapped with no clipping or overlap, and the toggle is a full-width two-up control with a clear selected state and comfortable touch height. But the type scale and vertical rhythm are tuned for portrait; at 375px tall the header block alone consumes the entire screen. The unselected "I have an idea" label is also noticeably lighter than the selected label on its gray track, weakening the read that it is a tappable alternative rather than a disabled half of the control. No other text-fit, clipping, or overlap problems are visible, and no overlay or scrim is present in this capture to judge.
entries.recommendation: Add a short-viewport treatment (e.g. a max-height/landscape media query) that reduces the heading size and the paragraph/section margins — or collapses the intro copy — so at 375px tall the segmented control and at least the first form field sit above the fold; while there, darken the unselected segment's label so it reads as selectable rather than disabled.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this frame is mostly healthy. The "Send us feedback" heading is near-white on the near-black card and reads crisply; the intro paragraph is a light warm-gray on the same card and stays fully legible at this size; the "← Back to drawing" link is a saturated violet that separates cleanly from the dark ground for a bold, above-body-size label; the SPLOTCH wordmark and its dot row are small but distinct.

The one visible weakness is the inactive half of the segmented toggle. The unselected "I have an idea" segment sits on a light-mid gray track, and its label is rendered in a muted gray only a step or two off that track — noticeably fainter than "Something's broken" on the selected dark segment beside it, and the weakest text in the frame despite being a primary form control that the user must read to choose a submission type. Unlike the deliberately recessed parent-facing glyphs described for the drawing screen, this is a main content-area choice on a standalone form, so low contrast here is not intentional recession; it reads as an unselected-state color that was tuned against a light-theme track and carried into night mode unchanged. The label is still readable, so this is a shortfall rather than a failure.

Nothing else in the visible area is an actionable contrast issue: the thinning of content along the bottom edge is the scroll-fade cue being drawn, and I have judged only the content sitting clear of it.
entries.recommendation: Raise the unselected segment label ("I have an idea") to a near-white or high-luminance gray against its lighter track in dark mode so it reaches at least 4.5:1, keeping the selected/unselected distinction carried by the track fill rather than by dimming the text.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this opening view is broadly sound. The "Privacy policy" heading and the intro paragraph render as near-white/light-gray on the dark charcoal card and are crisply legible; the "No ads. Ever. None." card text is likewise strong, with the red pill accent clearly visible. The "SPLOTCH" wordmark and its color dots read cleanly.

The one weak spot is the "← Back to drawing" link in the top-left: it is set in a saturated mid-purple on the near-black page background. Purple is the darkest-luminance hue available, and at this weight/size the link sits noticeably below the luminance of every other piece of text in the frame — it is the only element I have to look at directly to resolve rather than read at a glance. It is the primary navigation affordance on the page, so it should not be the dimmest text present.

Secondary, lower-confidence: the "Last updated August 20, 2026" line and the thin horizontal rule beside "THE SHORT VERSION" are quite low in contrast, though as tertiary metadata and a decorative divider that is defensible.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the dark-theme color of the "← Back to drawing" link (raise the purple's luminance toward the lighter tint used for the palette dots, or use the near-white body color with purple reserved for hover/focus) so the link meets at least the body text's contrast against the dark background.

entries.critique: In the 375px-tall landscape viewport the entire visible frame is chrome-plus-intro: back link, SPLOTCH BETA wordmark, a large "Join the Splotch beta" H1, a two-line lede, and the tab row. entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the visible frame is mostly sound: the "Join the Splotch beta" heading renders near-white on the dark card and is fully legible; the intro paragraph is a light gray that stays comfortably readable at this size; the active "Android" tab and its underline are a saturated purple that separates clearly from the panel, and the inactive "iPhone / iPad" tab with its device glyph is dimmer but still plainly readable as a secondary state. The "Back to drawing" link and the palette dots plus "SPLOTCH BETA" wordmark in the header both hold up against the black background.

The one weak point is the section eyebrow "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" at the bottom of the frame. It is set in small, widely letterspaced uppercase in a dark gray that sits only slightly above the card background — noticeably fainter than the horizontal rule directly above it, which itself is a hairline. Small caps with wide tracking already lose stroke mass, and at this size the label is hard to read without deliberate effort. Nothing in the frame indicates this is a faded scroll edge: there is no gradient thinning across it, the divider above it is crisp, and the text is uniformly dim rather than washed out toward the edge, so this reads as the label's own styling rather than an edge cue.
entries.recommendation: Raise the section-eyebrow color ("HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID") in dark mode to at least the same gray as the intro paragraph, or bump its weight, so the small letterspaced uppercase clears a readable contrast ratio against the near-black card.

No page behind an overlay, no scrim, and no corner controls appear in this crop, so nothing else is in scope.

entries.critique: The error screen renders cleanly at 812 × 375. A purple blob mark, the "Oops!" heading, a one-sentence explanation, and a single "Start over" pill button are stacked centered on a light gray ground, with the whole group vertically centered and comfortably clear of both the top and bottom edges. Hierarchy is unambiguous: large bold heading, smaller gray body copy, then the only interactive element rendered as a filled high-contrast purple pill — clearly the sole call to action. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping; the measure of the body copy is constrained so it wraps to two lines rather than running the full landscape width, which keeps it readable. The button is generously sized and padded, well above a comfortable touch target in this short-height landscape viewport, and separated from the copy by clear space. Contrast on the heading (near-black on near-white), the body line (mid-gray, still legible at this size), and the white-on-purple button label all read fine. No overlay or scrim is present, nothing scrolls or needs a fade cue, and no corner controls appear in this frame to assess. The only mildly awkward detail is the body copy's line break leaving "drawing." alone on the second line, which is a typographic nicety rather than an actionable defect. Nothing here warrants a finding.

entries.critique:
The compact landscape Settings card is clean and well-fit: title, close button, and the 2×2 grid of controls all sit inside the card with even gutters, no clipping, no overlap, and no text truncation. "Sound", "Night Mode", and "Advanced Controls" each pair an icon, a label, and a toggle at consistent heights, and the helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." is legible and clearly subordinate. The scrim over the palette, canvas, trash button, chevron, and settings gear is the expected dialog treatment, and both orientation segments being unfilled matches the unlocked-rotation state described.

The one actionable gap is labeling of the fourth cell. The other three cells state what they control in words ("Sound", "Night Mode", "Advanced Controls") next to a toggle; the fourth cell instead holds a bare Portrait/Landscape segmented control with no label naming what it does. Nothing visible in the card says these segments lock rotation rather than, say, switch the current view — and because neither segment is filled, the group also has no selected-state anchor to infer meaning from. Occupying a slot in a grid that otherwise reads as label-plus-switch makes the omission more noticeable, not less. Touch targets themselves are fine: both segments are full-height and comfortably wide.

Secondary, smaller: the segment labels and their glyphs render in a mid-gray on the light gray segment field, visibly lighter than the black row labels beside them. In the unselected resting state that is defensible, but it is the weakest text on an un-scrimmed card surface.
entries.recommendation: Add a short label to the fourth cell — e.g. "Rotation Lock" set in the same style and position as "Sound" and "Advanced Controls", with the Portrait/Landscape segments to its right — so the control's purpose is stated even while neither segment is active.

A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation. Captured in light mode on iPhone 13 mini in landscape at 812 × 375. Assess visible hierarchy, spacing, text fit, clipping, overlap, touch-target clarity, modal scrolling, and visual consistency. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.

entries.critique: The compact phone-landscape Settings shell renders cleanly at 812 x 375. The card is centered with even padding, the "Settings" title and the round close button sit clear of each other, and the 2x2 grid of control tiles is evenly gutted with consistent tile heights and radii. "Sound", "Night Mode", and "Advanced Controls" all fit on one line with no truncation, clipping, or collision with their toggles; the toggles are full-size and unambiguously on/off. The Portrait/Landscape segmented control shows both segments inactive, matching the stated intent for unlocked rotation, and both labels with their icons fit inside the track. The helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." is fully legible and sits inside the card with breathing room above its bottom edge. Nothing is cut off - the card ends well short of the viewport, and no region needs to scroll. Behind the scrim, the palette column, the docked trash button, the expand chevron at bottom-left, and the settings glyph at bottom-right are each locatable. No overlap, text-fit, or touch-target ambiguity found.

entries.surface_intent: When this image shows the compact phone-landscape Settings shell, its Portrait and Landscape orientation segments are both inactive while screen rotation is unlocked. A segment becomes active only after the parent locks rotation to that orientation.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the Settings card is broadly sound: "Settings", "Sound", "Night Mode", and "Advanced Controls" render as near-white on the dark card and read cleanly, and the purple/white toggles remain clearly distinguishable in their on state. The close (×) button in the top-right sits on a lighter circular disc and is legible.

The weak spot is the Portrait / Landscape orientation segment. Both segments are inactive per design intent, but their labels and small device icons are drawn in a mid-gray that sits on a segment panel only slightly lighter than the card, so they read appreciably fainter than every other label on the same card and their icon glyphs in particular lose definition. Since inactive here is the normal resting state (rotation unlocked), this is the state a parent sees most of the time, and it is the only control in the card whose label falls off in legibility.

The helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." is also dimmer than the card's other text, but it remains readable as a secondary caption and is not itself actionable.

Backgrounds outside the card (palette, chevron, gear, trash) are under the dialog scrim and out of scope; the chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable in the frame.
entries.recommendation: Raise the inactive Portrait/Landscape segment label and icon color in dark mode (toward the same near-white used for "Sound"/"Advanced Controls", at reduced opacity rather than a flat mid-gray) so the resting inactive state still clears text contrast, and keep the active state distinguished by the segment fill rather than by label brightness alone.

The docked trash button at the right edge and the faint chevron and settings glyphs at the bottom corners are both locatable and consistent with the settled decisions for this app.

entries.critique:
The Settings card renders well in night mode: the "Settings" title and the row labels (Sound, Advanced Controls, Night Mode) are near-white on the dark card and read cleanly, the purple/white toggles are unambiguous in their on state, and the close ✕ in its circular well is clearly visible. The scrim over the page behind is expected and the canvas/palette dimming below it is not judged.

The one soft spot is the Portrait / Landscape segmented control. Its two labels and their small device glyphs are the dimmest elements on the card — a mid-gray on a lighter-gray segment track, a much narrower separation than every other label on the same surface. They remain readable, but they sit noticeably below the card's own text standard, and the glyphs in particular start to fade into the track. Both segments being unselected is the intended resting state here, so this is only about the tone of the inactive label, not about which one is active.

The helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." is gray on the card ground but is a secondary hint and stays legible at this size, with its small phone glyph resolving fine.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground tone of the inactive Portrait/Landscape segment labels and their glyphs in night mode so they meet the same text contrast as the other row labels on the card, keeping the selected state distinguished by the segment's fill rather than by the label being dimmed.

Text fits its containers — "Advanced Controls", "Night Mode", and the footer line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." all sit on one line with no truncation, wrapping, or overlap. The 2×2 grid of control cells has even gutters and consistent rounded-rect treatment; toggles are right-aligned within their cells and read unambiguously as on (purple) versus off (gray). The Portrait/Landscape segmented control shows both segments in the inactive gray state, which is the documented resting appearance while rotation is unlocked, and its icon+label pairs are legible and non-clipped. Touch targets are comfortable: the toggles, the two orientation segments, and the close button each occupy generously sized hit areas with margin between them, and nothing crowds the card edge. No content is cut off at the card boundary, no scrolling region is implied or needed, and the parent-facing chevron and gear glyphs remain locatable in the lower corners despite the scrim. No actionable visible issue.

entries.critique:
The frame shows the compact phone-landscape Settings card over a dimmed, blurred canvas, so only the card and what sits on top of the scrim are in scope. Card contrast is generally sound in night mode: "Settings" and the row labels ("Sound", "Night Mode", "Advanced Controls") are near-white on the dark card and read cleanly, the purple/white toggles are unambiguous in their on state, and the close button's × is clearly visible against its lighter disc. The parent-facing chevron and gear glyphs in the bottom corners are faint by design and both remain locatable, so no finding there.

The weak spot is the muted text at the bottom right of the card. The "Portrait" and "Landscape" segment labels — correctly inactive here, since rotation is unlocked — are a mid-gray on the segment's mid-dark fill, and their small leading icons are dimmer still, sitting close to where small text stops being comfortably readable. The helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." with its small phone icon is likewise a dim gray on the card background at a small type size; it is the only instruction explaining why the full settings are absent, so it carries real weight and is the least legible text in the card. Inactive styling can stay clearly recessed relative to the active white labels while still clearing a comfortable contrast floor for small text; as drawn, both lean further down than that state needs.
entries.recommendation: Lift the night-mode foreground of the inactive Portrait/Landscape segment labels (and their icons) and of the "Switch to portrait for the full settings." helper line to a lighter gray that clears a comfortable small-text contrast floor against their dark fills, keeping them recessed from the active white row labels by tone rather than by dropping to a near-illegible gray.

The card's primary content holds up: "Settings", "Sound", "Night Mode" and "Advanced Controls" are near-white on the dark card, the purple toggle tracks with white knobs read unambiguously as on, and the close button's × is clear against its disc. entries.recommendation: Raise the night-mode brightness of the "Switch to portrait for the full settings." hint (and the Portrait/Landscape segment glyphs) by a step or two — at least up to the gray used for the inactive segment labels rather than below it — so the shell's only wayfinding instruction is not the lowest-contrast text on the card.

entries.critique:
The compact phone-landscape Settings shell renders correctly: the card is centered, the title and close button are well separated, the four rows fit within the card with even gutters, and no label is clipped or wrapped. "Advanced Controls", "Night Mode", and the helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." all fit on one line. Portrait and Landscape orientation segments both read as inactive against the shared gray track, which matches the stated unlocked-rotation state. Toggle pills and the segmented control are comfortably sized for touch, and the card clears the top and bottom edges of the 375px-tall viewport with margin to spare.

One inconsistency against the scrim behavior visible in the frame: the page behind the dialog is clearly darkened — the canvas is flat gray and the left-edge color swatches are visibly muted — yet the round trash button at the top right retains full-strength red fill with a bright yellow glyph, and the multi-color palette swatch at the bottom left also stays saturated. Those two elements sit at a higher apparent brightness than everything else behind the scrim, so the eye is pulled to the top-right corner while the Settings card is open. The chevron and the settings gear glyph are both locatable in the bottom corners as expected.
entries.recommendation: Apply the dialog scrim uniformly over the trash button and the multi-color palette swatch so they are darkened to the same degree as the rest of the page behind the Settings card, instead of remaining at full saturation above it.

entries.critique: Landscape drawing screen with the color palette as a left rail, canvas filling the rest, docked round trash button top-right, quiet chevron at the left-panel edge and quiet settings glyph bottom-right. Hierarchy reads correctly: the saturated swatches and the red trash button are the loud elements, the purple stroke is legible on the paper texture, and the two parent-facing glyphs are faint by design but both locatable (chevron beside the rail at mid-left, gear cog bottom-right). Swatch rows are evenly spaced in a 2-column grid with consistent diameters and gutters; the selected purple swatch carries a clear ring, and the last row (black + multicolor picker) sits fully inside the viewport with breathing room below — no clipping. No text is present to fit or truncate, no overlapping controls, and every tappable element is a large round target well clear of its neighbors. entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
In this landscape frame the color palette runs down the left edge as a two-column grid, and its last row — the black swatch and the multicolor/rainbow swatch — is cut horizontally by the bottom edge of the viewport. Roughly the lower quarter of both circles is missing, and the cut is a hard edge: there is no softening, thinning, or gradient over that last row, so it does not read as this app's scroll-fade cue. It reads as the grid overflowing the 375px height. Two swatches, one of them the black and one the special multicolor picker, are left as partial targets whose full extent and hit area are ambiguous, and if more rows exist below there is no visible signal of them.

Everything else in the frame holds up. The six round action buttons (brush, stroke width, coloring book, camera, AI, undo) sit in an evenly spaced row with consistent size, generous gaps, and white discs that separate cleanly from the paper texture; none overlap the palette column or each other, and none are clipped. The undo glyph is at full orange strength, consistent with a stroke being present on the canvas. The collapse chevron left of the panel and the settings gear in the opposite corner are both locatable as thin gray glyphs. The docked trash button reads as intended at the top-right. No text is present to fit or truncate, and no scrim is in play, so the canvas and palette are at full brightness as expected.
entries.recommendation: Fit the palette grid to the landscape viewport height — shrink the swatch size or reflow to more columns — so the bottom row is not sliced by the screen edge, and if the grid must scroll, apply the standard soft gradient fade over that last row instead of a hard cut.

entries.critique: The brush flyout renders cleanly. Four tools — pen, crayon, paintbrush, eraser — sit in a single white rounded card with even internal padding and consistent gaps; the selected pen carries a lavender fill and purple border that reads unambiguously as the active state against the three unselected glyphs. Each tile is roughly square and comfortably above a thumb-sized target, and the tiles are separated enough that adjacent taps are distinguishable. The card is horizontally aligned with the Actions Panel below it and clears it with visible vertical space, so nothing overlaps: the pen, wave, coloring-book, camera, AI, and undo buttons below remain fully visible and uncut, as do the chevron and the settings glyph in the corners (both locatable in the frame). No scrim is cast, consistent with this being a flyout rather than a dialog; the canvas, the color column along the left edge, and the docked trash button all stay at full brightness and are unobstructed by the flyout. There is no text in the flyout, so no fit or truncation risk. The color column's rows are fully drawn down to the bottom pair, with no element severed by the 375px viewport height. Icon scale, corner radius, and card elevation match the Actions Panel styling below, so the two rows read as one system. Landscape at this height leaves the flyout, the button panel, and the palette coexisting without crowding or forced scrolling.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique:
The stroke-width flyout itself is in good shape: five width choices sit in an evenly spaced row inside a white rounded card at full brightness (no scrim, as expected for this flyout), each preview stroke is drawn cleanly with no clipping against its tile, the widths step monotonically from thinnest at left to thickest at right so the hierarchy of choice is instantly readable, and the current selection is marked with a filled lavender tile and purple outline that is unambiguous against the four plain tiles. Tiles are roughly 50 px square with clear separation, so touch targets are legible and unlikely to be mis-hit. The card floats above the Actions Panel without overlapping any of the round buttons below it, and it clears the right-hand trash button and the top color palette entirely. There is no text in this menu, so no fit or truncation risk. The chevron and the settings gear are both locatable as thin gray glyphs in their respective bottom corners — quiet as intended, but findable.

The one visible problem is outside the flyout, in the left color palette. In this 375 px-tall landscape viewport the two-column swatch grid runs past the bottom of the screen: the black swatch and the multicolor swatch in the last visible row are sliced through by the viewport edge at roughly two-thirds height, with a hard crisp cut and no soft gradient fade painted over them. Every other row is a complete circle, so the abrupt half-circles read as a layout overflow rather than as this app's scroll-fade cue, and there is no visible signal that further colors exist below. The palette also has no visible scrim over it here, so this is the palette's own presentation, not an overlay effect.
entries.recommendation: In short landscape viewports, give the left color palette enough bottom padding (or a scroll container that ends on a whole row) that swatches are never sliced mid-circle by the viewport edge, and apply the standard gradient fade over its last visible row so the continued scroll is signalled.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the stroke-width flyout is broadly sound: the five tiles sit on a panel a step lighter than the canvas, the selected tile is marked with a bright lilac outline plus a lighter fill that reads clearly, and the four thicker preview strokes are a saturated lilac that stands well clear of the dark tile ground. The color palette swatches on the left, the trash button, and the enabled pencil/wave/coloring-book icons all hold up. The chevron and settings glyph are locatable in the bottom corners. No scrim is present and the page behind is at full brightness, consistent with this flyout's scope.

The one weak point is the leftmost (thinnest) preview stroke. Rendered as a roughly one-pixel hairline, antialiasing spreads its already mid-lilac color across partial pixels, so it lands noticeably grayer and dimmer than the other four and is the only mark in the flyout that is hard to resolve at a glance against the tile. Because the strokes are the sole content distinguishing one option from another, that thinnest option carries the least visual evidence of what it represents at exactly the size where it needs the most help.
entries.recommendation: Raise the thinnest stroke preview's rendered luminance in dark mode — draw it at a lighter tint than the thicker previews (or add a subtle stroke-width floor of ~1.5px for the preview only) so its perceived contrast against the tile matches the other four options.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
The honeycomb grid is well-organized — clean hue-per-column, value-per-row ordering, generous hex size with comfortable touch targets, and a clear white selection outline marking the current swatch. Two things are visibly wrong at this size.

1) The top and bottom hex rows are cut off by the card's own rounded rectangle. The first row's hexagons have flat, chopped top edges and the last row's have flat, chopped bottom edges, both terminating exactly at the card's inner boundary rather than showing their pointed/angled hex silhouette like every interior row. There is no soft gradient fade along either edge — the crop is a hard, full-opacity cut — so this does not read as the app's scroll-fade cue; it reads as a grid taller than its container being clipped. It also leaves ambiguity about whether more rows exist above/below.

2) There is no visible close or dismiss control anywhere on the card — no X, no chevron, no header, and no visible gap of scrim on the left where the underlying palette column is still at full brightness right up to the card edge. The only exit affordance appears to be tapping the scrim, which is undiscoverable.

Vertical padding inside the card is also asymmetric with horizontal padding: the left/right margins around the grid are comfortable, while top/bottom have essentially none, which is what produces the clipping.
entries.recommendation: Reduce the hex grid's row height (or the card's vertical padding budget) in short landscape viewports so the first and last rows render their full hexagon silhouette inside the card, and add a visible close control (X in a corner of the card) so the picker can be dismissed without relying on a scrim tap.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility of the open color-picker card are sound. The card is a light-edged rounded dark panel that separates clearly from the near-black page behind it, and every hexagonal swatch reads as a distinct filled shape against the panel fill — including the light end of the range (white, pale pink, pale lavender), which does not bloom or merge, and the muted gray-blue and brown columns, which stay separable from each other and from the panel. There is no text or iconography inside the card whose legibility could fail. The one swatch approaching the panel's own value is the near-black hex at the bottom right; it carries a lighter outline and remains locatable as a distinct selectable cell rather than reading as empty, so it clears the floor. Outside the card, the trash button at the right edge is fully legible (bright yellow glyph on a dark-red disc), the vertical color strip along the left edge keeps its hues distinct, and the settings gear in the bottom-right corner is findable as a thin gray glyph, which is its resting appearance here. Nothing in the frame is illegible or unlocatable.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The Coloring Books dialog fills nearly the whole 812×375 landscape viewport, and its scrim is applied unevenly. The bottom toolbar behind the card is clearly darkened and blurred, but the color-swatch column down the left edge (purple, blue, teal, yellow, red, black) and the red trash button at the right edge remain at full saturation and full sharpness. Those two zones are the most chromatic things in the frame, so they compete with the card for attention instead of receding behind it, and the intended "open card holds attention" effect only lands on the middle and lower thirds.

Within the card itself, hierarchy, spacing and text fit are sound: the "Coloring Books" title, the circled × close button, the four cover thumbnails and their labels (Farm, Dinosaurs, Creatures, Nature) are all clean, evenly gutter-spaced, unclipped and comfortably sized as touch targets. The second row of covers sits under the bottom scroll fade, which is the app's own continues-past-the-edge cue, so the card correctly signals more content. The practical consequence in this orientation is that only one full row of four books clears the fade — the picker is usable but shows a quarter of a screenful at a time — though that is a function of a 375px-tall viewport rather than a layout fault.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog's scrim (darken + blur) across the full page behind the card, including the left color-swatch column and the docked trash button, so no full-saturation background element sits outside the dimmed area.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique: In the night-mode Coloring Books dialog, the card sits on a scrimmed page and holds its own contrast well. "Coloring Books" is near-white on the dark card surface and reads cleanly. The four book labels (Farm, Dinosaurs, Creatures, Nature) are bold near-white on the slightly lighter tile fill and are crisply legible. The cover thumbnails are thin light line art on a dark tile; the strokes are fine but stay clearly above the tile background, and each subject (barn and cows, dinosaurs, unicorn and mushrooms, flowers and insects) is distinguishable at this size. Tile borders are subtle but sufficient to separate the four cards from the card surface. The close control in the top right is a gray glyph in a thin ring on the dark card — lower contrast than the title, but its shape is unambiguous and easy to locate. The second row of tiles is thinned and washed toward the bottom edge, which is the scroll fade being drawn, so it is excluded from judgement; the fully clear first row carries the assessment. Elements outside the card (palette swatches at left, trash button at right, corner glyphs) sit under the dialog scrim, and the settings glyph is still findable in the bottom-right corner. No element within the open card falls below usable legibility in this theme.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique: The Farm coloring-page grid is cut off with a hard edge at the modal card's bottom. In this 375 px-tall landscape frame the modal header (back chevron, "Farm" title, close button) consumes roughly 110 px, leaving only about 215 px for the grid — enough to show a single row of thumbnails clipped about a third of the way down the cat and cow illustrations. The clip is an abrupt hard edge flush with the card's rounded bottom border; no soft gradient fade is painted over that last row, so the scroll cue this app relies on is missing exactly where content continues past the edge. The result reads as truncated content rather than a scrollable region. Everything else in the frame is sound: the title and close button have clear hierarchy and comfortable spacing, the back chevron and close button are unambiguous round touch targets, the scrim over the palette and corner buttons is behaving as designed, the docked trash button is intentionally past the screen edge, and the settings gear glyph in the bottom-right corner is locatable.
entries.recommendation: In short landscape viewports, compact the modal header (reduce its vertical padding and title size) to reclaim grid height, and ensure the bottom fade gradient renders over the last visible thumbnail row so the truncated cards read as scrollable rather than clipped.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique: Landscape frame reads cleanly. The left color palette is a two-column grid of evenly sized, evenly spaced swatches with a clear selection ring on the purple swatch (the active-page chip state), and the last cell's multicolor "more colors" glyph is distinguishable without competing with the plain swatches. Every button in that row is fully drawn with even gaps and no overlap with the palette column at the left or with each other; the row clears the bottom edge with visible margin. The docked round trash button at top right is the intended edge-docked treatment. The settings gear in the bottom-right corner is a thin low-contrast glyph with no disc behind it, which is the intended parent-facing styling; its shape is clearly locatable in the frame, so it meets the findability floor. No text is present to wrap or truncate, no scrim is active, and no scrolling region shows a fade edge. Touch targets in both the palette and the button row are large and separated. I see no actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique: The threshold state's main feedback element — the red accept ring — is largely outside the frame. Only a lower-left arc of it is visible: the ring exits the top edge and the right edge, and the bulk of its circumference is off-canvas. It is also not concentric with the trash button it belongs to; the button sits on the ring's lower-left arc rather than at its center, so the visible fragment reads as a stray red curve crossing the corner rather than as a ring closing around the control. In landscape the vertical room is only 375px, so a ring of this radius cannot resolve at all here. The result is that the one cue distinguishing "held past threshold" from a normal press is unreadable in this viewport: the glow around the trash button and the very faint wash across the paper are the only remaining signals, and neither reads as a completion/confirm state. Everything else in the frame is sound: the left color column is evenly spaced with clear circular targets and no clipping, the selected purple swatch is unambiguously ringed, the expand chevron and the settings glyph are both locatable in their bottom corners, and no text is present to fit or truncate.
entries.recommendation: Center the accept ring on the trash button and clamp its radius to the shorter viewport dimension (with a margin) so the full ring renders inside the 375px-tall landscape frame instead of exiting the top and right edges.

entries.critique:
Night-mode frame at 812×375 showing the clear gesture held past threshold: a red accept ring arcing from the top-right, the round trash button docked at the right edge glowing red with a yellow trash glyph, the left color palette, a chevron at the bottom of the palette column, and the settings glyph in the bottom-right corner.

Contrast and legibility hold throughout. The trash glyph is yellow on saturated red inside a strong red glow — unambiguous against the near-black canvas, and its meaning survives the glow bloom. The accept ring reads as a continuous bright red stroke against the dark ground along its whole visible arc, so the threshold state is clearly signalled. The color-swatch grid is fully legible: each of the ten swatches is a distinct saturated hue on the dark panel, the white swatch and the multicolor swatch both separate cleanly from the background, and the selected purple swatch carries a visible lighter selection ring that distinguishes it from the unselected swatches.

The chevron beside the palette and the settings gear in the opposite corner are thin gray glyphs with no disc or outline behind them; both shapes are locatable in this image — the chevron's arrowhead and the gear's toothed disc each resolve — so they meet the findability floor, and their quietness is the intended resting styling.

The single dim purple stroke across the mid-canvas and the faintness of the canvas region are the wash that accompanies the clear gesture, which is stated design intent rather than a contrast fault. No text is present in the frame to assess. No actionable night-mode contrast or legibility issue.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The banner itself is legible and well-formed: a bold two-line title, a clear purple "How?" button, and a circular × close control, all on an unscrimmed canvas at full brightness. Hierarchy reads correctly (title > subtitle > actions), and the banner does not overlap the docked trash button, the settings glyph, or the panel chevron to its left — all three are locatable.

The one visible defect is text fit in the subtitle. "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" wraps to a second line consisting of the single orphan word "app," and that line sits flush against the card's bottom edge, with visibly less breathing room than the inset used on the card's top and sides. It reads as unbalanced and near-clipped rather than as an intentional two-line block. The landscape geometry aggravates it: the text column is squeezed between the app icon on the left and the "How?" button plus close control on the right, narrow enough to force the wrap in the first place.

No clipping of the color palette, no overlap between elements, and the "How?" and × touch targets are clearly sized and separated.
entries.recommendation: Increase the banner's bottom padding to match its top/side inset and widen the text column — or shorten the subtitle to one line that fits the landscape width — so "app" is not left as an orphan word pressed against the card's bottom border.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
The Grown-Ups Only gate card is taller than the 375px landscape viewport and its bottom keypad row is clipped. The card spans from the top of the frame to the bottom edge, and the final row containing the `0` key and the backspace key is cut roughly two-thirds of the way down — the card's rounded bottom corners are visible flanking that row, confirming the row is truncated by the card/viewport rather than sitting under a scroll fade. No fade, and no other continuation cue, is present along that edge. Functionally this blocks the gate: a parent cannot enter an answer containing a 0, and cannot delete a mistyped digit, and both keys expose partial, ambiguous touch targets.

The rest of the card is sound. The title and "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle sit clear of the logo mark with adequate leading. The `5 × 9 = _ _` challenge row reads cleanly, with the two dashed answer slots well separated from the operands and the equals sign. Keys 1 through 9 form an even three-column grid with consistent gutters and comfortable target sizes. The circular close button in the top-right corner is distinct, well contrasted against the white card, and does not crowd the title. Text fit is fine throughout — no wrapping, truncation, or overflow within any label.

The color palette along the left edge renders at full brightness while the canvas behind the card is darkened; noting it as an observation about scrim coverage only, not raised as an independent finding from this single frame.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the parental gate card to the viewport height on short landscape screens — cap it at roughly `max-height: 100dvh` minus a margin and make the keypad area scroll, or switch to a compact landscape layout that places the challenge row and keypad side by side — so the `0` and backspace keys are fully rendered and tappable at 812 × 375.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast and legibility of the Grown-Ups Only gate hold up. The open card is the thing to judge, and its content sits well clear of the scrim behind it: the "Grown-Ups Only" title renders as near-white on the dark card surface at a large weight and is crisp; the "Solve the problem to continue" subtitle is a lighter gray at small size but still comfortably separated from the card ground and readable without effort. The multiplication challenge itself is the strongest element — the "9" on a purple disc and the "4" on a blue disc are both white-on-saturated-fill and read instantly, with the "×" and "=" operators in white at adequate weight. The two empty answer slots are dashed gray outlines on the card; they are dimmer than the filled operands, but their shape and position are unambiguous and they are placeholders awaiting input rather than text to be read. The keypad is the bulk of the card and is solid: digits 0–9 are white glyphs on mid-gray key fills, each key clearly delineated from the card background, and the backspace glyph on its key is legible as an icon. The close ✕ in its top-right disc is light-on-dark and easy to pick out. Nothing on the card relies on a hue distinction alone or falls into a dark-on-dark or gray-on-gray trap. Behind the card, the palette circles down the left edge, the purple stroke on the canvas, the brush button, the collapse chevron near the bottom center-right, and the settings gear in the bottom-right corner all read dim and softened — that is the gate's full-page scrim doing its job, and the two parent-facing glyphs are additionally at their intended resting faintness; both the chevron and the gear are still locatable by shape in the frame, so neither owes a finding. The trash button at the right edge remains vivid but is not a legibility concern. No actionable night-mode contrast or legibility defect is visible.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The "Pick a style" card itself is in good shape: title and close button sit clear of the grid, the 4×2 thumbnail grid is evenly gutted, all eight labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) fit on one line under their tiles with no truncation or collision, and the card fits within the 375px height without clipping the bottom row. The close ✕ is a clear circular target in the top-right corner.

The visible problem is scrim coverage. The canvas behind the card is plainly darkened and blurred, and the corner buttons peeking under the card's lower edge are dimmed too — but the vertical color palette rail down the left side is rendered at full brightness and full saturation (large purple, blue, teal, green, ochre, orange, red, magenta, black discs plus the multicolor swatch), as is the red trash button on the right. In this landscape frame those are the highest-chroma elements present, and with no scrim over them they visually outrank the muted pastel thumbnails inside the open dialog, pulling attention off the card the dialog is meant to hold. The rail also still reads as tappable: nothing visually indicates whether tapping a color while the style picker is open does anything.

This appears specific to the landscape layout, where the palette occupies a left rail sitting outside the darkened region.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to the full viewport in landscape so the left color rail and the right trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, matching the scrim behavior these dialogs are specified to have.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open AI-result card is largely sound: "Making your picture…" is near-white on the dark card and fully legible, the sub-line "This takes about 30 seconds" is a mid-gray that still separates cleanly from the card ground, and the close button is a white glyph in a white ring on the bright preview panel, so it reads at a glance. The parent-facing chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both locatable as shapes.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
The AI result card renders cleanly: the generated rainbow fills the rounded image frame with no clipping or distortion, the close button sits clear in the top-right corner at a comfortable tap size, and the "Download" pill is centered below with legible white text on purple and a clear icon-plus-label pairing. The "AI-generated picture · Report" caption sits below the card on the scrim, reads legibly, and the Report flag is distinguishable as a separate tappable element. Card margins are even and nothing overlaps in the landscape 812 × 375 frame.

The one visible problem is scrim coverage. The dialog clearly darkens the page behind it — the canvas, the trash button, the settings glyph, and the chevron are all visibly dimmed — but the color palette column along the left edge is not. Its swatches are at full brightness and full saturation, so a two-column grid of large, vivid discs competes directly with the open card for attention, and the frame reads as two lit surfaces rather than one card over a suppressed page. Because the dimming is plainly applied everywhere else in the same frame, this is an inconsistency in the overlay treatment, not a styling choice on the palette. It is most conspicuous at this viewport, where the short landscape height puts the bright column immediately alongside the card.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the left color palette so it is darkened and blurred along with the canvas and corner controls, keeping the AI result card the only fully lit surface in the frame.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
In scope for this dark-mode capture: the open AI card and the caption row drawn on top of the scrim. The card itself holds up — the generated rainbow sits on a light-blue field with plenty of separation from the dark card, the "Download" label is white on a saturated purple pill and reads cleanly, and the ✕ close glyph is a light stroke on a circular outline that stays visible against the card's dark surface. The palette swatches, trash button, chevron and settings glyph behind the card are under the dialog scrim, so their dimness is the scrim, not a finding.

The one weak spot is the caption row under the card: "AI-generated picture", the dot separator, and the small red flag icon beside "Report". The caption and separator are a mid-gray on the near-black scrimmed background and are noticeably fainter than any other text in the frame, and the flag is a small saturated red mark on that same dark ground — a hue/value pairing that carries very little luminance contrast at this glyph size. "Report" is the only affordance in this row and its icon is the part that signals what the affordance does, so this isn't a deliberately-recessive parent control like the corner glyphs; it's a labeled action rendered dimmer than the card it belongs to. Legibility is degraded but not lost — the words are still readable at this size — so this reads as a low-severity night-mode contrast issue rather than a blocking one.
entries.recommendation: Lift the caption row on dark: raise "AI-generated picture" and the dot separator toward a lighter neutral (roughly #b8b8c0 or brighter) for at least 4.5:1 against the dark background, and either lighten the Report flag to a desaturated red/pink tuned for dark backgrounds or pair it with the same brighter neutral as its label so the icon carries comparable luminance contrast to the text it sits beside.
