entries.critique: The confirmation dialog's top is cut off by the viewport. The first visible line begins mid-sentence ("art style, and exact instruction sent to the AI go to a grown-up at Splotch. We look within 24 hours, and the report is deleted after 30 days."), and the card's top edge, rounded corner, and any title are all above the frame. No fade or other cue is painted along that top edge, and the text sits hard against the screen edge with no padding, so the truncation reads as broken rather than as a scrollable region. The rest of the card is sound: the two thumbnails ("The AI picture" / "The drawing behind it") are evenly sized, aligned, and fully legible with unclipped captions; Cancel and Send report are large, well separated, clearly tappable, and the primary action is correctly weighted in filled purple against the muted secondary. The failure is specific to landscape height — at 375px the card is taller than the viewport and is anchored so the overflow spills off the top instead of being scrolled into view from a settled starting position.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the dialog to the viewport height with internal scrolling that starts at the top of its content, so the heading and the opening of the retention sentence are visible on open, with the fade cue at the bottom edge where content continues.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal card is well formed: palette emoji, headline "Let's try drawing something else!", two-line body, "For grown-ups" label, and the "Report this refusal" button stack with even vertical rhythm; no text clipping, truncation, or overlap at 812x375, and the card fits the landscape viewport with margin above and below. The close button is a clearly bounded circular target inset within the card's top-right corner, unambiguous as tappable and not colliding with the emoji or heading. The chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable in the bottom corners, so the parent-facing controls meet their findability floor.

The actionable issue is scrim coverage. This is a dialog that should lay one scrim over the whole page behind it, but only the central canvas region is darkened and blurred. The left-edge color palette column renders at full saturation - the purple, teal, green, amber, crimson and black swatches are as vivid as they would be with no overlay at all - and the red docked trash button at the top right is likewise at full brightness. The result is that two high-chroma zones flank the white card and compete with it for attention; the red trash button is arguably the second most salient element in the frame while a refusal dialog is open, which is exactly the attention split the scrim exists to prevent. It also reads as inconsistent within the frame itself: the same overlay dims one part of the page and not the rest.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to the full viewport so it also covers the left color-palette column and the docked trash button, leaving the refusal card as the only element at full contrast.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique:
The server-error dialog is legible and structurally sound — the sad-face emoji and the single line "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!" are centered, fully within the card, unclipped, and set against white with strong contrast; the circular X close button in the top-right corner is a clearly bounded, adequately sized target. The scrim is doing its job over most of the page: canvas, the bottom-left chevron, the bottom-right gear, and the docked trash button are all visibly darkened and sit back appropriately, and both parent-facing glyphs remain findable.

The visible problem is that the scrim does not cover the left color palette. The vertical swatch rail (purple with selection ring, blue, teal, green, gold, orange, red, magenta, black, and the white multicolor chip) is rendered at full brightness and full saturation, while everything to the right of roughly x=155 is dimmed. The boundary shows as a hard vertical seam running the height of the frame. Against a uniformly dimmed page, this bright saturated column becomes the highest-chroma region in the image and competes directly with the modal for first fixation — the eye is pulled to the swatches before the error message. The palette also still reads as interactive while a modal is open, which is ambiguous about whether it is tappable.

Lesser point: in this 812x375 landscape frame the card's content is concentrated in its upper half, leaving roughly a third of the card as empty white below the text, and the copy instructs the user to "try again" while offering no retry control — only the close button.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to cover the left color-palette rail as it already covers the canvas and corner controls, so the open error card is the brightest element in the frame and no page chrome reads as active behind the overlay.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
In this 812 × 375 landscape frame the admin page shows only its masthead ("← Back to drawing", the dot logo + SPLOTCH ADMIN, "Admin", "Manage AI access codes", "Sign out") and the yellow Netlify Blobs persistence warning. Everything visible renders cleanly: no clipping, no overlap, text fits its containers, the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip wraps without breaking the paragraph, and the warning card has even padding on all sides. "Sign out" is a well-sized pill with clear affordance; the back link is legible violet on white. Hierarchy within what is shown is correct — title dominates, subtitle recedes, the warning is distinct without shouting.

The one actionable issue is vertical budget. The masthead consumes roughly 200px of the 375px viewport before any content begins, so the "ACCESS CODES · 2" divider lands flush against the bottom edge and the ledger rows and free-grant metrics are entirely below the fold. On this short landscape viewport the screen's actual subject is invisible at rest — the user sees a title, a subtitle, and a warning, and must scroll before the page does anything. The divider being sliced at the frame edge also offers no partial row to signal that a list follows.

No touch-target, modal, or consistency problems are visible; the ledger and metrics themselves cannot be judged as they are not rendered here.
entries.recommendation: At short viewport heights (roughly ≤420px), compress the admin masthead — smaller "Admin" display size, tighter top padding and gaps between title, subtitle and warning card, optionally collapsing the subtitle — so the "ACCESS CODES · 2" divider and at least the first ledger row sit above the fold.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin view is mostly sound. The page sits on a near-black ground with a slightly lighter charcoal card; "Admin" in white and the "Manage AI access codes" subhead both read cleanly. The persistence warning is the strongest element in the frame — cream card, dark brown body text, a bolded "Netlify Blobs is unavailable." lead-in, and an inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip that stays legible against the pale fill — an appropriate inversion for a warning in dark mode. The "Sign out" pill (light lavender label on muted purple) is readable and clearly reads as a control.

Two small-text items are weak. The "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark at top right and the "ACCESS CODES · 2" section label above the divider are both small, letterspaced, all-caps gray on the dark card; at that size and weight they are the dimmest text in the frame and sit noticeably below the surrounding body copy. The section label in particular is a structural heading for the ledger plus a record count — information a parent is meant to read, not decorative chrome — yet it is harder to read than the subhead under a much larger title. The "← Back to drawing" link is purple on near-black; it is locatable and clearly reads as a link, but it is the lowest-contrast interactive text on the screen and the arrow glyph in particular thins out.

No overlay, scrim, faded scroll edge, or disabled-state styling is visible in this frame, so nothing here is accounted for by those conventions.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the small all-caps gray text — the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark and the "ACCESS CODES · 2" section label — to a brighter neutral (roughly #b8b8c4 or above on this charcoal card) so letterspaced small caps clear 4.5:1, and nudge the "Back to drawing" link purple toward a lighter tint for the same reason.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
The access-code section reads cleanly at 812×375: the "ACCESS CODES · 2" rule, the add-code field with its filled "Add code" button, and the two code rows form a clear hierarchy, with monospace code names distinct from the actions beside them. Nothing is clipped, overlapped, or truncated; "daycare-club" and "page-inventory-harness" both fit with room to spare, and the expanded row's "Copy link" / "Remove" pair sits on its own full-width line separated by a hairline divider, with "Remove" tinted red to mark it destructive. Spacing between the input row, the expanded actions, and the following "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" header is even.

The one visible inconsistency is the disclosure control. On the expanded row the chevron sits inside a filled lavender rounded square with an obvious tappable footprint matched in height to the outlined "Copy" button beside it; on the collapsed row it is a bare thin chevron glyph on the card background with no disc, fill, or outline, visibly narrower and shorter than the adjacent "Copy" button. The collapsed state is the one a user must find first to reach a row's actions, so the weaker-looking of the two is the entry point, and its hit area is unstated on screen. This is an admin-facing control in a row of otherwise fully bordered buttons, so it does not fall under the deliberately quiet parent-facing glyph styling described for the canvas screen.
entries.recommendation: Give the collapsed-row chevron the same visible container as the expanded one — a subtle outlined or lightly filled rounded square matching the "Copy" button's height — reserving the stronger lavender fill for the expanded/active state so the affordance reads in both states.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across this admin access-code view is mostly sound: the row keys (`daycare-club`, `page-inventory-harness`) are near-white monospace on the dark card and read cleanly, the "Add code" button pairs white on saturated purple, and "Copy" / "Copy link" purple-on-dark sits comfortably legible.

Two weak points are visible. (1) The "Remove" label in the expanded row is a desaturated muted rose on a near-black panel — it is the lowest-contrast interactive text in the frame, noticeably fainter than the "Copy link" label sitting beside it in the same button row, and it is the destructive action, which is the one label that should not be the hardest to read. (2) The collapsed-row chevron on `page-inventory-harness` is drawn as a thin gray glyph on the card ground with no fill behind it; its shape is locatable, but it is markedly dimmer than the same chevron on the expanded row above it, which carries a filled purple-tinted disc. Since these are peer row controls in a table, the disparity makes the collapsed affordance read as inactive rather than as a peer of the one above it.

The small-caps section labels ("ACCESS CODES · 2", "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0") are dim gray at small size, but as static structural headings that is acceptable subordination rather than a failure.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "Remove" label to a brighter, more saturated red that clears at least 4.5:1 against the dark button panel — it should be at minimum as luminous as the "Copy link" label next to it — and lift the collapsed-row chevron to the same glyph brightness as the expanded-row chevron so both row toggles read as equally active.

entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: The frame shows a clean resting canvas. The color palette renders as a left-edge rail of ten circular swatches in a 2-column grid, all fully within the viewport with even gutters and no row clipped at the bottom edge; the active purple swatch is clearly marked with a ring, and the multicolor "more colors" swatch is distinguishable from the solid colors. The rail is separated from the drawing surface by a subtle vertical divider, and the canvas itself is empty with a light paper texture, so hierarchy is unambiguous: bright saturated tools on the left, artwork area at rest. The red trash button sits docked at the top-right in its intended docked position. The expand chevron in the bottom-left and the settings gear in the bottom-right are both locatable — the chevron's arrow shape and the gear's toothed outline are each resolvable in the image — so the findability floor for those two parent-facing controls is met, and their low contrast is the intended resting styling. No overlap, no text is present to fit or truncate, no overlay or scrim is open, and no scrolling region shows a fade edge to judge. Touch targets for the swatches are large and well-separated. I see no actionable visible defect.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in surface is mostly solid: the "Admin" heading and "Manage AI access codes" subtitle are near-white on the dark card, the purple "Sign in" button holds a legible white label, and the input outline is discernible against its fill. The weakness is confined to the smallest gray type. The "SIGN IN" section label is small, uppercase and letterspaced in a mid-gray that sits close to the dark card background, and the "Admin access key" placeholder in the text field is a similarly weak gray. These are the smallest glyphs in the frame, which is exactly where dark-mode contrast should be highest rather than lowest. The placeholder matters most because it is the only cue telling a signed-out administrator what the field expects. The hairline rule trailing the section label is also near the edge of visibility, though it is decorative and carries no information.
entries.recommendation: Raise the small gray text tier in dark mode: brighten the "SIGN IN" section label and the "Admin access key" input placeholder to a lighter gray that clears 4.5:1 against the card background at their small size.

entries.surface_description: The complete release history at its opening position.
entries.critique:
The changelog opens cleanly: "← Back to drawing" and the Splotch dot-logo sit balanced at the top, the "Changelog" title and its two-line subtitle are well set with comfortable leading, and the two-column split (CONTENTS rail with the rule, entry body with matching "Version 1.5.0" heading and right-aligned date) is consistent and correctly aligned across the columns. The active TOC item is clearly marked with the lavender fill plus left accent bar, and its date subline fits. Text fit is fine everywhere visible: no truncation, wrapping, or overlap, and nothing collides with the container edges. The bottom of the frame thins out over the third TOC row and the second bullet, which is the region's scroll fade being drawn rather than a defect.

The one real issue is vertical budgeting for this short landscape viewport. Of the 440px height, roughly 260px — nearly 60% — goes to the back link, title, and subtitle before any release content begins, so the opening position shows only a single readable bullet ("Create 10 free AI pictures—no key needed.") of the newest release and two-and-a-fraction TOC entries. The complete release history at rest reads as mostly masthead; a parent scanning what changed has to scroll immediately. The header block is sized as if for a portrait or desktop viewport rather than a 440px-tall one.

TOC rows are generously tall and read as comfortably tappable; no touch-target ambiguity is visible.
entries.recommendation: In short-height landscape viewports, compress the changelog header — reduce the "Changelog" title size and the top/bottom margins around it, and drop the subtitle to one line or hide it — so at least the first release's full "New" list clears the fold at the opening position.

Touch targets — the two theme segments, the contents row, and the back link — are each generously sized for landscape phone use. The lavender "Not sure? Start here" card at the bottom is cut by the viewport edge, but that is the fold of a scrolling page at its opening position, not clipping. No modal is open, so nothing about scrim or dialog scrolling is testable here. Nothing visible is actionable.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast holds up across most of the opening view: the H1 "Splotch design system", the intro paragraph, the "CONTENTS" label, the "16 sections" link and the violet "Back to drawing" link all read cleanly against the near-black background. The Light/Dark segmented control shows a clear active/inactive distinction — the "Dark" pill is filled and legible, and "Light" with its sun icon stays readable in the unselected half. The purple "Not sure? Start here" card at the bottom edge carries its white heading well, and the palette dots plus the SPLOTCH wordmark at top right are crisp.

The weak point is the "Sources:" metadata line under the intro paragraph. It is the smallest type on the page, and its plain-prose segments — the arrow, "(npm run gen:tokens)", and especially the trailing "the icon set / the shipped components" — are set in a dark mid-gray that sits very close to the page background. At this size it is the hardest text in the frame to resolve. The monospace fragments in the same line (lib/design/tokens.ts, tokens.css, lib/palette.ts) are tinted amber and violet and read fine, which makes the surrounding gray look thinner still. This is body-level provenance content on a styleguide's opening screen, not a deliberately recessive control, so the low contrast is not doing intentional work.

Secondarily, the "Design system" label in the top bar beside the theme toggle is also a fairly low-contrast gray, though its larger size keeps it findable.</critique>
</invoke>
entries.recommendation: Lighten the gray token used for the small "Sources:" metadata line (and the same token on the "Design system" top-bar label) so this smallest-size text clears at least 4.5:1 against the dark page background, instead of relying on the inline code tints to carry the line.

entries.critique: In this 956 × 440 landscape frame the page is almost entirely masthead: "Back to drawing", the "Send us feedback" title, and a three-line explanatory paragraph consume the top ~250px, so by the time the Something's broken / I have an idea toggle and the "What went wrong?" label appear, the first input is only half visible — its placeholder "Describe what happened, and what you expected instead…" is bisected by the bottom edge of the viewport. Nothing that lets the user complete the task (the full textarea, any further fields, the submit control) is on screen at rest; the entire form is below the fold in the device's default landscape height. The cut at the bottom edge is a hard crop through the middle of a text line with no soft gradient fade painted over it, so this edge is not carrying the app's normal "there is more below" cue either — the user gets a truncated word-shape rather than the intended thinning. Everything actually visible is otherwise clean: the title and body copy have generous, consistent margins, the toggle's selected/unselected states are clearly differentiated by the raised white pill against the gray track, both segment labels fit their halves with room to spare, the back link and the Splotch wordmark sit at comfortable opposite corners with no overlap, and the card's rounded container is inset evenly on left and right. The complaint is purely that the vertical budget is spent on preamble in the one orientation where vertical space is scarcest.
entries.recommendation: Tighten the landscape header so the form starts above the fold: at short viewport heights (e.g. max-height ~500px) reduce the title size and collapse the three-line intro paragraph to one line or a tappable "why we ask" disclosure, so the toggle and the full first textarea are visible without scrolling — and make sure the bottom scroll edge carries the standard gradient fade rather than a hard crop.

entries.review_description: Feedback. The standalone bug report and feature idea form. Captured in night mode on iPhone 16 Pro Max in landscape at 956 × 440. Assess only night-mode contrast and legibility. Ignore layout and responsive composition. Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the visible portion of the Feedback screen holds up. "Send us feedback" is near-white on the dark card and reads at very high contrast; the intro paragraph is a light gray that stays comfortably legible at this size; "← Back to drawing" is a saturated lavender that separates clearly from the near-black background; the SPLOTCH wordmark and its color dots are crisp. In the segmented control, the selected "Something's broken" is bold near-white on a darker recessed fill (strong contrast), and the unselected "I have an idea" is a lighter gray on the raised gray track — dimmer than the selected label, but still cleanly readable as a deselected option rather than a legibility failure. The section label "What went wrong?" is bold and high-contrast. The textarea placeholder at the very bottom is faint and thinning, but it sits inside the soft gradient fade marking that the page continues past the bottom edge, so that softening is the scroll cue being drawn and not a contrast finding. No text, control, or glyph in this frame is unfindable or unreadable on its own merits.

entries.critique: Opening view of the privacy policy in landscape. Hierarchy is clear: back link and brand lockup on one row, large "Privacy policy" title, a two-line intro, then a labeled "THE SHORT VERSION" section rule with the last-updated date right-aligned on the same baseline. The card of colored-dot bullets ("No ads.", "No tracking.", "No accounts.") is readable, with bold lead-ins against lighter explanatory text and even row separators. Spacing is consistent, no text is clipped horizontally, nothing overlaps, and the "← Back to drawing" link is a legible, clearly tappable target. The third bullet row is bisected by the bottom of the viewport, which is ordinary page scroll at the opening position rather than a layout fault. No actionable visible issue.

entries.surface_description: Google Play closed-test instructions, on the Android tab of the beta page.
entries.critique: Hierarchy, alignment and text fit are clean: "Join the Splotch beta" sits clearly above a two-line intro, the Android / iPhone tabs are unambiguous with the active tab marked by both purple color and an underline, and the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" eyebrow with its rule reads correctly as a section start. No clipping, overlap, or wrapping faults; the back link and brand mark are balanced across the top. The thinning of the "1 Join the testers group" row at the bottom edge is the intended scroll fade, not a defect. The actionable problem is vertical budget in this 440px-tall landscape viewport: roughly the top 300px go to card padding, the header row, an oversized display title, a two-line intro sentence, tabs, and a section eyebrow, so the first step's heading only just appears at the very bottom and no instruction content — no link, button, or step body — is visible at all. On the page whose entire purpose is the Google Play closed-test steps, a landscape user sees only chrome and must scroll before anything actionable exists.
entries.recommendation: Under a short-viewport/landscape media query, tighten the header block — reduce the display title size and top card padding, collapse the two-line intro to one line, and shrink the gaps around the tab row and the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" eyebrow — so at least the first step's body clears the fade on load.

entries.critique: Visible content is clean and consistent: "← Back to drawing" and the SPLOTCH BETA dot-mark sit balanced across the top; the H1, the two-line intro, and the tab row step down in size and weight with clear hierarchy. The tab bar reads correctly — "iPhone / iPad" is purple with a purple underline while "Android" is neutral, so the active tab is unambiguous, and both tabs have icon+label with comfortable padding and generous tap width. The "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" eyebrow with its trailing rule is well spaced from the tab row. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems: both intro lines break cleanly and nothing collides with the card's rounded edges. Step 1 ("Install TestFlight" with its numbered pink disc) sits under the scroll fade at the bottom edge, which is the app's documented continues-past-the-edge cue, so its softness is not a finding. The one substantive observation is proportional: at 956 × 440 landscape the header block (back link, H1, two-line intro, tabs, eyebrow) consumes essentially the entire viewport, so the page's actual payload — the TestFlight steps — begins right at the fade line and no instruction content is legible without scrolling. Nothing is broken, but the top matter's density is tuned for portrait height rather than this short landscape one.
entries.recommendation: Tighten the vertical rhythm above the steps at short viewport heights (e.g. reduce the H1 size and the gaps around the intro paragraph and tab row under a max-height breakpoint) so at least the first numbered step is fully readable above the scroll fade in a 440px-tall landscape viewport.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog itself is in good shape: title, close button, the two toggle rows and the orientation segment pair are evenly spaced, all labels fit without clipping or overlap, the helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." sits clear of the card edge, and both Portrait and Landscape segments read as inactive, matching the stated unlocked-rotation intent.

The visible problem is the scrim. This is a dialog that is supposed to lay one scrim over the whole page, darkening the canvas, the color palette and the corner controls together. In this frame the scrim is clearly applied to the center canvas (mid-gray, with the chevron and gear muted behind it) but the left color-palette column and the round red trash button at the top right are rendered at full, unmuted saturation — the purple, teal, green, red and multicolor swatches and the yellow trash glyph are as vivid as they would be undimmed. The result is a hard vertical seam down the left side at roughly x=155 where the darkened region stops, and two bright zones flanking a dimmed middle. Visually the palette and trash button now compete with the open card for attention, which is the opposite of what the scrim is for, and the trash button in particular reads as still live and tappable while a modal is open.

Nothing else here rises to a finding: the parent-facing chevron and gear glyphs are both locatable, the trash button's docked overhang past the right edge is the intended docking, and no text is truncated.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim to cover the full viewport so the left color-palette column and the docked trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas and corner controls — render the scrim above those layers (raise its z-order or move it to the top-level overlay root) rather than only over the canvas region, eliminating the bright vertical band at the left edge.

The two most colorful elements on screen therefore sit outside the scrim and compete with the open card for attention, and the abrupt brightness edge reads as an incomplete overlay layer.

entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim (dim + blur) over the left color-palette column and the trash button so one continuous overlay covers the whole page behind the Settings card, removing the bright vertical seam at the palette's right edge.

entries.critique:
Night-mode read of the compact phone-landscape Settings shell. The open card carries a scrim over the page behind it, so the card is what I judged.

Holding up well: the "Settings" title and the three row labels (Sound, Night Mode, Advanced Controls) are near-white on the dark card and read cleanly; their leading icons are legible; the three purple toggles have a bright white knob and a saturated track that separates clearly from the card at a glance. The close × sits in a lighter circular button at top right and is easy to find. The chevron at bottom left and the gear at bottom right are faint by design, and I can locate both glyph shapes in the frame, so they meet the findability floor.

One weak spot: the helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." and its small phone icon are rendered in a dim gray against the dark card and are noticeably dimmer than every other piece of text on the card — at this size it is the one string I had to look at deliberately rather than read. It is the only instruction telling the parent how to reach the full settings, so it is the text least able to afford being the dimmest thing present.

The Portrait / Landscape segment labels are also gray, but both segments are inactive here while rotation is unlocked, and their labels still sit clearly above their inset track — they read as available-but-unselected rather than illegible, so I am not counting them.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "Switch to portrait for the full settings." caption (and its phone icon) to a brighter secondary-text gray on the dark card — closer to the row-label brightness — so the only wayfinding instruction on this shell is not the dimmest text in the card.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog itself is in good shape: clear title, generous card padding, four evenly sized rows on a 2×2 grid, toggles and segments vertically centered with their labels, no clipped or wrapped text, and a close button with clear separation from the card edge. Both orientation segments read inactive, which matches the stated unlocked-rotation intent, and the helper line "Switch to portrait for the full settings." explains the compact shell.

The visible problem is the scrim behind the dialog. The canvas in the middle of the frame is clearly darkened and softened, but that treatment stops at a hard vertical seam around x≈155: the color palette column to its left keeps a white background and fully saturated swatches (purple, blue, teal, green, olive, red, magenta, black, rainbow), and the red trash button at the top right is likewise at full brightness and saturation. So the same overlay dims some background elements and leaves others untouched, and the brightest, most colorful area in the whole image is the palette column rather than the open card. The visible straight-edged boundary between dimmed and undimmed background also reads as a rendering seam rather than an intentional edge. The two low-contrast parent glyphs (chevron at bottom left, gear at bottom right) are both locatable, and touch targets, spacing, and text fit inside the card are fine.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full page behind the card — including the left color-palette column and the docked trash button — so the entire background is dimmed uniformly and no hard vertical seam remains between covered and uncovered regions.

entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The frame shows the drawing canvas with a single purple stroke, the left-edge color palette, the docked trash button at the upper right, and the expanded bottom action drawer (brush, stroke-width, image, camera, AI, undo) with the collapse chevron to its right and the settings glyph in the opposite corner.

Hierarchy reads correctly: the six drawer buttons are the loudest cluster, each a white rounded card with a saturated glyph, clearly grouped and clearly tappable; the chevron and settings glyph sit back as thin gray marks, and both shapes are locatable in the image (chevron at the drawer's right end, gear in the bottom-right corner), so the findability floor is met. The trash button's edge docking and the palette's bottom fade are the intended docking and scroll-cue treatments, and the drawer's own row sits fully inside the 440px height with no truncation.

Touch targets are unambiguous: each card is a self-contained ~48px square with visible bounds and consistent corner radius, and none overlap each other, the palette column, or the canvas stroke. No labels are present, so there is no text-fit or wrapping exposure. The palette column is fully legible above its faded strip, with consistent swatch size, spacing, and the selected-swatch ring on the purple chip matching the stroke on the canvas. No scrim is present here and no element is dimmed in a way that would suggest an unintended disabled state — undo, AI, and camera all render at full contrast, consistent with a stroke being on the canvas.

Nothing in this frame is clipped, overlapped, mis-sized, or inconsistent in a way that would be actionable.

entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique: In the stroke-width flyout (no scrim, so full-brightness scope), the five preview tiles are dark charcoal cards on the dark canvas and the brush stroke inside each is the same purple at the same value. Because the thin strokes have so little area, the two leftmost previews read as dim, near-neutral hairlines that barely separate from the tile fill; at a glance the first tile can look nearly empty. Contrast climbs only with stroke area, so the fourth and fifth read clearly while the affordance is weakest exactly where the size difference matters most. entries.recommendation: Lighten the preview stroke color for the thin options in dark mode (or brighten all preview strokes toward a high-luminance tint of the brush color) so the thinnest two reach clear contrast against the charcoal tile fill instead of relying on stroke area for visibility.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
The color-picker card itself is clean: the honeycomb grid is evenly spaced, hexes are large and unambiguous touch targets, the currently selected swatch is marked by a clear dark outline on the white hex (top right), and nothing is clipped, overlapped, or truncated. Card padding is generous and symmetric, and the whole grid fits within 956 × 440 with no scrolling needed. The bottom-corner chevron (left) and settings glyph (right) are both locatable as expected quiet parent controls.

The visible problem is the scrim. The canvas region behind the card is clearly darkened to a flat gray, but the vertical color-palette rail down the left edge and the red round trash button at the top right are rendered at full brightness — the palette swatches and the trash disc are as saturated and as high-contrast as anything in the open dialog, and the trash is in fact the single most eye-catching element in the frame. Because the scrim visibly stops short of those two areas, they are not covered background: they read as live, tappable controls sitting alongside an open modal, which both splits attention away from the card and leaves a destructive clear-drawing action apparently reachable while a dialog is up. The inconsistency is also visible as a hard edge — the bright left rail butts directly against the dimmed field with no transition.

Secondarily, the card offers no visible close or dismiss affordance; with the scrim not reading as a continuous tap-to-dismiss surface (part of it is bright, undimmed UI), there is no on-screen way to tell how to leave the picker without choosing a color.
entries.recommendation: Extend the color-picker's scrim over the full viewport so the left color-palette rail and the red trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas — matching the other dialogs — and add a visible close affordance (or make the whole scrim an obvious dismiss surface) to the picker card.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The Coloring Books dialog renders cleanly: the title sits clear at top-left, the round close button is unambiguous and well separated in the top-right corner, and the four covers in the first row are evenly gutted, uniformly sized, and each label ("Farm", "Dinosaurs", "Creatures", "Nature") fits on one line inside its card with no truncation or overlap. The second row is thinned by the bottom fade, correctly signalling more content below; judging only the content clear of that strip, nothing is misaligned or mislabelled. The page behind — color swatches down the left edge, the tool row along the bottom, the faint gear glyph in the bottom-right corner — is dimmed by the dialog scrim as expected, and the gear's shape is still locatable.

One thing does not follow that pattern: the red trash button at the top-right of the frame is drawn at full saturation and full brightness while everything else behind the dialog is scrimmed. It is the brightest, highest-chroma element in the entire image, sitting outside the card and pulling the eye off the open dialog and away from the close button that shares that same corner region. Two round controls of very different visual weight now occupy adjacent space in the top-right, which muddies which one the tap belongs to while the picker is open. Its docked position past the edge is settled design; what is visible here is that it alone appears to escape the overlay's scrim treatment applied to every other background control.
entries.recommendation: Include the docked trash button in the dialog scrim so it dims and blurs with the rest of the background while the coloring-book card is open, leaving the card's close button as the only full-contrast round control in that corner.

On the card, the "Coloring Books" heading is white on a dark charcoal panel and reads cleanly, and the cover tiles use a slightly lighter fill than the panel so each tile is distinguishable from its background. The second cover row is thinned by the scroll fade along the bottom edge, which is the intended cue and not judged. No text, control, or glyph on the card is illegible against its background in night mode.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique: The coloring-page picker dialog occupies nearly the full 440px landscape height, leaving a scroll viewport of roughly 250px for the page grid. Both thumbnails are cut partway down — the cow's legs and the cat's flowers are sliced by a hard horizontal edge at the modal's bottom boundary, with no gradient thinning visible along that edge and no page labels beneath the cards. No card in the grid sits fully clear of the cut, so nothing readable-as-complete is offered before the user scrolls, and the truncation reads as clipping rather than as the app's fade cue. The rest of the frame holds up: "Farm" and the back chevron are legible with generous header spacing, the close X is a well-sized target clearly separated from the title row, the scrim correctly dims the palette and toolbar behind, and the settings glyph at bottom-right is locatable.
entries.recommendation: In short-viewport landscape, tighten the modal header band and thumbnail aspect ratio so at least one full page card plus its label fits above the fold, and ensure the grid's bottom fade is painted over the last visible row instead of ending in a hard cut.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
The open "Farm" card is the thing to judge, and its content holds up in night mode: the title "Farm" is near-white on the dark card and fully legible, and the two page thumbnails render as bright white line art on dark tiles with strong separation (the softening at their lower edge is the scroll fade being drawn, not a legibility fault).

The weak point is the card's own two navigation controls. Both the back chevron at top-left and the close "×" at top-right are drawn as mid-gray glyphs inside barely-visible gray discs sitting on the dark card surface — the disc fill is only a shade off the card background, and the glyph strokes are thin and dim relative to the crisp white title beside them. These are dialog chrome, not the deliberately-recessed parent-facing chevron/settings glyphs, so they are expected to read as ordinary affordances; here the close button in particular reads noticeably fainter than the title it sits level with, and against the busy white line art below it the eye is pulled away from it. It is findable, but it is the dimmest interactive element on the card by a clear margin, and it is the primary way out of this overlay.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground contrast of the "Farm" card's back-chevron and close-"×" glyphs (and lift their disc fills a step off the card background) so these dialog controls read at roughly the strength of the card title rather than as the faintest marks on the card.

entries.critique:
Frame shows the drawing canvas with the vertical color palette docked along the left edge, the docked red trash button at the top-right edge, the collapsed-panel chevron at bottom-left of the canvas, and the settings gear at bottom-right. No text, modal, or scrolling region is exercised in this frame.

On the coachmark itself, judged only on what is drawn: the ghost trash disc mid-canvas is legible as a pink circle with a white/yellow trash glyph, and the pink arc sweeping up and off the right edge reads as a motion path. The weak point is the black pointing-hand cursor, drawn overlapping the lower-right quadrant of that disc rather than beside it. Its dark outline crosses the disc edge against the saturated pink fill, so the hand's fingers and the trash lid collide and neither shape resolves cleanly at this size — the one place in the frame where two coachmark elements are stacked instead of adjacent. The motion arc also passes behind the disc, putting a third overlapping edge in the same small region.
entries.recommendation: Offset the pointing-hand cursor so it sits clear of the ghost trash disc — e.g. just below/right with only the fingertip touching — and give it a light halo or outline so its silhouette separates from the saturated pink fill and the motion arc behind it.

entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique: Visible content: left palette column of ten swatches (purple swatch ringed as active), a single pale purple stroke across the canvas, the red trash button glowing at the right edge, a large red circular arc crossing the top-right corner, plus the bottom-left chevron and bottom-right gear (both locatable as thin gray glyphs). The accept ring is the problem: its center lies offscreen beyond the top-right corner, so only an arc is visible — it enters at the top edge, bulges left, and exits at the right edge. Critically, the trash button it is meant to confirm sits OUTSIDE that arc, to its lower-left, not at or near its center. The ring therefore does not visually enclose or claim its target; it reads as an unrelated red curve drawn across the corner of the canvas, with only the shared red hue linking it to the button glow. Because the majority of the ring is beyond the 956x440 viewport, its circular form must be inferred rather than seen, weakening the 'held past threshold' signal at the moment it matters most. Other aspects pass: swatches are evenly spaced and non-overlapping, no text is present to fit or clip, no modal or scrolling region is open, and both parent-facing quiet glyphs are findable.
entries.recommendation: Anchor the accept ring on the trash button so the button sits at the ring's center, and size/inset it so the full ring — or at minimum a clearly readable majority, symmetric about the button — falls inside the 956x440 landscape viewport, rather than being centered offscreen with the button outside the arc.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique: The install banner card's supporting text does not fit within its container in this landscape viewport. The title "Add Splotch to your home screen" wraps to two lines, pushing the two-line subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" downward so that its final line sits flush against the bottom rounded border of the card with effectively zero bottom padding — the text baseline/descenders are pinched by the card edge, and the card's bottom border in turn sits only a few pixels above the bottom of the 440px-tall viewport. This reads as a text-fit/near-clipping problem rather than an intentional treatment, and it is the only element in the frame whose text crowds its own boundary. Hierarchy inside the card is otherwise correct: bold dark title, smaller gray secondary line, a saturated purple "How?" pill as the primary action, and a neutral round × dismiss at comparable size, both clearly separated with unambiguous, adequately sized touch targets and good contrast against the white card. The palette column at left, the canvas strokes, the docked round trash button at top right, the collapse chevron at bottom left, and the settings glyph at bottom right are all present and locatable; no overlap between the banner and any control is visible, and the page behind is at full brightness with no scrim, consistent with a non-modal banner.
entries.recommendation: Give the banner text room in short landscape viewports: widen the text column (or reduce/tighten the title so it stays on one line), add explicit bottom padding inside the card so the subtitle's last line clears the rounded border, and raise the card a few more points off the bottom viewport edge.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
The banner reads clearly overall: icon, two-line title, "How?" pill, and round close button form a legible header row, and the divider separates it cleanly from the instruction paragraph, whose inline Share and chevron glyphs sit on the baseline without breaking line rhythm. Palette column, canvas strokes, docked trash button, expand chevron and settings glyph are all visible and unobstructed; no scrim is present and nothing overlaps the card. The one actionable problem is vertical padding inside the card at this height. The subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" wraps to a second line sitting almost flush against the divider rule below it, with visibly less room than the gap above the title. The crowding repeats at the bottom: the final line "first." ends only a few pixels above the card's bottom border, far less than the horizontal inset on the same paragraph, so the text reads as pressed against the edge. The card also bottoms out very close to the 440px viewport floor, leaving essentially no margin below it, which is what forces the interior padding to collapse. No text is clipped and descenders render fully, so this is polish rather than a fit failure.</critique>
</invoke>
entries.recommendation: In short landscape viewports, hold a fixed minimum bottom padding inside the card (matching the paragraph's left/right inset) below the last instruction line and a consistent gap above the divider, and reserve a small margin between the card and the screen edge — letting the card scroll internally if content no longer fits rather than collapsing interior padding.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique: The parent gate card overflows the 440px-tall landscape viewport. Its footer — "Manage these checks in" / "Settings › Parent Center" — is sliced by the bottom edge of the frame: the second line renders only its top portion, with the descenders and the rest of the row cut away, and the card's bottom padding and rounded bottom corners never appear. There is no fade gradient over that edge, so this is hard clipping by the viewport rather than the app's scroll-fade cue, and no scroll affordance is visible to reach the cut content. The rest of the card is sound: "Grown-Ups Only", the subtitle, the 6 × 9 prompt with its two empty answer slots, and the full 0–9 keypad plus backspace all fit with even gutters and generous key targets; the close button sits clear in the top-right corner. The left color palette column, however, reads at full brightness while the canvas behind the card is darkened, so the scrim does not cover the whole page uniformly here — the swatches compete with the dialog for attention at the left edge.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the gate card to the landscape viewport height (e.g. max-height with internal scrolling or a reduced footer/keypad spacing) so the "Settings › Parent Center" footer row renders fully above the bottom edge, and extend the dialog scrim across the left palette column so the whole page behind the card is dimmed.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The AI style picker card itself is well formed: "Pick a style" heads the card, eight thumbnails sit on an even 4x2 grid with consistent gutters and equal tile sizes, and every label (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) fits on a single line under its tile with no truncation or wrapping. The Sticker tile carries a clear selection ring, so current state is legible. The circular close button sits at the top-right of the card, is visually distinct, and is well separated from the nearest thumbnail, so it reads as its own touch target. The card fits within the 440px landscape height with clear margin above and below, and there is no fade edge or partially cut row anywhere in it, so nothing implies hidden scrollable content.

The actionable problem is that the dialog scrim is applied unevenly. Only the central canvas area behind the card is darkened and blurred. The full-height color palette column along the left edge is at full brightness and full saturation, the round drawing-tool buttons across the bottom are at full brightness, and the red trash button at the top right is fully saturated - visibly brighter than the canvas immediately beside it. This produces a bright vertical band down the left third of the frame and a bright strip along the bottom that compete with the open card for attention, and the saturated red trash button is among the highest-contrast elements in the frame while the dialog is open. The bright/dim boundary is directly visible as a hard vertical edge between the palette column and the darkened canvas.

The chevron and the bottom-right settings glyph are both locatable in the image, so they meet the findability floor.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim across the entire viewport so the left color palette column, the bottom actions panel, and the trash button are darkened and blurred to the same degree as the canvas, instead of scrimming only the central canvas region.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The AI-result card is well composed: dial, "Making your picture…", the 30-second sub-line, and the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill stack in clear priority order; each text line fits on one line with no clipping, and the close button sits clear of the card corner with room around it.

The problem is scrim coverage. Only the central canvas band is dimmed — it reads gray — while the full-height color-palette column down the left edge is still on a bright white ground with its swatches at full saturation, and the red trash button at top right is likewise at full strength. So the page behind the dialog is darkened in one region and untouched in two others, and the two most saturated objects in the frame (the swatch grid, the red/yellow trash) sit outside the scrim competing with the card for attention; the eye is pulled left before it lands on the dialog. The boundary also shows as a hard vertical seam where the white palette column meets the gray canvas.

The chevron at bottom left and the settings glyph at bottom right are both locatable. Nothing is clipped or overlapped, and the card needs no scrolling at this height.
entries.recommendation: Apply the dialog scrim across the whole viewport rather than the canvas region alone, so the left-edge color-palette column and the top-right trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas while the AI card is open.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the open AI-result card is mostly sound: "Making your picture…" is near-white on the dark card and reads clearly, the "This takes about 30 seconds" subline is dimmer but still legible, the ✕ close button sits in a light-outlined disc against the dark card top-right and is easy to find, and the parent-facing chevron (bottom-left) and gear (bottom-right) glyphs are both locatable in the frame. The progress dial is high-chroma magenta over a very dark card, so its filled/unfilled split is unambiguous.

The one weak spot is the primary action, "Keep drawing while you wait": the label is rendered in a light lavender that sits close in both lightness and hue to its own muted violet pill, so the text has noticeably less separation from its background than any other text on the card, and it is the smallest-weight element carrying an action. In night mode this is the element most likely to read as soft or half-dissolved into the button, and it is the control the user is actually meant to press while the dial spins.
entries.recommendation: Raise the contrast of the "Keep drawing while you wait" label against its violet pill — lighten the label toward the near-white used for "Making your picture…" and/or darken/desaturate the pill fill — so the button text has clearly more separation from its background than the surrounding secondary copy.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
The dialog itself is in good shape: the generated rainbow sits in a rounded frame with even margins inside the white card, the "Download" button is a large, clearly tappable purple pill with icon and label fully fitted, and the round close button in the top-right corner of the card is unobstructed with adequate clearance from the image edge. The "AI-generated picture · Report" chip below the card reads cleanly, with the flag icon and "Report" text legible and no truncation. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable — the expand chevron at the left of the bottom bar and the gear in the bottom-right corner. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems anywhere in the frame.

The visible problem is the scrim's coverage. The canvas area behind the card is dimmed as expected, but the color palette column along the left edge is not: its swatches (purple, blue, teal, green, mustard, orange, red, magenta, black, and the multicolor chip) render at full saturation and full brightness against the dimmed page, and the red trash button at the top right is likewise undimmed and fully vivid. In landscape the palette occupies a tall left column of roughly a sixth of the frame width, so the result is two bands of the brightest, most colorful elements on screen sitting outside the darkening while the modal is open. They compete directly with the card for attention and, being full-strength and tappable-looking, they also read as still-active controls rather than as blocked background.
entries.recommendation: Extend the modal scrim over the full page in landscape so the left-edge color palette column and the top-right trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, matching the treatment the rest of the background already receives.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
The dialog itself holds up well in night mode: the AI result card sits on a light panel with a bright image, the "Download" pill is a saturated purple with white label and icon that reads cleanly, and the circular close button is a white-outlined glyph at the card's corner — all easily legible. The scrim behind is doing its job, and the palette swatches, trash button, chevron and settings glyph beneath it read dim as expected from that darkening; both parent-facing glyphs (chevron bottom-left, gear bottom-right) remain locatable in the frame.

The one thing drawn on top of the scrim rather than inside the card is the caption row: "AI-generated picture" plus a flag icon and "Report" link, sitting directly on the near-black darkened canvas. The caption is a mid-gray at small size and sits at the low end of comfortable; the "Report" affordance is worse — a medium purple close in luminance to its near-black backdrop, and its small flag icon in the same purple is the weakest mark in the frame. Since this is the only reporting path for a generated image and it is deliberately placed outside the bright card, it should not be the least legible element on screen. Nothing else in the frame presents an actionable night-mode contrast or legibility problem.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the on-scrim caption row for dark mode — raise "Report" and its flag icon to a light lavender/near-white tone (and nudge the "AI-generated picture" gray up) so both clear roughly 4.5:1 against the darkened canvas behind them.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique: The report-confirmation dialog renders cleanly at 956 × 440. Hierarchy is clear: bold title, a body paragraph in secondary gray, a two-up preview row with captions, then a two-button footer where "Send report" carries the filled purple emphasis and "Cancel" the tinted secondary treatment. All text fits its container — the four-line retention paragraph wraps without clipping or overflow, and both image captions ("The AI picture", "The drawing behind it") sit fully within their column widths. The two preview cards are equal size, aligned on a shared baseline, and neither thumbnail is squashed or cropped awkwardly. Padding is even on left and right, and vertical rhythm between title, paragraph, previews, and footer is consistent. In this short landscape viewport the card still fits the frame with margin above and below and shows no scroll cut, no truncated line, and no element overlap. The circular close button straddles the top-right card edge as an intentional overhang and is fully drawn and unobstructed. Both footer buttons are wide, tall, and clearly separated, so touch targets are unambiguous. The darkened, blurred page behind — palette, canvas, corner controls — is the dialog scrim described as intended, and the faint bottom-corner glyphs are locatable (the settings gear at bottom right and the panel chevron at left edge are both visible). Contrast on the card itself is comfortable for title, body, captions, and both button labels.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the report-confirmation card is largely sound. The heading "Report this picture" is near-white on the dark card and reads crisply; the retention paragraph ("...deleted after 30 days.") is a light gray that stays comfortably legible at this size. The primary "Send report" button is white on a saturated purple fill with strong separation, and "Cancel" is white on a muted purple-gray fill that still reads clearly as a button with legible text. The two thumbnail captions, "The AI picture" and "The drawing behind it", are small and gray but their letterforms remain resolvable. The AI thumbnail itself is bright and unaffected. The page behind is darkened and blurred by the dialog scrim, so the palette column, the trash button, and the corner glyphs are out of scope; the settings glyph in the bottom-right corner is still locatable as a shape.

The one weak spot on the card itself is the close control at the top-right: the ✕ glyph is a mid-gray stroke sitting on a dark circular disc whose value is very close to the card background, so the affordance has little edge definition and the glyph reads faint relative to every other control on the card. Unlike the corner chevron and settings glyphs, this is a dialog dismissal control on an in-focus card, where the intended read is "clearly actionable", not "recede behind the artwork". It is findable but the weakest interactive element in the frame.
entries.recommendation: Raise the close control's contrast on the report card: lighten the ✕ stroke toward the same near-white used for the heading, and either brighten the disc behind it or give it a visible border so the button separates from the card surface.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique: The refusal card is well formed: the palette emoji, the headline "Let's try drawing something else!", the two-line body, the "For grown-ups" caption and the "Report this refusal" pill are centered with even vertical rhythm, no text is clipped or overflowing, nothing overlaps, and the circular close button sits clear of the content in the top-right corner. The settings glyph in the bottom-right and the panel chevron at bottom-left are both locatable. The visible defect is uneven scrim coverage: the canvas region directly behind the card is darkened and blurred, but the left color-palette column renders on a bright white ground with fully saturated swatches, and the trash button at top-right is at full red/yellow saturation. Those two areas sit at normal page brightness while the strip between them is dimmed, so the scrim reads as covering only the canvas rather than the whole page. The result is that the palette column and the trash button are the highest-chroma elements in the frame and pull attention away from the open refusal dialog, weakening the intended hierarchy.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim so it covers the full viewport — including the left color-palette column and the docked trash button — so every background element is darkened to the same degree and the refusal card is the brightest, highest-contrast thing on screen.

entries.surface_description: The child-safe refusal treatment.
entries.critique:
The refusal dialog lays a scrim over the canvas and palette, so judgement rests on the card itself. The card reads well overall: "Let's try drawing something else!" is near-white and bold on the dark card, the two-line body copy sits at a gray that is clearly legible, the "Report this refusal" pill has light text on a saturated purple fill with obvious edges, and the circled ✕ close button top-right has a visible ring and bright glyph. The corner chevron and settings gear are both locatable at bottom-left and bottom-right as designed.

The one weak element is the "For grown-ups" label above the button. It is the smallest type on the card, in a mid-gray visibly dimmer than the body copy directly above it — dimmer than the text it qualifies, even though it is the cue telling a parent the button below is theirs. It is card text inside the open dialog, where normal readability is the standard, not one of the intentionally recessed parent glyphs. At this size and weight it is the first thing on the card to fail at a glance.
entries.recommendation: Raise the "For grown-ups" label to at least the same gray as the card's body copy (or increase its size/weight), so the only cue marking the button below as parent-facing is not the dimmest text in the dialog.

entries.surface_description: The generic generation failure treatment.
entries.critique: The AI error dialog gives no way to act on its own instruction: the copy reads "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!" but the only control in the card is the circular close X at the top right. The user is told to retry and given nothing to retry with — they must dismiss and rediscover the AI button. The card is also compositionally hollow: it spans roughly 200–390px vertically, yet the emoji and single text line sit in the upper-middle, leaving the bottom ~35% empty, reading as a layout waiting for a button that never arrives. Separately, the dialog scrim is applied inconsistently. The canvas, the panel chevron, and the settings glyph behind the card are clearly darkened, but the color-palette rail down the left edge stays at full brightness — white background, fully saturated swatches — as does the red trash button at the top right. Those are the most chromatically intense elements in the frame and they pull attention away from the open card; the seam is visible as a hard vertical edge at x≈157 where dimmed canvas meets undimmed rail. Within the card itself hierarchy is fine: readable dark-on-white text, no clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems, and the close button is a clearly bounded circular target with adequate corner padding.
entries.recommendation: Add a primary "Try again" button in the empty lower half of the card so the copy's instruction is directly actionable, and extend the dialog scrim over the left color-palette rail and the trash button so the whole page behind the card is dimmed uniformly.

entries.critique:
The error card's own content carries the assessment. The message "Hmm, that didn't work. Please try again!" is rendered in a near-white light gray on the card's dark charcoal surface at a comfortable size, and reads cleanly with ample contrast; the frowning-face emoji above it is fully saturated and legible. The close button in the card's top-right is a white ring with a white X on the card surface — the highest-contrast element in the frame and unambiguously findable. The card surface itself is lifted a step above the darkened page behind it, so its edges are discernible without relying on a border.

Elements drawn on top of the scrimmed page also hold up: the color palette swatches along the left are individually distinguishable by hue including the two dark-on-dark ones (deep red and muted magenta), the round trash button at the top right retains its red fill and yellow-on-white glyph, the collapse chevron near the bottom-left of the panel area is locatable as a small gray arrow shape, and the settings gear in the bottom-right corner is locatable as a gray cog glyph. Both of those last two read faint by design, but their shapes can be found.

The darkened, softened canvas behind the card is the dialog scrim doing its job. No night-mode contrast or legibility defect is visible.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique: At 956x440 landscape, roughly three-quarters of the viewport height is page chrome: top margin, "Back to drawing" link, "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark, a display-size "Admin" heading, a "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, and a three-line persistence warning. No ledger rows and no free-grant metrics — the stated purpose of this page — are readable without scrolling. The bottom cut is a hard edge rather than the app's soft gradient fade, so nothing signals that content continues. Everything visible is otherwise well-formed: the amber warning wraps cleanly with its inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip fitting on-line, the input and "Add code" button are aligned with comfortable touch targets, "Sign out" is clear of the heading, and there is no clipping, overlap, or text-fit failure.
entries.recommendation: At short/landscape viewport heights, compress the page chrome — reduce the "Admin" heading size, drop the redundant "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, and tighten the top margin and wordmark-row spacing — so the access-codes section header and at least one ledger row clear the fold; apply the standard gradient fade at the bottom edge if that region scrolls.

entries.surface_description: The ledger, persistence warning, and free-grant metrics.
entries.critique: Night-mode legibility is broadly sound here: the "Admin" heading, "Manage AI access codes" subtitle, "ACCESS CODES · 2" label, the "Add a code..." placeholder, the input border, the "← Back to drawing" link, and the white-on-purple "Add code" button all separate clearly from the dark ground. First, in the light cream persistence-warning panel, the bold lead-in "Netlify Blobs is unavailable." is dark enough to read, but the amber-brown continuation sentence ("You're viewing a local-only copy... lost on the next restart.") is markedly lighter against the cream and is the faintest body text in the frame — and it carries the most consequential message on the page. The inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST code chip is weaker again, its gray-brown monospace sitting close in value to its own tinted chip background. Second, the "Sign out" button is light lavender text on a muted dark-purple fill, the lowest-separation interactive control visible, reading distinctly softer than the adjacent "Add code" button.
entries.recommendation: Darken the warning panel's body text and the inline ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST chip text toward the same weight as the bold "Netlify Blobs is unavailable." lead-in so the whole warning meets body-text contrast on the cream ground, and lighten the "Sign out" label (or deepen its purple fill) to widen its text/fill separation.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique: Landscape phone view of the admin access-code list. Hierarchy reads cleanly: section label "ACCESS CODES · 2" with a rule, then the add-code row, then the card of code rows. The expanded row shows "daycare-club" in monospace with a "Copy" button and an active (filled) chevron, and beneath it a full-width two-up of "Copy link" and "Remove" — both buttons are comfortably tall and wide, well separated by a gutter, with Remove tinted red to distinguish the destructive action. The collapsed row below ("page-inventory-harness") mirrors the same layout with a resting chevron. No text is truncated, clipped, or overlapping; the monospace code labels, button labels, and section headers all fit with room to spare, and the divider between the expanded row's actions and the next row keeps the two rows from reading as one block. Vertical rhythm between the input row, the card, and the "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" heading is even. The amber warning banner at the top and the card edge at the bottom thin out at the viewport edges, which is the scrolling-region fade cue rather than a legibility fault; everything clear of those strips is fully legible. Touch targets are unambiguous — Copy, the chevron, Copy link, and Remove all present as discrete controls at adequate size and spacing for a thumb in landscape.

entries.surface_description: The in-place row expansion on phones and inline actions on tablets.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this admin panel is largely sound. The banner text (yellow on a warm dark-olive card), the "ACCESS CODES · 2" and "FREE GENERATION GRANTS · SAMPLE 0" section labels, the monospace code names `daycare-club` and `page-inventory-harness`, the "Add code" button's white label on violet, and the "Copy" outline buttons all read cleanly at a glance. Inside the expanded row, "Copy link" (violet) and "Remove" (rose) both sit comfortably above their dark row fills and are unambiguously legible and distinguishable from each other. The inline `ALLOWED_TOKENS_LIST` code chip inside the banner is slightly muddier than the surrounding sentence — the chip's own background lifts toward the text color — but it stays readable.

The one weak element is the collapsed chevron on the `page-inventory-harness` row. It is a thin gray glyph on the row's dark fill with no button, disc, or outline behind it, and it is noticeably fainter than the expanded row's chevron, which sits on a filled violet swatch. This is a per-row expand/collapse affordance in an admin list, not one of the two parent-facing corner controls that are intentionally recessed, so it does not inherit that exemption — the collapsed and expanded states of the same control should not differ this much in weight. Its shape is still locatable, so this is a weakness rather than a disappearance.

Placeholder text "Add a code…" in the input is dim relative to the field, as placeholders normally are, and does not rise to a finding on its own.
entries.recommendation: Give the collapsed row chevron the same container treatment as the expanded one — a filled or outlined square button behind the glyph, with the glyph raised to at least the weight of the adjacent "Copy" button's label — so both states of the row toggle carry equal visual weight in dark mode.

entries.surface_description: The blank drawing surface and its resting canvas chrome.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the resting canvas holds up. The dark charcoal canvas carries a subtle texture that stays well below any content in luminance, so nothing competes with future strokes. The color palette rail runs on a slightly darker vertical strip, and all nine swatches — purple, blue, teal, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, white — read as saturated, clearly separated discs against it; the white swatch in particular is unambiguous rather than blowing out. The active purple swatch carries a visible ring plus a lighter halo, so the selected state is distinguishable in dark mode without relying on color alone. The multicolor palette-picker button at the bottom of the rail is legible as a distinct flower-shaped glyph. The docked trash button at the top right is a bright warm orange-to-pink disc with a white trash glyph on it, comfortably the strongest element in the frame, which is right for a destructive control. The two parent-facing glyphs are quiet by design and both are locatable in this image: the chevron sits just right of the palette rail near the bottom edge, and the settings gear sits in the bottom-right corner, each rendered as a thin gray shape with visible interior detail (the gear's teeth and center hole resolve) — faint, but findable, which is the floor they owe. No scrim, flyout, or scrolling fade is in play here, and no disabled-state buttons are visible. Nothing in this frame is an actionable night-mode contrast or legibility defect.

entries.surface_description: The server-rendered administrator sign-in surface.
entries.critique:
Hierarchy reads correctly: "Admin" heading, subtitle, a rule-flanked SIGN IN section label, then a single input plus primary button. Text fits everywhere — no clipping, truncation, or overlap; the placeholder, the "SPLOTCH ADMIN" wordmark with its dot motif, and the "← Back to drawing" link are all fully rendered. Touch targets are adequate for tablet: the input and the "Sign in" button are both roughly 50px tall, and the button's purple fill against white is clearly actionable. No modals or scrolling regions are present.

The one visible weakness is vertical composition. The card is anchored to the top of the 744px-tall viewport and ends around y=383, leaving roughly half the screen as empty gray. Inside the card, the content stops at the button (y≈325) but the card continues to y≈383, producing a bottom pad noticeably deeper than the space between other elements and an unbalanced, top-heavy block on a landscape tablet. The "← Back to drawing" link also sits tight to the card's top edge relative to the generous side and bottom padding.

Secondary, minor: the horizontal rule after "SIGN IN" runs the full card width while the form beneath occupies only about two-thirds of it, so the section divider promises a wider content region than the form fills.
entries.recommendation: Vertically center the sign-in card in the viewport (or cap its top offset) and tighten the card's bottom padding to match its top/side padding, so the short form reads as a balanced centered block rather than a top-anchored panel with a large trailing void.
