entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this sign-in card is mostly sound: "Admin" and "Manage AI access codes" read as near-white and light gray on the dark card, the "Back to drawing" link is a saturated violet that separates cleanly from the panel, and the input border and its "Admin access key" placeholder are both discernible. Two weak points are visible. (1) The primary "Sign in" button uses white label text on a mid-tone lavender fill; the two are close in perceived lightness, so the label reads softer than the body copy above it despite being the page's primary action — the least legible text on the card is the one on its most important control. (2) The "SIGN IN" section label is small, letter-spaced, all-caps gray, and the hairline rule extending from it is nearly indistinguishable from the card background, so the section header sits at the edge of readability at this size. Everything else in frame holds up in dark mode.
entries.recommendation: Darken the "Sign in" button fill (a deeper violet) so its white label clears 4.5:1, and lift the "SIGN IN" section label and its divider rule a step lighter against the card.

entries.critique: The Changelog opening view reads cleanly at 1133 × 744. Hierarchy is unambiguous: "← Back to drawing" and the Splotch wordmark sit on one header line, the large "Changelog" title dominates, and a two-line subtitle sets context before the content splits into a left CONTENTS rail and a right detail column separated by a hairline rule. In the rail, the active entry (Version 1.5.0, August 12, 2026) is marked with a lavender fill plus a purple left bar and purple text, and the seven version rows each pair a bold title with a lighter date at a consistent rhythm — no crowding, no baseline drift. The right column repeats the version and right-aligns its date on the same line, then groups notes under emoji-led "New", "Improved", and "Fixed" headings with consistent bullet indentation and line spacing. All text fits its measure; nothing wraps awkwardly, overlaps, or is truncated mid-word, and the two-line subtitle breaks sensibly. Row heights in the contents rail are generous enough to be comfortably tappable and each row's hit area is clearly delimited by the spacing and the active-row highlight. The last visible line ("Magic brush and picture saves recover from rare canvas failures") thins toward the bottom edge — the documented scroll-fade cue for content continuing past the edge — and everything clear of that faded strip is fully legible. Color use is restrained and consistent: one purple accent for the back link and active state, neutral grays for dates and rules, near-black for body copy. No clipping, overlap, or visual-consistency problems are visible.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Opening view of the styleguide at 1133×744 reads cleanly: header with theme toggle and wordmark, a left nav with a clearly selected "Color" item, and a well-ranked content column (H1, deck, sources line, callout card, part label, section heading). Spacing is even, nothing overlaps, nothing is clipped at the edges, and the sidebar/content boundary is consistent. Nav rows are generously tall and easy to hit; the Light/Dark segmented control shows an unambiguous selected state.

One actionable nit: inline code tokens are allowed to break across lines. "var(--…)" in the Foundations paragraph splits so that "var(-" ends one line and "-…)" starts the next, and in the callout "--" trails the end of a line before "text-strong" begins the next. A broken token reads as two different tokens and is easy to mis-copy, which matters more on a page whose whole purpose is naming exact token strings. Everything else in the frame — text fit, contrast, alignment, consistency of the code-token styling — is fine at this size.
entries.recommendation: Apply `white-space: nowrap` (with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` only as a last-resort fallback) to inline `code` spans in prose so token names like `var(--…)` and `--text-strong` never break across two lines.

entries.surface_description: The public living styleguide at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast holds up across most of the frame: the H1, sidebar nav labels, the active "Color" pill, section headings and body prose all sit at comfortable brightness against the near-black page, and the purple "Not sure? Start here" callout keeps its heading and inline code tokens clearly readable over its violet surface.

The weak point is the small metadata line under the intro: "Sources: lib/design/tokens.ts → tokens.css (npm run gen:tokens) · lib/palette.ts · the icon set · the shipped components". Its plain-gray segments — the word "Sources:", the interpuncts, and especially the trailing "· the icon set · the shipped components" — render at a very low-luminance gray at roughly 11px, noticeably dimmer than any other prose on the page and close to fading into the background. The purple link fragments in the same line read fine, which makes the gray runs look accidentally under-weighted rather than deliberately secondary. A secondary caption is a legitimate role, but at this size in dark mode it lands below a comfortable reading floor.

A milder version of the same thing appears in the callout body, where the muted lavender running text is dimmer than the code tokens beside it, though it stays legible.

Nothing else is an issue: the theme toggle's inactive "Light" label is dim by state, and the crayon-dot row and SPLOTCH wordmark in the header are clear.
entries.recommendation: Raise the foreground color of the small "Sources:" metadata line (the gray non-link segments, including the trailing "· the icon set · the shipped components") to a lighter dark-mode muted token so that ~11px text clears roughly 4.5:1 against the page background, or bump that line's size/weight to match the other secondary prose.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique:
The page reads cleanly overall: strong title hierarchy, a well-formed two-column split with the form at left and the "What happens next" card at right, no clipped text, no overlap, and no scrolling region or overlay in the frame. Tabs, textarea, and the "Send report" button are all comfortably sized for touch.

The one actionable item is the "Include device info" checkbox. The box itself renders at roughly 20×20 px with the label text sitting beside it, and there is no visible hit area (no padded row, no bounding highlight) suggesting the label is part of the target. On a tablet in landscape this is the smallest interactive element on the screen by a wide margin — every other control here is at least ~44 px tall — so it reads as an undersized and ambiguous tap target next to otherwise generously sized controls. It also sits tight against the textarea above it (~14 px gap), which crowds it further and makes it easy to miss as an interactive row rather than a caption.

Secondary, minor: the helper text below the checkbox ("Your report goes to our private support tracker…") is left-aligned to the checkbox row but is visually indistinguishable in weight and spacing from the checkbox label's parenthetical, so the two grey strings blur into one block of fine print.
entries.recommendation: Make the "Include device info" row a full-width tappable control at least 44 px tall — enlarge the checkbox and wrap the box plus its label in a single padded, clickable row — and add a bit more vertical separation between it and the textarea above.

entries.surface_description: The standalone bug report and feature idea form.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on this feedback form is largely sound: the "Send us feedback" heading, intro paragraph, "What went wrong?" label, the purple "Send report" button, and the "What happens next" panel (including the underlined privacy policy link on its tinted violet ground) all read cleanly against the dark card. The one actionable contrast/legibility problem is the segmented control. The selected segment "Something's broken" is filled near-black — darker than the surrounding card — while the unselected segment "I have an idea" is filled a noticeably lighter gray, and the two labels sit at similar brightness. In a dark theme the lighter, more forward chip reads as the active one, so the selection state is inverted or at least ambiguous; the only separation is a faint inner border. Milder, and not on its own actionable: the textarea placeholder "Describe what happened, and what you expected instead…" and the unchecked "Include device info" checkbox are the dimmest interactive affordances in the frame, sitting close in value to their field fills, though both remain locatable and readable.
entries.recommendation: Reverse the segmented control's dark-mode fills so the selected segment is the lighter/raised surface (or give it the accent purple fill with white label) and the unselected segment recedes to the card background, so active state is carried by contrast rather than by a subtle border.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique: At the opening scroll position the privacy page reads cleanly at 1133 × 744. Hierarchy is clear and well-staged: "← Back to drawing" and the SPLOTCH dot-mark sit on one aligned top row, the H1 "Privacy policy" dominates, a two-line intro follows at comfortable measure, and the "THE SHORT VERSION" eyebrow with its rule and right-aligned "Last updated August 20, 2026" cleanly separates the summary card. Inside the card, six color-chip rows are evenly spaced with consistent divider rules, bold lead-ins and regular follow-on text; no row wraps, collides, or truncates, and the chips align on a common left edge with the text baseline. Spacing between blocks is consistent and the card's inset from the page container is symmetric left and right. Text fit is good throughout — no overflow, clipping, or overlap anywhere in the frame, and the rounded page container's edges are intact. Below, "THE DETAILS" begins with a sidebar nav item ("What stays on your device", highlighted with a left accent bar) beside the matching section heading; both are cut only by the bottom of the viewport, which is ordinary below-the-fold continuation at the opening position rather than a layout fault. Only one interactive control is on screen, the back link, which is clearly styled as a link in the accent purple with an arrow affordance and sits with ample clear space; no modals, scrims, or flyouts are present, and no touch target is crowded or ambiguous. Visual consistency — type ramp, eyebrow treatment, rule weight, color-chip palette, corner radii — holds across the whole visible region.

entries.surface_description: The public privacy policy at its opening position.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this privacy page is broadly healthy. The "Privacy policy" heading, the intro paragraph, the bold lead-ins ("No ads.", "No tracking.", …) and their trailing sentences all render as light warm-gray on the near-black page and card, and read cleanly at this size. The "← Back to drawing" link is a saturated lavender that stands off the dark background without glowing. The colored pills beside each promise row are bright enough to be distinguishable from one another (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple) and are decorative rather than load-bearing, so their contrast is not a legibility risk. The card's 1px border and the hairline row dividers are faint but that is separation, not information.

The one soft spot is the small-caps metadata band: the section eyebrows "THE SHORT VERSION" and "THE DETAILS", the rule beside them, and the right-aligned "Last updated August 20, 2026" are drawn in a mid-gray that sits noticeably below the body text on this dark ground, at a smaller size and with wide letterspacing that thins the strokes further. They stay findable, but the date in particular is real content a parent may want to check, and it is the weakest legible text in the frame. Nothing else here is a night-mode fault: the partially visible left nav item and heading at the bottom edge are simply the fold, not a contrast problem.
entries.recommendation: Lift the small-caps section eyebrows and the "Last updated …" date to a brighter gray in dark mode — closer to the secondary body text tone used in the promise rows — so the smallest, most letterspaced text is not also the lowest-contrast text on the page.

entries.critique: Hierarchy reads cleanly: back link and brand mark on one top row, then a large "Join the Splotch beta" title, a two-line intro, the Android/iPhone-iPad tab pair with the active tab marked by purple text plus an underline, then the "HOW TO JOIN ON ANDROID" eyebrow and the numbered steps. No text is clipped, truncated, or overlapping — the bold inline emphases ("Join group", "same Google account", "Become a tester") sit inline without breaking the line rhythm. The "Join the testers group" button is a filled purple pill with generous padding, a clear touch target, and its label fits with margin on all sides. The tabs are widely spaced and comfortably tappable. Content continues past the bottom edge, and the thinning of step 2's second line into the lower boundary is the app's gradient fade scroll cue being drawn, judged as such rather than as blur or a legibility fault; everything clear of that strip is crisp. Type styling, purple accent usage, and corner radii are consistent across the frame. No modal is open here, so nothing to assess for scrim or dialog scrolling.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this iOS tab is largely healthy: the "Join the Splotch beta" heading, the intro paragraph, the step titles ("Install TestFlight", "Accept the invitation"), the step body copy, and the white-on-purple "Get TestFlight from Apple" button all read cleanly against the near-black card. The active "iPhone / iPad" tab is legible in purple with a purple underline, and the bottom of the step-2 paragraph thins into the region's fade, which is the scroll cue being drawn rather than a legibility fault.

The one weak spot is the step-number badges. The "1" and "2" sit inside small dark discs whose fill is only slightly lighter than the page background, and the numerals themselves are rendered in a dim, desaturated tone at a very small size. Against the surrounding full-strength white step titles they read washed out, and the digits are hard to resolve at a glance — the "2" in particular nearly disappears into its disc. These are ordinal wayfinding markers for a sequential set-up flow, not deliberately-quiet parent-facing controls, so they should carry ordinary body-text contrast.

The eyebrow label "HOW TO JOIN ON IPHONE OR IPAD" and the inactive "Android" tab are both muted but still comfortably resolvable as secondary-hierarchy text, and I would not flag them.
entries.recommendation: Raise the step-number badges' contrast in dark mode — lighten the numeral to the same near-white used for the step titles (or at least a high-contrast tint of the accent), and/or increase the disc fill's separation from the page background, so "1" and "2" resolve at a glance.

The single visible flaw is line breaking in the supporting copy: on an 1133 px-wide landscape viewport the paragraph is constrained to roughly 310 px, so "Something went wrong. entries.recommendation: Widen the supporting paragraph's max-width (or apply balanced text wrapping) so "Something went wrong. Let's start a fresh drawing." fits on one line at landscape tablet widths instead of orphaning "drawing." on its own line.

entries.recommendation: Darken the "Start over" button's purple fill in dark mode (or increase the label weight/size) so the white label clears 4.5:1 against the fill, while keeping the fill light enough to remain clearly distinct from the near-black page.

Spacing between the rail, detail pane, and card edges is even, and the card is comfortably inset from the viewport on all sides.

The selected "Light" segment is legible as a raised white pill against the gray track; the two toggles read unambiguously (rotation off, sound on), and the volume slider fill matches the stated 50%. Touch targets are generous: rail rows, segment thirds, toggles, and the close button are all well above a comfortable tap size, with clear separation.

Both scrolling regions end in the app's soft gradient fade — the rail below "What's New" and the detail pane below "WHAT MAKES SOUND" — painted over the last row, which is the documented affordance rather than a defect; all content clear of those strips is crisp. The page behind is under the dialog's scrim, so the dimmed palette column, the docked trash button, and the low-contrast chevron and gear glyphs in the bottom corners are the intended background treatment; both corner glyph shapes remain locatable. No compact phone-landscape shell or orientation segments appear in this capture, so nothing there to assess.

No clipping, overlap, misalignment, or contrast problem is visible in the elements this frame puts in scope.

entries.critique:
The open Settings card is generally legible in night mode: "Settings", the "Sound" and "Tool Drawer" section titles, the selected "Sound" nav item, and the nav list labels read as near-white on the dark card. Toggles clearly read as on (purple track, white knob) and the volume fill is a bright violet bar clearly distinct from its dark track.

The weak point is the setting-row text inside the panels. The primary row labels — "Sound", "Drawing", "Deleting", "Enable Advanced Controls" — plus "Volume", the "50%" value, and the "WHAT MAKES SOUND" caps header are rendered in a mid-gray on the slightly-lighter row fill, noticeably dimmer than the white nav labels immediately to their left. These labels carry the meaning of each toggle, and they sit at the bottom of the usable contrast range rather than comfortably above it. "50%" is the worst case: small, gray, and the only textual readout of the slider value. The small speaker/pencil/trash row glyphs are likewise low-contrast, though redundant with their labels.

The "Enable Advanced Controls" row sits under the scroll fade, so it is judged only as far as the fade allows; the same gray-label pattern is visible on rows clear of the fade. Nothing else is a finding: the corner chevron and gear glyphs are locatable, the dimmed canvas and palette are the dialog scrim, and the trash button's edge docking is intended.
entries.recommendation: Raise the setting-row label, value, and group-header text inside the panels ("Sound", "Volume", "50%", "Drawing", "Deleting", "WHAT MAKES SOUND") to the same near-white token used by the nav list, reserving the dimmer gray only for genuinely secondary description lines.

entries.critique:
The Settings card reads well overall: clear "Settings" title, distinct sidebar/content split, consistent purple pill styling on the drawing-tool toggles with visible check marks, an unambiguous on-state switch for Enable Advanced Controls, and a well-formed close button. Both scrolling regions (sidebar past "What's New", content past the "Coloring" heading) show the expected soft fade, and content clear of those strips is fully legible. No clipping, overlap, or text-fit problems in the card; row heights and gutters are even.

One actionable thing: the Button Size slider has no visible thumb or handle. The track shows only a purple fill ending flush at ~60% with a square-ended edge against the gray remainder, so there is no grab affordance and no target to aim at — it reads more like a progress bar than a control. The "100%" value label sits far right, adjacent to nothing, which reinforces that reading. Everything else on the panel signals interactivity explicitly (switch knob, pill checkmarks), making this the one control whose operability is not visually stated.

Minor and not counted against it: the "Undo" pill occupies a half-width cell with an empty slot beside it, which is a normal consequence of an odd count in a two-column grid.
entries.recommendation: Give the Button Size slider a visible circular thumb at the fill boundary, sized to a comfortable touch target and raised above the track, so the control is identifiable and grabbable rather than reading as a progress bar.

entries.critique:
The Settings card renders cleanly at this size: two-column layout with the category rail left and the "Coloring" pane right, generous card padding, correct active state on "Coloring" (tinted pill plus left accent bar), and no truncation, overlap, or text clipping anywhere. Toggle rows are well-spaced with clear label/description hierarchy, the on/off states are distinguishable by both fill and knob position, and "Remove downloaded pictures" is a legible, comfortably sized destructive-tinted button. Both scroll regions show the expected soft fade over their last row ("What's New"/the trailing rail item, and the "Create AI images" row under the "AI Art" heading), so the continuation cue is present and the content clear of the fade is fully legible. The close button is a distinct outlined circle at the card's top-right with clear separation from the title. The settings gear at bottom-right and the panel chevron at bottom-left are both locatable as faint gray glyphs, which is their intended resting appearance.

One inconsistency is visible: the scrim behind the card darkens and blurs the canvas, but the vertical color-swatch rail down the left edge and the round trash button at the top right are still rendered at full brightness and full saturation — they sit visually forward of the dimmed page and compete with the open card for attention, especially the saturated red trash disc. The scrim appears to stop at the canvas rather than covering the full page behind the dialog.
entries.recommendation: Extend the settings dialog's scrim to cover the entire page behind it — including the left color-swatch rail and the docked trash button — so no background chrome renders at full brightness beside the open card.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog with AI Art selected is well composed: clear title, readable section header, consistent card grouping, toggles at a consistent right-edge column, and the sidebar's AI Art row is unambiguously selected via tint plus left accent bar. Text fits without clipping or overlap; the sidebar's bottom edge and the right pane's bottom row both thin into the intended scroll fade, and the partially visible "Auto-Save AI Images" row plus the cut sidebar item read as scrollable rather than broken. Access Code field, its monospace value, and the "Forget" button sit on one baseline with adequate spacing.

The actionable problem is the scrim's coverage. The page behind the dialog is darkened and blurred — visible in the canvas, the bottom-corner chevron and gear — but two page-level elements are not covered by it: the vertical color palette along the entire left edge renders at full saturation and brightness, and the red trash button at the top right does the same. Those two elements are the most chromatically intense things in the frame and now compete directly with the open card for attention, which is the opposite of what the scrim exists to do. The left palette in particular runs the full height of the window as a bright column of ten saturated discs beside a dimmed background, so the dimming reads as patchy rather than as a deliberate whole-page treatment.

Touch targets in the card are clear and well separated; the close button is a distinct outlined circle with clearance from the card corner.
entries.recommendation: Extend the settings dialog's scrim so it covers the full page including the left color-palette rail and the docked trash button, so every element behind the card is dimmed and blurred consistently instead of two saturated regions punching through at full brightness.

entries.recommendation: Raise the Access Code field's value text toward the same near-white tone used for the card's row titles (or at least the level of the body paragraph above it) so the code is unambiguously readable in dark mode.

entries.critique:
The Saving pane reads cleanly: section title, three rows in a grouped card with icon, label, sub-label and a right-aligned control each, consistent spacing, no clipping or overlap. Toggles and the "Choose folder" pill are large enough to read as separate hit targets, and the selected "Saving" nav item is clearly marked with a fill plus left accent bar. Both the left nav list and the right content pane end in the app's soft fade, correctly signalling more content below.

The one visible defect is in the Parent Center table header at the bottom of the right pane: "EVERY TIME" and "PER SESSION" each wrap onto two lines while the adjacent "NEVER" stays on one, so the three column labels sit on mismatched baselines and the header row reads as ragged rather than as one aligned set of choices. The wrap is not caused by the fade — the words are legible — it is a width-fit problem in those columns, and it is the first thing the parent sees when scrolling into the section that carries the actual protection settings. Spacing between "PER SESSION" and "NEVER" is also noticeably tighter than between "EVERY TIME" and "PER SESSION", weakening the read that these are three equal options.
entries.recommendation: Give the three Parent Center choice columns equal fixed widths sized to hold "EVERY TIME" and "PER SESSION" on one line (or bottom-align the header cells if wrapping must stay), so the three labels share a baseline and equal gutters.

entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the open Settings card is largely sound: "Install", "Feedback", the numbered row titles, the body paragraph, and the left-rail item labels all read as light text on the dark card with comfortable separation, and the selected "Install" row (purple fill plus left accent bar) is unambiguous. The close button ring and glyph in the top-right are visible against the card. The palette column, trash button, chevron, and gear behind the card sit under the dialog scrim, so their dimness is the scrim and out of scope.

The one weak spot is the small uppercase eyebrow labels — "IOS" above the install rows and "SEND FEEDBACK" above the paragraph. They are rendered in a mid-gray at a small size with letterspacing, noticeably dimmer than the body copy immediately beneath them, and "IOS" in particular nearly recedes into the card ground. Because these are the only thing grouping the rows under a platform heading, losing them costs real structure. Secondarily, the inactive "I have an idea" segment's label is dimmer than the active "Something's broken" label; this is legible and reads correctly as the unselected state, so it is not itself a finding, but it sits close to the floor.

Nothing else in the frame shows a night-mode legibility problem: the numeral prefixes "1." and "2." are dimmer than their titles but remain readable, and the chevrons at the row ends are faint yet locatable. The placeholder text at the bottom edge falls inside the scroll fade and is judged as the fade cue rather than a contrast fault.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance of the small uppercase section eyebrows ("IOS", "SEND FEEDBACK") in dark mode to at least the level of the body paragraph text, so that at their small size and letterspacing they clear 4.5:1 against the card ground.

entries.critique:
The Settings dialog reads cleanly at this size: the two-pane split (nav list left, content right) has clear hierarchy, the "Settings" title, "About" section heading, logo, tagline, links, and monospace version string are all legible with comfortable spacing, no text clipping, wrapping faults, or overlap. Row targets in the nav list are tall and well separated, the selected "About" row is unambiguously marked with a tinted fill and left accent bar, and the close X sits in its own circular target clear of the title. Links ("See all releases →", "Privacy Policy", "View on GitHub") are distinguishable by color and placement. The page behind is scrimmed as intended, so the dimmed palette column and corner glyphs are out of scope; the settings gear and panel chevron are both locatable at the bottom corners.

One thing is visibly off in the left nav's scrolling region. At the very top of the list a partial row is sliced by the header edge — only the lower sliver of its icon and none of its label survive — and the cut is a hard horizontal edge rather than the soft gradient fade this app uses to mark continuing scroll content. Compare the same list's bottom edge, where "About" ends flush with no fade either, so nothing in the frame signals that the list scrolls or that items exist above the visible ones. The result is an amputated icon fragment sitting directly under the title, which reads as a rendering seam rather than as an intentional overflow cue.
entries.recommendation: Apply the app's standard soft gradient fade to the top (and bottom, when overflowing) edge of the left settings nav list, and add a few pixels of scroll padding so a partially scrolled row is thinned out by the fade instead of being sliced by a hard header edge.

Night-mode contrast on the open Settings card is mostly sound: the "Settings" title, the left nav labels ("Sound", "Tool Drawer", … "About"), the release-note body copy, and the "See all releases →" and "View on GitHub" links all read cleanly against the dark card, and the selected "About" row has a clear purple fill plus left accent bar. The close button ring in the top-right is visible against the card.

Two items sit noticeably below everything else on the card. The version string "Version 1.5.0+012688c" is rendered in a small monospace face in a dim gray that is the faintest text in the frame — on the card's near-black surface its stem contrast is visibly weaker than the tagline directly above it, and the alphanumeric hash (where every glyph carries meaning and cannot be inferred from context) is exactly the kind of string that needs more, not less, contrast. The tagline "A joyful, kid-friendly drawing app" is also a muted gray, though large enough to stay comfortably legible.

entries.critique: Night-mode contrast holds across everything judgeable in this frame. The purple ink stroke sits clearly against the dark textured canvas — its lavender fill and slightly lighter core read as an intentional stroke, not a smudge, with no ambiguity against the near-black ground. The color palette rail along the left edge shows nine saturated swatches (purple, blue, teal, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, white) plus a multi-color picker, each fully separated from the dark rail background and from one another; the white swatch, the hardest case on a dark rail, is unambiguously a filled disc rather than a hole. The active-color selection is legible: the top purple swatch carries a visible ring, distinguishable from the unselected swatches below it at a glance. The docked trash button in the top-right renders a crisp white trash glyph on a warm red-to-pink gradient disc, high contrast and unmistakable; the portion sitting past the screen edge is the intended dock, not a contrast matter. The chevron at bottom-left and the gear at bottom-right are both faint gray glyphs, which is the intended parent-facing styling — and both shapes are locatable in the image (the chevron's arrowhead and the gear's toothed ring are each resolvable), so they meet the findability floor. No overlay or scrim is present, so no element is being judged through dimming. Nothing in the frame falls below a usable contrast level.

entries.surface_description: The expanded auxiliary-control drawer over a drawing.
entries.critique:
The expanded actions drawer sits flush against the bottom of the 744px-tall viewport with no bottom padding, and the round buttons are visibly cropped: the pencil, wave, coloring-book, camera, AI, and undo circles all terminate in a flat horizontal cut at the frame edge instead of closing as circles, and the small labels/badges beneath the coloring-book and camera icons are sliced through. Unlike the trash button, this row reads as clipped rather than deliberately docked — the cut is dead-flat along the screen edge across six buttons at once, and the icons themselves stay centered as if the full circle were expected to be visible. This also shortens the usable touch target on the bottom side of each button in the primary tool row, which is the row the child uses most.

The rest of the frame holds up: the drawer's six buttons are evenly spaced with consistent diameters and clear separation from one another; the color palette down the left rail is evenly pitched with a clearly ringed selected swatch; the single purple stroke on the canvas confirms the undo/AI/screenshot buttons are in their enabled, full-contrast state, and they read as such. Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable — the collapse chevron sits just right of the undo button and the gear sits in the bottom-right corner — so their quiet styling is arriving as intended without becoming unfindable. No overlap between the drawer and the palette, no text overflow, no scrim in play here.
entries.recommendation: Add bottom safe-area padding to the expanded actions drawer so the full circumference of each round button (and its label/badge) clears the viewport edge at 744px landscape height, matching the clearance the buttons already have from each other horizontally.

No text is present in the flyout, so there is no wrapping, truncation, or fit issue. All four glyphs sit fully inside their tiles and inside the card; the card's rounded corners are intact on all sides, with no clipping against the canvas, the color rail on the left, or the button row below. The flyout clears the Actions Panel with a visible gap and does not overlap the round buttons or the color palette. Tiles are large and square with generous padding, reading as comfortably tappable at this device size, and the card is small enough to show all its contents at once with no scrolling region and therefore no fade edge to evaluate. The page behind is at full brightness, consistent with the brush flyout casting no scrim; the color rail, canvas, and corner controls remain at normal contrast. The collapse chevron beside the Actions Panel and the settings gear in the opposite corner are both locatable as thin gray glyphs, meeting the findability floor. entries.surface_description: Line-width choices with live brush previews.
entries.critique:
The stroke-width flyout reads cleanly on its own terms: five choices in a single row on a white rounded card, widths escalating left to right, generous ~66 px spacing between hit areas, and the active choice (third) marked with a purple rounded outline and tinted fill that is unambiguous at a glance. Text fit is not a factor — the card is icon-only. No clipping, no overlap with the color rail on the left or the actions panel below (roughly a 10 px breathing gap between the card's bottom edge and the tops of the round buttons). The soft thinning at the card's right edge over the fifth stroke is the documented scroll-fade cue, so the row is judged on the four strokes clear of it, which are crisp. Page behind is at full brightness, consistent with a no-scrim flyout.

The one visible issue is anchoring. The card spans roughly x=164–500 and centers near x=332, while its trigger — the wavy stroke-width button — sits at about x=194, near the card's far left corner. The card therefore floats over the coloring-book, camera, AI, and undo buttons rather than over the control that opened it, and there is no caret, tail, or edge alignment tying it back. With the brush button (x=122) also underneath the card's left portion, ownership between the two adjacent tool buttons is visually ambiguous: nothing in the frame says these strokes belong to the wavy button rather than the brush.

Secondary and minor: the two thinnest previews render as gray rather than the purple of the three wider ones, so the row reads as two disabled entries followed by three active ones rather than as one continuous width ramp. The selected-state outline resolves it, but the color shift is doing unintended work.

The chevron at x=545 and the settings glyph at bottom-right are both locatable as shapes, so they meet the findability floor.
entries.recommendation: Anchor the stroke-width flyout to its trigger — align the card's left edge (or a small caret) with the wavy stroke-width button at x≈194 instead of centering it over the middle of the actions panel — and render all five stroke previews in the same active color so the row reads as one width ramp rather than two disabled entries plus three enabled ones.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
The honeycomb grid itself reads well: nine columns of hexagons tile edge-to-edge with consistent gaps, no swatch is clipped by the card, and the white card holds even margins on all four sides against the scrimmed page. The currently selected color is marked by a dark outline on the white hex at top right, which is legible. Touch targets are large (roughly 60px hexes) and well separated. There is no text in the card, so no fit or overflow concerns, and no evidence of scroll continuation (the bottom row sits clear of the card edge with no fade), so the whole palette appears to be shown at once. The left-edge color rail, the docked trash button, the expand chevron at bottom left and the settings gear at bottom right are all locatable.

The actionable gap is dismissal: the open card carries no visible close control, no title bar, and no other affordance indicating how to exit. Every other element in the frame is behind the scrim, so the only inferable dismissal paths are tapping a color or tapping the scrim — neither of which is signalled. Compared with the other dialogs this app ships, this card presents as a chrome-less panel, which is a consistency gap as well as a usability one for a child-facing surface where an accidental open has no obvious escape.
entries.recommendation: Add a visible close affordance to the color picker card — a round X button in the card's top-right corner (or top-left, matching whatever the settings card uses), sized to the same touch target as the other round buttons — so the dialog can be dismissed without selecting a color.

entries.surface_description: The responsive honeycomb color grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast across the honeycomb picker is mostly healthy: the mid- and high-chroma hexes (pinks, oranges, yellows, greens, blues, magentas) all sit well clear of the card's dark gray surface, and the left-edge palette strip's swatches likewise read distinctly against the page. The card itself is lifted a step above the page background, so its boundary is legible.

The one visible weakness is the darkest end of the grid. The bottom-right hex is essentially the same value as the card surface behind it and is only discernible because of a thin gray stroke around it; without that outline it would be invisible, and the outline itself is faint enough that the swatch reads as an empty hole in the grid rather than as a selectable black color. Its immediate neighbors — the very dark maroon at the bottom of the red column and the dark brown/near-black hexes in the second-from-right column — are similarly close in luminance to the card and lose their inter-cell separation, so that corner of the honeycomb turns into an indistinct dark mass where individual targets can't be told apart at a glance. This is specific to night mode: on a dark card, the low end of the value ramp collapses.

The white and light-gray hexes at the top right read cleanly, and the settings glyph in the bottom-right corner and the chevron at bottom-left are both locatable as shapes, consistent with their intended quiet parent-facing treatment.
entries.recommendation: In dark mode, give the near-black and very-dark swatches a brighter, consistently applied border (and/or a lighter inset surround) so each dark hex reads as a distinct, filled, selectable cell against the card surface rather than as a gap in the grid.

entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique:
The Coloring Books dialog itself is in good shape: title, 4×2 cover grid, and labels are evenly spaced with consistent card sizing, no clipped or truncated labels, no overlap, and a clearly hit-sized close button in the top-right corner. Both rows sit clear of the card's bottom edge with no fade strip, so nothing reads as cut off. The chevron and settings glyphs are both locatable in the bottom corners.

The one visible problem is the scrim's coverage. The canvas area behind the card is visibly darkened and blurred, but the surrounding chrome is not: the full-height color palette rail along the left edge is at full saturation (nine bright color discs plus the multicolor swatch), the round trash button top-right is at full red, and the bottom Actions Panel buttons (brush, stroke width, coloring-book, camera, AI, undo) are at full brightness and color. The result is a bright frame of controls surrounding a dimmed center, so the strongest color in the frame is outside the open dialog rather than in it, and the palette rail in particular pulls the eye away from the covers the child is meant to choose from. It also reads inconsistently with the stated dialog behavior — the scrim appears to be applied to the canvas layer only rather than to the whole page behind the card.
entries.recommendation: Render the dialog scrim above the full page chrome — the left color-palette rail, the docked trash button, and the bottom Actions Panel — rather than over the canvas layer alone, so everything behind the Coloring Books card is darkened and blurred uniformly.

Design decisions already settled for this app, given as context for what you are looking at rather than as a judgement of it: The round trash button that clears the drawing is docked against the edge of the screen on purpose, with part of it deliberately past the edge; it is not being clipped or cut off by the viewport. Pressing it undocks it. The chevron that expands and collapses the bottom-corner button panel, and the settings button in the opposite bottom corner, are drawn as thin low-contrast gray glyphs with no filled button, disc, or outline behind them, so they sit back from the child’s artwork; they are the parent-facing controls on this screen, and a child who never notices them is the point. Seeing them read as quiet, subdued, faint, easy to overlook at a glance, or much weaker than the drawing tools is that styling arriving, in either theme, and is the resting appearance of those two controls rather than a contrast finding about them. The floor they still owe is that the glyph remains findable: report one only when you cannot locate its shape anywhere in this image. Where a scrolling region continues past its edge, this app marks it with a soft gradient fade along that edge, and deliberately ships no arrow, scrollbar, or second indicator beside it. The fade is painted over the last line, row, or card rather than beside it, so that content thins out toward the edge and can read as blurred, smeared, washed out, grayed, or half-erased. That thinning is the cue itself being drawn — not a rendering artifact, a focus or compression fault, or a legibility problem in the region — so judge a scrolling region on the content that sits clear of its faded strip. Several overlays here are dialogs that lay one scrim over the whole page behind them — the settings card, the color picker, the coloring-book and AI cards, the parent gate, the admin action sheet — darkening and blurring the canvas, the color palette along the top edge, and the corner buttons together, in both themes, so the open card holds attention. Where you can see that the page behind an overlay has been darkened that way, background content reading dim, gray, soft, or blurred is that scrim rather than the styling of the elements beneath it, and the contrast and legibility to judge are those of the open card — its text, its controls, its close button — together with anything drawn on top of the scrim. The brush and stroke-width flyouts cast no scrim: where the page behind an overlay is still at full brightness, every element in the frame keeps its usual scope. In the bottom-corner panel of round buttons (the Actions Panel), the undo, AI, and screenshot buttons are drawn at reduced contrast whenever they are disabled, which is how this app marks them unavailable until at least one stroke is on the canvas. That reduced contrast is intended for those three buttons while they are in that disabled state; it is not a claim about their contrast once they are enabled. Judge only visible evidence. Use severity pass, low, medium, or high. A pass means there is no actionable visible issue and requires a null recommendation; otherwise give one specific recommendation. Return concise issue-category tags.
entries.surface_description: The installed coloring-book cover grid.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast on the coloring-book picker holds up. The card sits several steps lighter than the scrimmed page behind it, so its edge is clearly defined; "Coloring Books" reads as bright white on that panel, and the × close button in its own dark disc is plainly visible at top right. The eight cover tiles are lighter still than the card body, and every cover is drawn in white line art on that tile — the farm, dinosaur, creature, nature, objects, shapes, space and vehicle scenes are each individually readable, with fine details (fence pickets, snail shell, crane arm, tiny stars) surviving at this size. The eight titles under the covers are all legible; the lower row renders a touch brighter than the upper row, but the upper-row labels ("Farm", "Dinosaurs", "Creatures", "Nature") still read cleanly against their tiles and the difference does not push any of them toward illegibility. Behind the scrim, the color swatch column, the tool row and the red trash button read dim and soft, which is the dialog scrim doing its job rather than a contrast fault in those elements. The chevron beside the tool row and the settings gear at bottom right are both locatable as thin gray glyphs, meeting their findability floor.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
The "Farm" coloring-page grid dialog is open, but the page behind it is not darkened or blurred. The left color-swatch rail (purple, blue, teal, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, black, plus the multicolor palette button), the round red trash disc at top right, and the whole bottom actions row (pencil, stroke-width, photo, camera, AI, undo, chevron, gear) are all at full brightness and full saturation, matching or exceeding the visual weight of the open card. The saturated red trash disc competes directly with the dialog for first fixation, and the bright color rail runs the full left edge of the frame beside the card. Because the card is a plain white surface on a light background with only a soft shadow separating it, the absence of the scrim leaves no clear figure/ground split and the modal does not read as the focused layer.

Secondary, following from the same absence: the bottom row of thumbnails (dog, duckling) is cut off by the card's rounded bottom edge with no visible fade or thinning across those cards — the ball, paws, cattails, and pond lines stay fully crisp right up to the crop. In this frame the grid therefore reads as hard-cropped rather than as continuing below, so the "more pages below" affordance is not legible.

Within the card itself there are no defects: the "Farm" title, back chevron, and × close button are correctly sized, spaced, and unclipped; the two-column thumbnail grid has even gutters and consistent card radii; line art is legible at this size. Touch targets in the bottom row are separable and finger-sized, and both the panel chevron and the settings gear are locatable as thin gray glyphs.
entries.recommendation: Apply the app's standard dialog scrim (darken + blur the full page) behind the Farm coloring-page card as the other overlays do, so the color rail, trash button, and bottom actions row recede and the card holds focus; with the scrim in place, verify the grid's bottom-edge fade renders over the last thumbnail row.

entries.surface_description: A coloring book drilled into its page grid.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast in this coloring-page picker is largely sound. The "Farm" title renders near-white on the dark card and is fully legible. The four page thumbnails use white line art on near-black tiles — high contrast, and every animal, fence, cloud and flower detail is readable, including the fine hatching on the hay bale and the pond ripples. The two bottom rows thin out toward the card's lower edge, which is the scroll fade being drawn, so the content clear of that strip is what I judged and it holds up. The color palette down the left edge keeps each swatch distinguishable from the dark ground and from its neighbors, including the darker green and maroon. The drawing tools along the bottom read at full strength; the trash button at top right is high-contrast red-on-white.

The weak point is the card's own two controls. The back chevron at top left and the close "×" at top right are both drawn as thin mid-gray glyphs inside barely-visible circles on the dark card surface. These are card chrome inside the open dialog, not the two exempted parent-facing controls (the panel chevron and the settings gear), so they owe normal contrast — and against the card's dark surface they sit close to the surrounding fill. Both are locatable, but they are the primary and only means of leaving or backing out of this view, and they are noticeably dimmer than the title text sitting between them.
entries.recommendation: Raise the stroke and circle-fill contrast of the dialog's back chevron and close "×" in dark mode so both glyphs read at roughly the strength of the adjacent "Farm" title rather than as faint gray marks on the card surface.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique: Hierarchy and legibility are sound. The vertical color rail on the left edge has consistent swatch size and spacing, and the active purple swatch is clearly ringed. The line art is crisp and unobstructed, with no overlap between the drawing tools and the artwork. The coloring-book button carries a visible warm outline marking it as the active page chip, which is distinguishable from its neighbors at a glance. Undo, AI, and screenshot are drawn at reduced contrast consistent with the documented disabled state, and the pen and stroke-width buttons read at full strength. The chevron and settings glyphs in the bottom corners are both locatable in the frame. The docked trash button in the top-right reads as intended. No clipped or truncated text, no modal or scrim present, no overlapping controls. The single actionable observation is spacing: the bottom Actions Panel row sits flush against the bottom edge of the 744px-tall viewport, with the round buttons' lower arcs reaching the final few pixels, while every other edge carries a clear inset — the color rail has real left and top margin, and the trash button has a visible top offset. On a landscape iPad this places the touch targets on the home-indicator strip and makes the row read as pushed off the layout rather than seated within it.
entries.recommendation: Add a bottom inset to the Actions Panel row (and the settings/chevron glyphs on the same baseline) so the round buttons clear the bottom edge and the home-indicator strip, matching the margin already used on the left color rail and around the docked trash button.

entries.surface_description: A selected page with its active-page chip.
entries.critique: Night-mode contrast reads well throughout. The line art is white on a near-black charcoal canvas, giving a very high line-to-ground separation, and every contour of the cat, hay bale, fence, clouds, flowers and grass is cleanly resolved with no muddying. The left color rail's swatches all sit clearly against the dark strip, including the white swatch, which retains a visible edge, and the currently selected purple swatch is distinguishable by its ring. The active-page chip on the coloring-book button in the Actions Panel reads as a distinct gold/amber outline against the dark panel and is easy to identify as the applied state. The red round trash button in the top-right is high-contrast with a clearly legible white bin glyph. Within the Actions Panel, the brush, wave/stroke-width, book, camera and undo glyphs are all locatable and shaped clearly against their dark discs. The bottom-corner chevron and the settings gear in the opposite corner are both faint gray glyphs, but each shape is findable in the frame, which is the floor they owe under the stated styling. No overlay scrim is present, and no scrolling-fade region needs to be discounted. I found no legibility or contrast defect that is actionable on this evidence.

entries.critique: The coachmark itself reads cleanly: a translucent trash disc with a hand glyph beside it, drawn over empty canvas with the large pink drag-arc behind it. Nothing about it is clipped, overlapped, or illegible in this frame, and the docked trash button top-right, the chevron bottom-left and the settings gear bottom-right are all locatable. The one visible problem is in the left color rail: the top (purple) swatch is hard-cut by the top edge of the viewport — its selection ring is sliced flat across the top with no rounded cap, and there is no fade or thinning at that edge to signal a scroll region. The bottom rainbow/custom-color swatch likewise sits flush against the bottom edge with its ring nearly touching the frame. So the rail reads as an unpadded column whose end items collide with the screen edges rather than as a deliberately docked or scrollable strip, and the selected-state ring on the active color — the one swatch whose ring carries meaning — is the element that loses part of its shape.
entries.recommendation: Add top and bottom padding to the left color rail (at least the swatch ring's stroke plus a few px) so the first and last swatches, including the selection ring on the active color, sit fully inside the viewport instead of being cut by the screen edges.

entries.surface_description: The accept ring and paper wash while held past threshold.
entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique:
The frame shows the drag-to-clear gesture held past threshold: the red trash button sits undocked at roughly (881, 281), and the threshold feedback is a very large red-outlined circle with a soft red inner glow whose center lies off-frame beyond the top-right corner. Only an arc of that circle is visible, entering the top edge near x≈810 and exiting the right edge near y≈355.

The problem is association. The trash button is not at the center of that ring, nor visibly enclosed by it — the arc passes above and right of the button, which sits on the outside of the arc's concave side, separated by roughly 80–100 px at the nearest point. With the ring's center off-screen there is nothing on the canvas tying the arc to the control under the finger; it reads as an unexplained red stroke sweeping across the top-right of the paper rather than as an accept target. The soft red wash bleeding toward the button is the only link, and it is diffuse and low-contrast against the cream paper.

Secondary: at this held-past-threshold moment nothing states the outcome. There is no label and no icon change, and the canvas holds only a single faint purple horizontal stroke at y≈371 — no washed icon set is visible. So the frame gives a red arc, a red button, and near-blank paper, with no confirmation that release will clear the drawing.

Everything else is clean: the left color rail is evenly spaced with a clear selected state (purple, ringed) and large unambiguous targets; both parent-facing gray glyphs are locatable — chevron at (115, 706), gear at (1101, 712). No text to clip, no overlap, no scrolling region in view.
entries.recommendation: Constrain the accept ring so its full circumference stays within the viewport and is centered on (or clearly encloses) the dragged trash button, so the threshold state reads as a target around that control rather than an off-screen arc; if the ring must stay oversized, add a short label such as "Release to clear" anchored beside the button.

entries.surface_description: The accept ring and paper wash while held past threshold.
entries.surface_intent: The faint icons washed over the canvas are the intended effect: they signal that clearing the drawing is underway.
entries.critique:
Night mode, clear-gesture held past threshold. The elements that carry the gesture read well: the docked trash button is a saturated red disc with a bright yellow trash glyph on it (strong contrast), and the red accept ring sweeping across the upper right is clearly visible against the near-black canvas. The washed faint icons over the canvas are the intended clearing effect. The chevron at bottom left and the gear at bottom right are both locatable as shapes — quiet by design, no finding. The color swatch column at the left edge is bright and each hue is distinguishable, with the selected purple swatch carrying a visible ring.

The one weak element is the horizontal progress/threshold bar in the middle of the canvas (roughly x=333–873, y=371). It is a muted violet fill on a near-black canvas with no visible track, outline, or contrasting unfilled remainder. At this luminance it reads as a barely-there smudge — it is the least visible thing on screen, yet it is the feedback that tells the user how far the hold has progressed toward clearing the drawing. Because there is no discernible boundary between filled and unfilled portions, its state cannot be read at a glance in night mode. It is also the only element here that competes for legibility with the deliberately-quiet parent controls, which is the wrong ranking for a destructive-action progress indicator.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance of the clear-progress bar's fill in dark mode (e.g. toward the bright accent violet used on the selected swatch, or match the red of the accept ring so it reads as part of the same destructive gesture) and give it a faint visible track behind the unfilled portion so the filled/unfilled boundary is readable against the near-black canvas.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
The install banner is well-formed overall: the Splotch mark, two-line title, subtitle, purple "How?" button and a circular × close control read clearly on the white card against the light canvas, with the card's rounded border and drop shadow separating it from the paper texture. The three purple strokes, the left color rail, the docked trash button, the collapse chevron at bottom-left and the settings gear at bottom-right are all locatable, and the page behind the banner is at full brightness, consistent with a non-modal prompt. Touch targets on the card ("How?" pill and the × disc) are distinct and comfortably sized for the tablet.

The one visible defect is vertical text fit inside the card. The subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" wraps to a second line whose final word, "app", sits flush against the card's bottom inner edge — the descender-height band below the baseline is essentially zero, so the text reads as pressed into the border rather than padded away from it. The block is also visibly bottom-heavy relative to the top inset: the title's cap-height clears the top border by a comfortable margin, while the wrapped subtitle line has none at the bottom, so the copy column looks vertically misbalanced against the vertically centered icon, button and close control beside it. The banner as a whole also sits very low in the viewport, with the card's bottom edge close to the screen bottom, which compounds the cramped impression.

No clipping of glyphs, no overlap between the copy column and the "How?" button or × control, and no truncation of any string was observed; this is a padding/leading issue rather than a content-loss one.
entries.recommendation: Increase the banner card's bottom padding (and/or the copy column's line-height) so the wrapped subtitle's last line clears the card's inner bottom edge by at least the same inset used at the top, keeping the text column vertically balanced against the centered icon, "How?" button, and close control.

entries.surface_description: The earned iOS home-screen prompt after a few strokes.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the install banner is mostly sound: the card sits on a dark slate ground with a visible violet border, and the title "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white and cleanly legible. The Splotch mark reads fine. The parent-facing chevron (bottom left) and settings gear (bottom right) are faint by design but both shapes are locatable, so no finding there; the trash button and palette are legible.

The one actionable contrast issue is the supporting line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app." It is rendered in a mid-gray at a notably smaller size than the title, and against the dark card it reads as the weakest text in the frame — visibly dimmer than the title above it and than the "How?" label. Since this line carries the explanation of what the action does, it is doing real communicative work and is not a deliberately recessive parent control.

Secondary, milder: the "×" dismiss glyph is a gray mark on a barely-lighter dark disc, so its affordance leans on the disc rather than the glyph; it is findable but sits close to the floor. The "How?" button's violet label on a low-saturation violet fill is legible but is the lowest-contrast interactive label on the card.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the banner's supporting line ("Opens full-screen, just like a real app") toward the near-white used for the title — roughly a light neutral at 75–85% opacity rather than mid-gray — so it clears comfortable body-text contrast on the dark card; apply the same lift to the "×" dismiss glyph.

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique: In the expanded install-banner instructions, every line break falls mid-phrase around the inline icons: line 1 ends on the "Add to Home Screen" plus-square icon with its quoted label pushed to line 2; line 2 ends on the chevron glyph, splitting the quoted string across lines as "View / More"; line 3 is a single orphaned word, "first." The inline share and plus icons also sit above the surrounding text baseline, so the passage reads as mixed-height fragments rather than a sentence. The card is roughly 420px wide inside a 1133px landscape frame, so the three-line wrap is not forced by available width. Separately, the card's internal vertical rhythm is uneven: a conspicuous empty band sits between the header row and the instruction block, and the padding below "first." is about double the padding above the header, leaving the expanded content low and off-center in its container. No clipping or overlap is present; the header, "How?" button and × close are well separated and comfortably sized; the color rail is evenly spaced; the trash button, the bottom-left chevron and the bottom-right settings glyph are all locatable.
entries.recommendation: Keep each icon bound to the phrase it belongs to — wrap "[share icon] Share", "[plus icon] \"Add to Home Screen\"" and "[chevron] \"View More\"" in non-breaking inline groups (white-space: nowrap) and give the inline glyphs vertical-align: middle (or -0.1em baseline offset) so they sit on the text baseline; widen the card slightly in landscape so the instruction reads in one or two clean lines with no orphaned "first."

entries.surface_description: The expanded iOS Share-sheet guidance.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on the install banner is broadly sound. The card sits on a lighter panel than the canvas with a visible purple border, so it separates cleanly from the background. The heading "Add Splotch to your home screen" is near-white on the dark card and fully legible. The instruction paragraph beneath the divider ("Tap ⬆ Share at the bottom of the screen, then choose "Add to Home Screen". If you don't see it, tap ⌄ "View More" first.") is light gray with the quoted labels rendered in brighter, bolder white, so the actionable phrases carry the most weight — the correct emphasis order. The inline share and "add to home screen" glyphs and the chevron are drawn at roughly the same value as the surrounding text and stay identifiable at their small size. The "How?" pill uses dark violet text on a light lavender fill, a strong positive-contrast pairing, and the × close control is a light glyph on a muted circle that is easy to find.

The one weak element is the subtitle line "Opens full-screen, just like a real app". It is set at the smallest type size in the frame, in a mid-gray that is noticeably dimmer than both the heading above it and the instruction text below it, on a dark card. At that size the stroke weight leaves little margin, and it is the least readable text in the image despite being body copy rather than a deliberately recessed parent control. Everything else in scope — the palette swatches along the left edge, the trash button's icon on its warm fill, and the corner glyphs whose shapes remain locatable — presents no night-mode legibility problem.
entries.recommendation: Raise the value of the banner subtitle "Opens full-screen, just like a real app" toward the same light gray used for the instruction paragraph (or increase its size/weight slightly) so the smallest text on the card is not also its dimmest.

entries.surface_description: The multiplication challenge protecting a sensitive operation.
entries.critique:
The parent gate card is legible in night mode. "Grown-Ups Only" is near-white on the dark card and reads strongly; the subtitle "Solve the problem to continue" is a lighter gray but comfortably readable at size. The 0–9 keypad tiles are the clearest element in the card — white numerals on medium-dark tiles, each tile edge distinguishable from the card ground, and the backspace glyph reads clearly. The close ✕ in its circular button at top right is white on gray and easy to find. The footer line "Settings › Parent Center" is muted but still resolvable, with the gear and person glyphs visible. The operand chips (purple 6, blue 9) carry white numerals with adequate separation, and the "×" and "=" operators, while dim gray, are readable.

The one weak spot is the pair of dashed answer placeholders to the right of "=". They are drawn as very faint dashed outlines only slightly lighter than the card background — noticeably fainter than every other element in the card, including the already-muted footer text. These are the target of the interaction: they show where tapped digits will land and how many digits are expected. In night mode they nearly dissolve into the card, so a parent scanning the gate may not immediately see that two entry slots exist or where their input is going. This is an element inside the open card, at full brightness with no scrim over it, so it falls squarely in scope.

No other contrast or legibility problem is visible: the canvas, palette, and corner controls behind the dialog are dimmed by the dialog's scrim as expected, and the quiet chevron and settings glyphs at the bottom corners are both locatable in the frame.
entries.recommendation: Raise the luminance of the two empty answer placeholders in dark mode — brighten the dashed stroke to at least the level of the keypad tile chrome, and consider a subtly filled slot behind it, so the entry positions are as visible as the keypad the user is about to tap.

entries.surface_description: Style selection over the child’s drawing preview.
entries.critique:
The "Pick a style" card itself is well-formed: the title and round close button sit on one line with clear separation; the 4x2 grid of style thumbnails is evenly gutter-spaced with consistent tile sizing; all eight labels (Magical, Crayon, Watercolor, Paper, Felt, Sticker, Cartoon, Clay) fit on a single line, centered under their thumbnails, with no truncation, wrap, or overlap; tiles are large, unambiguous touch targets; the card is centered in the 1133x744 frame with even padding and no clipping; and the full grid fits without scrolling, so no scroll-fade cue is required or missing inside it.

The visible defect is at the layer boundary. This is a dialog card, but the page behind it is at full brightness with no darkening or blur: the color-swatch rail down the left edge is fully saturated and crisp, the red trash button at top-right is at full strength, and the entire bottom row of drawing tools (brush, stroke width, coloring book, camera, AI, undo) plus the panel chevron and the settings gear are all sharp and undimmed. Without that separation the modal reads as one more floating panel rather than the element holding focus. The bright red trash button competes directly with the card for first attention, and the six colorful tool buttons along the bottom read as equally live and tappable while a style choice is pending. The card is a white surface on a plain light canvas, so a soft shadow is the only thing establishing it as a layer, which compounds the weak separation in light mode.

Other checks pass: both low-contrast parent controls are locatable (the chevron immediately right of the undo button, the gear at bottom-right), the trash button's docked-past-the-edge treatment is present as specified, and no tool button shows disabled-state dimming.
entries.recommendation: Apply the app's standard dialog scrim behind the AI style card — the same darken-and-blur over the canvas, color rail, trash button, and corner button panel that the settings and color-picker overlays use — so the open card is the only fully bright, fully tappable surface in the frame.

entries.surface_description: The progress dial over the blurred drawing preview.
entries.critique: The AI "Making your picture…" card is presented as a scrimmed dialog: the canvas, the bottom-corner chevron, and the settings gear behind it are all clearly darkened and desaturated. But the scrim does not reach two regions of the frame. The full-height color palette column along the left edge renders at full brightness and full saturation — every swatch (purple, blue, teal, green, olive, orange, red, magenta, black, and the multi-color flower) is as vivid as it would be with no overlay open — and the round red trash button docked at the top-right edge is likewise at full strength, glowing brighter than anything in the frame except the dial itself. The result is that the two most saturated color regions on screen sit outside the dimmed layer while the dialog is modal, so attention is split three ways: the pink progress dial in the center, the vertical stripe of saturated swatches at the left, and the red disc at the top right. The palette stripe in particular runs the entire 744px height and, at full chroma against a dark scrim, reads as an active, tappable control set at a moment when the modal has taken over the screen. Everything within the card itself is sound: "Making your picture…" and "This takes about 30 seconds" are fully legible with clear size and weight hierarchy, the "Keep drawing while you wait" pill has generous padding and an ample touch target, the round close button at the card's top-right is unambiguous and clear of the preview edge, and nothing is clipped, overlapping, or overflowing. Spacing between the preview panel, the two text lines, and the button is even and unhurried. The one card-internal weakness is minor: the progress dial reads as a nearly solid filled disc with only a thin hairline seam marking the boundary, so the proportion completed is very hard to judge at a glance — the "how far along am I" signal that a dial is for is not really conveyed.
entries.recommendation: Extend the AI card's scrim over the full viewport so the left color-palette column and the docked trash button are darkened and desaturated along with the canvas and corner controls, leaving the card and its dial as the only full-brightness elements while the dialog is open.

entries.critique:
The AI result dialog itself is clean: the generated picture fills the card with even margins, the rounded close button sits clear of the image in the top-right corner with a comfortable touch target, and the "Download" pill is centered, well-padded, and legible with its icon and label fitting inside. The "AI-generated picture · Report" caption below the card is small but readable and its flag icon and link text are grouped clearly. No clipping, overlap, or text overflow anywhere in the card. The dimmed, blurred canvas behind reads as the intended scrim.

The one visible inconsistency is that the scrim does not cover the whole page. The vertical color palette down the left edge and the round trash button at the top right are rendered at full brightness and full saturation while everything else behind the dialog is darkened. The ten saturated swatches form the highest-contrast column in the frame and compete directly with the modal for attention, and the red trash button at the top right sits at the same brightness as the modal's own close button just below it, so two bright circular targets stack in the same corner region with different meanings. Because those controls look undimmed, they also read as still active while a blocking dialog is open, which is ambiguous for touch on a tablet.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the full viewport so the left color palette and the top-right trash button are darkened and blurred along with the canvas, keeping the AI result card and its caption the only elements at full brightness.

entries.surface_description: The generated picture, download action, and report flag.
entries.critique:
Night-mode contrast on this AI-result screen holds up well overall. The open card is the thing to judge: the generated rainbow sits on a light panel with no dimming, the "Download" button is a saturated purple pill with a white label and white download glyph — clearly the strongest affordance in the frame and easily read — and the close button is a filled white disc with a dark ✕ against the picture's light-blue sky, so its shape and hit target are unambiguous. The card's dark chrome is a lighter charcoal than the page behind it, so the card edge is discernible without a border.

The two elements drawn on top of the scrim below the card are the weak point. "AI-generated picture" renders as a mid-gray on the near-black page and is readable but muted; the adjacent "Report" affordance, with its small flag glyph, is a desaturated red on that same near-black ground at small type size. Red-on-black is the least forgiving pairing in a dark theme — the red channel carries nearly all the luminance, so effective contrast sits at or just under the small-text threshold, and the thin flag icon fares worse than the word beside it. Report is a safety-relevant control on a screen showing generated imagery to a child, so it is the one label here that should not be the dimmest text in the frame.

Both parent-facing glyphs are locatable: the collapse chevron at the bottom left and the settings gear at the bottom right are each findable by shape, so neither is a finding. The docked trash button at the top right and the color column at the left read as intended, and the picture itself has no legibility problem.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the "Report" label and its flag glyph — shift to a lighter, less saturated red, or pair the red glyph with a near-white label — so the small text clears roughly 4.5:1 against the dark page, and nudge the "AI-generated picture" caption up a step so the caption is not brighter than the actionable control beside it.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
The report confirmation dialog itself is well formed: "Report this picture" heading, a five-line retention paragraph that wraps cleanly with no clipping or overflow, two labeled thumbnails ("The AI picture", "The drawing behind it") at equal size with captions fully legible, and a Cancel / Send report pair that are large, clearly separated, and weighted so the primary action is obvious. Padding is even and nothing overlaps.

The visible defect is inconsistent scrim coverage. The page behind the overlay is darkened across the AI result card, its Download button, and the bottom "AI-generated picture · Report" chip, but the color-palette column along the left edge is not: its swatches render at full saturation on a white strip that is clearly brighter than the adjacent scrimmed area, with a hard vertical seam where the two treatments meet at roughly x=84. The docked trash button at top right is similarly still at full red saturation while everything around it is dimmed. So the most colorful, highest-contrast elements in the frame are exactly the ones the modal should be suppressing, and they pull attention away from a confirmation that carries a data-retention notice.
entries.recommendation: Extend the dialog scrim over the left color-palette strip and the docked trash button so the whole page behind the report modal is dimmed uniformly, removing the bright vertical seam at the palette's right edge.

entries.surface_description: The confirmation and retention notice before a report is sent.
entries.critique:
Judging only the open "Report this picture" card and its controls (the page behind it carries the dialog scrim, so the dimmed canvas, palette, Download pill and corner glyphs are out of scope; the chevron at bottom-left and the settings glyph at bottom-right are both locatable).

The card itself holds up well in night mode: the heading is near-white on the dark plum surface, the retention body copy stays fully legible at its smaller size, the two thumbnail captions ("The AI picture", "The drawing behind it") are readable, the close ✕ in the top-right of the AI panel is visible against the darkened image behind it, and the primary "Send report" button is white on saturated violet with strong separation.

The one weak element is the secondary "Cancel" button. Its label is a desaturated lavender sitting on a dark plum fill that is only slightly lighter than the card surface, so the text-to-fill contrast lands noticeably below its neighbour and reads as the faintest interactive text in the card. The button's own edge against the card is also very low, so the control reads more as a tinted block of text than as a button. This is a destructive-adjacent choice ("back out of sending a report") that a parent needs to read quickly, and it is not covered by any of the settled decisions above — it is not scrimmed, not disabled-state styling, and not one of the deliberately quiet parent glyphs.
entries.recommendation: Lighten the "Cancel" label toward the card's near-white body text color (or raise the button fill's lightness) so the secondary action clears 4.5:1 against its own fill, and give the button a visible border so it reads as a control rather than tinted text.
